children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, among my monk disciples who are inclined through faith, this monk <s>Vakkalī</s> is the foremost."

children.text: tato bhagavān bhikṣusahasraparivṛto vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi kurvan sūrpārakaṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surrounded by a thousand monks and performing varied miracles, arrived at the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati yadi ekena dvāreṇa praviśāmi apareṣāṃ bhaviṣyati anyathātvam ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One considered, "If I enter through one gate, the others will feel that it is otherwise for them.

children.text: yannvaham ṛddhyaiva praviśeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I enter precisely by <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power)?"

children.text: tata ṛddhyā upari vihāyasā madhye sūrpārakasya nagarasyāvatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then by <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power) he descended from the upper air into the middle of the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sūrpārakādhipatī rājā āyuṣmān pūrṇo dārukarṇī stavakarṇī trapukarṇī te ca saptadaśa putrāḥ svakasvakena parivāreṇa yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ anekāni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, the king, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>Dārukarṇī</s>, <s>Stavakarṇī</s>, <s>Trapukarṇī</s>, and those seventeen sons, each with his own retinue, approached the Blessed One, along with many hundreds of thousands of living beings.

children.text: tato bhagavānanekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairanugamyamāno yena candanamālaḥ prāsādas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, followed by many hundreds of thousands of living beings, approached the palace named <s>Candanamāla</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

children.text: sa janakāyo bhagavantamapaśyaṃścandanamālaṃ prāsādaṃ bhettumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the crowd could not see the Blessed One, they began to break open the <s>Candanamāla</s> palace.

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati yadi candanamālaḥ prāsādo bhetsyate dātṝṇāṃ puṇyāntarāyo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One considered, "If the <s>Candanamāla</s> palace is broken, there will be an obstruction to the merit of the donors.

children.text: yannvahamenaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ nirminuyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to make it of crystal?"

children.text: sa bhagavatā sphaṭikamayo nirmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was made of crystal by the Blessed One.

children.text: tato bhagavatā tasyāḥ pariṣada āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature of that assembly, gave such a Dharma teaching that, after hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of living beings attained a great distinction.

children.text: kaiścinmokṣabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlāni utpāditāni kaiścinnirvedhabhāgīyāni kaiścit srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam kaiścidanāgāmiphalam kaiścit sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiścit śrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni kaiścit pratyekabodhau kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittānyutpāditāni ||
children.translated_text: Some produced roots of good conducive to liberation; some produced those conducive to <s>nirveda</s> (penetrating disenchantment). Some realized the fruit of stream-entry; some the fruit of once-returning; some the fruit of non-returning; some, through the abandonment of all defilements, realized arhatship. Some gave rise to thoughts directed toward disciple-awakening, some toward solitary-buddha awakening, and some gave rise to thoughts directed toward unsurpassed complete awakening.

children.text: yadbhūyasā sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthāpitā ||
children.translated_text: For the most part that assembly was established as inclined toward the Buddha, bent toward the Dharma, and sloping toward the Saṃgha.

children.text: atha dārukarṇī stavakarṇī trapukarṇī ca praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya āsanāni prajñāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayanti samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālam manyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dārukarṇī</s>, <s>Stavakarṇī</s>, and <s>Trapukarṇī</s> gathered excellent foods to be eaten and consumed, arranged seats, and announced the time to the Blessed One by a messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready, if the Blessed One now thinks it the proper time."

children.text: tena khalu samayena kṛṣṇagautamakau nāgarājau mahāsamudre prativasataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time the two nāga kings <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s> were dwelling in the great ocean.

children.text: tau saṃlakṣayataḥ bhagavān sūrpārake nagare dharmaṃ deśayati ||
children.translated_text: They perceived, "The Blessed One is teaching the Dharma in the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>."

children.text: gacchāvaḥ dharmaṃ śroṣyāva iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let us go; we will hear the Dharma."

children.text: tatastau pañcanāgaśataparivārau pañcanadīśatāni saṃjanya sūrpārakaṃ nagaraṃ samprasthitau ||
children.translated_text: Then the two of them, each with a retinue of five hundred nāgas and having produced five hundred rivers, set out for the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.

children.text: asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Buddhas, Blessed Ones, are not subject to forgetfulness.

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati imau kṛṣṇagautamau nāgarājau yadi sūrpārakaṃ nagaramāgamiṣyataḥ agocarīkariṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One perceived, "If these two nāga kings, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s>, come to the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, they will make it no proper field of resort."

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanamāmantrayate pratigṛhāṇa mahāmaudgalyāyana tathāgatasyātyayikapiṇḍapātam ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: "Receive, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the Tathāgata's urgent alms-food."

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ pañca me maudgalyāyana ātyayikapiṇḍapātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "For what reason? <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, I have five urgent alms-foods."

children.text: katame pañca āgantukasya gamikasya glānasya glānopasthāyakasyopadhivārikasya ca ||
children.translated_text: "What five? Those for one who has arrived, for one who is departing, for one who is sick, for one attending the sick, and for one guarding the requisites."

children.text: asmiṃstvarthe bhagavānupādhau vartate ||
children.translated_text: In this matter, however, the Blessed One was acting with regard to a special circumstance.

children.text: atha bhagavān maudgalyāyanasahāyo yena kṛṣṇagautamakau nāgarājau tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, accompanied by <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, went to the place where the two nāga kings <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s> were.

children.text: tau kathayataḥ samanvāharata nāgendrau sūrpārakaṃ nagaramagocarībhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He said to them, "Attend, lords of nāgas: the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> will become unsuitable as a resort."

children.text: tau kathayataḥ tādṛśena bhadanta prasādena vayamāgatā yanna śakyamasmābhiḥ kuntapipīlikasyāpi prāṇinaḥ pīḍāmutpādayituṃ prāgeva sūrpārakanagaranivāsino janakāyasyeti ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Venerable sir, we have come with such faith that it would not be possible for us to cause pain even to a tiny ant, much less to the body of people living in the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>."

children.text: tato bhagavatā kṛṣṇagautamakayor nāgarājayostādṛśo dharmo yaṃ śrutvā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatau dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gatau śikṣāpadāni ca gṛhītāni ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One taught such a Dharma to the two nāga kings <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s> that, after hearing it, they went for refuge to the Buddha, went for refuge to the Dharma and the Saṃgha, and accepted the training rules.

children.text: bhagavān bhaktakṛtyaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One began to perform the business of the meal.

children.text: ekaiko nāgaḥ saṃlakṣayati aho bata bhagavān mama pānīyaṃ pibatu iti ||
children.translated_text: Each nāga thought, "Ah, may the Blessed One drink my water!"

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati yadi ekasyaiva pānīyaṃ pāsyāmi eṣāṃ bhaviṣyati anyathātvam ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One perceived, "If I drink the water of only one of them, there will be a feeling of exclusion among these others."

children.text: upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: "A skillful arrangement must be made."

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanamāmantrayate gaccha maudgalyāyana yatra pañcānāṃ nadīśatānāṃ saṃbhedaḥ tasmādudakasya pātrapūramānaya ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: "Go, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, to the place where the five hundred rivers meet, and bring a bowlful of water from there."

children.text: evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yatra pañcānāṃ nadīśatānāṃ saṃbhedastatrodakasya pātrapūramādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> replied to the Blessed One; then he went to the place where the five hundred rivers met, took a bowlful of water from there, and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavata udakasya pātrapūramupanāmayati ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he offered the bowlful of water to the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavatā gṛhītvā paribhuktam ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One took it and consumed it.

children.text: āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ saṃlakṣayati pūrvamuktaṃ bhagavatā duṣkarakārakau hi bhikṣavaḥ putrasya mātāpitarau āpyāyakau poṣakau saṃvardhakau stanyasya dātārau citrasya jambudvīpasya darśayitārau ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> thought, "Previously the Blessed One said, 'Monks, mother and father are doers of what is difficult for a son: they refresh him, nourish him, raise him, give him milk, and show him the varied continent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."

children.text: ekenāṃśena putro mātaraṃ dvitīyena pitaraṃ pūrṇavarṣaśataṃ paricaret yadvā asyāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ maṇayo muktā vaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvarta iti evaṃrūpe vā vividhaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayen neyatā putreṇa mātāpitroḥ kṛtaṃ vā syādupakṛtaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "If a son were to attend upon his mother on one shoulder and his father on the other for a full hundred years, or were to establish them in lordship and sovereignty over whatever jewels, pearls, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, emerald, cat's-eye, ruby, and right-turning conches there are on this great earth, not by that much would a son have done what should be done for his parents or repaid their help."

children.text: yastu asāvaśrāddhaṃ mātāpitaraṃ śraddhāsampadi samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati duḥśīlaṃ śīlasampadi matsariṇaṃ tyāgasampadi duṣprajñaṃ prajñāsampadi samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati iyatā putreṇa mātāpitroḥ kṛtaṃ vā syādupakṛtaṃ veti ||
children.translated_text: "But if someone induces, trains, settles, and establishes unbelieving parents in the wealth of faith; immoral parents in the wealth of moral discipline; miserly parents in the wealth of giving; and foolish parents in the wealth of wisdom, by that much a son has done what should be done for his parents and has repaid their help."

children.text: mayā ca mātur na kaścidupakāraḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And I have done no service for my mother."

children.text: yadahaṃ samanvāhareyaṃ kutra me mātā upapanneti ||
children.translated_text: "Let me consider where my mother has been reborn."

children.text: samanvāhartuṃ saṃvṛttaḥ paśyati marīcike lokadhātau upapannā ||
children.translated_text: He began to consider, and he saw that she had been reborn in the world-system <s>Marīcika</s>.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati kasya vineyā paśyati bhagavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He thought, "By whom is she to be trained?" He saw: "By the Blessed One."

children.text: tasyaitadabhavat dūraṃ vayamihāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "We have come a long way here."

children.text: yannvahametamarthaṃ bhagavato nivedayeyamiti bhagavantamidamavocat uktaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā pūrvam duṣkarakārakau hi bhikṣavaḥ putrasya mātāpitarau iti ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, "I should report this matter to the Blessed One," he said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, it was formerly said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, a son's mother and father are performers of difficult deeds.'"

children.text: tanmama mātā marīcike lokadhātau upapannā sā ca bhagavato vineyā ||
children.translated_text: Now my mother has been reborn in the <s>Marīcika</s> world-system, and she is one to be trained by the Blessed One.

children.text: tadarhati bhagavāṃs tāṃ vinetumanukampāmupādāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore may the Blessed One, out of compassion, deign to train her.

children.text: bhagavān kathayati maudgalyāyana kasya ṛddhyā gacchāmaḥ bhagavan madīyayā ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, by whose <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power) shall we go?" "Blessed One, by mine."

children.text: tato bhagavānāyuṣmāṃśca mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ sumerumūrdhni pādān sthāpayantau samprasthitau ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One and the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, placing their feet on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, set out.

children.text: saptame divase marīcikaṃ lokadhātumanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day they reached the <s>Marīcika</s> world-system.

children.text: adrākṣīt sā bhadrakanyā āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ dūrādeva ||
children.translated_text: That good young woman saw the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> from afar.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ sasambhramāt tatsakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati cirādbata putrakaṃ paśyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: And having seen him, she approached him hurriedly and said, "After so long, indeed, I see my little son."

children.text: tato janakāyaḥ kathayati bhadanto 'yaṃ pravrajito vṛddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the crowd said, "This venerable one is an old renunciant.

children.text: iyaṃ ca kanyā ||
children.translated_text: And this one is a young woman.

children.text: kathamasya mātā bhavatīti āyuṣmān maudgalyāyanaḥ kathayati bhavantaḥ mama ime skandhā anayā saṃvṛddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: How can she be his mother?" The venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> said, "Sirs, these aggregates of mine were brought up by her.

children.text: tena mameyaṃ māteti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore she is my mother."

children.text: tato bhagavatā tasyā bhadrakanyāyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā tayā bhadrakanyayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature of that good young woman, the Blessed One gave such a teaching of the Dharma, one that brought realization of the four noble truths, that after hearing it that good young woman split apart with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (identity-view) rising up with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of <s>srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry).

children.text: sā dṛṣṭasatyā trirudānamudānayati pūrvavat yāvat pratiṣṭhāpitā devamanuṣyeṣu ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the truth, she uttered a solemn utterance three times, as before, up to the words that she was established among gods and humans.

children.text: āha ca ||
children.translated_text: And she said:

children.text: tavānubhāvātpihitaḥ sughoro hyapāyamārgo bahudoṣaduṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Through your power the very dreadful road to the bad destinies, corrupted by many faults, has been closed.

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā nirvāṇamārgaṃ ca mayopalabdham ||
children.translated_text: The meritorious path to heaven has been opened, and the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been obtained by me.

children.text: tvadāśrayāccāptamapetadoṣaṃ mamādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By relying on you, today I have obtained the pure, very purified eye, free from faults.

children.text: prāptaṃ ca kāntaṃ padamāryakāntaṃ tīrṇā ca duḥkhārṇavapāramasmi ||
children.translated_text: The lovely state, beloved by the noble ones, has been reached, and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.

children.text: jagati daityanarāmarapūjita vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmaya
children.translated_text: O you who are worshiped in the world by daityas, men, and immortals, free from the disease of birth, old age, and death,

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana saphalamadya mune tava darśanam ||
children.translated_text: O sage, your sight, very hard to obtain through thousands of existences, has today become fruitful."

children.text: atikrāntāhaṃ bhadanta atikrāntā eṣāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "I have crossed over, venerable sir; I have crossed over. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dharma, and to the community of monks.

children.text: upāsikāṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāmabhiprasannām ||
children.translated_text: And from today onward, for as long as life lasts, regard me as a laywoman, living, gone for refuge, and filled with faith.

children.text: adhivāsayatu me bhagavānadya piṇḍapātena sārdhamāryamahāmaudgalyāyaneneti ||
children.translated_text: May the Blessed One accept my alms-meal today together with noble <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavāṃstasyā bhadrakanyāyāstūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One accepted the good young woman's invitation by silence.

children.text: atha sā bhadrakanyā bhagavantamāyuṣmantaṃ ca mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that good young woman knew that the Blessed One and the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> were comfortably seated, she satisfied and served them with her own hand with pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten. Knowing that the Blessed One had eaten, had washed his hands, and that his bowl had been removed, she took a lower seat and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the Dharma.

children.text: bhagavatā tasyā dharmo deśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Dharma was taught to her by the Blessed One.

children.text: āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pātragrāhakaḥ pātraṃ niryātayati ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the Blessed One's bowl-bearer, handed over the bowl.

children.text: bhagavatā abhihitaḥ maudgalyāyana gacchāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, let us go."

children.text: gacchāmo bhagavan ||
children.translated_text: "Let us go, Blessed One."

children.text: kasya ṛddhyā tathāgatasya bhagavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By whose <s>ṛddhi</s>?" "By that of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Blessed One."

children.text: yadi evam samanvāhara jetavanam ||
children.translated_text: "If so, bring <s>Jetavana</s> to mind."

children.text: āgatāḥ smo bhagavan āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "We have arrived, Blessed One; we have arrived."

children.text: maudgalyāyanastato vismayāvarjitamatiḥ kathayati kiṃ nāmeyaṃ bhagavann ṛddhir manojavā maudgalyāyana ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, his mind overcome with wonder, said, "What indeed, Blessed One, is this <s>ṛddhi</s>?" "It is swift as thought, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>."

children.text: na mayā bhadanta vijñātamevaṃ gambhīramevaṃ gambhīrā buddhadharmā iti ||
children.translated_text: "Venerable sir, I did not know that the qualities of Buddhas were so deep, so very deep.

children.text: yadi vijñātamabhaviṣyat tilaśo 'pi me saṃcūrṇitaśarīreṇānuttarāyāḥ samyaksambodheścittaṃ vyāvartitamabhaviṣyat ||
children.translated_text: Had I known, even if my body were crushed into pieces like sesame seeds, my mind would not have turned away from unsurpassed complete awakening.

children.text: idānīṃ kiṃ karomi dagdhendhana iti ||
children.translated_text: What am I to do now, when the fuel has already been burned?"

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā pūrṇena karma kṛtam yenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam yena dāsyāḥ kukṣau upapannaḥ pravrajya ca sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam bhagavānāha pūrṇena bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitāni avaśyambhāvīni ||
children.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts: "Venerable sir, what karma was done by the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> that he was born in a rich family, one of great wealth and great possessions? What karma was done that he was born in the womb of a slave-woman, and that after going forth he directly realized arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements?" The Blessed One said, "Monks, deeds were done and accumulated by the monk <s>Pūrṇa</s>; they had obtained their requisites, their conditions had matured, they stood present like a flood, and they were bound to come to pass.

children.text: pūrṇena karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni ||
children.translated_text: Deeds were done and accumulated by <s>Pūrṇa</s>.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks, deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, deeds done and accumulated, good and bad, ripen only in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatairapi
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish, even over hundreds of kalpas.

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, after obtaining the necessary conditions and the proper time, deeds bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'sminneva bhadrakalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Monks, in the past, in this very good aeon, when people had a lifespan of twenty thousand years, a fully awakened Buddha named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a well-gone one, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans.

children.text: buddho bhagavān vārāṇasīṃ nagarīmupaniśritya viharati ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in dependence on the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: tasyāyaṃ śāsane pravrajitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This man had gone forth in his teaching.

children.text: tripiṭakasaṃghasya ca dharmavaiyāvṛtyaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: And he performed service connected with the Dharma for the saṃgha of those who knew the three baskets.

children.text: yāvadanyatamasyārhata upadhivāraḥ prāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, in due course, the turn for sweeping came to a certain arhat.

children.text: sa vihāraṃ saṃmarṣṭumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to sweep the monastery.

children.text: vāyunetaścāmutaśca saṃkāro nīyate ||
children.translated_text: But the rubbish was carried here and there by the wind.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati tiṣṭhatu tāvad yāvadvāyurupaśamaṃ gacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: He thought, 'Let it remain for now, until the wind becomes calm.'

children.text: vaiyāvṛtyakareṇāsaṃmṛṣṭo vihāro dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The service monk saw that the monastery had not been swept.

children.text: tena tīvreṇa paryavasthānena kharavākkarma niścāritam kasya dāsīputrasyopadhivāra iti ||
children.translated_text: With intense agitation he let loose a harsh act of speech: 'What slave woman's son has the sweeping turn?'

children.text: tena arhatā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: That was heard by the arhat.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati paryavasthito 'yam ||
children.translated_text: He thought, 'This man is overcome by agitation.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu tāvat ||
children.translated_text: Let it be for now.

children.text: paścāt saṃjñāpayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: I shall make him understand later.'

children.text: yadā asya paryavasthānaṃ vigataṃ tadā tasya sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati jānīṣe tvaṃ ko 'hamiti sa kathayati jāne tvaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane pravrajito 'hamapīti ||
children.translated_text: When his agitation had passed, the arhat approached him and said, 'Do you know who I am?' He said, 'I know. You have gone forth in the teaching of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and so have I.'

children.text: sa kathayati yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi tu yanmayā pravrajya caraṇīyaṃ tatkṛtam ahaṃ sakalabandhanābaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'Even though that is so, nevertheless what had to be done by me after going forth has been done; I am bound by no fetter at all.

children.text: kharaṃ te vākkarma niścāritam ||
children.translated_text: A harsh act of speech has been uttered by you.

children.text: atyayamatyayato deśaya ||
children.translated_text: Confess the transgression as a transgression.

children.text: apyevaitatkarma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchediti ||
children.translated_text: Perhaps this karma may come to thinness, exhaustion, and complete wearing away.'

children.text: tenātyayamatyayato deśitam ||
children.translated_text: He confessed the transgression as a transgression.

children.text: yattena naraka upapadya dāsīputreṇa bhavitavyam tannarake nopapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, though he should have been reborn in hell and become a slave woman's son, he was not reborn in hell.

children.text: pañca tu janmaśatāni dāsyāḥ kukṣau upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for five hundred births he was born in the womb of a slave woman.

children.text: yāvadetarhyapi carame bhave dāsyā eva kukṣau upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And even now, in this final existence, he has been born in the womb of a slave woman.

children.text: yat saṃghasyopasthānaṃ kṛtam tenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he had attended on the saṃgha, he was born in a family rich, very wealthy, and possessed of great enjoyments.

children.text: yattatra paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Because he had recited there, studied, and gained skill in the skandhas, after going forth in my teaching he has directly realized arhatship through the abandoning of all defilements.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntaśuklo vipākaḥ vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, the result of entirely black deeds is entirely black; the result of entirely white deeds is entirely white; and the result of mixed deeds is mixed.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, having abandoned entirely black deeds and mixed ones, attention should be directed only to entirely white deeds.

children.text: ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, you should train yourselves.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti ||
children.translated_text: Delighted in mind, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 3
yadā rājñā māgadhena ajātaśatruṇā vaidehīputreṇa naukramo mātāpitrormāpitastadā vaiśālakairlicchavibhirbhagavato 'rthe naukramo māpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, had a bridge of boats built by his parents, then the <s>Licchavis</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s> had a bridge of boats built for the Blessed One's sake.

children.text: nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti vayaṃ vinipatitaśarīrā yannu vayaṃ phaṇasaṃkrameṇa bhagavantaṃ nadīm gaṅgāmuttārayema iti ||
children.translated_text: The nāgas thought, 'We have bodies fallen into an inferior state; what if we helped the Blessed One cross the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> by means of a bridge of hoods?'

children.text: taiḥ phaṇasaṃkramo māpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They built a bridge of hoods.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma rājagṛhāt śrāvastīṃ gantum yo yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣava utsahate rājño māgadhasyājātaśatrorvaidehīputrasya nausaṃkrameṇa nadīgaṅgāmuttartum sa tena taratu yo vā bhikṣavo vaiśālakānāṃ licchavīnāṃ nausaṃkrameṇa so 'pi tenottaratu ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'To go from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, whichever of you monks is able to cross the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> by the boat bridge of <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, let him cross by that; or whichever monks are able to cross by the boat bridge of the <s>Licchavis</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, let them also cross by that.

children.text: ahamapi āyuṣmatā ānandena bhikṣuṇā sārdhaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇasaṃkrameṇa nadīṃ gaṅgāmuttariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: But I, together with the venerable monk <s>Ānanda</s>, will cross the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> by the bridge of the nāgas' hoods.'

children.text: tatra kecit rājño māgadhasyājātaśatrorvaidehīputrasya nausaṃkrameṇottīrṇāḥ kecit vaiśālikānāṃ licchavīnāṃ nausaṃkrameṇa ||
children.translated_text: There some crossed by the boat bridge of <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, and some by the boat bridge of the <s>Licchavis</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

children.text: bhagavānapi āyuṣmatā ānandena sārdhaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇasaṃkrameṇottīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One too crossed together with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> by the bridge of the nāgas' hoods.

children.text: athānyatamopāsakastasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain lay follower at that time spoke a verse:

children.text: ye tarantyarṇavaṃ saraḥ setuṃ kṛtvā visṛjya palvalāni
children.translated_text: 'Those who cross the ocean or lake, having made a bridge and left behind the puddles,

children.text: kolaṃ hi janāḥ prabandhitā uttīrṇā medhāvino janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people, after binding together a raft, have crossed; wise people have crossed over.

children.text: uttīrṇo bhagavān buddho brāhmaṇastiṣṭhati sthale
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, the Buddha, has crossed over; the brāhmaṇa stands on dry ground.

children.text: bhikṣavo 'tra parisnānti kolaṃ badhnanti śrāvakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the monks bathe all around; the disciples bind together a raft.

children.text: kiṃ kuryādudapānena āpaścet sarvato yadi
children.translated_text: What would one do with a well, if water were everywhere?

children.text: chittveha mūlaṃ tṛṣṇāyāḥ kasya paryeṣaṇāṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: Having cut off here the root of craving, for what should one go seeking?'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: adrākṣīdbhagavānanyatamasmin bhūbhāge unnatonnataṃ pṛthivīpradeśam ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One saw, in a certain place, a tract of earth that was raised higher and higher.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarāyuṣmantamāmantrayate icchasi tvamānanda yo 'sau yūpa ūrdhvaṃ vyāmasahasraṃ tiryak ṣoḍaśapravedho nānāratnavicitro divyaḥ sarvasauvarṇo rājñā mahāpraṇādena dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ āplāvitaḥ taṃ draṣṭum etasya bhagavan kālaḥ etasya sugata samayaḥ yo 'yaṃ bhagavān yūpamucchrāpayet bhikṣavaḥ paśyeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And having seen it, he again addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to see that yūpa (sacrificial post), which is a thousand fathoms high, sixteen spans across, adorned with many kinds of jewels, divine, entirely golden, and which, after King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> had given gifts and made merit, was submerged in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>? Blessed One, this is the time for it; Sugata, this is the occasion: if the Blessed One were to raise up the yūpa, the monks would see it."

children.text: tato bhagavatā cakrasvastikanandyāvartena jālāvanaddhenānekapuṇyaśatanirjātena bhītānāmāśvāsanakareṇa pṛthivī parāmṛṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One touched the earth with his hand, which bore the wheel, svastika, and nandyāvarta marks, was covered with a net-pattern, had arisen from many hundreds of merits, and gave reassurance to the frightened.

children.text: nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti kimarthaṃ bhagavatā pṛthivī parāmṛṣṭeti yāvat paśyanti yūpaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The nāgas considered, "For what reason has the Blessed One touched the earth?" and then they saw that he wished to see the yūpa.

children.text: tatastairucchrāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then it was raised up by them.

children.text: bhikṣavo yūpaṃ draṣṭumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monks began to look at the yūpa.

children.text: āyuṣmānapi bhaddālī alpotsukaḥ pāṃsukūlaṃ sīvyati ||
children.translated_text: But the venerable <s>Bhaddālī</s>, being unconcerned, was sewing his rag-robe.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma ārohapariṇāhaṃ nimittaṃ bhikṣavo yūpasya gṛhṇīta antardhāsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, take note of the yūpa's height, circumference, and marks; it will disappear."

children.text: antarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It disappeared.

children.text: bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ paśya bhadanta bhikṣavo yūpaṃ paśyanti ||
children.translated_text: The monks asked the Buddha, the Blessed One: "Look, venerable sir, the monks are looking at the yūpa.

children.text: āyuṣmānapi bhaddālī alpotsukaḥ pāṃsukūlaṃ sīvyati ||
children.translated_text: But the venerable <s>Bhaddālī</s>, being unconcerned, is sewing his rag-robe.

children.text: kiṃ tāvat vītarāgatvādāhosvit paryupāsitapūrvatvāt tadyadi tāvad vītarāgatvāt santyanye 'pi vītarāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is this because he is free from passion, or because he has attended upon it before? If it is because he is free from passion, there are other passionless ones too.

children.text: atha paryupāsitapūrvatvāt kutra kena paryupāsitamiti ||
children.translated_text: But if it is because he has attended upon it before, where and by whom was it attended upon?"

children.text: bhagavānāha api bhikṣavo vītarāgatvādapi paryupāsitapūrvatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, it is both because he is free from passion and because he has attended upon it before."

children.text: kutrānena paryupāsitam ||
children.translated_text: "Where was it attended upon by him?"

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo rājābhūt praṇādo nāma śakrasya devendrasya vayasyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "In the past, monks, there was a king named <s>Praṇāda</s>, a companion of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ anekadhanasamudito 'hamaputraśca ||
children.translated_text: He had no son and desired a son; putting his cheek in his hand, he remained absorbed in thought: 'I am endowed with abundant wealth, and yet I am without a son.

children.text: mamātyayād rājavaṃśasamucchedo bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: After my death, the royal lineage will be cut off.'

children.text: tataḥ śakreṇa dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaśca mārṣa kasmāt tvaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparastiṣṭhasīti sa kathayati kauśila anekadhanasamudito 'hamaputraśca ||
children.translated_text: Then he was seen by <s>Śakra</s> and asked, 'Friend, why do you stand absorbed in thought, with your cheek in your hand?' He said, '<s>Kauśika</s>, I am endowed with abundant wealth, and yet I am without a son.

children.text: mamātyayād rājavaṃśasyocchedo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: After my death, the royal lineage will be cut off.'

children.text: śakraḥ kathayati mārṣa mā tvaṃ cintāparastiṣṭha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said, 'Friend, do not stand absorbed in worry.

children.text: yadi kaścit cyavanadharmā devaputro bhaviṣyati tatte putratve samādāpayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: If there is some devaputra (divine son) whose nature is to fall from heaven, I will cause him to take on the state of being your son.'

children.text: dharmatā khalu cyavanadharmaṇo devaputrasya pañca pūrvanimittāni prādurbhavanti akliṣṭāni vāsāṃsi saṃkliśyanti amlānāni mālyāni mlāyante daurgandhaṃ mukhānniścarati ubhābhyāṃ kakṣābhyāṃ svedaḥ pragharati sve cāsane dhṛtiṃ na labhate ||
children.translated_text: Now it is the rule that five preliminary signs appear for a devaputra whose nature is to fall: his unstained garments become stained; his unwithered garlands wither; a bad smell comes from his mouth; sweat pours from both armpits; and he finds no steadiness on his own seat.

children.text: yāvadanyatamasya devaputrasya pañca pūrvanimittāni prādurbhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: Eventually the five preliminary signs appeared for a certain devaputra.

children.text: sa śakreṇa devendreṇoktaḥ mārṣa praṇādasya rājño 'gramahiṣyāḥ kukṣau pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhāṇeti ||
children.translated_text: He was told by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, 'Friend, take rebirth-linking in the womb of King <s>Praṇāda</s>'s chief queen.'

children.text: sa kathayati pramādasthānaṃ kauśika ||
children.translated_text: He said, '<s>Kauśika</s>, that is a place of negligence.

children.text: bahukilbiṣakāriṇo hi kauśika rājānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For kings, <s>Kauśika</s>, commit many offenses.

children.text: mā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kṛtvā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: May I not, after ruling the kingdom unrighteously, become destined for hell.'

children.text: śakraḥ kathayati mārṣa ahaṃ te smārayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said, 'Friend, I will remind you.'

children.text: pramattāḥ kauśika devā ratibahulāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The gods, <s>Kauśika</s>, are negligent and devoted to pleasure.'

children.text: evametanmārṣa ||
children.translated_text: 'That is so, friend.

children.text: tathāpi tvahaṃ bhavantaṃ smārayāmi ||
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, I will remind you.'

children.text: tena praṇādasya rājño 'gramahiṣyāḥ kukṣau pratisaṃdhirgṛhītā ||
children.translated_text: Then he took rebirth-linking in the womb of King <s>Praṇāda</s>'s chief queen.

children.text: yasminneva divase pratisaṃdhirgṛhītā tasmin divase mahājanakāyena praṇādo muktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the very day on which he took rebirth-linking, a great cry was uttered by the mass of people for <s>Praṇāda</s>.

children.text: sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā ||
children.translated_text: After eight or nine months had passed, she gave birth.

children.text: dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A boy was born: handsome, fair to see, pleasing, fair-skinned, golden in color, with a head shaped like a parasol, long arms, a broad forehead, joined eyebrows, and a high nose.

children.text: tasya jñātayaḥ saṃgamya samāgamya nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti ||
children.translated_text: His relatives gathered and assembled, and they determined his name: 'What shall be the boy's name?'

children.text: jñātaya ūcur yasminneva divase 'yaṃ dārako mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāntaḥ tasminneva divase mahājanakāyena nādo muktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The relatives said, 'On the very day when this boy entered his mother's womb, a great cry was uttered by the mass of people.

children.text: yasminneva divase jātastasminneva divase mahājanakāyena nādo muktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the very day when he was born, a great cry was uttered by the mass of people.

children.text: tasmāt bhavatu dārakasya mahāpraṇāda iti nāma ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let the boy's name be <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>.'

children.text: tasya mahāpraṇāda iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: His name was established as <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>.

children.text: mahāpraṇādo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradatto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyām ||
children.translated_text: The boy <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two nurses for carrying him on the shoulder, two nurses for cleaning him, two milk-nurses, and two play-nurses.

children.text: so 'ṣṭābhirdhātrībhirunnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was carried and raised by the eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, clarified butter, and other especially heated and suitable provisions.

children.text: āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam ||
children.translated_text: He grew quickly, like a lotus standing in a lake.

children.text: yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had become grown, he was set to learning letters.

children.text: saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse nikṣepe vastuparīkṣāyāṃ dāruparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ hastiparīkṣāyāmaśvaparīkṣāyāṃ kumāraparīkṣāyāṃ kumārīparīkṣāyām so 'ṣṭāsu parīkṣāsūdghaṭṭako vācakaḥ paṭupracāraḥ paṇḍitaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In reckoning and counting, in accounting, withdrawal, deposit, and placing, in the examination of goods, the examination of wood, the examination of jewels, the examination of elephants, the examination of horses, the examination of boys, and the examination of girls, he became an expositor, a reader, skilled in practice, and learned in the eight examinations.

children.text: sa yāni tāni rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhnābhiṣiktānāṃ janapadaiśvaryasthāmavīryam anuprāptānāṃ mahāntaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalam abhinirjityādhyāsatāṃ pṛthag bhavanti śilpasthānakarmasthānāni tadyathā hastiśikṣāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe śare dhanuṣi prayāṇe niryāṇe 'ṅkuśagrahe pāśagrahe tomaragrahe yaṣṭibandhe padabandhe śikhābandhe dūravedhe marmavedhe 'kṣuṇṇavedhe dṛḍhaprahāritāyāṃ pañcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he became trained in those several arts and occupations that belong to kings, kṣatriyas anointed on the head, who have attained lordship, power, and strength over their realms and who, after conquering the great circle of the earth, occupy it: namely, in elephant-training, horseback riding, chariotry, the arrow, the bow, marching forth, setting out, taking up the goad, taking up the noose, taking up the javelin, staff-binding, foot-binding, topknot-binding, distant shooting, striking vital points, unerring shooting, and firmness of blow, becoming accomplished in the five positions.

children.text: dharmatā khalu na tāvat putrasya nāma prajñāyate yāvat tāto jīvati ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed the rule that a son's name is not made known as long as his father is alive.

children.text: apareṇa samayena praṇādo rājā kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At another time King <s>Praṇāda</s> passed away.

children.text: mahāpraṇādo rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> was established in the kingdom.

children.text: sa yāvattāvad dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā adharmeṇa kārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After ruling the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s> for some time, he began to rule it contrary to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śakreṇa devendreṇoktaḥ mārṣa mayā tvaṃ praṇādasya rājñaḥ samādāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said, "Sir, I arranged for you to be taken as the son of King <s>Praṇāda</s>.

children.text: mā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāraya mā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyasīti ||
children.translated_text: Do not rule the kingdom contrary to <s>dharma</s>; do not become destined for hell."

children.text: sa yāvattāvad dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā punarapi adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After ruling the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s> for some time, he again began to rule it contrary to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dvirapi śakreṇoktaḥ mārṣa mayā tvaṃ praṇādasya rājñaḥ putratve samādāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A second time <s>Śakra</s> said, "Sir, I arranged for you to be taken as the son of King <s>Praṇāda</s>.

children.text: mā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāraya mā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyasīti ||
children.translated_text: Do not rule the kingdom contrary to <s>dharma</s>; do not become destined for hell."

children.text: sa kathayati kauśika vayaṃ rājānaḥ pramattā iti ratibahulāḥ kṣaṇād vismarāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Kauśika</s>, we kings are heedless, much given to pleasure; in a moment we forget.

children.text: kiṃcittvamasmākaṃ cihnaṃ sthāpaya yaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānāni dāsyāmaḥ puṇyāni kārayiṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Set up some sign for us, seeing which we will give gifts and perform meritorious deeds."

children.text: na ca śakyate vinā nimittena puṇyaṃ kartum ||
children.translated_text: And without a sign it is not possible to make merit.

children.text: tataḥ śakreṇa devendreṇa viśvakarmaṇo devaputrasyājñā dattā gaccha tvaṃ viśvakarman rājño mahāpraṇādasya niveśane ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, gave an order to the god's son <s>Viśvakarman</s>: "Go, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, to the residence of King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>.

children.text: divyaṃ maṇḍalavāṭaṃ nirmiṇu yūpaṃ cocchrāpaya ūrdhvaṃ vyāmasahasreṇa tiryak ṣoḍaśapravedhaṃ nānāratnavicitraṃ sarvasauvarṇamiti ||
children.translated_text: Construct a divine circular pavilion, and raise up a <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post), one thousand fathoms high, sixteen spans across, adorned with various jewels, entirely of gold."

children.text: tato viśvakarmaṇā devaputreṇa mahāpraṇādasya rājño niveśane divyo maṇḍalavāṭo nirmito yūpaścocchritaḥ ūrdhvaṃ vyāmasahasraṃ nānāratnavicitro divyaḥ sarvasauvarṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the god's son <s>Viśvakarman</s> constructed a divine circular pavilion in the residence of King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, and the <s>yūpa</s> was raised up, one thousand fathoms high, divine, adorned with various jewels, entirely of gold.

children.text: tato mahāpraṇādena rājñā dānaśālā māpitā ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> had a hall for giving built.

children.text: tasya mātulo 'śoko nāma yūpasya paricārako vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His maternal uncle, named <s>Aśoka</s>, was appointed attendant of the <s>yūpa</s>.

children.text: tato yūpadarśanodyuktaḥ sarva eva jambudvīpanivāsī janakāya āgatya bhuktvā yūpaṃ paśyati svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti ||
children.translated_text: Then the entire body of people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, intent on seeing the <s>yūpa</s>, came, ate, looked at the <s>yūpa</s>, and did not perform their own work.

children.text: tataḥ kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Consequently the work of agriculture ceased.

children.text: rājñaḥ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante ||
children.translated_text: The king's tax revenues did not arise.

children.text: amātyaiḥ stokāḥ karapratyāyā upanītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ministers brought in only small tax revenues.

children.text: mahāpraṇādo rājā pṛcchati bhavantaḥ kasmāt stokāḥ karapratyāyā upanītāḥ deva jambudvīpanivāsī janakāya āgatya bhuktvā yūpaṃ paśyati svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> asked, "Sirs, why have only small tax revenues been brought in?" "Your Majesty, the body of people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> comes, eats, looks at the <s>yūpa</s>, and does not perform its own work.

children.text: kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The work of agriculture has ceased.

children.text: rājñaḥ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhanta iti ||
children.translated_text: The king's tax revenues do not arise."

children.text: rājā kathayati samucchidyatāṃ dānaśāleti ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "Let the hall for giving be shut down."

children.text: taiḥ samucchinnā ||
children.translated_text: They shut it down.

children.text: tato 'pyasau janakāyaḥ svapathyadanamādāya bhuktvā yūpaṃ nirīkṣamāṇastiṣṭhati svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti ||
children.translated_text: Even after that, the body of people, taking along its own food for the road, ate and stood gazing at the <s>yūpa</s>, and did not perform its own work.

children.text: kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The work of agriculture ceased.

children.text: tathāpi karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante ||
children.translated_text: Even so, the tax revenues did not arise.

children.text: rājā pṛcchati bhavantaḥ dānaśālāḥ samucchinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king asked, "Sirs, the halls for giving have been shut down.

children.text: idānīṃ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhanta iti ||
children.translated_text: Why now do the tax revenues not arise?"

children.text: amātyāḥ kathayanti deva janakāyaḥ svapathyadanamādāya bhuktvā yūpaṃ nirīkṣamāṇastiṣṭhati svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti ||
children.translated_text: The ministers said, "Your Majesty, the body of people takes along its own food for the road, eats, and stands gazing at the <s>yūpa</s>; it does not perform its own work.

children.text: kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ yataḥ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante ||
children.translated_text: The work of agriculture has ceased; therefore the tax revenues do not arise."

children.text: tato rājñā mahāpraṇādena dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā sa yūpo nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāmāplāvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, after giving gifts and performing meritorious deeds, had that <s>yūpa</s> submerged in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau mahāpraṇādasyāśoko nāma mātulaḥ eṣa evāsau bhaddālī bhikṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? That maternal uncle of <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, named <s>Aśoka</s>, is this very monk <s>Bhaddālī</s>.

children.text: tatrānena paryupāsitapūrvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There it had formerly been tended by him.

children.text: kutra bhadantāsau yūpo vilayaṃ gamiṣyati bhaviṣyanti bhikṣavo 'nāgate 'dhvani aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣo manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Where, venerable sir, will that <s>yūpa</s> come to dissolution?" "Monks, in a future time there will be human beings whose lifespan is eighty thousand years.

children.text: aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ śaṅkho nāma rājā bhaviṣyati saṃyamanī cakravartī caturantavijetā dhārmiko dharmarājā saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among human beings whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, there will be a king named <s>Śaṅkha</s>, a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), conqueror of the four quarters, righteous, a king of <s>dharma</s>, endowed with the seven jewels.

children.text: tasyemānyevaṃrūpāṇi sapta ratnāni bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: His seven jewels will be of this kind."

children.text: tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam ||
children.translated_text: Namely, there will be the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the jewel-gem, the woman-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the commander-jewel as the seventh.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And he will have a full thousand sons, courageous, heroic, handsome in form, and crushers of hostile armies.

children.text: sa imāmeva samudraparyantāṃ pṛthivīmakhilām akaṇṭakām anutpīḍām adaṇḍenāśastreṇa dharmeṇa samayena abhinirjityādhyāvasiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will conquer and inhabit this whole earth bounded by the ocean, entire, free from thorns and free from oppression, without punishment and without weapons, by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and by concord.

children.text: śaṅkhasya rājño brahmāyur nāma brāhmaṇaḥ purohito bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Śaṅkha</s> will have a brahmin domestic priest named <s>Brahmāyus</s>.

children.text: tasya brahmavatī nāma patnī bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will have a wife named <s>Brahmavatī</s>.

children.text: sā maitreyāṃśena sphuritvā putraṃ janayiṣyati maitreyaṃ nāma ||
children.translated_text: She, being animated by a portion of <s>Maitreya</s>, will give birth to a son named <s>Maitreya</s>.

children.text: brahmāyurmāṇavo 'śītimāṇavakaśatāni brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The young brahmin <s>Brahmāyus</s> will teach brahminical mantras to eight hundred young students.

children.text: sa tān māṇavakān maitreyāya anupradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: He will hand those students over to <s>Maitreya</s>.

children.text: maitreyo māṇavo 'śītimāṇavakasahasrāṇi brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The young <s>Maitreya</s> will teach brahminical mantras to eighty thousand young students.

children.text: atha catvāro mahārājāścaturmahānidhisthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the four great kings, stationed at the four great treasure-hoards,

children.text: piṅgalaśca kaliṅgeṣu mithilāyāṃ ca pāṇḍukaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgala</s> among the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, and <s>Pāṇḍuka</s> at <s>Mithilā</s>,

children.text: elāpatraśca gāndhāre śaṅkho vārāṇasīpure ||
children.translated_text: <s>Elāpatra</s> in <s>Gāndhāra</s>, and <s>Śaṅkha</s> in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: enaṃ ca yūpamādāya śaṅkhasya rājña upanāmayiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: will take this sacrificial post and present it to King <s>Śaṅkha</s>.

children.text: śaṅkho 'pi rājā brahmāyuṣe brāhmaṇāyānupradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Śaṅkha</s> too will hand it over to the brahmin <s>Brahmāyus</s>.

children.text: brahmāyurapi brāhmaṇo maitreyāya māṇavāyānupradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: The brahmin <s>Brahmāyus</s> too will hand it over to the young <s>Maitreya</s>.

children.text: maitreyo 'pi māṇavasteṣāṃ māṇavakānāmanupradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: The young <s>Maitreya</s> too will hand it over to those young students.

children.text: tataste māṇavakāstam yūpaṃ khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ chittvā bhājayiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those young students will cut that sacrificial post into piece after piece and divide it among themselves.

children.text: tato maitreyo māṇavakastasya yūpasyānityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tenaiva saṃvegena vanaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then the young <s>Maitreya</s>, seeing the impermanence of that sacrificial post, will, through that very shock of religious urgency, resort to the forest.

children.text: yasminneva divase vanaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati tasminneva divase maitreyāṃśena sphuritvā anuttaraṃ jñānamadhigamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: On the very day on which he resorts to the forest, on that same day, animated by the portion of <s>Maitreya</s>, he will attain unsurpassed knowledge.

children.text: tasya maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddha iti saṃjñā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will be known as <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: yasminneva divase maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddho 'nuttarajñānamadhigamiṣyati tasminneva divase śaṅkhasya rājñaḥ saptaratnānyantardhāsyante ||
children.translated_text: On the very day on which <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, attains unsurpassed knowledge, on that same day King <s>Śaṅkha</s>'s seven jewels will disappear.

children.text: śaṅkho 'pi rājā aśītikoṭṭarājasahasraparivāro maitreyaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Śaṅkha</s> too, with a retinue of eighty thousand kings, will follow <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, into renunciation.

children.text: yadapyasya strīratnaṃ viśākhā nāma sāpi aśītistrīsahasraparivārā maitreyaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And his woman-jewel, named <s>Viśākhā</s>, will also, with a retinue of eighty thousand women, follow <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, into renunciation.

children.text: tato maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddho 'śītibhikṣukoṭiparivāro yena gurupādakaḥ parvatastenopasaṃkramiṣyati yatra kāśyapasya bhikṣorasthisaṃghāto 'vikopitastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, surrounded by eighty koṭis of monks, will approach <s>Gurupādaka</s> mountain, where the undisturbed collection of the bones of the monk <s>Kāśyapa</s> remains.

children.text: gurupādakaparvato maitreyāya samyaksambuddhāya vivaramanupradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gurupādaka</s> mountain will open a cleft for <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: yato maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ kāśyapasya bhikṣoravikopitam asthisaṃghātaṃ dakṣiṇena pāṇinā gṛhītvā vāme pāṇau pratiṣṭhāpya evaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati yo 'sau bhikṣavo varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma śāstā loka utpannastasyāyaṃ śrāvakaḥ kāśyapo nāmnā alpecchānāṃ saṃtuṣṭānāṃ dhūtaguṇavādināmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitreya</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, taking the undisturbed collection of the bones of the monk <s>Kāśyapa</s> with his right hand and placing it in his left hand, will teach the Dharma to his disciples thus: 'Monks, that teacher named <s>Śākyamuni</s> arose in the world among people whose lifespan was a hundred years. This is his disciple named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who was designated foremost among those of few wishes, the contented, and those who proclaimed the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (austere virtues).'

children.text: śākyamuneḥ parinirvṛtasyānena śāsanasaṃgītiḥ kṛtā iti ||
children.translated_text: After <s>Śākyamuni</s> had attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the compilation of the teaching was made by him.

children.text: te dṛṣṭvā saṃvegamāpatsyante kathamidānīmīdṛśenātmabhāvenedṛśā guṇagaṇā adhigatā iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, they will be seized by religious urgency, thinking, 'How now were such groups of qualities attained in such a bodily form?'

children.text: te tenaiva saṃvegenārhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Through that very shock of religious urgency they will directly realize arhatship.

children.text: ṣaṇṇavatikoṭyo 'rhatāṃ bhaviṣyanti dhūtaguṇasākṣātkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There will be ninety-six koṭis of arhats who have realized the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (austere virtues).

children.text: yaṃ ca saṃvegamāpatsyante tatrāsau yūpo vilayaṃ gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And when they are seized by that religious urgency, that sacrificial post will there pass into dissolution.

children.text: ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo dvayo ratnayoryugapalloke prādurbhāvāya bhagavānāha praṇidhānavaśāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, for two jewels to appear in the world at the same time?' The Blessed One said, 'By the power of a vow.'

children.text: kutra bhagavan praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'Where, Blessed One, was the vow made?'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani madhyadeśe vāsavo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: 'Monks, in the past, in a former time, in the Middle Country, a king named <s>Vāsava</s> ruled a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: tasya sadāpuṣpaphalā vṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: His trees always bore flowers and fruit.

children.text: devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati ||
children.translated_text: The rain-cloud, from time to time, gave proper streams of rain.

children.text: atīva śasyasampattirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: The abundance of grain was exceedingly great.

children.text: uttarāpathe dhanasaṃmato nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In the northern region a king named <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> ruled a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: tasyāpi sadāpuṣpaphalā vṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: His trees too always bore flowers and fruit.

children.text: devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: The rain-cloud, from time to time, gave proper streams of rain.

children.text: atīva śasyasampattirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: The abundance of grain was exceedingly great.

children.text: yāvadapareṇa samayena vāsavasya rājñaḥ putro jāto ratnapratyuptayā śikhayā ||
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, a son was born to King <s>Vāsava</s> with a crest inlaid with jewels.

children.text: tasya vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā ratnaśikhīti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: After performing his birth festival in detail, the name <s>Ratnaśikhin</s> was established for him.

children.text: so 'pareṇa samayena jīrṇāturamṛtasaṃdarśanādudvigno vanaṃ saṃśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At another time, alarmed by the sight of old age, sickness, and death, he resorted to the forest.

children.text: yasminneva divase vanaṃ saṃśritastasminneva divase 'nuttaraṃ jñānamadhigatam ||
children.translated_text: On the very day on which he resorted to the forest, on that very day he attained unsurpassed knowledge.

children.text: tasya ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddha iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: The designation "<s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha" arose for him.

children.text: athāpareṇa samayena dhanasaṃmato rājā upariprāsādatalagato 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Then, at another time, King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> was standing on the upper terrace of the palace, surrounded by a group of ministers.

children.text: so 'mātyānāmantrayate bhavantaḥ kasyacidanyasyāpi rājño rājyamevamṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: He addressed the ministers: "Sirs, is the kingdom of any other king also so prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and filled with many people?

children.text: sadāpuṣpaphalā vṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Are its trees always bearing flowers and fruit?

children.text: devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: Does the deity, from time to time, properly send down streams of water?

children.text: atīva śasyasampattirbhavati yathā asmākamiti madhyadeśād vaṇijaḥ paṇyamādāyottarāpathaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is there very great abundance of crops, as there is among us?" Merchants from <s>Madhyadeśa</s>, taking merchandise, had gone to <s>Uttarāpatha</s>.

children.text: te kathayanti asti deva madhyadeśe vāsavo nāma rājā iti ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Your Majesty, in <s>Madhyadeśa</s> there is a king named <s>Vāsava</s>."

children.text: sahaśravaṇādeva dhanasaṃmatasya rājño 'marṣa utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the mere hearing of this, anger arose in King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>.

children.text: sa saṃjātāmarṣo 'mātyānāmantrayate saṃnāhayantu bhavantaścaturaṅgaṃ balakāyam ||
children.translated_text: With anger arisen, he addressed the ministers: "Sirs, array the fourfold army.

children.text: rāṣṭrāpamardanamasya kariṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: We will crush his kingdom."

children.text: tato dhanasaṃmato rājā caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyamaśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ madhyadeśamāgatya gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe kūle 'vasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, having arrayed the fourfold army, the elephant corps, horse corps, chariot corps, and infantry corps, came to <s>Madhyadeśa</s> and took up position on the southern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: aśrauṣīdvāsavo rājā dhanasaṃmato rājā caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyamaśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ madhyadeśamāgatya gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe kūle 'vasthita iti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Vāsava</s> heard: "King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, having arrayed the fourfold army, the elephant corps, horse corps, chariot corps, and infantry corps, has come to <s>Madhyadeśa</s> and taken up position on the southern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ so 'pi caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyamaśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare kūle 'vasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when he had heard this, he too arrayed the fourfold army, the elephant corps, horse corps, chariot corps, and infantry corps, and took up position on the northern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: atha ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastayorvinayakālaṃ jñātvā nadyā gaṅgāyāstīre rātriṃ vāsamupagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, knowing that it was the time to discipline those two, spent the night on the bank of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: ratnaśikhinā samyaksambuddhena laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, produced a worldly thought.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yadā buddhā bhagavanto laukikaṃ cittamutpādayanti tasmin samaye śakrabrahmādayo devā bhagavataścetasā cittamājānanti ||
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that when Buddhas, Blessed Ones, produce a worldly thought, at that time gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> know the thought in the Blessed One's mind by means of their own minds.

children.text: atha śakrabrahmādayo devā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: teṣāṃ varṇānubhāvena mahānudārāvabhāsaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the splendor of their appearance, a great and noble radiance arose.

children.text: dhanasaṃmatena rājñā dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was seen by King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaramātyān pṛcchati kimayaṃ bhavanto vāsavasya rājño vijite mahānudārāvabhāsaḥ te kathayanti deva vāsavasya rājño vijite ratnaśikhī nāma samyaksambuddha utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen it, he asked the ministers, "Sirs, what is this great and noble radiance in the realm of King <s>Vāsava</s>?" They said, "Your Majesty, in King <s>Vāsava</s>'s realm a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> has arisen.

children.text: tasya śakrabrahmādayo devā darśanāyopasaṃkramanti ||
children.translated_text: The gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> approach him for the sake of seeing him.

children.text: tenaivodārāvabhāsaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, this noble radiance has arisen.

children.text: maharddhiko 'sau mahānubhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is of great <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power) and great might.

children.text: tasyāyamanubhāva iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his power."

children.text: dhanasaṃmato rājā kathayati bhavantaḥ yasya vijite īdṛśaṃ dvipādakaṃ puṇyakṣetramutpannam yaṃ śakrabrahmādayo 'pi devā darśanāyopasaṃkrāmanti tasyāhaṃ kīdṛśamanarthaṃ kariṣyāmi tena tasya dūto 'nupreṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> said, "Sirs, what harm shall I do to him in whose realm such a two-footed field of merit has arisen, whom even gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> approach for the sake of seeing?" Therefore a messenger was sent to him:

children.text: vayasyāgaccha ||
children.translated_text: "Friend, come.

children.text: na te 'haṃ kiṃcit kariṣyāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall do nothing to you.

children.text: puṇyamaheśākhyastvam yasya vijite dvipādakaṃ puṇyakṣetraṃ ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddho 'yam ||
children.translated_text: You are great and renowned through merit, since in your realm this two-footed field of merit, <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has arisen.

children.text: śakrabrahmādayo devā darśanāyopasaṃkrāmanti ||
children.translated_text: The gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> approach him for the sake of seeing him.

children.text: kiṃtu kaṇṭhāśleṣaṃ te dattvā gamiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: But I will go after giving you an embrace around the neck.

children.text: evamāvayoḥ parasparaṃ cittasaumanasyaṃ bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Thus there will be mutual happiness of mind between us."

children.text: vāsavo rājā viśvāsaṃ na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Vāsava</s> did not trust him.

children.text: sa yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇo vāsavo rājā ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat mama bhadanta dhanasaṃmatena rājñā saṃdiṣṭam priyavayasyāgaccha na te 'haṃ kiṃcit kariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Sitting to one side, King <s>Vāsava</s> said this to <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha: "Venerable sir, King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> has sent me this message: 'Dear friend, come. I shall do nothing to you.

children.text: kaṇṭhāśleṣaṃ dattvā gamiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I will give you an embrace around the neck and go.

children.text: evamāvayoḥ parasparaṃ cittasaumanasyaṃ bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Thus there will be mutual happiness of mind between us.'

children.text: tatra mayā kathaṃ pratipattavyam ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ kathayati gaccha mahārāja śobhanaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: How should I proceed in this matter?" <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, said, "Go, great king; it will be well."

children.text: bhagavan kiṃ mayā tasya pādayor nipatitavyam mahārāja balaśreṣṭhā hi rājānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Blessed One, should I fall at his feet?" "Great king, kings are foremost in strength.

children.text: nipatitavyam ||
children.translated_text: You should fall down."

children.text: atha vāsavo rājā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s> bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, rose from his seat, and departed.

children.text: yena dhanasaṃmato rājā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He approached King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya dhanasaṃmatasya rājñaḥ pādayor nipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he fell at the feet of King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>.

children.text: tato dhanasaṃmatena rājñā kaṇṭhe śleṣaṃ dattvā viśvāsamutpādya preṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> gave him an embrace around the neck, inspired confidence in him, and sent him away.

children.text: atha vāsavo rājā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s> approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He approached, bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇo vāsavo rājā ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat kasya bhadanta sarve rājānaḥ pādayor nipatanti rājño mahārāja cakravartinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sitting to one side, King <s>Vāsava</s> said this to <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha: "Venerable sir, at whose feet do all kings fall?" "At the feet of a great king, a cakravartin, O great king."

children.text: atha vāsavo rājā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena ratnaśikhī tathāgataḥ samyaksambuddhastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the Tathāgata, the fully awakened Buddha, and said this to <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha: "May the Blessed One consent to a meal at my house tomorrow, together with the community of monks."

children.text: atha vāsavo rājā tāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñāpya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, during that very night, prepared pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten; rising early in the morning, he arranged seats, set out water vessels, and by a messenger announced the time to <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. May the Blessed One now consider the time."

children.text: atha ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena rājño vāsavasya bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, dressed himself, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by the community of monks and preceded by the community of monks, went to the place of King <s>Vāsava</s>'s meal-offering.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

children.text: atha rājā vāsavo ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, knowing that <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, was comfortably seated, satisfied and served him with pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten, with his own hand.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ bhadanta kuśalamūlena rājā syāṃ cakravartīti ||
children.translated_text: After satisfying and serving him repeatedly with pure foods to be chewed and eaten, and knowing that the Blessed One <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, had eaten, had washed his hands, and had put away his bowl, he fell at his feet and began to make an aspiration: "Venerable sir, by this root of merit may I become a king, a cakravartin."

children.text: tatsamanantaraṃ ca śaṅkha āpūritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after that, a conch was blown.

children.text: tato ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddho vāsavaṃ rājānamidamavocat bhaviṣyasi mahārāja aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śaṅkho nāma rājā cakravartīti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, said this to King <s>Vāsava</s>: "You will become, O great king, when the people have a lifespan of eighty thousand years, a cakravartin king named <s>Śaṅkha</s>."

children.text: tata uccaśabdo mahāśabdo jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a loud sound, a great sound, arose.

children.text: dhanasaṃmato rājā kolāhalaśabdaṃ śrutvā amātyān pṛcchati kimeṣa bhavanto vāsavasya rājño vijite kolāhalaśabdaḥ śrūyate iti tairāgamya niveditam deva ratnaśikhinā samyaksambuddhena vāsavo rājā cakravartirājye vyākṛta iti janakāyo hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, hearing the sound of commotion, asked his ministers, "Why, sirs, is this sound of commotion heard in King <s>Vāsava</s>'s realm?" They came and reported, "Your Majesty, because <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, has predicted King <s>Vāsava</s> for the kingship of a cakravartin, the people are thrilled, pleased, and delighted."

children.text: tena kolāhalaśabdo jāta iti ||
children.translated_text: "For that reason this sound of commotion has arisen."

children.text: atha dhanasaṃmato rājā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> approached <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇo dhanasaṃmato rājā ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat kasya bhadanta sarve cakravartinaḥ pādayor nipatanti tathāgatasya mahārāja arhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya ||
children.translated_text: Sitting to one side, King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> said this to <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha: "Venerable sir, at whose feet do all cakravartins fall?" "At the feet of the Tathāgata, the arhat, the fully awakened Buddha, O great king."

children.text: atha dhanasaṃmato rājā utthāyāsanādekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenāñjalim praṇamya ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
