children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and said this to <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha: "May the Blessed One consent to a meal at my house tomorrow, together with the community of monks."

children.text: adhivāsayati ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddho dhanasaṃmatasya rājño 'pi tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, consented to King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>'s invitation too by remaining silent.

children.text: atha dhanasaṃmato rājā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanaṃ viditvā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, knowing that <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, had consented by silence, bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and departed from the presence of <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha.

children.text: atha dhanasaṃmato rājā tāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, during that very night, prepared pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten; rising early in the morning, he arranged seats, set out water vessels, and by a messenger announced the time to <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. May the Blessed One now consider the time."

children.text: atha ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena dhanasaṃmatasya rājño bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, dressed himself, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, went to the place of King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>'s meal-offering.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

children.text: atha dhanasaṃmato rājā sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ tatpramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, knowing that <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and the community of monks headed by him were comfortably seated, satisfied and served them with pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten, with his own hand.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpya saṃpravārya ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ pādayor nipatya sarvamimaṃ lokaṃ maitreṇāṃśena sphuritvā praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena śāstā loke bhaveyaṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddha iti ||
children.translated_text: After satisfying and serving <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the perfect Buddha, in many ways with pure, excellent food to be chewed and eaten, with his own hand, and after knowing that he had eaten, washed his hands, and had his bowl removed, he fell at his feet, suffused this entire world with a portion of loving-kindness, and began to make an aspiration: "By this root of merit, may I become a teacher in the world, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfect Buddha."

children.text: ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ kathayati bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ mahārāja aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ maitreyo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddha iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the perfect Buddha, said, "You will become, great king, among people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Maitreya</s>, an arhat, a perfect Buddha."

children.text: tatpraṇidhānavaśād dvayo ratnayorloke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Through the power of that aspiration, there will be an appearance of the two jewels in the world.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: The monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 4
bhagavān nyagrodhikāmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One arrived at <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya nyagrodhikāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the forenoon, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Nyagrodhikā</s> for alms.

children.text: kapilavastuno brāhmaṇasya dārikā nyagrodhikāyāṃ niviṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: A brāhmaṇa's daughter from <s>Kapilavastu</s> was staying in <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>.

children.text: adrākṣīt sā brāhmaṇadārikā bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam ||
children.translated_text: That brāhmaṇa girl saw the Blessed One adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with the eighty minor marks, adorned with a fathom-wide aura, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, lovely on every side.

children.text: sahadarśanādasyā etadabhavat ayaṃ sa bhagavāñ śākyakulanandanaścakravartikulād rājyamapahāya sphītamantaḥpuraṃ sphītāni ca kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi pravrajita idānīṃ bhikṣāmaṭate ||
children.translated_text: At the sight of him, this occurred to her: "This is that Blessed One, the joy of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, who abandoned kingship in a lineage of universal monarchs, a flourishing inner palace, and flourishing treasuries and granaries, went forth, and now wanders for alms.

children.text: yadi mamāntikātsaktukabhikṣāṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ahamasmai dadyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: If he would accept a gift of meal-flour from me, I would give it to him."

children.text: tato bhagavatā tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya pātramupanāmitam yadi te bhagini parityaktam ākīryatāmasmin pātra iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing her thought with his mind, extended his bowl: "Sister, if it has been set aside by you, pour it into this bowl."

children.text: tato bhūyasyā mātrayā tasyāḥ prasāda utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then an even greater measure of faith arose in her.

children.text: jānāti me bhagavāṃścetasā cittamiti viditvā tīvreṇa prasādena bhagavate saktubhikṣāṃ dattavatī ||
children.translated_text: Knowing, "The Blessed One knows my thought with his mind," she gave the Blessed One the gift of meal-flour with intense faith.

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitamupadarśitam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātāḥ puṣparāgapadmarāgavajravaiḍūryamusāragalvārkalohitakādakṣiṇāvartaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavarṇā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed the nature of things that, at the time when buddhas, blessed ones, manifest a smile, rays of blue, yellow, red, and white, with the colors of topaz, ruby, diamond, beryl, musāragalva, arkalohitaka, right-turning conch shell, stone, coral, gold, and silver, issue from their mouth; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastādgacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahavahuhuvamutpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmamavīciparyantān narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣṇībhūtvā nipatanti ||
children.translated_text: Those that go downward reach the hells as far as <s>Avīci</s>: <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall having become cool, and in the cold hells they fall having become warm.

children.text: tenānugatāsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ te pratiprasrabhyante ||
children.translated_text: Through contact with them, at that very moment the special torments of those beings are stilled.

children.text: teṣāmevaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutā āhosvidanyatropapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: It occurs to them, "Friends, have we fallen from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?"

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavānnirmitam visarjayati ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of producing faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created form.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ nāpyanyatropapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the created form, it occurs to them, "Friends, we have not fallen from here, nor have we been reborn somewhere else."

children.text: te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya tannarakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Having made their minds deeply faithful toward the created form, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in that hell and take rebirth-linking among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭādgacchanti tāścāturmahārājikān devān gatvā trāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino devān brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhānatapān sudṛśān sudarśānakaniṣṭhaparyantān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyudghoṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward reach the gods as far as <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>: the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and proclaim, "Impermanent, painful, empty, without self."

children.text: gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante ||
children.translated_text: And they recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Strive, go forth, apply yourselves to the teaching of the Buddha;

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: shake off the army of Death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this dharma and discipline

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring about the end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, after wandering throughout the great trichiliocosm, follow the Blessed One himself, behind and behind.

children.text: tadyadi bhagavānatītaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to declare the past, they disappear behind him.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastādantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to declare the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to declare rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyāmantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to declare rebirth as an animal, they disappear in his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rebirth among the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), they disappear at his big toes.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunorantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rebirth among human beings, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict the kingship of a powerful <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict the kingship of a <s>cakravartin</s>, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (awakening as a disciple), they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyāmantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: yadi anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyorṇāyāmantarhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those flames circumambulated the Blessed One three times and disappeared into his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkramitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A mass of many kinds, variegated with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāt divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the regions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises."

children.text: gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: And he spoke two verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "Buddhas, whose arising has gone beyond ordinary becoming, who have abandoned wretchedness and pride, who are the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus-fiber, without a cause.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīrabuddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: At this moment, having known for yourself with steadfast wisdom the longing of the listeners, O ascetic, lord of conquerors,

children.text: dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: remove, O bull of sages, the doubt that has arisen, with steadfast, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The Protectors, the fully awakened ones, whose firmness is like the lord of salt-water oceans, do not show a smile without reason.

children.text: yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke.

children.text: bhagavānāha evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetupratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: The Tathāgatas, arhats, fully awakened Buddhas, <s>Ānanda</s>, do not manifest a smile without cause and condition.

children.text: dṛṣṭā tavaiṣā sā ānanda brāhmaṇadārikā yayā prasādajātayā mahyaṃ saktubhikṣānupradattā dṛṣṭā bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that brahmin girl who, having become filled with faith, gave me an alms-offering of parched flour?" "I saw her, venerable sir."

children.text: asāvānanda brāhmaṇadārikā anena kuśalamūlena trayodaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "That brahmin girl, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, will not go to a bad destiny for thirteen kalpas.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi devāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca saṃvācya saṃsṛtya paścime bhave paścime nikete paścime samucchraye paścima ātmabhāvapratilambhe supraṇihito nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Rather, after passing and wandering among gods and human beings, in her last existence, her last dwelling, her last bodily support, her final acquisition of an individual existence, she will become a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Supraṇihita</s>."

children.text: sāmantakena śabdo visṛtaḥ amukayā brāhmaṇadārikayā prasādajātayā bhagavate saktubhikṣā pratipāditā sā bhagavatā pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛteti ||
children.translated_text: A report spread through the surrounding area: "A certain brahmin girl, having become filled with faith, presented the Blessed One with an alms-offering of parched flour, and she has been predicted by the Blessed One for <s>pratyekabodhi</s>."

children.text: tasyāśca svāmī puṣpasamidhāmarthāyāraṇyaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Her husband had gone to the forest for flowers and firewood.

children.text: tena śrutaṃ mama patnyā śramaṇāya gautamāya saktubhikṣā pratipāditā sā ca śramaṇena gautamena pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛtā iti ||
children.translated_text: He heard, "My wife presented an alms-offering of parched flour to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, and the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> predicted her for <s>pratyekabodhi</s>."

children.text: śrutvā punaḥ saṃjātāmarṣo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he heard this, anger arose in him, and he went to where the Blessed One was.

children.text: bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya bhagavantamidamavocat agamadbhavān gautamo 'smākaṃ niveśanam agamaṃ brāhmaṇa satyaṃ bhavate tayā mama patnyā saktubhikṣā pratipāditā sā ca tvayā pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛtā iti satyaṃ brāhmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: After exchanging with the Blessed One various face-to-face words of greeting and cordial conversation, he said this to the Blessed One: "Did master <s>Gautama</s> come to our dwelling?" "I did come, brahmin." "Is it true, sir, that my wife presented you with an alms-offering of parched flour, and that you predicted her for <s>pratyekabodhi</s>?" "It is true, brahmin."

children.text: tvaṃ gautama cakravartirājyamapahāya pravrajitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Gautama</s>, you went forth after abandoning the kingship of a <s>cakravartin</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ nāma tvametarhi saktubhikṣāhetoḥ samprajānan mṛṣāvādaṃ sambhāṣase kaste śraddhāsyati iyatpramāṇasya bījasyeyat phalamiti tena hi brāhmaṇa tvāmeva prakṣyāmi yathā te kṣamate tathaivaṃ vyākuru ||
children.translated_text: How, then, can you now knowingly speak falsehood for the sake of an alms-offering of parched flour? Who will believe you, that from a seed of such a size there could be such a fruit?" "In that case, brahmin, I will ask you yourself; answer just as you think fit.

children.text: kiṃ manyase brāhmaṇa asti kaścittvayā āścaryādbhuto dharmo dṛṣṭas tiṣṭhantu tāvat bho gautama anye āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, brahmin? Have you seen any wonderful and marvelous thing?" "Let other wonderful and marvelous things be for the moment, <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: yo mayā asyāmeva nyagrodhikāyāmāścaryādbhuto dharmo dṛṣṭaḥ sa tāvacchrūyatām ||
children.translated_text: Hear, then, the wonderful and marvelous thing that I have seen in this very <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>.

children.text: asyāṃ bho gautama nyagrodhikāyāṃ pūrveṇa nyagrodho vṛkṣo yasya nāmneyaṃ nyagrodhikā tasyādhastāt pañca śakaṭaśatāni asaṃsaktāni tiṣṭhanti anyonyāsambādhamānāni ||
children.translated_text: In this <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, on the eastern side there is a banyan tree, because of whose name this place is called <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>; beneath it five hundred carts stand without touching one another and without crowding each other.

children.text: kiyatpramāṇaṃ tasya nyagrodhasya phalam kiyat tāvat kedāramātram ||
children.translated_text: "How large is the fruit of that banyan? Is it perhaps the size of a field?"

children.text: no bho gautama kiliñjamātram ||
children.translated_text: "No, <s>Gautama</s>." "The size of a mat?"

children.text: tailikacakramātram ||
children.translated_text: "The size of an oilman's wheel?"

children.text: śakaṭacakramātram ||
children.translated_text: "The size of a cartwheel?"

children.text: gopiṭakamātram ||
children.translated_text: "The size of a cow's fodder basket?"

children.text: bilvamātram ||
children.translated_text: "The size of a bilva fruit?"

children.text: kapitthamātram no bho gautama sarṣapacatuṣṭayabhāgamātram ||
children.translated_text: "The size of a kapittha fruit?" "No, <s>Gautama</s>; it is the size of a quarter of a mustard seed."

children.text: kaste śraddhāsyati iyatpramāṇasya bījasyāyaṃ mahāvṛkṣo nirvṛtta iti śraddadhātu me bhavān gautamo mā vā ||
children.translated_text: "Who will believe you, that from a seed of such a size this great tree has arisen? Let master <s>Gautama</s> believe me or not."

children.text: naitat pratyakṣaṃ kṣetram ||
children.translated_text: "Is this not a directly visible case?

children.text: tāvadbho gautama nirupahataṃ snigdhamadhuramṛttikāpradeśaṃ bījaṃ ca navasāraṃ sukhāropitam ||
children.translated_text: For there, <s>Gautama</s>, the patch of soil is unimpaired, rich, sweet, and soft, and the seed was fresh in its essence and well planted.

children.text: kālena ca kālaṃ devo vṛṣyate tenāyaṃ mahānyagrodhavṛkṣo 'bhinirvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And rain falls from time to time; therefore this great banyan tree has arisen."

children.text: atha bhagavānasminnutpanne gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then, when this matter had arisen, the Blessed One spoke a verse:

children.text: yathā kṣetre ca bījena pratyakṣastvamiha dvija
children.translated_text: Just as here in a field the seed is directly evident to you, O twice-born one,

children.text: evaṃ karmavipākeṣu pratyakṣā hi tathāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too, in the ripenings of karma, the Tathāgatas are directly evident.

children.text: yathā tvayā brāhmaṇa dṛṣṭametadalpaṃ ca bījaṃ sumahāṃśca vṛkṣaḥ
children.translated_text: As you have seen, O brāhmaṇa, this seed is small and the tree is very great;

children.text: evaṃ mayā brāhmaṇa dṛṣṭametat alpaṃ ca bījaṃ mahatī ca saṃpat ||
children.translated_text: so I too have seen this, O brāhmaṇa: the seed is small, and the prosperity is great.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tato bhagavatā mukhāt jihvāṃ nirnamayya sarvaṃ mukhamaṇḍalamācchāditam yāvat keśaparyantam upādāya sa ca brāhmaṇo 'bhihitaḥ kiṃ manyase brāhmaṇa yasya mukhāt jihvāṃ niścārya sarvam mukhamaṇḍalamācchādayati api tvasau cakravartirājyaśatasahasrahetorapi samprajānan mṛṣāvādaṃ bhāṣeta no bho gautama ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One extended his tongue from his mouth, covered the whole circle of his face up to the edge of his hair, and addressed that brāhmaṇa: "What do you think, brāhmaṇa? Would one who, drawing out his tongue from his mouth, covers the whole circle of his face knowingly speak a falsehood even for the sake of a hundred thousand kingdoms of a cakravartin?" "No, sir <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: tato 'nveva gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then, immediately after that, he spoke a verse:

children.text: apyeva hi syādanṛtābhidhāyinī mameha jihvārjavasatyavāditā
children.translated_text: Even if this tongue of mine, straight and truth-speaking, could be one that utters falsehood,

children.text: tadevametanna yathā hi brāhmaṇa tathāgato 'smītyavagantumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: that is not so, brāhmaṇa; therefore you should understand that I am the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇo 'bhiprasannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that brāhmaṇa became deeply confident.

children.text: tato 'sya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam atikrānto 'haṃ bhadanta atikrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature, the Blessed One gave such a teaching of the Dharma, leading to penetration of the four noble truths, that, having heard it, the brāhmaṇa shattered with the vajra of knowledge the mountain of the view of a real self, rising with twenty peaks, and realized the fruit of stream-entry. "I have gone beyond, venerable sir; I have gone beyond."

children.text: eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "I here go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dharma, and to the community of monks.

children.text: upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatamabhiprasannam ||
children.translated_text: Accept me from this day forward, as long as life lasts and breath remains, as a lay follower who has gone for refuge and is full of confidence."

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that brāhmaṇa rejoiced in and approved the Blessed One's words, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet, rose from his seat, and departed.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: The monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

children.text: Chapter 5
atha bhagavān hastināpuramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One arrived at <s>Hastināpura</s>.

children.text: anyatamo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ dūrādeva dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva parvataṃ samantato bhadrakaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhagavantamabhigamya gāthābhiḥ stotumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A certain brāhmaṇa saw the Blessed One from afar, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his limbs radiant with the eighty minor marks, adorned with a fathom-wide radiance, shining more brightly than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain, altogether lovely. Seeing him, he approached the Blessed One and began to praise him with verses:

children.text: suvarṇavarṇo nayanābhirāmaḥ prītyākaraḥ sarvaguṇairupetaḥ
children.translated_text: Golden in color, delightful to the eyes, a source of joy, endowed with every virtue,

children.text: devātidevo naradamyasārathis tīrṇo 'si pāraṃ bhavasāgarasya ||
children.translated_text: god beyond gods, charioteer of men to be tamed, you have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of becoming.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitamupadarśitam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti pūrvavad yāvad bhagavata ūrṇāyāmantarhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is the rule that whenever buddhas, blessed ones, manifest a smile, as before, up to the point where the rays disappear into the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with joined palms, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkramitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: A cluster, variegated with thousands of different colors, has issued from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by it the regions all around were illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises.

children.text: gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: And he spoke a verse:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: Buddhas, free from arising, having abandoned misery and pride, are the supreme causes in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Jinas, whose enemies are conquered, do not display without reason a smile white like conch and lotus-fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīrabuddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: At this moment, having yourself understood with steady wisdom what the listeners desire, O ascetic, lord of Jinas,

children.text: dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: remove the arisen doubt, O bull among sages, with firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened protectors, firm as the king of the salty ocean, do not display a smile without cause;

children.text: yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the crowds of people desire to hear the purpose for which the steadfast ones display a smile.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhagavānāha evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetupratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas manifest a smile.

children.text: dṛṣṭaste ānanda brāhmaṇo yena tathāgato gāthayā abhiṣṭutaḥ dṛṣṭo bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, the brāhmaṇa by whom the Tathāgata was praised with a verse?" "I saw him, venerable sir."

children.text: asau anena kuśalamūlena viṃśatikalpaṃ vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "By this root of merit he will not go to a bad destiny for twenty kalpas.

children.text: kiṃtu devāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca gatvā saṃsṛtya paścime nikete paścime samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe stavārho nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Rather, after passing among gods and humans, in his final dwelling, his final bodily support, and his final attainment of individual existence, he will become a pratyekabuddha named <s>Stavārha</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti paśya bhadanta anena brāhmaṇena bhagavānekayā gāthayā stuto bhagavatā ca pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛta iti ||
children.translated_text: The monks, overcome by doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts: "See, venerable sir, this brāhmaṇa praised the Blessed One with a single verse, and the Blessed One has predicted him for individual awakening."

children.text: bhagavānāha na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'dhvani anenāhamekayā gāthayā stutaḥ mayā ca pañcasu grāmavareṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, it is not only now. In a past time too, I was praised by him with a single verse, and I established him in five excellent villages.

children.text: tacchṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Listen to this, and apply your minds well and thoroughly; I shall speak."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "Once, monks, in a past time, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled over a kingdom that was prosperous, thriving, well-provisioned, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: sa cātīva kavipriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he was exceedingly fond of poets.

children.text: vārāṇasyāmanyatamo brāhmaṇaḥ kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there was a certain Brahmin, a poet.

children.text: sa brāhmaṇyocyate brāhmaṇa śītakālo vartate ||
children.translated_text: His Brahmin wife said to him, "Brahmin, the cold season is now here.

children.text: gaccha asya rājñaḥ kaccidanukūlaṃ bhāṣitaṃ kṛtvā kadācit kiṃcit śītatrāṇaṃ saṃpadyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Go to this king and make some speech favorable to him; perhaps some protection against the cold may be obtained."

children.text: sa samprasthitaḥ yāvadrājā hastiskandhārūḍho nirgacchati ||
children.translated_text: He set out, and just then the king came out mounted on the back of an elephant.

children.text: sa brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati kiṃ tāvadrājānaṃ stunomi āhosviddhastināgamiti ||
children.translated_text: The Brahmin considered, "Should I now praise the king, or the elephant?"

children.text: tasyaitadabhavat ayaṃ hastināgaḥ sarvalokasya priyo manāpaśca ||
children.translated_text: This occurred to him: "This elephant is dear and pleasing to all the people.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu tāvadrājā hastināgaṃ tāvadabhiṣṭaumīti ||
children.translated_text: Let the king be for now; I will first praise the elephant."

children.text: gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: And he spoke a verse:

children.text: airāvaṇasyākṛtitulyadeho rūpopapanno varalakṣaṇaiśca
children.translated_text: "Your body is equal in form to that of <s>Airāvaṇa</s>; you are endowed with beauty and excellent marks.

children.text: lakṣe praśasto 'si mahāgajendra varṇapramāṇena surūparūpa ||
children.translated_text: You are renowned among multitudes, great lord of elephants, handsome in color and proportion, truly beautiful in form."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke.

children.text: tato rājā abhiprasanno gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, greatly pleased, spoke a verse:

children.text: yo me gajendro dayito manāpaḥ prītiprado dṛṣṭiharo narāṇām
children.translated_text: "You speak words of praise for this lord of elephants of mine, dear and pleasing, a giver of joy, captivating the eyes of men.

children.text: taṃ bhāṣase varṇapadāni tasya dadāmi te grāmavarāṇi pañca ||
children.translated_text: For that, I give you five excellent villages."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau hastināgaḥ ahameva tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: "What do you think, monks? The elephant of that time was none other than I myself at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: tadāpyahamanenaikayā gāthayā stutaḥ mayā cāyaṃ pañcagrāmavareṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then too I was praised by him with a single verse, and by me he was established in five excellent villages.

children.text: etarhi anenaikagāthayā stutaḥ mayāpi cāyaṃ pratyekabodhau vyākṛta iti ||
children.translated_text: Now he has praised me with a single verse, and by me he has been predicted for <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening)."

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.

children.text: Chapter 6
bhagavāñśrughnāmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One arrived at <s>Śrughnā</s>.

children.text: śrughnāyāmindro nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrughnā</s> there lived a Brahmin named <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: sa ca rūpayauvanaśrutamanuprāpto na mamāsti kaścit tulya ityatīva vikatthate ||
children.translated_text: He had attained beauty, youth, and learning, and he boasted exceedingly, "There is no one equal to me."

children.text: bhagavāṃścānyatamasmin pradeśe purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, in a certain place, was seated before the community of monks on a seat that had been prepared, teaching the Dharma.

children.text: aśrauṣīdindro nāma brāhmaṇaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrughnāmanuprāpta iti ||
children.translated_text: The Brahmin named <s>Indra</s> heard, "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has arrived at <s>Śrughnā</s>."

children.text: tasyaitadabhavat śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrūyate 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādika iti ||
children.translated_text: This occurred to him: "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is said to be handsome, lovely to behold, and pleasing.

children.text: gacchāmi paśyāmi kiṃ mamāntikādabhirūpatara āhosvinneti ||
children.translated_text: I will go and see whether he is more handsome than I am, or not."

children.text: sa nirgato yāvat paśyati bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam ||
children.translated_text: He went out, and then he saw the Blessed One, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, shining with the eighty minor marks, ornamented with a fathom-wide radiance, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat kiṃ cāpi śramaṇo gautamo mamāntikādabhirūpataraḥ noccatara iti ||
children.translated_text: After seeing him, this occurred to him: "Although the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is more handsome than I am, he is not taller."

children.text: sa bhagavato mūrdhānamavalokayitumārabdho yāvanna paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He began to look at the crown of the Blessed One's head, but he could not see it.

children.text: sa ūrdhvataraṃ pradeśamārūḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He climbed up to a higher place.

children.text: tatra bhagavānindraṃ brāhmaṇamāmantrayate alaṃ brāhmaṇa khedamāpatsyase ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the Brahmin <s>Indra</s>: "Enough, Brahmin; you will become weary.

children.text: yadi sumerumūrdhānamapi abhiruhya tathāgatasya mūrdhānamavalokayasi tathā sutarāṃ khedamāpatsyase na ca drakṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Even if you were to climb to the summit of <s>Sumeru</s> and look for the crown of the Tathāgata's head, you would all the more become weary, and you would not see it.

children.text: api tu na tvayā śrutaṃ sasurāsurajagadanavalokitamūrdhāno buddhā bhagavanta iti api tu yadīpsasi tathāgatasya śarīrapramāṇaṃ draṣṭum tava gṛhe 'gnihotrakuṇḍaṃ tasyādhastādgośīrṣacandanamayī yaṣṭirupatiṣṭhate tāmuddhṛtya māpaya ||
children.translated_text: But have you not heard that the blessed Buddhas have heads unlooked upon by the world together with its gods and asuras? Still, if you wish to see the measure of the Tathāgata's body, in your house, beneath the fire-offering pit, there is a staff made of gośīrṣa sandalwood. Take it up and measure.

children.text: tattathāgatamātāpaitṛkasyāśrayasya pramāṇamiti ||
children.translated_text: That is the measure of the Tathāgata's body born from his mother and father."

children.text: indro brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati etadasyāścaryaṃ na kadācinmayā śrutam gacchāmi paśyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: The Brahmin <s>Indra</s> considered, "This is a marvel of his; I have never heard such a thing before. I will go and see."

children.text: tvaritatvaritagato 'gnihotrakuṇḍakasyādhastāt khanitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going very quickly, he began to dig beneath the fire-offering pit.

children.text: sarvaṃ tathaiva ||
children.translated_text: Everything was exactly so.

children.text: so 'bhiprasannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became deeply inspired with faith.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ sarvajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He considered, "Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is omniscient.

children.text: gacchāmi paryupāsitumiti ||
children.translated_text: I will go and attend upon him."

children.text: sa prasādajāto yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Filled with faith, he approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he exchanged with the Blessed One various face-to-face words of greeting, cordial and pleasing conversation, and sat down to one side.

children.text: tato bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yathendreṇa brāhmaṇena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature, the Blessed One gave such a teaching of the Dharma that led to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that the Brahmin <s>Indra</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of personality-view that had risen with twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ kathayati atikrānto 'haṃ bhadanta atikrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the truth, he said, "I have crossed beyond, venerable sir; I have crossed beyond.

children.text: eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dharma, and to the community of monks.

children.text: upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: Please regard me as a lay follower from this day onward, for as long as life lasts, one who has gone for refuge while endowed with life."

children.text: abhiprasanno 'thendro brāhmaṇa utthāyāsanāt ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat yadi bhagavānanujānīyāt ahaṃ gośīrṣacandanamayyā yaṣṭyā mahaṃ prajñapayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Brahmin <s>Indra</s>, deeply inspired with faith, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "If the Blessed One permits it, I would arrange a great festival with the staff made of gośīrṣa sandalwood."

children.text: bhagavānāha gaccha brāhmaṇa anujñātaṃ prajñapayasi ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Go, Brahmin. It is permitted; you may arrange it."

children.text: tatastena viviktāvakāśe mahatā satkāreṇāsau yaṣṭirucchrāpitā mahaśca prajñapitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in a secluded place he had that staff raised with great honor, and a festival was arranged.

children.text: anyairapi brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ kuśalamadhiṣṭhānāya bhavatviti viditvā kulā baddhā ||
children.translated_text: Other brāhmaṇas and householders too, knowing, "May this be for the establishment of merit," became attached by families.

children.text: indreṇa brāhmaṇena yaṣṭyā mahaḥ prajñapita iti indramaha indramaha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Because a festival with the staff had been arranged by the brāhmaṇa <s>Indra</s>, the designation "the <s>Indra</s> festival, the <s>Indra</s> festival" arose.

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate āgamaya ānanda yena toyikā ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Come, <s>Ānanda</s>; let us go to <s>Toyikā</s>."

children.text: evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstoyikāmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One arrived at <s>Toyikā</s>.

children.text: tasmiṃśca pradeśe brāhmaṇo lāṅgalaṃ vāhayati ||
children.translated_text: And in that region a brāhmaṇa was driving a plough.

children.text: athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam ||
children.translated_text: Then he saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with the eighty minor marks, adorned with a fathom-wide aura, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, lovely on every side.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati yadi bhagavantaṃ gautamamupetyābhivādayiṣyāmi karmaparihāṇirme bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he reflected, "If I approach the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> and salute him, there will be a loss in my work."

children.text: atha nopetyābhivādayiṣyāmi puṇyaparihāṇirbhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "But if I do not approach and salute him, there will be a loss of merit."

children.text: tat ko 'sau upāyaḥ syāt yena me karmaparihāṇir na syānnāpi puṇyaparihāṇiriti ||
children.translated_text: "What means, then, could there be by which there would be no loss in my work and no loss of merit either?"

children.text: tasya buddhirutpannā atrastha evābhivādanaṃ karomi ||
children.translated_text: The thought arose in him: "I will make my salutation while standing right here."

children.text: evaṃ na karmaparihāṇir na puṇyaparihāṇiriti ||
children.translated_text: "In this way there will be no loss in my work and no loss of merit."

children.text: tena yathāgṛhītayaiva pratodayaṣṭyā tatrasthenaivābhivādanaṃ kṛtam abhivādaye buddhaṃ bhagavantamiti ||
children.translated_text: With the goad-staff just as he had taken it up, he made his salutation while standing right there, saying, "I salute the Buddha, the Blessed One."

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate bhavakṣayakaraḥ kṣaṇam eṣa brāhmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "For this brāhmaṇa this moment brings about the destruction of becoming."

children.text: sacedasyaivaṃ samyaksampratyayajñānadarśanaṃ pravartate etasmin pradeśe kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopito 'sthisaṃghātastiṣṭhatīty ahamanenopakrameṇa vandito bhaveyam evamanena dvābhyāṃ samyaksambuddhābhyāṃ vandanā kṛtā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: "If right conviction, knowledge, and vision should arise in him in this way, 'In this place the undisturbed mass of bones of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, stands,' then by this very act I would have been venerated by him; thus veneration would have been made by him to two fully awakened Buddhas."

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ asminnānanda pradeśe kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopito 'sthisaṃghātastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: "Why is that? In this place, <s>Ānanda</s>, the undisturbed mass of bones of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, stands."

children.text: athāyuṣmānānando laghulaghveva caturguṇamuttarāsaṅgaṃ prajñapya bhagavantamidamavocat niṣīdatu bhagavān prajñapta evāsane ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> very quickly spread out his upper robe folded fourfold and said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One sit down; a seat has been prepared."

children.text: evamayaṃ pṛthivīpradeśo dvābhyāṃ samyaksambuddhābhyāṃ paribhukto bhaviṣyati yacca kāśyapena samyaksambuddhena yaccaitarhi bhagavatā iti ||
children.translated_text: "Thus this region of earth will have been used by two fully awakened Buddhas: by <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, and now by the Blessed One."

children.text: niṣaṇṇo bhagavān prajñapta evāsane ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.

children.text: niṣadya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātam avikopitaṃ draṣṭum etasya bhagavan kālaḥ etasya sugata samayaḥ yaṃ bhagavān bhikṣūṇāṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopitaṃ śarīrasaṃghātamupadarśayet ||
children.translated_text: After sitting down, he addressed the monks: "Do you wish, monks, to see the undisturbed bodily mass of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha?" "This is the time, Blessed One; this is the occasion, Sugata, for the Blessed One to show the monks the undisturbed bodily mass of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha."

children.text: dṛṣṭvā bhikṣavaścittamabhiprasādayiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: "Having seen it, the monks will make their minds deeply faithful."

children.text: tato bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One produced an ordinary thought.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavanto laukikaṃ cittamutpādayanti tasmin samaye kuntapipīlikā api prāṇino bhagavataścetasā cittamājānanti ||
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that, at the time when buddhas, blessed ones, produce an ordinary thought, even small creatures and ants know with their minds the thought in the Blessed One's mind.

children.text: nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavatā laukikacittamutpāditamiti paśyanti kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātamavikopitaṃ draṣṭukāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The nāgas reflected, "For what reason has the Blessed One produced an ordinary thought?" They saw, "He wishes to see the undisturbed bodily mass of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha."

children.text: tatastaiḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopitaśarīrasaṃghāta ucchrāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the undisturbed bodily mass of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, was raised up by them.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma udgṛhṇīta bhikṣavo nimittam ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Take note of the sign, monks."

children.text: antardhāsyati ||
children.translated_text: "It will disappear."

children.text: antarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It disappeared.

children.text: rājñā prasenajitā śrutaṃ bhagavatā śrāvakāṇāṃ darśanāyāvikopitaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātaṃ samucchritamiti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> heard, "The undisturbed bodily mass of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, has been raised up by the Blessed One for the sight of his disciples."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ kutūhalajātaḥ sahāntaḥpureṇa kumārairamātyairbhaṭabalāgrair naigamajānapadaiśca draṣṭuṃ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he became curious and set out to see it together with his inner court, princes, ministers, foremost soldiers, townspeople, and country folk.

children.text: evaṃ virūḍhakaḥ anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ ṛṣidattaḥ purāṇaḥ sthapatiḥ viśākhā mṛgāramātā anekāni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kutūhalajātāni draṣṭuṃ samprasthitāni pūrvakaiśca kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni ||
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, <s>Ṛṣidatta</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s> the master builder, <s>Viśākhā Mṛgāramātā</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of beings, made curious and impelled by former roots of merit, set out to see it.

children.text: yāvadasau antarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But by then it had disappeared.

children.text: taiḥ śrutam antarhito 'sau bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātadhātur avikopita iti ||
children.translated_text: They heard, "That undisturbed relic, the bodily mass of the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, has disappeared."

children.text: śrutvā ca punasteṣāṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyamutpannam vṛthā asmākamāgamanaṃ jātamiti ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, sorrow and dejection arose in them: "Our coming has been in vain."

children.text: athānyatamena copāsakena sa pradeśaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain lay devotee circumambulated that place.

children.text: evaṃ ca cetasā cittamabhisaṃskṛtam asmānme padāvihārāt kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: And he shaped this thought in his mind: "How much merit will there be for me from this going on foot?"

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstasya mahājanakāyasyāvipratisārasaṃjananārthaṃ tasya copāsakasya cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in order to produce freedom from remorse in that great crowd of people, and knowing with his mind the thought in that lay follower's mind, spoke a verse:

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of gold <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold

children.text: yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ padāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān ||
children.translated_text: are not equal to the wise man who, with a confident mind, makes a walking circuit at Buddha shrines.

children.text: anyatamena upāsakena tasmin pradeśe mṛttikāpiṇḍo dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A certain lay follower gave a lump of clay at that place.

children.text: evaṃ ca cittamabhisaṃskṛtam padāvihārasya tāvadiyat puṇyamākhyātaṃ bhagavatā anyatra ||
children.translated_text: And his thought was formed in this way: "So much merit for the walking circuit has been declared by the Blessed One; apart from that,

children.text: mṛttikāpiṇḍasya kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti atha bhagavāṃstasyāpi cetasā cittamājñāya bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: how much merit will there be for the lump of clay?" Then the Blessed One, knowing his thought also with his mind, spoke:

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of gold <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold

children.text: yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitta āropayenmṛttikapiṇḍamekam ||
children.translated_text: are not equal to the one who, with a confident mind, places a single lump of clay on Buddha shrines.

children.text: tataḥ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmṛttikāpiṇḍasamāropaṇaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, many hundreds of thousands of living beings placed lumps of clay there.

children.text: aparaistatra muktapuṣpāṇyavakṣiptāni evaṃ ca cittamabhisaṃskṛtam padāvihārasya mṛttikāpiṇḍasya ceyat puṇyamuktaṃ bhagavatā asmākaṃ tu muktapuṣpāṇāṃ kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Others scattered loose flowers there. And their thought was formed in this way: "So much merit for the walking circuit and the lump of clay has been stated by the Blessed One; but how much merit will there be for our loose flowers?" Then the Blessed One, knowing their thought also with his mind, spoke a verse:

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of gold <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold are not equal to this:

children.text: yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ āropayenmuktasupuṣparāśim ||
children.translated_text: the one who, with a confident mind, places a heap of loose, excellent flowers on Buddha shrines.

children.text: aparaistatra mālāvihāraḥ kṛtaḥ cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam muktapuṣpāṇāṃ bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam ||
children.translated_text: Others made a <s>mālāvihāra</s> (garland arrangement) there, and their thought was formed: "So much merit for loose flowers has been stated by the Blessed One.

children.text: asmākaṃ mālāvihārasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: How much merit will there be for our <s>mālāvihāra</s>?" Then the Blessed One, knowing their thought also with his mind, spoke a verse:

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇavāhā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of loads of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold

children.text: yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitto mālāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān ||
children.translated_text: are not equal to the wise man who, with a confident mind, makes a <s>mālāvihāra</s> at Buddha shrines.

children.text: aparaistatra pradīpamālā dattā cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam mālāvihārasya bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam ||
children.translated_text: Others gave a row of lamps there, and their thought was formed: "So much merit for the <s>mālāvihāra</s> has been stated by the Blessed One.

children.text: asmākaṃ pradīpadānasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: How much merit will there be for our gift of lamps?" Then the Blessed One, knowing their thought also with his mind, spoke a verse:

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇakoṭyo jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of crores of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold

children.text: yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ pradīpadānaṃ prakaroti vidvān ||
children.translated_text: are not equal to the wise man who, with a confident mind, makes a gift of lamps at Buddha shrines.

children.text: aparaistatra gandhābhiṣeko dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Others made an offering of perfumed sprinkling there.

children.text: evaṃ cetasā cittamabhisaṃskṛtam pradīpasya bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam ||
children.translated_text: Their thought was formed in this way: "So much merit for the lamp has been stated by the Blessed One.

children.text: asmākaṃ gandhābhiṣekasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: How much merit will there be for our perfumed sprinkling?" Then the Blessed One, knowing their thought also with his mind, spoke a verse:

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇarāśayo jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of heaps of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold

children.text: yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitto gandhābhiṣekaṃ prakaroti vidvān ||
children.translated_text: are not equal to the wise man who, with a confident mind, makes a perfumed sprinkling at Buddha shrines.

children.text: aparaistatra chatradhvajapatākāropaṇaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Others erected umbrellas, banners, and flags there.

children.text: evaṃ ca cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: And knowing their thought in this way with his mind, he spoke a verse:

children.text: tiṣṭhantaṃ pūjayedyaśca yaścāpi parinirvṛtam
children.translated_text: Whoever worships him while he is standing present, and whoever worships him after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: samaṃ cittaṃ prasādyeha nāsti puṇyaviśeṣatā ||
children.translated_text: if their minds are equally made clear with faith here, there is no difference in merit.

children.text: evaṃ hyacintiyā buddhā buddhadharmāpyacintiyā
children.translated_text: For Buddhas are inconceivable, and the qualities of Buddhas too are inconceivable;

children.text: acintiye prasannānāṃ vipāko 'pi acintiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those who have faith in what is inconceivable, the ripening too is inconceivable.

children.text: teṣām acintiyānām apratihatadharmacakravartinām
children.translated_text: Of those inconceivable ones, turners of the unobstructed wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: samyaksambuddhānāṃ nālaṃ guṇapāramadhigantum ||
children.translated_text: the perfectly awakened Buddhas, one is not able to reach the far limit of their qualities.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tato bhagavatā tasya mahājanakāyasya tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> to that great crowd of people that, having heard it, many hundreds of thousands of living beings attained a great distinction.

children.text: kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni kaiścit pratyekabodhau kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau kaiścinmūrdhāgatāni kaiścinmūrdhānaḥ kaiściduṣṇagatānyāsāditāni kaiścit satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayaḥ kaiścitsrotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam kaiścit sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam yadbhūyasā buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇāḥ saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthāpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some produced thoughts toward the awakening of a disciple, some toward individual awakening, and some toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. Some reached the summit stages, some the summits themselves, some attained the heat stages, some the acquiescences conforming to the truths; some realized the fruit of stream-entry, some the fruit of once-returning, and some realized arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements. For the most part they were established as inclined toward the Buddha, bent toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and sloping toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: atha anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavantamidamavocat yadi bhagavānanujānīyāt atra mahaṃ prajñāpayeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said this to the Blessed One: "If the Blessed One permits it, I would arrange a festival here."

children.text: anujānāmi gṛhapate prajñāpayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: "I permit it, householder; it should be arranged."

children.text: tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā mahaḥ prajñāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> arranged a festival.

children.text: toyikāmaha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: It came to be known by the name <s>Toyikāmaha</s>.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

children.text: Chapter 7
atha bhagavān kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, wandering on tour through the districts of <s>Kośala</s>, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: He stayed at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: aśrauṣīdanāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ bhagavān kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard: "The Blessed One, wandering on tour through the districts of <s>Kośala</s>, has arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāma iti ||
children.translated_text: He is staying at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he again approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇamanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: As the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> was sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed him, made him accept, stirred him up, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dharma.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: After instructing him, making him accept, stirring him up, and gladdening him in many ways with a discourse on the Dharma, he became silent.

children.text: anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhuktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena iti ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to him: "May the Blessed One consent to take tomorrow's meal in my house, together with the community of monks."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapatestūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> by remaining silent.

children.text: anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yena svaniveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, knowing by the Blessed One's silence that he had consented, rejoiced in and approved the Blessed One's words, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet, departed from the Blessed One's presence, and approached his own residence.

children.text: upasaṃkramya dauvārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate na tāvadbhoḥ puruṣa tīrthyānāṃ praveśo dātavyo yāvad buddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he addressed the doorkeeper: "Good man, no entrance is to be given to the tīrthyas (non-Buddhist ascetics) until the community of monks headed by the Buddha has eaten.

children.text: tataḥ paścādahaṃ tīrthyānāṃ dāsyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: After that I shall give to the tīrthyas."

children.text: evamāryeti dauvārikaḥ puruṣo 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, noble sir," the doorkeeper answered the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti ||
children.translated_text: During that very night the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> prepared pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten; rising early, he arranged seats, set out water jars, and announced the time to the Blessed One through a messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. Let the Blessed One judge when it is now the proper time."

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapaterbhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the place of the meal at the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s home.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down before the community of monks on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: atha anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, satisfied and served them with pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten with his own hands.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: After satisfying and serving them in many ways with pure and excellent foods to be chewed and eaten with his own hands, and knowing that the Blessed One had eaten, had washed his hands, and had put away his bowl, he took a lower seat and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the Dharma.

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapo 'nyatamasmādāraṇyakācchayanāsanāt dīrghakeśaśmaśrurlūhacīvaro jetavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, with long hair and beard and wearing a coarse robe, came to <s>Jetavana</s> from a certain forest lodging.

children.text: sa paśyati jetavanaṃ śūnyam ||
children.translated_text: He saw that <s>Jetavana</s> was empty.

children.text: tenopadhivārikaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kutra buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgha iti ||
children.translated_text: He asked the attendant, "Where is the community of monks headed by the Buddha?"

children.text: tena samākhyātam anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinopanimantrita iti ||
children.translated_text: The attendant explained, "They have been invited by the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>."

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati gacchāmi tatraiva piṇḍapātaṃ paribhokṣyāmi buddhapramukhaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ paryupāsiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He considered, "I will go there and take my alms meal there, and I will attend upon the community of monks headed by the Buddha."

children.text: so 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He went to the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: ato dauvārikena uktaḥ ārya tiṣṭha mā pravekṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: There the doorkeeper said to him, "Noble sir, stop. You may not enter."

children.text: kasyārthāya anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā ājñā dattā mā tāvat tīrthyānāṃ praveśaṃ dāsyasi yāvadbuddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhuktam ||
children.translated_text: "For what reason?" "The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> gave an order: 'You are not to give entrance to the tīrthyas until the community of monks headed by the Buddha has eaten.

children.text: tataḥ paścāt tīrthyānāṃ dāsyāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: After that I shall give to the tīrthyas.'"

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ saṃlakṣayati tasya me lābhāḥ sulabdhāḥ yanmāṃ śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ śramaṇaśākyaputrīya iti na jānante ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> considered, "My gains are well gained, in that faithful brāhmaṇas and householders do not recognize me as an ascetic, a son of the Śākyas.

children.text: gacchāmi kṛpaṇajanasyānugrahaṃ karomīti viditvā udyānaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will go and do a kindness for poor people." Having understood this, he went to the park.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati adya mayā kasyānugrahaḥ kartavya iti ||
children.translated_text: He considered, "For whom should I do a kindness today?"

children.text: yāvadanyatamā nagarāvalambikā kuṣṭhābhidrutā sarujārtā pakvagātrā bhikṣāmaṭati ||
children.translated_text: Just then a certain woman dependent on the city, afflicted with leprosy, pained and distressed, her limbs suppurating, was wandering for alms.

children.text: sa tasyāḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He approached her.

children.text: tasyāśca bhikṣāyāmāyāsaḥ sampannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in her alms there was some gruel.

children.text: tayā āyuṣmān mahākāśyapo dṛṣṭaḥ kāyaprāsādikaścittaprāsādikaḥ śāntena īryāpathena ||
children.translated_text: She saw the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, pleasing in body and pleasing in mind, with a peaceful deportment.

children.text: sā saṃlakṣayati nūnaṃ mayā evaṃvidhe dakṣiṇīye kārā kṛtā yena me iyamevaṃrūpā samavasthā ||
children.translated_text: She considered, "Surely some offense was committed by me toward such a worthy recipient of gifts, because of which I have fallen into this condition.

children.text: yadi āryo mahākāśyapo mamāntikādanukampāmupādāya ācāmaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ahamasmai dadyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: If noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, out of compassion for me, would accept this gruel from me, I would give it to him."

children.text: tata āyuṣmatā mahākāśyapena tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya pātramupanāmitam yadi te bhagini parityaktam dīyatāmasmin pātra iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, knowing with his mind the thought in her mind, held out his bowl: "If you have set it aside, sister, give it into this bowl."

children.text: tatastayā cittamabhiprasādya tasmin pātre dattam ||
children.translated_text: Then, making her mind deeply clear with faith, she gave it into that bowl.

children.text: makṣikā ca patitā ||
children.translated_text: And a fly had fallen into it.

children.text: sā tāmapanetumārabdhā ||
children.translated_text: She began to remove it.

children.text: tasyāstasminnācāme 'ṅguliḥ patitā ||
children.translated_text: As she did so, her finger fell into that gruel.

children.text: saṃlakṣayati kiṃcāpyāryeṇa mama cittānurakṣayā na choritaḥ api tu na paribhokṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: She considered, "Although the noble one did not throw it away out of consideration for my state of mind, still he will not eat it."

children.text: athāyuṣmatā mahākāśyapena tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya tasyā eva pratyakṣamanyatamaṃ kuḍyamūlaṃ niśritya paribhuktam ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, knowing her thought with his mind, ate it in her very presence, leaning against the base of a wall.

children.text: sā saṃlakṣayati kiṃcāpi āryeṇa mama cittānurakṣayā paribhuktam nānenāhāreṇāhārakṛtyaṃ kariṣyati iti ||
children.translated_text: She considered, "Although the noble one has eaten it out of consideration for my state of mind, he will not accomplish the purpose of nourishment with this food."

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapastasyāścittamājñāya tāṃ nagarāvalambikāmidamavocat bhagini prāmodyamutpādayasi ahaṃ tvadīyenāhāreṇa rātriṃdivasamatināmayiṣyāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, knowing her thought, said this to that woman dependent on the city: "Sister, produce joy. With your food I shall pass the night and day."

children.text: tasyā atīva audbilyamutpannam mamāryeṇa mahākāśyapena piṇḍapātaḥ pratigṛhīta iti ||
children.translated_text: Very great elation arose in her: "My alms-food has been accepted by the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>."

children.text: tata āyuṣmatī mahākāśyape cittamabhiprasādya kālaṃ gatā tuṣite devanikāye upapannā ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made her mind deeply faithful toward the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, she died and was reborn in the divine host of <s>Tuṣita</s>.

children.text: sā śakreṇa devendreṇa dṛṣṭā ācāmaṃ pratipādayantī cittamabhiprasādayantī kālaṃ ca kurvāṇā ||
children.translated_text: She had been seen by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, offering rinsing-gruel, making her mind deeply faithful, and dying.

children.text: no tu dṛṣṭā kutropapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: But he had not seen where she had been reborn.

children.text: sa narakān vyavalokayitumārabdho na paśyati tiryak ca pretaṃ ca manuṣyāṃścāturmahārājikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāvanna paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He began to look through the hells; he did not see her. Then among animals, pretas, humans, the gods of the Four Great Kings, and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, he did not see her anywhere.

children.text: tathā hyadhastāddevānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate no tūpariṣṭāt ||
children.translated_text: For the knowledge and vision of gods operates downward, but not upward.

children.text: atha śakro devānāmindro yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya gāthābhigītena praśnaṃ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he asked a question in a verse-song:

children.text: carataḥ piṇḍapātaṃ hi kāśyapasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: "While the great-souled <s>Kāśyapa</s>

children.text: kutrāsau modate nārī kāśyapācāmadāyikā ||
children.translated_text: was wandering for alms, where does that woman rejoice, the giver of rinsing-gruel to <s>Kāśyapa</s>?"

children.text: bhagavānāha ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.text: tuṣitā nāma te devāḥ sarvakāmasamṛddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Those gods are called <s>Tuṣita</s>, endowed with every object of desire;

children.text: yatrāsau modate nārī kāśyapācāmadāyikā ||
children.translated_text: there that woman rejoices, the giver of rinsing-gruel to <s>Kāśyapa</s>."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke.

children.text: atha śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhavat ime ca tāvanmanuṣyāḥ puṇyāpuṇyānām apratyakṣadarśino dānāni dadati puṇyāni kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "These humans, though they do not directly see merit and demerit, give gifts and perform meritorious deeds.

children.text: ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśanena puṇyānāṃ svapuṇyaphale vyavasthitaḥ kasmāt dānāni na dadāmi puṇyāni vā na karomi ayamāryo mahākāśyapo dīnānāthakṛpaṇavanīpakānukampī ||
children.translated_text: I, who directly see meritorious deeds and am established in the fruit of my own merit, why should I not give gifts or perform meritorious deeds? This noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> has compassion for the poor, the helpless, the destitute, and beggars.

children.text: yannvahamenaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādayeyam ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to present him with a lump of alms-food?"

children.text: iti viditvā kṛpaṇavīthyāṃ gṛhaṃ nirmitavān avacīravicīrakaṃ kākābhilīnakaṃ nātiparamarūpaṃ kuvindaṃ cātmānamabhinirmāya udūḍhaśiraskaḥ saṇaśāṭikānivāsitaḥ sphaṭitapāṇipādo vastraṃ vāyitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having understood this, he created a house in a poor street, shabby, tattered, one where crows huddled, not at all handsome; and, creating himself as a weaver, with dishevelled hair, wearing a garment of hempen cloth, and with cracked hands and feet, he began to weave cloth.

children.text: śacī api devakanyā kuvindanaryā veśadhāriṇī tasarikāṃ kartumārabdhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śacī</s> too, the divine maiden, taking the form of a weaver's wife, began to make a shuttle.

children.text: pārśve cāsyā divyā sudhā sajjīkṛtā tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Beside her stood divine nectar, prepared and ready.

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ kṛpaṇānāthavanīpakajanānukampako 'nupūrveṇa tadgṛhamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, compassionate toward the poor, helpless, and beggarly people, gradually arrived at that house.

children.text: duḥkhitako 'yamiti kṛtvā dvāre sthitena pātraṃ prasāditam ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, "This man is afflicted," he stood at the door and held out his bowl.

children.text: śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa divyayā sudhayā pūritam ||
children.translated_text: It was filled with divine nectar by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: athāyuṣmato mahākāśyapasyaitadabhavat ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>:

children.text: divyaṃ cāsya sudhābhaktam ayaṃ ca gṛhavistaraḥ
children.translated_text: "This food is divine nectar,
