children.text: suviruddhamiti kṛtvā jāto me hṛdi saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but this household setting is quite at odds with it; therefore doubt has arisen in my heart."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he thought.

children.text: dharmatā hyeṣā asamanvāhṛtya arhatāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate ||
children.translated_text: For this is the nature of things: the knowledge and vision of arhats does not operate without directing attention.

children.text: sa samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to direct his attention.

children.text: yāvat paśyati śakraṃ devendram ||
children.translated_text: At once he saw <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: sa kathayati kauśika kiṃ duḥkhitajanasyāntarāyaṃ karoṣi yasya te bhagavatā dīrgharātrānugato vicikitsākathaṃkathāśalyaḥ samūla ārūḍho yathāpi tattathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena ||
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Kauśika</s>, why do you obstruct a suffering person, you whose thorn of doubt and uncertainty, followed through the long night by the Blessed One, has been uprooted root and all by the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha?"

children.text: ārya mahākāśyapa kiṃ duḥkhitajanasyāntarāyaṃ karomi ime tāvat manuṣyāḥ puṇyānām apratyakṣadarśino dānāni dadati puṇyāni kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: "Noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, how am I obstructing a suffering person? These humans, though they do not directly see meritorious deeds, give gifts and perform meritorious deeds.

children.text: ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī eva puṇyānāṃ kathaṃ dānāni na dadāmi nanu coktaṃ bhagavatā ||
children.translated_text: I directly see meritorious deeds. How could I not give gifts? And was it not said by the Blessed One:

children.text: karaṇīyāni puṇyāni duḥkhā hyakṛtapuṇyatā
children.translated_text: 'Meritorious deeds should be done, for not having made merit is painful;

children.text: kṛtapuṇyāni modante asmiṃlloke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: those who have made merit rejoice in this world and in the next.'"

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti āyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ samanvāhṛtya kulāni piṇḍapātaṃ praveṣṭumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From then on, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> began to enter households for alms only after directing his attention.

children.text: atha śakro devendra ākāśasthaścāyuṣmato mahākāśyapasya piṇḍapātaṃ carato divyayā sudhayā pātraṃ pūrayati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, standing in the sky, would fill the bowl of the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> with divine nectar as he wandered for alms.

children.text: āyuṣmānapi mahākāśyapaḥ pātramadhomukhaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: But the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> would turn the bowl face downward.

children.text: annapānaṃ choryate ||
children.translated_text: Food and drink would be spilled out.

children.text: etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti ||
children.translated_text: The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānāha tasmādanujānāmi piṇḍopadhānaṃ dhārayitavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Therefore I authorize that a support for the alms-bowl should be carried."

children.text: sāmantakena śabdo visṛtaḥ amukayā nagarāvalambikayā āryo mahākāśyapa ācāmena pratipāditaḥ sā ca tuṣite devanikāye upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: A report spread through the neighboring region: "By such-and-such a woman dependent on the city, the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> was presented with rinsing-gruel, and she has been reborn in the divine host of <s>Tuṣita</s>."

children.text: rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena śrutam amukayā nagarāvalambikayā āryo mahākāśyapa ācāmena pratipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> heard, "By such-and-such a woman dependent on the city, the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> was presented with rinsing-gruel.

children.text: sā tuṣite deve upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: She has been reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he again approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: To King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, seated to one side, the Blessed One showed, instructed, encouraged, and delighted him with a Dharma discourse. After showing, instructing, encouraging, and delighting him in many ways with a Dharma discourse, he became silent.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavānāryamahākāśyapamuddiśya bhaktaṃ saptāhena iti ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One consent to a meal from me in seven days, dedicated to noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitas tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to King <s>Prasenajit</s> by remaining silent.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, knowing from the Blessed One's silence that he had consented, departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastāmeva rātriṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñāpya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, that very night, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> prepared fine hard and soft foods, rose early, arranged seats, set out water-jars, and announced the time to the Blessed One by a messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. Let the Blessed One now consider the proper time."

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>'s meal-offering.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared in front of the community of monks.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, satisfied and served them with his own hands with pure, excellent hard and soft foods.

children.text: anyatamaśca kroḍamallako vṛddhānte cittamabhiprasādayaṃstiṣṭhati ayaṃ rājā pratyakṣadarśī eva puṇyānāṃ sve puṇyaphale pratiṣṭhāpito 'tṛpta eva puṇyairdānāni dadāti puṇyāni karoti ||
children.translated_text: And a certain <s>Kroḍamallaka</s> stood nearby, at the edge of the group, making his mind deeply faithful: "This king sees the results of merit directly. Established in the fruit of his own merit, yet still not satisfied with merit, he gives gifts and makes merit."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo 'nekaparyāyeṇa buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastāt niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, after satisfying and serving in many ways the community of monks headed by the Buddha with pure, excellent hard and soft foods, knew that the Blessed One had eaten, washed his hands, and put away his bowl; taking a lower seat, he sat down before the Blessed One to hear the Dharma.

children.text: tato bhagavatā abhihitaḥ mahārāja kasya nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśāmi kiṃ tava āhosvidyena tavāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasūtamiti rājā saṃlakṣayati māṃ bhagavān piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to him, "Great king, in whose name shall I assign the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (offering-dedication)? In yours, or in the name of the one by whom more abundant merit than yours has been produced?" The king thought, "The Blessed One is eating my alms-food.

children.text: ko 'nyo mamāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyatīti viditvā kathayati bhagavan yena mamāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasūtaṃ tasya bhagavān nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatu iti ||
children.translated_text: Who else could have produced more abundant merit than I?" Knowing this, he said, "Blessed One, let the Blessed One assign the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in the name of the one by whom more abundant merit than mine has been produced."

children.text: tato bhagavatā kroḍamallakasya nāmnā dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One assigned the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in the name of the <s>Kroḍamallaka</s>.

children.text: evam yāvat ṣaḍdivasān ||
children.translated_text: In this way it continued for as many as six days.

children.text: tato 'nyadivase rājā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ mama bhagavān piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte kroḍamallakasya nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśati iti ||
children.translated_text: Then on another day the king rested his cheek on his hand and remained absorbed in thought: "The Blessed One eats my alms-food, but assigns the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in the name of the <s>Kroḍamallaka</s>."

children.text: so 'mātyairdṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was seen by the ministers.

children.text: te kathayanti kimarthaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthita iti rājā kathayati bhavantaḥ kathaṃ na cintāparastiṣṭhāmi yatredānīṃ sa bhagavān mama piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte kroḍamallakasya nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatīti tatraiko vṛddho 'mātyaḥ kathayati alpotsuko bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Why are you resting your cheek on your hand and remaining absorbed in thought?" The king said, "Gentlemen, how could I not remain absorbed in thought, when now the Blessed One eats my alms-food but assigns the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in the name of the <s>Kroḍamallaka</s>?" Then one elderly minister said, "Let Your Majesty be free from concern.

children.text: vayaṃ tathā kariṣyāmo yathā śvo bhagavān devasyaiva nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatīti ||
children.translated_text: We will act so that tomorrow the Blessed One will assign the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in Your Majesty's own name."

children.text: taiḥ pauruṣeyāṇāmājñā dattā yataḥ śvo bhavadbhiḥ praṇīta āhāraḥ sajjīkartavyaḥ prabhūtaścaiva samudānayitavyo yathopārdhaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pātre patati upārdhaṃ bhūmau iti ||
children.translated_text: They gave orders to the servants: "Tomorrow you must prepare excellent food and bring together a great quantity of it, so that one half falls into the monks' bowls and one half onto the ground."

children.text: amātyairaparasmin divase prabhūta āhāraḥ sajjīkṛtaḥ praṇītaśca ||
children.translated_text: On the following day the ministers prepared a great quantity of food, and excellent food at that.

children.text: tataḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pariveṣitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they began to serve the comfortably seated community of monks headed by the Buddha.

children.text: upārdhaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pātre patati upārdhaṃ bhūmau ||
children.translated_text: One half fell into the monks' bowls, and one half onto the ground.

children.text: tataḥ kroḍamallakāḥ pradhāvitāḥ bhūmau nipatitaṃ gṛhṇīma iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Kroḍamallakas</s> ran forward, saying, "Let us take what has fallen on the ground."

children.text: te pariveṣakair nivāritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They were stopped by the servers.

children.text: tataḥ kroḍamallakaḥ kathayati yadyasya rājñaḥ prabhūtamannam svāpateyamasti santyanye 'pi asmadvidhā duḥkhitakā ākāṅkṣante ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Kroḍamallaka</s> said, "If this king has much food and property of his own, there are also other suffering people like us who long for it.

children.text: kimarthaṃ na dīyate kimanenāparibhogaṃ choritena iti ||
children.translated_text: Why is it not given? What is the use of this being thrown away without being used?"

children.text: tasya kroḍamallakasya cittavikṣepo jātaḥ na śakyaṃ tena tathā cittaṃ prasādayitum yathāpūrvam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Kroḍamallaka</s>'s mind became distracted, and he could no longer make his mind faithful as before.

children.text: tato rājā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā na mama nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatīti viditvā dakṣiṇāmaśrutvaiva praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, after feeding the community of monks headed by the Buddha, realized, "He has not assigned the dedication in my name," and went inside without even hearing the dedication.

children.text: tato bhagavatā rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya nāmnā dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One assigned the dedication in the name of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s>.

children.text: hastyaśvarathapattiyāyino bhuñjānasya puraṃ sanairgamaṃ paśyasi phalaṃ hi rūkṣikāyā alavaṇikāyāḥ kulmāṣapiṇḍakāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You see the city, with elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry moving about, of one who enjoys it; for it is the fruit of a rough, unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s> (lump of coarse pulse).

children.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat bahuśo bahuśo bhadanta bhagavatā rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya niveśane bhuktvā nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Many, many times, revered sir, the Blessed One has eaten in the residence of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s> and assigned the dedication in his name.

children.text: nābhijānāmi kadācidevaṃrūpāṃ dakṣiṇāmādiṣṭapūrvām ||
children.translated_text: I do not recall that a dedication of such a kind has ever been assigned before."

children.text: bhagavānāha icchasi tvamānanda rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasyālavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍakām ārabhya karmaplotiṃ śrotum etasya bhagavan kālaḥ etasya sugata samayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to hear the <s>karmaploti</s> (thread of karma) concerning King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s> and the unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s>?" "This is the time, Blessed One; this is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasyālavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍakāmārabhya karmaplotiṃ varṇayet bhagavataḥ śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed One describe the <s>karmaploti</s> concerning King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s> and the unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s>. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will remember it."

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the monks.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karpaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: "In the past, monks, a householder was living in a certain <s>Karpaṭaka</s>.

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam ||
children.translated_text: He brought a wife from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati ||
children.translated_text: Together with her he played, delighted himself, and enjoyed himself.

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While he was playing, delighting himself, and enjoying himself, a son was born to him.

children.text: sa unnīto vardhitaḥ paṭuḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The boy was raised and brought up, and became capable.

children.text: yāvadasau gṛhapatiḥ patnīmāmantrayate bhadre jāto 'smākamṛṇahārako dhanahārakaśca ||
children.translated_text: At length that householder addressed his wife: "Good woman, one who will carry our debts and our wealth has been born to us.

children.text: gacchāmi paṇyamādāya deśāntaramiti ||
children.translated_text: I shall go to another country with merchandise."

children.text: sā kathayati āryaputra etat kuruṣva iti ||
children.translated_text: She said, "Noble son, do that."

children.text: sa paṇyamādāya deśāntaraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking merchandise, he went to another country.

children.text: tatraivānayena vyasanamāpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, through misfortune, he fell into calamity.

children.text: alpaparicchado 'sau gṛhapatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That householder had little property.

children.text: tasya gṛhapaterdhanajātaṃ parikṣīṇam ||
children.translated_text: The wealth that the householder had possessed was exhausted.

children.text: so 'sya putro duḥkhito jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His son became distressed.

children.text: tasya gṛhapatervayasyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder had a friend.

children.text: tena tasya dārakasya mātā abhihitā ayaṃ tava putraḥ kṣetraṃ rakṣatu ahamasya sukhaṃ bhuktena yogodvahanaṃ kariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: He said to the boy's mother, "Let this son of yours guard the field. I will provide for his maintenance with good food."

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: "Let it be so."

children.text: sa tasya kṣetraṃ rakṣitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to guard that man's field.

children.text: sa tasya sukhaṃ bhaktakena yogodvahanaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man began to provide for his maintenance with pleasant food.

children.text: yāvadapareṇa samayena parvaṇī pratyupasthitā ||
children.translated_text: Then, on another occasion, a festival day arrived.

children.text: tasya dārakasya mātā saṃlakṣayati adya gṛhapatipatnī suhṛtsambandhibāndhavaiḥ saha śramaṇabrāhmaṇabhojanena vyagrā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The boy's mother thought, "Today the householder's wife will be occupied with feeding ascetics and brahmins together with friends, connections, and kinsmen.

children.text: gacchāmi sānukālaṃ tasya dārakasya bhaktaṃ nayāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: I will go at the proper time and bring the boy's food."

children.text: sā sānukālaṃ gatvā gṛhapatipatnyā etamarthaṃ niveśayati ||
children.translated_text: She went at the proper time and set out this matter before the householder's wife.

children.text: sā ruṣitā kathayati na tāvacchramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo dadāmi jñātīnāṃ vā tāvat preṣyamanuṣyāya dadāmi adya tāvat tiṣṭhatu śvo dviguṇaṃ dāsyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: She, angered, said, "I have not yet given to ascetics and brahmins, nor to my relatives; should I give now to a hired servant? Let it stand today. Tomorrow I will give double."

children.text: tatastasya dārakasya mātā saṃlakṣayati mā me putro bubhukṣitakaḥ sthāsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then the boy's mother thought, "May my son not remain hungry."

children.text: tayā ātmano 'rthe 'lavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍakā sampāditā ||
children.translated_text: For herself she had prepared an unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s>.

children.text: sā tāmādāya gatā ||
children.translated_text: Taking it, she went.

children.text: tena dārakeṇa dūrata eva dṛṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: The boy saw her from far off.

children.text: sa kathayati amba asti kiṃcinmṛṣṭaṃ mṛṣṭam sā kathayati putra yadeva prātidaivasikaṃ tadapyadya nāsti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Mother, is there anything especially tasty?" She said, "Son, today there is not even what there is every day.

children.text: mayā ātmano 'rthe 'lavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍikā sādhitā ||
children.translated_text: For myself I cooked an unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s>.

children.text: tāmahaṃ gṛhītvā āgatā ||
children.translated_text: I have brought that with me.

children.text: etāṃ paribhuṅkṣveti ||
children.translated_text: Eat this."

children.text: sa kathayati sthāpayitvā gacchasveti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Set it down and go."

children.text: sā sthāpayitvā prakrāntā ||
children.translated_text: She set it down and departed.

children.text: asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya ||
children.translated_text: When Buddhas do not arise, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas) arise in the world, compassionate toward the lowly and poor, devoted to remote beds, seats, and food, the world's unique recipients of gifts.

children.text: yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddhastatpradeśamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain <s>pratyekabuddha</s> arrived in that region.

children.text: sa tena dṛṣṭaḥ kāyaprāsādikaścittaprāsādikaśca śānteryāpathavartī ||
children.translated_text: The boy saw him: pleasing in body, pleasing to the mind, and moving in a peaceful mode of conduct.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati nūnaṃ mayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūte dakṣiṇīye kārā na kṛtā yena me īdṛśī samavasthā ||
children.translated_text: He thought, "Surely I have not rendered service to such a true recipient of gifts; because of that, this is the condition I have come to.

children.text: yadyayaṃ mamāntikād alavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍikāṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ahamasmai dadyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: If he would accept this unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s> from me, I would give it to him."

children.text: tato 'sau pratyekabuddhastasya daridrapuruṣasya cetasā cittamājñāya pātraṃ prasāritavān bhadramukha sacette parityaktam dīyatāmasmin pātra iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, knowing with his mind the thought in the mind of that poor man, stretched out his bowl: "Good sir, if your mind has relinquished it, place it in this bowl."

children.text: tatastena tīvreṇa prasādena sā alavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍakā tasmai pratyekabuddhāya pratipāditā ||
children.translated_text: Then, with intense faith, he presented that unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s> to the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau daridrapuruṣaḥ eṣa evāsau rājā prasenajit kauśalastena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: "What do you think, monks? The poor man who was there at that time and on that occasion is this very King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s>."

children.text: yadanena pratyekabuddhāyālavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍakā pratipāditā tena karmaṇā ṣaṭkṛtvo deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān ṣaṭkṛtvo 'syāmeva śrāvastyāṃ rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ tenaiva ca karmaṇā avaśeṣeṇa etarhi rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because by him a coarse, unsalted lump of <s>kulmāṣa</s> was presented to a pratyekabuddha, by that karma he exercised royal authority and sovereignty six times among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, and six times in this very <s>Śrāvastī</s> he was a crowned kṣatriya king. And by the remainder of that same karma he has now become a crowned kṣatriya king.

children.text: so 'sya tamahaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi ||
children.translated_text: It is with reference to him that I say this.

children.text: hastyaśvarathapattiyāyino bhuñjānasya puraṃ sanairgamanam ||
children.translated_text: Going with elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, enjoying the city with slow progress,

children.text: paśyasi phalaṃ hi rūkṣikāyā alavaṇikāyā kulmāṣapiṇḍakāyāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: you see indeed the fruit of that coarse, unsalted lump of <s>kulmāṣa</s>.

children.text: sāmantakena śabdo visṛtaḥ bhagavatā rājñaḥ prasenajito 'lavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍakāmārabhya karmaplotirvyākṛtā iti ||
children.translated_text: A report spread through the neighboring region: "The Blessed One has explained the karmic course of King <s>Prasenajit</s> with regard to the unsalted lump of <s>kulmāṣa</s>."

children.text: rājñāpi prasenajitā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> also heard it.

children.text: sa yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: To King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, seated to one side, the Blessed One showed, instructed, encouraged, and delighted him with a Dharma discourse.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: After showing, instructing, encouraging, and delighting him in many ways with a Dharma discourse, he became silent.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā bhagavantamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃstraimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgheneti ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One consent to a three-month rains residence from me, together with the community, with robes, alms-food, beds, seats, and medicinal requisites for illness."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> by remaining silent.

children.text: tato rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena buddhamukhāya bhikṣusaṃghāya traimāsyaṃ śatarasaṃ bhojanaṃ dattam ||
children.translated_text: Then by King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> food of a hundred flavors was given for three months to the community of monks headed by the Buddha.

children.text: ekaikaśca bhikṣuḥ śatasahasreṇa vastreṇācchāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And each monk was clothed with a garment worth a hundred thousand.

children.text: tailasya ca kumbhakoṭiṃ samudānīya dīpamālā abhyudyato dātum ||
children.translated_text: Having gathered a koti of jars of oil, he was preparing to give rows of lamps.

children.text: tatra bhakte pūjāyāṃ ca mahān kolāhalo jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, over the meal and the worship, a great commotion arose.

children.text: yāvadanyatamā nagarāvalambikā atīva duḥkhitā ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile a certain woman dependent on the city was extremely poor.

children.text: tayā kroḍamallakena bhikṣāmaṭantyā uccaśabdaḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As she was wandering for alms with a small bowl, she heard the loud noise.

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ pṛcchati bhavantaḥ kimeṣa uccaśabdo mahāśabda iti ||
children.translated_text: After hearing it, she asked, "Gentlemen, what is this loud noise, this great sound?"

children.text: aparaiḥ samākhyātam rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghastraimāsyaṃ bhojitaḥ ekaikaśca bhikṣuḥ śatasahasreṇa vastreṇa ācchāditaḥ tailasya kumbhakoṭiṃ ca samudānīya dīpamālā abhyudyato dātumiti ||
children.translated_text: Others explained: "King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> has fed the community of monks headed by the Buddha for three months; each monk has been clothed with a garment worth a hundred thousand; and, having gathered a koti of jars of oil, he is preparing to give rows of lamps."

children.text: tatastasyā nagarāvalambikāyā etadabhavat ayaṃ tāvadrājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ puṇyairatṛpto 'dyāpi dānāni dadāti puṇyāni karoti ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to that woman dependent on the city: "This King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, though still unsatisfied with merit, gives gifts even today and makes merit.

children.text: yannvahamapi kutaścit samudānīya bhagavataḥ pradīpaṃ dadyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I too should obtain something from somewhere and give a lamp to the Blessed One?"

children.text: tayā khaṇḍamallake tailasya stokam yācayitvā pradīpaṃ prajvālya bhagavataścaṅkrame dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She begged a little oil in a broken bowl, lit a lamp, and placed it on the Blessed One's walking path.

children.text: pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yathāyaṃ bhagavāñ śākyamunirvarṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma śāstā loka utpannaḥ evamahamapi varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunireva śāstā bhaveyam ||
children.translated_text: Falling at his feet, she made this vow: "By this root of wholesome action, just as this Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, has arisen in the world as a teacher named <s>Śākyamuni</s> among people whose lifespan is a hundred years, so may I too become a teacher, precisely <s>Śākyamuni</s>, among people whose lifespan is a hundred years.

children.text: yathā cāsya śāriputramaudgalyāyanāgrayugaṃ bhadrayugamānando bhikṣurupasthāyakaḥ śuddhodanaḥ pitā mātā mahāmāyā rāhulabhadraḥ kumāraḥ putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And just as his foremost pair is <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, an excellent pair, just as the monk <s>Ānanda</s> is his attendant, <s>Śuddhodana</s> his father, <s>Mahāmāyā</s> his mother, and Prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> his son,

children.text: yathāyaṃ bhagavān dhātuvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā parinirvāsyati evamahamapi dhātuvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā parinirvāpayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: and just as this Blessed One will pass into final nirvāṇa after arranging the division of relics, so may I too pass into final nirvāṇa after arranging the division of relics."

children.text: yāvat sarve te dīpā nairvāṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then all those lamps were extinguished.

children.text: sa tayā prajvalitaḥ pradīpaḥ prajvalatyeva ||
children.translated_text: But the lamp lit by her continued to burn.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatām na tāvadupasthāyakāḥ pratisaṃlīyante na yāvadbuddhā bhagavantaḥ pratisaṃlīnā iti ||
children.translated_text: For this is the nature of the blessed Buddhas: their attendants do not retire until the blessed Buddhas have retired.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ saṃlakṣayati asthānamanavakāśo yadbuddhā bhagavanta āloke śayyāṃ kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> considered: "It is impossible; there is no occasion for blessed Buddhas to prepare a bed while there is light.

children.text: yannvahaṃ dīpam nirvāpayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to extinguish the lamp?"

children.text: sa hastena nirvāpayitumārabdho na śaknoti ||
children.translated_text: He began to extinguish it with his hand, but he could not.

children.text: tataścīvarakarṇikena tato vyajanena tathāpi na śaknoti nirvāpayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then he tried with the corner of his robe, and then with a fan, but still he could not extinguish it.

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate kimetadānandeti ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "What is this, <s>Ānanda</s>?"

children.text: sa kathayati bhagavan mama buddhirutpannā asthānamanavakāśo yadbuddhā bhagavanta āloke śayyāṃ kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Blessed One, this thought arose in me: 'It is impossible; there is no occasion for blessed Buddhas to prepare a bed while there is light.

children.text: yannvahaṃ dīpaṃ nirvāpayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to extinguish the lamp?'

children.text: so 'haṃ hastena nirvāpayitumārabdho na śaknomi tataścīvarakarṇikena tato vyajanena tathāpi na śaknomīti ||
children.translated_text: So I began to extinguish it with my hand, but I cannot; then with the corner of my robe, and then with a fan, but still I cannot."

children.text: bhagavānāha khedamānanda āpatsyase ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "You will only weary yourself, <s>Ānanda</s>.

children.text: yadi vairambhakā api vāyavo vāyeyuḥ te 'pi na śaknuyur nirvāpayituṃ prāgeva hastagataścīvarakarṇiko vyajanaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Even if the <s>Vairambhaka</s> winds were to blow, they could not extinguish it, much less a corner of a robe held in the hand or a fan."

children.text: tathā hi ayaṃ pradīpastayā dārikayā mahatā cittābhisaṃskāreṇa prajvalitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For indeed, this lamp was kindled by that girl with a great formation of resolve in her mind.

children.text: api tu ānanda bhaviṣyatyasau dārikā varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But, <s>Ananda</s>, in a future generation with a lifespan of one hundred years, that girl will become a <s>tathagata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, named <s>Sakyamuni</s>.

children.text: śāriputramaudgalyāyanau tasyāgrayugaṃ bhadrayugam ānando bhikṣurupāsakaḥ śuddhodanaḥ pitā mahāmāyā mātā kapilavastu nagaram rāhulabhadraḥ kumāraḥ putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sariputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyayana</s> will be his foremost pair, his auspicious pair; the monk <s>Ananda</s> will be his attendant, <s>Suddhodana</s> his father, <s>Mahamaya</s> his mother, the city <s>Kapilavastu</s> his city, and the prince <s>Rahulabhadra</s> his son.

children.text: sāpi dhātuvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā parinirvāsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: And she too, after making a division of relics, will pass completely into nirvana.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 8

buddho bhavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrairdhanibhiḥ paurairbrāhmaṇairgṛhapatibhiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairdevair nāgairyakṣairasurairgaruḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragairiti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavāṃllābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at <s>Sravasti</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anathapindada</s>'s park, honored, held in reverence, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, Brahmins, householders, guild-masters, caravan leaders, gods, nagas, yakshas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; thus the Buddha, the Blessed One, venerated by gods, nagas, yakshas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, together with his community of disciples, was a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for the sick.

children.text: tatra khalu varṣāvāsaṃ bhagavānupagato jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: There, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anathapindada</s>'s park, the Blessed One had entered upon the rains residence.

children.text: atha tadaiva pravāraṇāyāṃ pratyupasthitāyāṃ saṃbahulāḥ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that very invitation ceremony had arrived, several merchants living in <s>Sravasti</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇān saṃbahulāñśrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One showed, instructed, encouraged, and delighted the several merchants living in <s>Sravasti</s>, who were seated to one side, with a Dharma discourse.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: After showing, instructing, encouraging, and delighting them in many ways with a Dharma discourse, he became silent.

children.text: atha saṃbahulāḥ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ yenāyuṣmānānandastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the several merchants living in <s>Sravasti</s>, having rejoiced in and approved the Blessed One's speech, bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet, departed from the Blessed One's presence, and approached the venerable <s>Ananda</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramyāyuṣmata ānandasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the venerable <s>Ananda</s>'s feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: saṃbahulāñ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇija āyuṣmānānando dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ananda</s> showed, instructed, encouraged, and delighted the several merchants living in <s>Sravasti</s> with a Dharma discourse.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: After showing, instructing, encouraging, and delighting them in many ways with a Dharma discourse, he became silent.

children.text: atha te vaṇija utthāyāsanebhya ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yenāyuṣmānānandastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya āyuṣmantamānandamidamavocan kiṃcitte āryānanda śrutaṃ varṣoṣito bhagavān katameṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyatīti yadvayaṃ tadyātrikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīmahe dharmatā caiṣā ṣaṇmahānagaranivāsino vaṇijo yasyāṃ diśi buddhā bhagavanto gantukāmā bhavanti tadyātrikabhāṇḍaṃ samudānayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward the venerable <s>Ananda</s>, and said this to the venerable <s>Ananda</s>: "Have you heard anything, noble <s>Ananda</s>? Since the Blessed One has spent the rains, in which countries will he undertake his tour, so that we may gather the merchandise needed for that journey? For this is the regular practice: the merchants living in the six great cities gather journey-merchandise in whatever direction the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, wish to go."

children.text: sa kathayati buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ kiṃ na pṛcchatha durāsadā hi buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Why do you not ask the Buddha, the Blessed One? For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are hard to approach and difficult to prevail upon."

children.text: na śaknumo vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ praṣṭum ||
children.translated_text: "We are not able to ask the Blessed One."

children.text: mamāpi bhavanto durāsadā hi buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "For me too, sirs, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are hard to approach and difficult to prevail upon.

children.text: ahamapi na śaknomi bhagavantaṃ praṣṭum ||
children.translated_text: I too am not able to ask the Blessed One."

children.text: yadi bhadantānandasyāpi durāsadā buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ kathaṃ bhadantānando jānīte 'mukāṃ diśaṃ bhagavān gamiṣyatīti nimittena vā bhavantaḥ parikathayā vā ||
children.translated_text: "If the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are hard to approach and difficult to prevail upon even for venerable <s>Ananda</s>, how does venerable <s>Ananda</s> know, 'The Blessed One will go in such-and-such a direction'? Is it by a sign, sirs, or by incidental talk?"

children.text: kathaṃ nimittena yāṃ diśaṃ bhagavān gantukāmastato 'bhimukho niṣīdati evaṃ nimittena ||
children.translated_text: "How by a sign? In whatever direction the Blessed One wishes to go, he sits facing that way. Thus it is by a sign.

children.text: kathaṃ parikathayā teṣāṃ janapadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate evaṃ parikathayā ||
children.translated_text: How by incidental talk? He speaks in praise of those countries. Thus it is by incidental talk."

children.text: kutomukho bhadantānanda bhagavān niṣīdati katameṣāṃ ca janapadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate magadhābhimukho bhavanto bhagavān niṣīdati māgadhakānāṃ janapadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: "Facing which way, venerable <s>Ananda</s>, does the Blessed One sit, and of which countries does he speak in praise?" "Sirs, the Blessed One sits facing <s>Magadha</s>, and he speaks in praise of the countries of <s>Magadha</s>."

children.text: api tu bhavanto 'ṣṭādaśānuśaṃsā buddhacārikāyām ||
children.translated_text: "Moreover, sirs, there are eighteen advantages in a Buddha's tour.

children.text: katame 'ṣṭādaśa nāgnibhayaṃ nodakabhayaṃ na siṃhabhayaṃ na vyāghrabhayaṃ na dvīpitarakṣuparacakrabhayaṃ na caurabhayaṃ na gulmatarapaṇyātiyātrābhayaṃ na manuṣyāmanuṣyabhayam ||
children.translated_text: What are the eighteen? There is no danger from fire, no danger from water, no danger from lions, no danger from tigers, no danger from leopards, hyenas, or enemy armies, no danger from thieves, no danger connected with patrols, crossings, merchandise, or excessive tolls on the journey, and no danger from humans or nonhumans.

children.text: kālena ca kālaṃ divyāni rūpāṇi dṛśyante divyāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante udārāś cāvabhāsāḥ prajñāyante ātmavyākaraṇāni ca śrūyante dharmasambhoga āmiṣasambhogo 'lpābādhā ca buddhacārikā ||
children.translated_text: And from time to time divine forms are seen, divine sounds are heard, lofty radiances appear, personal predictions are heard, there is enjoyment of the Dharma, there is enjoyment of material gifts, there is little illness, and there is a Buddha's tour."

children.text: atha saṃbahulāḥ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijaḥ āyuṣmataḥ ānandasya bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya āyuṣmata ānandasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the several merchants living in <s>Sravasti</s>, having rejoiced in and approved the venerable <s>Ananda</s>'s speech, bowed with their heads at the venerable <s>Ananda</s>'s feet, rose from their seats, and departed.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhā bhagavanto jīvanto dhriyanto yāpayanto mahākaruṇayā saṃcodyamānāḥ parānugrahapravṛttāḥ kālena kālamaraṇyacārikāṃ caranti nadīcārikāṃ parvatacārikāṃ śmaśānacārikāṃ janapadacārikāṃ caranti ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is the nature of things that the blessed Buddhas, while living, remaining, and sustaining life, impelled by great compassion and engaged in benefiting others, from time to time wander through forests, along rivers, over mountains, among charnel grounds, and through countries.

children.text: asmiṃstvarthe buddho bhagavān magadheṣu janapadacārikāṃ cartukāmastadeva pravāraṇāṃ pravārayitvā āyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma gaccha ānanda bhikṣūṇāmārocaya itaḥ saptame divase tathāgato magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: In this matter, the Buddha, the Blessed One, wishing to travel through the countries of <s>Magadha</s>, made the pravāraṇā ceremony that very day and addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, inform the monks: 'On the seventh day from now the <s>Tathāgata</s> will travel through the countries of <s>Magadha</s>.'"

children.text: yo yuṣmākam utsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ janapadacārikāṃ cartum sa cīvarakarma karotu ||
children.translated_text: "Whoever among you is able to travel through the country together with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him attend to his robe-work."

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati bhagavānāyuṣmanta itaḥ saptame divase magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One, and he informed the monks: "Venerable ones, on the seventh day from now the Blessed One will travel through the countries of <s>Magadha</s>."

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate bhagavatā sārdhaṃ magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cartum sa cīvarakarma karotu ||
children.translated_text: "Whoever among you is able to travel through the countries of <s>Magadha</s> together with the Blessed One, let him attend to his robe-work."

children.text: atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ saṃbahulaiśca śrāvastīnivāsibhirvaṇigbrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ sārdhaṃ magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surrounded by a group of monks, preceded by the community of monks, and accompanied by many merchants, brahmins, and householders living in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, set out to travel through the countries of <s>Magadha</s>.

children.text: atha saṃbahulāśca śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then many merchants living in <s>Śrāvastī</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantamidamavocan adhivāsayatvasmākaṃ bhagavān yāvacca śrāvastī yāvacca rājagṛham atrāntarā cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One consent to accept from us, as far as from <s>Śrāvastī</s> to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, and in the region between them, robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicines and requisites for the sick, together with the community of monks."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavān saṃbahulānāṃ śrāvastīnivāsināṃ vaṇijāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to those many merchants living in <s>Śrāvastī</s> by remaining silent.

children.text: atha saṃbahulāḥ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those many merchants living in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, understanding the Blessed One's consent from his silence, departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: atha samprasthite buddhe bhagavati antarā ca śrāvastīmantarā ca rājagṛham atrāntarānmahāṭavyāṃ caurasahasraṃ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the Buddha, the Blessed One, had set out, in the region between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in a great forest there lived a thousand bandits.

children.text: adrākṣīttaccaurasahasraṃ bhagavantaṃ sārthaparivṛtaṃ bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: That thousand bandits saw the Blessed One surrounded by the caravan and preceded by the community of monks.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ parasparaṃ kathayanti gacchatu bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, they said to one another, "Let the Blessed One go with the community of his disciples.

children.text: śeṣaṃ sārthaṃ muṣiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We will plunder the rest of the caravan."

children.text: ityanuvicintya sarve javena prasṛtā yena sārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having considered this, they all rushed swiftly toward the caravan.

children.text: bhagavatā abhihitāḥ kimetadbhavantaḥ samārabdham caurāḥ kathayanti vayaṃ smo bhadanta caurā aṭavīcarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said to them, "Good sirs, what is this you have begun?" The bandits said, "Venerable sir, we are bandits, forest-rovers.

children.text: nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vāṇijyā na gaurakṣyam ||
children.translated_text: We have no farming, nor trade, nor cattle-keeping.

children.text: anenopakrameṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this means we make our livelihood.

children.text: gacchatu bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed One go with the community of his disciples.

children.text: śeṣaṃ sārthaṃ muṣiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We will plunder the rest of the caravan."

children.text: bhagavānāha mamaiṣa sārthaḥ saṃniśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "This caravan has taken refuge in me.

children.text: api tu sakalasya sārthasya parigaṇayya suvarṇaṃ gṛhṇīdhvam ||
children.translated_text: But count up the gold value of the whole caravan and take it."

children.text: tathā bhavatviti caurasahasreṇa pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: "So be it," the thousand bandits agreed.

children.text: asmin sārthe ye upāsakā vaṇijastaiḥ kṛtsnasya sārthasya mūlyaṃ gaṇayya caurāṇāṃ niveditam iyanti śatāni sahasrāṇi ceti ||
children.translated_text: Then the lay-devotee merchants in that caravan calculated the value of the whole caravan and reported it to the bandits, saying, "So many hundreds and thousands."

children.text: tatasteṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ sārthaniṣkrayārthaṃ bhagavatā nidhānaṃ darśitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, for the ransom of the caravan, the Blessed One showed the bandits a treasure-store.

children.text: tatastena caurasahasreṇa sārthamūlyapramāṇaṃ suvarṇaṃ gṛhītam avaśiṣṭaṃ tatraivāntarhitam ||
children.translated_text: Then that thousand bandits took gold equal to the value of the caravan, and the remainder vanished right there.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavatā sārthaścaurasahasrāt pratimokṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way the caravan was released by the Blessed One from the thousand bandits.

children.text: anupūrveṇa bhagavān rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due order the Blessed One arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text: punarapi bhagavān sārthaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto rājagṛhāt śrāvastīṃ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again the Blessed One, surrounded by the caravan and preceded by the community of monks, set out from <s>Rājagṛha</s> for <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: tathaiva caurasahasrasakāśāt sārtho niṣkrītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way the caravan was ransomed from the thousand bandits.

children.text: evaṃ dvitricatuṣpañcaṣaḍvārāṃśca caurasahasrasakāśād āgamanagamanena sārthaḥ paritrāto mūlyaṃ cānupradattam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, on a second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth occasion, as he went and returned, the caravan was protected from the thousand bandits and the price was paid over.

children.text: saptamaṃ tu vāraṃ bhagavān sārtharahito bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ śrāvastyā rājagṛhaṃ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But on the seventh occasion the Blessed One, without a caravan and preceded by the community of monks, set out from <s>Śrāvastī</s> for <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text: adrākṣīccaurasahasraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sārthavirahitaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The thousand bandits saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, without a caravan and surrounded by the community of monks.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ parasparaṃ saṃlapanti bhagavān gacchatu bhikṣusaṃghaṃ muṣiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, they spoke with one another: "Let the Blessed One go; we will plunder the community of monks.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ eṣo hi bhagavān suvarṇapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? For this Blessed One is a giver of gold."

children.text: ityuktvā sarvajavena pradhāvitā bhikṣūn muṣitumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, they ran with all speed and began to plunder the monks.

children.text: bhagavatā cābhihitāḥ vatsāḥ mama ete śrāvakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said to them, "Children, these are my disciples."

children.text: caurāḥ kathayanti jānāsyeva bhagavan vayaṃ caurā aṭavīcarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The bandits said, "You know, Blessed One, that we are bandits, forest-rovers.

children.text: nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vaṇijyā na gaurakṣyam ||
children.translated_text: We have no farming, nor trade, nor cattle-keeping.

children.text: anena vayaṃ jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this means we make our livelihood."

children.text: tato bhagavatā caurāṇāṃ mahānidhānaṃ darśitam evaṃ coktāḥ vatsāḥ yāvadāptaṃ dhanaṃ gṛhṇītheti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One showed the bandits a great treasure-store and said this: "Children, take as much wealth as is enough for you."

children.text: tatastena caurasahasreṇa tasmānmahānidhānādyāvadāptaṃ suvarṇamādattam avaśiṣṭaṃ tatraivāntarhitam ||
children.translated_text: Then that thousand of thieves took from that great treasure as much gold as they could obtain, while the remainder disappeared right there.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstaccaurasahasram yāvadāptaṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā tato 'nupūrveṇa rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, after satisfying that thousand of thieves with as much wealth as they had obtained, gradually arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s> from there.

children.text: tatasteṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ buddhirutpannā yā kācidasmākaṃ śrīsaubhāgyasampat sarvāsau buddhaṃ bhagavantamāgamya ||
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in those thieves: "Whatever prosperity, good fortune, and wealth we have, all of it has come because of the Buddha, the Blessed One.

children.text: yannu vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghamasmin pradeśe bhojayema iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we should feed the Blessed One, together with the community of his disciples, in this region."

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcidbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānām ekarakṣāṇām ekavīrāṇām advayavādināṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ trividhadamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ caturvaiśāradyaviśāradānām udārārṣabhasamyaksiṃhanādanādināṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcaskandhavimocakānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍāyatanabhedakānāṃ saṃghātavihāriṇāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇayaśasāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānāṃ saptasamādhipariṣkāradāyakānām āryāṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānām āryamārgapudgalanāyakānāṃ navānupūrvasamāpattikuśalānāṃ navasaṃyojanavisaṃyojanakānāṃ daśadikparipūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānām
children.translated_text: Meanwhile there is nothing at all that the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, do not know: they are greatly compassionate, the sole protectors, the sole heroes, teachers of non-duality, abiding in calm and insight, skilled in the three matters of discipline, firmly established on the soles of their feet in the four bases of supernatural power, crossed beyond the four floods, long familiar through the long night with the four means of gathering disciples, mighty with the ten powers, confident in the four fearlessnesses, uttering the lofty, noble, proper lion's roar, free from the five factors, liberators from the five aggregates, gone beyond the five destinies, breakers of the six sense-bases, dwelling in collectedness, renowned for the perfection of the six perfections, rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, givers of the adornments of the seven concentrations, guides to the noble eightfold path, leaders of persons on the noble path, skilled in the nine successive attainments, separators from the nine fetters, famous throughout the ten directions, distinguished above the ten hundred beings who exercise mastery.

children.text: trī rātrestrirdivasasya ṣaṭkṛtvo rātriṃdivasena buddhacakṣuṣā lokam vyavalokayanti kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayāmi kasyāvaropitāni vivardhayāmi kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ kaṃ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhāt parimocayāmi ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kamahamapāyād vyutthāpya svarge mokṣaphale ca pratiṣṭhāpayāmi kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanuprayacchāmi kasya buddhotpādavibhūṣitaṃ lokaṃ saphalīkaromi kamāryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam ko hīyate ko vardhate ||
children.translated_text: Three times by night and three times by day, six times in the course of day and night, they survey the world with the Buddha-eye: "Whose unplanted roots of merit shall I plant? Whose planted ones shall I increase? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into confinement? Who has fallen into hardship, danger, and confinement? Whom shall I free from hardship, danger, and confinement? Who is sinking toward the bad destinies, inclined to the bad destinies, sloping down to the bad destinies? Whom shall I raise up from a bad destiny and establish in heaven and in the fruit of liberation? To whom, sunk in the mud of sensual desire, shall I give a hand to lift him up? For whom shall I make the world, adorned by the arising of a Buddha, fruitful? Whom, bereft of noble wealth, shall I establish in the lordship and sovereignty of noble wealth? Who is declining? Who is increasing?"

children.text: apyevātikramedvelāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of makaras, might perhaps overstep its shore at the proper tide,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velāmatikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha does not overstep the proper time for the calves who are to be trained.

children.text: yathā hi mātā priyamekaputrakaṃ hyavekṣate rakṣati cāsya jīvitam
children.translated_text: For just as a mother watches over her dear only son and protects his life,

children.text: tathaiva vaineyajanaṃ tathāgato hyavekṣate rakṣati cāsya saṃtatim ||
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Tathāgata</s> watches over the people to be trained and protects their continuity.

children.text: sarvajñasaṃtānanivāsinī hi kāruṇyadhenurmṛgayatyakhinnā
children.translated_text: For the cow of compassion, dwelling in the lineage of the omniscient one, searches tirelessly

children.text: vaineyavatsān bhavaduḥkhanaṣṭān vatsān praṇaṣṭāniva vatsalā gauḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the calves to be trained, lost in the suffering of existence, like a loving cow for calves that have strayed.

children.text: tato bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ vaineyakālamapekṣya rājagṛhādanupūrveṇa bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣugaṇapuraskṛto dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāraścandanaścandanaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāraḥ pūrvavat yāvanmahākaruṇayā samanvāgatas tāṃ sālāṭavīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, observing the proper time for training those thieves, went gradually from <s>Rājagṛha</s>, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by a group of monks: tamed, with a tamed retinue; peaceful, with a peaceful retinue; cooled like sandalwood, with a sandalwood-like retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; comforted, with a comforted retinue; as before, down to being endowed with great compassion, he reached that <s>Sālāṭavī</s> forest.

children.text: adrākṣīttaccaurasahasraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ dūrādevāgacchantam ||
children.translated_text: That thousand of thieves saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, together with the community of disciples, coming from afar.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaścittānyabhiprasādya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after seeing him, they made their minds deeply serene and went to where the Blessed One was.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantamidamavocan adhivāsayatu asmākaṃ bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they fell at the Blessed One's feet and said this to him: "May the Blessed One consent to take tomorrow's meal inside our dwelling, together with the community of monks."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavāṃstasya caurasahasrasya tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to that thousand of thieves by remaining silent.

children.text: atha caurasahasraṃ bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato'ntikāt prakrāntam ||
children.translated_text: Then the thousand of thieves, knowing from the Blessed One's silence that he had consented, departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: atha taccaurasahasraṃ tāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyase ||
children.translated_text: Then that thousand of thieves, during that very night, prepared pure, excellent hard and soft foods; rising early in the morning, they arranged seats, set out water-jars, and announced the time to the Blessed One by a messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. Let the Blessed One now consider the proper time."

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena tasya caurasahasrasya bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the meal-offering of that thousand of thieves.

children.text: atha taccaurasahasraṃ buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṃghasya candanodakena pādau prakṣālayāmāsa ||
children.translated_text: Then that thousand of thieves washed the feet of the community of monks headed by the Buddha with sandalwood water.

children.text: atha bhagavān prakṣālitapāṇipādaḥ purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, his hands and feet washed, sat down on the prepared seat before the community of monks.

children.text: niṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcatarāṇyāsanāni gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was seated, they satisfied and served them with their own hands with pure and excellent foods, both hard and soft. When they knew that the Blessed One had eaten, that his hands had been washed and his bowl removed, they took lower seats and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavatā teṣāmāśayānuśayaṃ viditvā dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā tena caurasahasreṇa tasminnevāsane niṣaṇṇena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing their dispositions and latent tendencies and understanding their element and nature, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, when that thousand of thieves heard it while seated on that very seat, they split apart with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of personality-view rising with twenty peaks, and realized the fruit of <s>srotāpatti</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭasatyāśca kathayanti idamasmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ na rājñā na devatābhir na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair neṣṭair na svajanabandhuvargeṇa yadasmābhirbhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitramāgamya ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the truths, they said, "Venerable sir, this was not done for us by mother or father, by a king, by deities, by departed ancestors, by śramaṇas and brahmins, by cherished ones, or by the circle of our own kinsmen: that, having approached the Blessed One as a good spiritual friend,

children.text: uddhṛto narakatiryakpretebhyaḥ pādaḥ pratiṣṭhāpito devamanuṣyeṣu paryantīkṛtaḥ saṃsāraḥ ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ uttīrṇā aśrusāgarāḥ laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: our foot has been lifted up from the hells, animals, and pretas; it has been set among gods and humans; saṃsāra has been brought to its limit; oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; seas of tears have been crossed; mountains of bones have been overstepped.

children.text: labhema vayaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam ||
children.translated_text: May we obtain, venerable sir, going forth, ordination, and the state of monks in the well-proclaimed <s>dharmavinaya</s>.

children.text: carema vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam ||
children.translated_text: May we practice <s>brahmacarya</s> in the presence of the Blessed One."

children.text: tato bhagavatā brāhmeṇa svareṇābhihitāḥ eta vatsāḥ carata brahmacaryam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed them in the voice of Brahmā: "Come, children; practice <s>brahmacarya</s>."

children.text: vācāvasāne bhagavato muṇḍāḥ saṃvṛttāstraidhātukavītarāgāḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the Blessed One's utterance they became shaven-headed, free from desire for the three realms, regarding clods and gold alike, with minds equal toward the palm of the hand and the sky, like both axe and sandalwood, their eggshell of ignorance split open by knowledge, possessed of knowledge, superknowledges, and analytic insights, and turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor.

children.text: sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyāśca saṃvṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They became worthy to be worshiped, honored, and saluted by the gods together with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ paśya bhadanta bhagavatā idaṃ caurasahasraṃ saptavāraṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā atyantaniṣṭhe 'nuttare yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitam ||
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, cutter off of all doubts: "See, venerable sir: after satisfying this thousand of thieves seven times with wealth, the Blessed One has established them in final certainty, in unsurpassed security from bondage, in <s>nirvāṇa</s>."

children.text: bhagavānāha na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'pyadhvani mayā asyaiva caurasahasrasya sakāśādanekabhāṇḍasahasraḥ sārtho niṣkrītaḥ na ca śakitāḥ saṃtarpayitum ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Not only now, monks. In the past too, by me, a caravan with many thousands of goods was redeemed from the presence of this very thousand of thieves, and yet they could not be satisfied.

children.text: tato mayā anekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairdevamanuṣyaduṣprāpyāṃ śakrabrahmādyairapi duradhigamāṃ badaradvīpayātrāṃ varṣaśatena sādhayitvā etadeva caurasahasramārabhya kṛtsno jāmbudvīpaḥ suvarṇarajatavaiḍūryasphaṭikādyai ratnaviśeṣairmanorathepsitaiścopakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ saṃtarpayitvā daśabhiḥ kuśalaiḥ karmapathaiḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, through many hundreds of thousands of hardships, after accomplishing in a hundred years the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, hard for gods and humans to attain and difficult even for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the others to reach, I satisfied the whole of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, beginning with this very thousand of thieves, with special jewels such as gold, silver, beryl, and crystal, and with special requisites desired in their minds, and I established them in the ten wholesome paths of action.

children.text: tacchṛṇuta bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminneva jambudvīpe vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati sma ṛddhaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskaradurbhikṣarogāpagatam ||
children.translated_text: Listen to this. In the past, monks, in a former time, in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled the kingdom, prosperous, secure, abundant in food, crowded with many people, and free from strife, quarrel, tumult, uproar, thieves, famine, and disease.

children.text: priyamivaikaputrakamiva rājyaṃ kārayati ||
children.translated_text: He ruled the kingdom as if it were a beloved only son.

children.text: tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ priyaseno nāma sārthavāhaḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī ||
children.translated_text: At that time there lived in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> a caravan leader named <s>Priyasena</s>, rich, very wealthy, greatly prosperous, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam ||
children.translated_text: A wife was brought for him from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍate ramate paricārayati ||
children.translated_text: He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself together with her.

children.text: atha anyatama udārapuṇyamaheśākhyaḥ sattvo 'nyatamasmāt praṇītāddevanikāyāccyutvā tasyāḥ prajāpatyāḥ kukṣimavakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain being of lofty merit and great influence, having fallen from a certain excellent class of gods, descended into the womb of his wife.

children.text: pañcāveṇīyā dharmā ihaikatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme ||
children.translated_text: There are five special qualities here among certain women of wise nature.

children.text: katame pañca raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti kālaṃ jānāti ṛtuṃ jānāti garbhamavakrāntaṃ jānāti yasyāḥ sakāśādgarbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti dārakaṃ jānāti dārikāṃ jānāti ||
children.translated_text: What are the five? She knows a man who is impassioned; she knows the time; she knows the season; she knows that an embryo has entered; she knows from whom the embryo has entered; she knows a boy; she knows a girl.

children.text: saceddārako bhavati dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: If it is a boy, he remains leaning on the right side of the womb.

children.text: saceddārikā bhavati vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: If it is a girl, she remains leaning on the left side of the womb.

children.text: sā āttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhasva āpannasattvāsmi saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Joyful, she informs her husband: "By good fortune, noble son, prosper; I have become pregnant.

children.text: yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And since it remains leaning on my right side, it will certainly be a boy."

children.text: so 'pyāttamanā āttamanā udānamudānayati apyevāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam ||
children.translated_text: He too, joyful, joyfully uttered this exclamation: "Perhaps I shall see the face of a son, long desired.

children.text: jāto me syānnāvajātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May one be born to me who is not ill-born.

children.text: kṛtyāni me kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: May he do what needs to be done for me.

children.text: bhṛtaḥ pratibharet ||
children.translated_text: Having been supported by me, may he support me in return.

children.text: dāyādyaṃ pratipadyeta ||
children.translated_text: May he take up the inheritance.

children.text: kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: May my family lineage endure for a long time.

children.text: asmākaṃ cāpyatītakālagatānām uddiśya dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā nāmnā dakṣiṇāmādiśet idaṃ tayor yatra tatropapannayorgacchator anugacchatviti ||
children.translated_text: And when we have gone into the past, after giving gifts and making merit with us in mind, may he assign the offering in our name, saying, 'May this follow those two, wherever they have been reborn and wherever they go.'"

children.text: āpannasattvāṃ caināṃ viditvā upariprāsādatalagatāmayantritāṃ dhārayati uṣṇa uṣṇopakaraṇaiḥ śīte śītopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptairāhārair nātiśītair nātyuṣṇair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhāraiḥ hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīmapsarasamiva nandanavanacāriṇīṃ mañcānmañcaṃ pīṭhātpīṭham avatarantīm adharimāṃ bhūmim ||
children.translated_text: And knowing that she was pregnant, he kept her on an upper story of the palace, unrestricted, with amenities suited to heat and cold, and with foods prescribed by physicians, neither too cold nor too hot, neither too bitter nor too sour nor too salty nor too sweet nor too pungent nor too astringent, foods free from excess of bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent tastes. Her limbs were adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, and, like an apsaras wandering in <s>Nandana</s> Grove, she came down to the lower floor from couch to couch and seat to seat.

children.text: na cāsyāḥ kiṃcidamanojñaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadeva garbhasya paripākāya ||
children.translated_text: And she was not made to hear any unpleasant sound at all, solely for the maturation of the fetus.

children.text: sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā ||
children.translated_text: After eight or nine months had passed, she gave birth.

children.text: dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāso dṛḍhakaṭhinaśarīro mahānagrabalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A boy was born, handsome, beautiful to behold, pleasing, fair, golden in complexion, with an umbrella-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, joined eyebrows, a high nose, a firm and hard body, and great, foremost strength.

children.text: tasya jñātayaḥ saṃgamya samāgamya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatirātriṃdivasāni tasya jātasya jātamahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma ayaṃ dārakaḥ priyasenasya sārthavāhasya putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: His relatives, gathering and assembling, celebrated the birth of the newborn for three weeks, twenty-one days and nights, and then settled his name: "What should the boy's name be? This boy is the son of the caravan leader <s>Priyasena</s>."

children.text: tadbhavatu dārakasya nāma supriya iti ||
children.translated_text: "Therefore let the boy's name be <s>Supriya</s>."

children.text: supriyo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhya upanyasto dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāmaṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām ||
children.translated_text: The boy <s>Supriya</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two milk-nurses, two carrying-nurses, two nurses for cleaning him, and two play-nurses.

children.text: so 'ṣṭābhirdhātrībhirunnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was lifted up and reared by those eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, clarified-butter essence, and other especially nourishing provisions.

children.text: āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam ||
children.translated_text: He grew quickly, like a lotus standing in a lake.

children.text: yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse nikṣepe hastiparīkṣāyāmaśvaparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ dāruparīkṣāyāṃ vastraparīkṣāyāṃ puruṣaparīkṣāyāṃ strīparīkṣāyām nānāpaṇyaparīkṣāsu paryavadātaḥ sarvaśāstrajñaḥ sarvakalābhijñaḥ sarvaśilpajñaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñaḥ sarvagatigatijña udghaṭṭako vācakaḥ paṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ paramatīkṣṇaniśitabuddhiḥ saṃvṛtto 'gnikalpa iva jñānena ||
children.translated_text: When he had become grown, he was put to writing, numeration, calculation, seals, withdrawal, deposit, and placement; he became thoroughly trained in the examination of elephants, horses, jewels, timber, cloth, men, women, and many kinds of merchandise. He became a knower of all śāstras, versed in all arts, skilled in all crafts, knowing the cries of all beings and the courses of all movements, an expounder, a reciter, learned, skillful in action, and of supremely sharp and keen intelligence, like fire in knowledge.

children.text: sa yāni tāni rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhnābhiṣiktānāṃ janapadaiśvaryasthāmavīryam anuprāptānāṃ mahāntaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalamabhinirjityādhyāvasatāṃ pṛthagbhavanti śilpasthānakarmasthānāni tadyathā hastigrīvāyām aśvapṛṣṭhe rathe tsarudhanuḥṣu upayāne niryāṇe 'ṅkuśagrahe tomaragrahe chedye bhedye muṣṭibandhe padabandhe dūravedhe śabdavedhe'kṣuṇṇavedhe marmavedhe dṛḍhaprahāritāyām pañcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became accomplished in the separate crafts and fields of action that belong to kings and anointed kṣatriyas who have attained the power and heroic might of lordship over districts and who, after conquering a great circle of earth, dwell upon it: namely, on the neck of an elephant, on the back of a horse, in a chariot, with sword and bow, in marching out and returning, in taking up the goad, in taking up the lance, in cutting, piercing, binding with the fist, binding with the foot, striking from afar, striking by sound, striking without missing, striking vital points, and striking hard; he became trained in the five stations.

children.text: dharmatā caiṣā na tāvat putrasya nāma nirgacchati yāvat pitā dhriyate ||
children.translated_text: And this is the nature of things: a son's name does not go forth so long as his father is alive.

children.text: athāpareṇa samayena priyasenaḥ sārthavāho glānībhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then at another time the caravan leader <s>Priyasena</s> fell ill.

children.text: sa mūlagaṇḍaputrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyairupasthīyamāno hīyata eva ||
children.translated_text: Though he was attended with medicines made of roots, bulbs, leaves, flowers, and fruits, he only declined.

children.text: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ
children.translated_text: All accumulations have destruction as their end; all elevations have falling as their end;

children.text: saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: all unions have separation as their end, and life has death as its end.

children.text: iti sa kāladharmeṇa saṃyuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus he came under the law of time.

children.text: kālagate priyasene sārthavāhe brahmadattena kāśirājñā supriyo mahāsārthavāhatve 'bhiṣiktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the caravan leader <s>Priyasena</s> had passed away, <s>Supriya</s> was consecrated to the rank of great caravan leader by <s>Brahmadatta</s>, king of <s>Kāśi</s>.

children.text: tena sārthavāhabhūtena iyamevaṃrūpā mahāpratijñā kṛtā sarvasattvā mayā dhanena saṃtarpayitavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had become caravan leader, he made a great vow of this kind: "All beings are to be satisfied by me with wealth."

children.text: alpaṃ ca deyaṃ bahavaśca yācakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The amount to be given was small, and the petitioners were many.

children.text: tato 'lpairahobhistaddhanaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: Then in a few days that wealth reached exhaustion and depletion.

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati alpaṃ ca deyaṃ bahavaśca yācakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> reflected: "The amount to be given is small, and the petitioners are many.

children.text: tato 'lpairahobhistaddhanaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: In a few days that wealth has reached exhaustion and depletion.

children.text: yannvahaṃ sāmudram yānapātraṃ samudānīya mahāsamudramavatareyaṃ dhanahārikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to equip a seagoing vessel and enter the great ocean as one bringing back wealth?"

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sāmudrayānapātraṃ samudānīya pañcamātrairvaṇikśataiḥ sārdhaṃ mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> equipped a seagoing vessel and entered the great ocean together with five hundred merchants.
