children.text: tato 'nupūrveṇa ratnadvīpaṃ gatvā ratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā svastikṣemābhyāṃ mahāsamudrāduttīrya sthalajairvahitrairbhāṇḍamāropya vārāṇasyabhimukhaḥ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, going in due course to Jewel Island, collecting jewels, and coming up from the great ocean in safety and security, he loaded the goods onto land vehicles and set out toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: aṭavīkāntāramadhyagataścaurasahasreṇāsāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he was in the middle of a forest wilderness, he was encountered by a thousand thieves.

children.text: tataste caurā muṣitukāmāḥ sarvajavena prasṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those thieves, wishing to plunder him, rushed forward with all speed.

children.text: supriyeṇa ca sārthavāhenāvalokyābhihitāḥ kimetadbhavantaḥ samārabdham caurāḥ kathayanti sārthavāha tvamekaḥ svastikṣemābhyāṃ gaccha avaśiṣṭaṃ sārthaṃ muṣiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, seeing them, said: "What is this, sirs, that you have begun?" The thieves said: "Caravan leader, you go on alone in safety and security; we will plunder the rest of the caravan."

children.text: sārthavāhaḥ kathayati mamaiṣa bhavantaḥ sārthaḥ saṃniśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The caravan leader said: "Sirs, this caravan has taken refuge in me."

children.text: nārhanti bhavanto muṣitum evamuktāścaurāḥ kathayanti vayaṃ smaḥ sārthavāhacaurā aṭavīcarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Gentlemen, you ought not to plunder." Addressed in this way, the bandits said, "We are caravan-bandits, forest-rovers.

children.text: nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vāṇijyā na gaurakṣyam ||
children.translated_text: We have no farming, nor trade, nor cattle-keeping.

children.text: anena vayaṃ jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this means we make our livelihood."

children.text: teṣāṃ supriyaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati sārthasya mūlyaṃ bhavanto gaṇyatām ||
children.translated_text: The caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> said to them, "Gentlemen, let the value of the caravan be reckoned.

children.text: ahameṣāmarthe mūlyaṃ dāsyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: I will pay the price for their sake."

children.text: tataste vaṇijaḥ parasparaṃ mūlyaṃ gaṇayitvā caurāṇāṃ nivedayanti iyanti śatāni sahasrāṇi ceti ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants calculated the value among themselves and reported it to the bandits: "So many hundreds and thousands."

children.text: tataḥ supriyeṇa sārthavāhena bhāṇḍaniṣkrayārthe svaṃ dravyamanupradattam ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> handed over his own wealth for the ransom of the goods.

children.text: caurasakāśāt sārthaḥ paritrātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The caravan was rescued from the bandits.

children.text: evaṃ dvistriścatuḥpañcaṣaḍvārāṃs tasyaiva caurasahasrasya sakāśāt supriyeṇa sārthavāhena sārthaḥ paritrāto mūlyaṃ cānupradattam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, on a second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth occasion, the caravan was rescued by the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> from that very thousand of bandits, and the price was handed over.

children.text: yāvat saptamaṃ tu vāraṃ supriyaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when the seventh occasion came, the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> had gone down to the great ocean.

children.text: tataḥ saṃsiddhayānapātro 'bhyāgato 'ṭavīkāntāramadhyagatastenaiva caurasahasreṇāsāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having come back with his ship successfully accomplished, he reached the middle of the forest wilderness and was set upon by that same thousand of bandits.

children.text: tataste caurā muṣitukāmāḥ sarvajavena prasṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those bandits, wishing to plunder, rushed forward with all speed.

children.text: supriyeṇa ca sārthavāhenāvalokyābhihitāḥ supriyo 'haṃ bhavantaḥ sārthavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, seeing them, said, "Gentlemen, I am <s>Supriya</s>, the caravan leader."

children.text: caurāḥ kathayanti jānāsyeva mahāsārthavāha vayaṃ caurā aṭavīcarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The bandits said, "You know well enough, great caravan leader, that we are bandits, forest-rovers.

children.text: nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vāṇijyaṃ na gaurakṣyam ||
children.translated_text: We have no farming, nor trade, nor cattle-keeping.

children.text: anena vayaṃ jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this means we make our livelihood."

children.text: tataḥ supriyeṇa sārthavāhena pūrvikāṃ pratijñāmanusmṛtya dṛḍhapratijñena tasya caurasahasrasya bhāṇḍamanupradattam ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, remembering his former promise and firm in his resolve, handed over goods to that thousand of bandits.

children.text: supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati ime caurā labdhaṃ labdhamarthajātasaṃnicayaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: The great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> reflected, "These bandits make an accumulation of every kind of wealth, whatever they obtain.

children.text: mayā ca mahatī pratijñā kṛtā sarvasattvā dhanena mayā saṃtarpayitavyā iti ||
children.translated_text: And I have made a great vow: all beings must be satisfied by me with wealth.

children.text: so 'hamimaṃ caurasahasraṃ na śaknomi dhanena saṃtarpayitum ||
children.translated_text: Yet I am not able to satisfy this thousand of bandits with wealth.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ sarvasattvān dhanena saṃtarpayiṣyāmīti cintāparo middhamavakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How, then, shall I satisfy all beings with wealth?" Absorbed in this thought, he fell asleep.

children.text: atha tasya mahātmana udārapuṇyamaheśākhyasyodāracetasopapannasya sarvasattvamanorathaparipūrakasya lokahitārthamabhyudgatasya anyatarā maheśākhyā devatā upasaṃkramya samāśvāsayati mā tvaṃ sārthavāha khedamāpadyasva ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain powerful deity approached that great-souled one, endowed with lofty merit and great renown, possessed of a generous mind, fulfiller of the desires of all beings, risen up for the welfare of the world, and comforted him: "Do not fall into weariness, caravan leader.

children.text: ṛddhiṣyati te praṇidhiriti ||
children.translated_text: Your vow will succeed."

children.text: asti khalu mahāsārthavāha asminneva jambudvīpe badaradvīpo nāma mahāpattano 'manuṣyāvacarito maheśākhyamanuṣyādhiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Great caravan leader, there is here in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s> a great port called <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, frequented by nonhuman beings and inhabited by powerful nonhuman beings.

children.text: santi tasmin badaradvīpe pradhānāni ratnāni sarvasattvavicitramanorathaparipūrakāṇi ||
children.translated_text: In that <s>Badaradvīpa</s> there are excellent jewels that fulfill the varied desires of all beings.

children.text: yadi mahāsārthavāho badaradvīpayātrāṃ sādhayet evamimāṃ mahatīṃ pratijñāṃ pratinistareta ||
children.translated_text: If the great caravan leader were to accomplish the voyage to <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, he would thereby fulfill this great vow.

children.text: iyaṃ hi mahāpratijñā śakrabrahmādīnāmapi dustarā prāgeva manuṣyabhūtasya ||
children.translated_text: For this great vow is hard to carry through even for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the others, much more for one who has become human."

children.text: ityuktvā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, that deity disappeared right there.

children.text: na ca śakitā supriyeṇa mahāsārthavāhena sā devatā praṣṭum katarasyāṃ diśi badaradvīpaḥ kathaṃ vā tatra gamyata iti ||
children.translated_text: And the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> was not able to ask that deity in which direction <s>Badaradvīpa</s> lay, or how one might go there.

children.text: atha supriyasya sārthavāhasya suptapratibuddhasya etadabhavat aho bata me sā devatā punarapi darśayet diśaṃ copāyaṃ ca vyapadiśed badaradvīpamahāpattanasya gamanāyeti cintāparo middhamavakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> awoke from sleep, this occurred to him: "Ah, if only that deity would show herself to me again and point out the direction and the means for going to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>." Absorbed in this thought, he fell asleep.

children.text: atha sā devatā tasya mahātmana udārapuṇyamaheśākhyasya dṛḍhodārapratijñasyodāravīryaparākramatām anikṣiptotsāhatāṃ viditvā upasaṃkramya evamāha mā tvaṃ sārthavāha khedamāpadyasva ||
children.translated_text: Then that deity, knowing the generous energy and heroic effort, and the unforsaken zeal, of that great-souled one of lofty merit and great renown, firm in his lofty vow, approached and said this: "Do not fall into weariness, caravan leader.

children.text: asti khalu mahāsārthavāha paścime digbhāge pañcāntaradvīpaśatāni samatikramya sapta mahāparvatāḥ uccāśca pragṛhītāśca sapta ca mahānadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Great caravan leader, in the western quarter, after passing beyond five hundred intermediate islands, there are seven great mountains, high and steep, and seven great rivers.

children.text: tān vīryabalena laṅghayitvā antaroddānam anulomapratilomadvayamāvartaḥ śaṅkhanābhaḥ śaṅkhanābhī ca nīlodastārakākṣaśca parvatau nīlagrīva eva ca vairambhā tāmrāṭavī veṇugulmaḥ sapta parvatāḥ sakaṇṭakāḥ kṣāranadī triśaṅkur ayaskilam aṣṭādaśavakro nadī ślakṣṇa eva ca dhūmanetramudakaṃ saptāśīviṣaparvatā nadī bhavati paścimā ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed them by the strength of energy, there are <s>Antaroddāna</s>, <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>, the two whirlpools, <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s> and <s>Śaṅkhanābhī</s>, the mountains <s>Nīloda</s>, <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, and also <s>Nīlagrīva</s>, <s>Vairambhā</s>, <s>Tāmrāṭavī</s>, and <s>Veṇugulma</s>, seven thorny mountains; the <s>Kṣāra</s> river, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, <s>Ayaskila</s>, the eighteen-bent river, and also <s>Ślakṣṇa</s>, <s>Dhūmanetra</s> water, seven mountains of venomous serpents, and the western river.

children.text: anulomapratilomo nāma mahāsamudraḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is a great ocean called <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>.

children.text: anulomapratilome mahāsamudre manuṣyānavacarite anulomapratilomā vāyavo vānti ||
children.translated_text: In the great ocean <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>, untrodden by human beings, winds blow with and against the course.

children.text: tatra yo 'sau puruṣo bhavati maheśākhyo maheśākhyadevatāparigṛhītaḥ sa mahatā puṇyabalena vīryabalena cittabalena mahāntaṃ plavamāsthāya anulomapratilomamahāsamudram avatarati ||
children.translated_text: There, if there is a man who is powerful and protected by powerful deities, he boards a great raft through the great strength of his merit, energy, and mind, and enters the great <s>Anulomapratiloma</s> ocean.

children.text: sa yanmāsena gacchati tadekena divasena pratyāhriyate ||
children.translated_text: The distance he travels in a month is drawn back in a single day.

children.text: evaṃ dvis triḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus it happens a second and a third time."

children.text: hriyamāṇaśca pratyāhriyamāṇaśca yadi madhyamāmudakadhārāṃ pratipadyate evamasau maitrībalaparigṛhīto lokahitārthamabhyudgamyottarati nistarati abhiniṣkramati ||
children.translated_text: And while he is being carried away and drawn back, if he reaches the middle current of water, then, embraced by the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), he rises up for the welfare of the world, crosses over, escapes, and gets out.

children.text: anulomapratilomaṃ mahāsamudraṃ samatikramya anulomapratilomo nāma parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed the great ocean with and against the current, there is a mountain named <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>.

children.text: anulomapratilome mahāparvate 'manuṣyāvacarite 'nulomapratilomā nāma vāyavo vānti yaiḥ puruṣastimirīkṛtanetro naṣṭasaṃjñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: On the great mountain <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>, not frequented by human beings, winds named <s>Anulomapratiloma</s> blow; by them a man stands there with his eyes darkened and his consciousness lost.

children.text: sa vīryabalenātmānaṃ saṃdhārya tasmādeva mahāparvatādamoghāṃ nāmauṣadhīṃ samanviṣya gṛhītvā netre añjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya anulomapratilomaṃ nāma mahāparvatamabhiniṣkramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Holding himself together by the power of energy, he must seek out from that very great mountain a medicinal herb named <s>Amoghā</s>, take it, anoint his eyes, bind it on his head, smear himself with it, and make his way across the great mountain named <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>.

children.text: sacedetaṃ vidhimanutiṣṭhate nāsya saṃmoho bhavati svastikṣemeṇātikramatyanulomapratilomaṃ mahāparvatam ||
children.translated_text: If he follows this procedure, he is not bewildered, and he passes safely and securely over the great mountain <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>.

children.text: sacedevaṃ vidhiṃ vā nānutiṣṭhati auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate labdhvā vā na gṛhṇāti sa ṣaṇmāsān muhyati unmādamapi prāpnoti ucchritya vā kālaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not follow this procedure, or does not find the herb, or, having found it, does not take it, he is bewildered for six months, may even go mad, or, being swept up, he dies.

children.text: anulomapratilomaṃ mahāparvataṃ samatikramya āvarto nāma mahāsamudraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed the great mountain <s>Anulomapratiloma</s>, there is a great ocean named <s>Āvarta</s>.

children.text: tatra vairambhakā vāyavo vānti yaistadudakaṃ bhrāmyate ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Vairambhaka</s> winds blow, by which that water is made to whirl.

children.text: tatra yo 'sau puruṣo bhavatyudārapuṇyavipākamaheśākhyo devatāparigṛhītaḥ sa mahatā puṇyabalena vīryabalena cittabalena kāyabalena mahāntaṃ plavamāsthāya āvartaṃ mahāsamudramavatarati ||
children.translated_text: There, the man who has the great power of the ripening of lofty merit and is protected by deities mounts a great raft and descends into the great ocean <s>Āvarta</s> through the great force of his merit, the force of his energy, the force of his mind, and the force of his body.

children.text: sa ekasminnāvarte saptakṛtvo bhrāmayitvā nirudhyate ||
children.translated_text: He is spun around seven times in one whirlpool and then sinks.

children.text: yojanaṃ gatvā dvitīye āvarte unmajjate ||
children.translated_text: After going one yojana, he rises up in a second whirlpool.

children.text: sa tasminnapyāvarte saptakṛtvo bhrāmayitvā nirudhyate ||
children.translated_text: In that whirlpool too he is spun around seven times and then sinks.

children.text: evaṃ dvitīye tṛtīye caturthe pañcame ṣaṣṭhe āvarte saptakṛtvo bhrāmayitvā nirudhyate yojanaṃ gatvā unmajjate ||
children.translated_text: In this way, in the second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth whirlpools, he is spun around seven times and then sinks; after going one yojana, he rises up.

children.text: evamasau maitrībalaparigṛhīto lokahitārthamabhyudgata uttarati nistaratyabhiniṣkrāmati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, embraced by the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), he has risen up for the welfare of the world, crosses over, escapes, and gets out.

children.text: āvartaṃ mahāsamudramabhiniṣkramya āvarto nāma parvato 'manuṣyāvacaritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having got out of the great ocean <s>Āvarta</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Āvarta</s>, not frequented by human beings.

children.text: tatra śaṅkho nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati raudraḥ paraprāṇaharo mahābalo mahākāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There dwells a rākṣasa named <s>Śaṅkha</s>, fierce, a taker of others' lives, of great strength and great body.

children.text: tasyopariṣṭādyojanamātre śaṅkhanābhī nāmauṣadhī divā dhūmāyate rātrau prajvalati ||
children.translated_text: Above him, at a distance of about a yojana, there is a medicinal herb named <s>Śaṅkhanābhī</s>, which smokes by day and blazes by night.

children.text: sā nāgaparigṛhītā tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: It remains protected by a nāga.

children.text: sa khalu nāgo divā svapiti rātrau carati ||
children.translated_text: Now that nāga sleeps by day and moves about by night.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa divā sukhasuptasya nāgasya ātmānaṃ samanurakṣatā nāgaśarīramaviheṭhayatā auṣadhibalena mantrabalena puṇyabalena śaṅkhanābhī auṣadhī grahītavyā ||
children.translated_text: There, by that man, while the nāga is happily asleep by day, while guarding himself and not injuring the nāga's body, the medicinal herb <s>Śaṅkhanābhī</s> must be taken by the power of the herb, the power of mantra, and the power of merit.

children.text: gṛhītvā netre añjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya āvartaḥ parvato 'dhiroḍhavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having taken it, he must anoint his eyes, bind it on his head, smear himself with it, and climb the mountain <s>Āvarta</s>.

children.text: sacedetāṃ vidhimanutiṣṭhati svastikṣemeṇātikrāmati āvartaṃ parvatam aviheṭhitaḥ śaṅkhanābhena rākṣasena ||
children.translated_text: If he follows this procedure, he passes safely and securely over the mountain <s>Āvarta</s>, unharmed by the rākṣasa <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s>.

children.text: sacedetāṃ vidhiṃ nānutiṣṭhati auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate labdhāṃ vā na gṛhṇāti tamenaṃ śaṅkhanābho rākṣasaḥ pañcatvamāpādayati ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not follow this procedure, or does not find the herb, or, having found it, does not take it, then the rākṣasa <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s> brings him to the state of the five elements.

children.text: āvartaṃ parvatamatikramya nīlodo nāma mahāsamudraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed the mountain <s>Āvarta</s>, there is a great ocean named <s>Nīloda</s>.

children.text: gambhīro 'yaṃ gambhīrāvabhāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is deep and has the appearance of depth.

children.text: nīlode mahāsamudre tārākṣo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati raktanetraḥ pradīptaśiroruho vikṛtacaraṇadaśananayanaḥ parvatāyatakukṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the great ocean <s>Nīloda</s> dwells a rākṣasa named <s>Tārākṣa</s>, red-eyed, with blazing hair, with deformed feet, teeth, and eyes, and with a belly extended like a mountain.

children.text: sacet svapiti vivṛtānyasya netrāṇi bhavanti tadyathā acirodito bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he sleeps, his eyes are open, like the newly risen sun.

children.text: audārikāścāsya āśvāsapraśvāsā gurugurukāḥ pravartante yathā meghasya garjato 'śanyāṃ ca sphūrjatyāṃ śabdaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His gross, rumbling inhalations and exhalations proceed like the sound of a cloud thundering and lightning crashing.

children.text: yadā jāgarti nimīlitānyasya bhavanti netrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: When he is awake, his eyes are closed.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa tasmādeva samudrakūlān mahāmakarīnām auṣadhīṃ samanviṣya gṛhya netre añjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya mahāntaṃ plavamāsthāya suptaṃ tārākṣaṃ dakarākṣasaṃ viditvā pūrvabuddhabhāṣitāmeraṇḍāṃ nāma mahāvidyāmuccārayatā mantrapadāṃ dakarākṣasasamīpena gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: There that man must, from that very ocean shore, seek out and take the medicinal herb <s>Mahāmakarī</s>, anoint his eyes, bind it on his head, smear himself with it, mount a great raft, recognize that <s>Tārākṣa</s>, the water-rākṣasa, is asleep, and, reciting the mantra-words of the great vidyā named <s>Eraṇḍā</s>, spoken by former Buddhas, go near the water-rākṣasa.

children.text: sacedetāṃ vidhiṃ nānutiṣṭhati auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate labdhāṃ vā na gṛhṇāti tamenaṃ tārākṣo dakarākṣasa ojaṃ vā ghaṭṭayati cittaṃ vā kṣipati sarveṇa vā sarvaṃ jīvitādvyaparopayati ||
children.translated_text: If he does not follow this procedure, or does not find the herb, or, having found it, does not take it, then <s>Tārākṣa</s>, the water-rākṣasa, either strikes his vital force, deranges his mind, or utterly deprives him of life by every means.

children.text: nīlodaṃ mahāsamudraṃ samatikramya nīlodo nāma mahāparvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed the great ocean <s>Nīloda</s>, there is a great mountain named <s>Nīloda</s>.

children.text: tatra nīlagrīvo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati pañcaśataparivāra ugratejā raudraḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There dwells a rākṣasa named <s>Nīlagrīva</s>, surrounded by five hundred attendants, fierce in power, cruel, and a taker of others' lives.

children.text: nīlodo mahāparvata ekanīlo 'khaṇḍo 'cchidro 'suṣiraḥ saṃvṛta ekaghanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The great mountain <s>Nīloda</s> is entirely blue, unbroken, without fissure, without hollow, enclosed, and a single solid mass.

children.text: apīdānīmanimiṣaṃ paśyato netrāṇi vyābādhayate mūrcchāṃ ca saṃjanayati ||
children.translated_text: Even now it injures the eyes of one who looks without blinking and produces fainting.

children.text: tasyopariṣṭādyojanamātre 'moghā nāmauṣadhī vicitrarūpā ||
children.translated_text: Above that, at a distance of one yojana, there is a medicine named <s>Amoghā</s>, varied in form.

children.text: sā nāgaparigṛhītā tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: It stands there guarded by a <s>nāga</s>.

children.text: sa khalu nāgo dṛṣṭiviṣo 'pi śvāsaviṣo 'pi sparśaviṣo 'pi daṃṣṭrāviṣo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: That <s>nāga</s> is poisonous by sight, poisonous by breath, poisonous by touch, and poisonous by fangs.

children.text: yadā svapiti tadā dhūmāyate ||
children.translated_text: When it sleeps, it gives off smoke.

children.text: yaḥ khalu tena dhūmena mṛgo vā pakṣī vā spṛśyate sa pañcatvamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: Any deer or bird that is touched by that smoke comes to death.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa śiraḥsnātenopoṣitena maitrāyatā karuṇāyatā avyāpannena cittenātmānaṃ samanurakṣatā nāgaśarīram aviheṭhayatā auṣadhī grahītavyā ||
children.translated_text: There the man, having bathed his head and fasted, with his mind set on friendliness, compassion, and non-harm, protecting himself and not injuring the body of the <s>nāga</s>, must take the medicine.

children.text: netre añjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya anena vidhinā jānatānuṣṭhitena nīlodaḥ parvato 'bhiroḍhavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After anointing his eyes, tying it on his head, and smearing himself with it, once this procedure has been knowingly carried out, he must climb Mount <s>Nīloda</s>.

children.text: timiraṃ na bhaviṣyati mūrcchā ca na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: There will be no darkness, and there will be no fainting.

children.text: na cāsya guhyakāḥ śarīre prahariṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Nor will the guhyakas strike his body.

children.text: sacedetāṃ vidhiṃ nānutiṣṭhati auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate labdhāṃ vā na gṛhṇāti tamenaṃ nīlagrīvo rākṣasaḥ pañcatvamāpādayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not follow this procedure, or does not obtain the medicine, or, having obtained it, does not take it, the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Nīlagrīva</s> will bring him to death.

children.text: nīlodaṃ parvataṃ samatikramya vairambho nāma mahāsamudraḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing Mount <s>Nīloda</s>, there is a great ocean named <s>Vairambha</s>.

children.text: vairambhe mahāsamudre vairambhā nāma vāyavo vānti yaistadudakaṃ kṣobhyate yatrāgatir makarakacchapavallakaśiśumārādīnāṃ pretapiśācakumbhāṇḍakaṭapūtanādīnāṃ kaḥ punarvādo manuṣyāṇām ||
children.translated_text: In the great ocean <s>Vairambha</s>, winds called <s>Vairambhas</s> blow, by which that water is churned up; there there is no passage for makaras, turtles, vallakas, śiśumāras, and the like, nor for pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, kaṭapūtanas, and the like, to say nothing of human beings.

children.text: tamutsṛjya uttareṇa vairambhasya mahāsamudrasya mahatī tāmrāṭavī anekayojanāyāmavistārā ||
children.translated_text: Leaving that aside, north of the great ocean <s>Vairambha</s> there is a great copper forest, many yojanas in length and breadth.

children.text: tasyāstāmrāṭavyā madhye mahat sālavanaṃ mahaccodapānam ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of that copper forest there is a great sāla grove and a great well.

children.text: tatra tāmrākṣo nāma ajagaraḥ prativasati raudraḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ paramadurgandhaḥ pañcayojanāyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There lives a python named <s>Tāmrākṣa</s>, fierce, taking the lives of others, exceedingly foul-smelling, and five yojanas long.

children.text: sa ṣaṇmāsān svapiti ||
children.translated_text: It sleeps for six months.

children.text: yadā svapiti tadā asya yojanaṃ sāmantakena lālāsya spharitvā tiṣṭhati yadā jāgarti alpāsya lālā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When it sleeps, its saliva spreads and remains for a yojana all around; when it is awake, its saliva is slight.

children.text: tasyopariṣṭānmahān veṇugulmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Above it there is a great thicket of bamboo.

children.text: tasmin veṇugulme mahatyaśmaśilā ||
children.translated_text: In that bamboo thicket there is a great stone slab.

children.text: tāṃ vīryabalena utpāṭya guhā ||
children.translated_text: When that has been torn up by strength and vigor, there is a cave.

children.text: tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ saṃmohanī nāmauṣadhī ||
children.translated_text: In that cave there is a medicine named <s>Saṃmohanī</s>.

children.text: sā rātriṃdivasaṃ prajvalati ||
children.translated_text: It blazes by night and day.

children.text: tāṃ gṛhītvā netre añjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya suptaṃ tāmrākṣamajagaraṃ viditvā auṣadhībalena mantrabalena vā ajagarabhavanasamīpena gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: Taking it, anointing his eyes, tying it on his head, and smearing himself with it, after ascertaining that the python <s>Tāmrākṣa</s> is asleep, he must go near the python's dwelling by the power of the medicine or by the power of a mantra.

children.text: sacedetāṃ vidhimanutiṣṭhati svastikṣemābhyāmatikramya aviheṭhitas tāmrākṣeṇājagareṇa tataḥ paścānmūlaphalāni bhakṣayatā gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: If he follows this procedure, having passed by safely and securely, unharmed by the python <s>Tāmrākṣa</s>, then afterward he should go on, eating roots and fruits.

children.text: mahatīṃ tāmrāṭavīmatikramya sapta parvatāḥ kaṇṭakaveṇupraticchannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the great copper forest, there are seven mountains covered with thorn-bamboos.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa tāmrapaṭṭaiḥ pādau baddhvā tān parvatān vīryabalena laṅghayitvā sapta kṣāranadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the man, binding his feet with copper plates, must leap over those mountains by strength and vigor; then there are seven alkaline rivers.

children.text: tāsāṃ tīre mahāśālmalīvanam ||
children.translated_text: On their bank there is a great śālmalī forest.

children.text: tataḥ śālmalīphalakaiḥ plavaṃ baddhvā abhiruhyātikramitavyā aspṛśatā pānīyam ||
children.translated_text: From there he must bind together a raft with śālmalī planks, climb onto it, and cross over without touching the water.

children.text: sacet spṛśet tadaṅgaṃ śīryate ||
children.translated_text: If he should touch it, that limb falls apart.

children.text: sapta kṣāranadīḥ samatikramya triśaṅkur nāma parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the seven alkaline rivers, there is a mountain named <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

children.text: triśaṅkau parvate triśaṅkavo nāma kaṇṭakāstīkṣṇāḥ sutīkṣṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On Mount <s>Triśaṅku</s> there are thorns called <s>Triśaṅkus</s>, sharp and very sharp.

children.text: tatastena puruṣeṇa tāmrapaṭṭairvetrapāśaiḥ pādau baddhvā atikramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: From there the man must cross with his feet bound by copper plates and cane straps.

children.text: triśaṅkuparvatamatikramya triśaṅkur nāma nadī ||
children.translated_text: After crossing Mount <s>Triśaṅku</s>, there is a river named <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

children.text: triśaṅkavo nāma kaṇṭakāstīkṣṇā aṣṭādaśāṅgulā udake 'ntargatāstiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Thorns called <s>Triśaṅkus</s>, sharp and eighteen finger-breadths long, are hidden in the water.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa śālmalīphalakaiḥ plavaṃ baddhvā atikramitavyam aspṛśatā pānīyam ||
children.translated_text: There the man must bind together a raft with śālmalī planks and cross without touching the water.

children.text: sacet patati tatraivānayena vyasanamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: If he falls, he meets disaster from that very danger there.

children.text: yathā triśaṅkuḥ parvataḥ evaṃ triśaṅkukā nāma nadī ||
children.translated_text: As is Mount <s>Triśaṅku</s>, so too is the river named <s>Triśaṅkukā</s>.

children.text: evamayaskilaḥ parvato 'yaskilā nāma nadī ||
children.translated_text: In the same way there is a mountain named <s>Ayaskila</s> and a river named <s>Ayaskilā</s>.

children.text: ayaskilānadīmatikramya aṣṭādaśavakro nāma parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the river <s>Ayaskilā</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Aṣṭādaśavakra</s>.

children.text: ucchritaśca sarvataḥ saṃvṛto 'dvārakaśca ||
children.translated_text: It is high, enclosed on every side, and without an entrance.

children.text: asya na kiṃcit nistaraṇamanyatra vṛkṣāgrād vṛkṣamadhiruhya gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: There is no way out of it at all except by climbing from the top of one tree to another tree.

children.text: aṣṭādaśavakraṃ parvatamatikramya aṣṭādaśavakrikā nāma nadī grāhamakarākulā saṃvṛtā ca ||
children.translated_text: After crossing Mount <s>Aṣṭādaśavakra</s>, there is a river named <s>Aṣṭādaśavakrikā</s>, thronged with grāhas and makaras and enclosed.

children.text: tatra vetrapāśaṃ baddhvā atikramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: There one must bind a cane rope and cross over.

children.text: sacet patati anayena vyasanamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: If he falls, he meets disaster from that danger.

children.text: aṣṭādaśavakrikāṃ nadīmatikramya ślakṣṇo nāma parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the river <s>Aṣṭādaśavakrikā</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Ślakṣṇa</s>.

children.text: ślakṣṇaḥ parvato mṛdurucchrito 'dvārakaśca ||
children.translated_text: Mount <s>Ślakṣṇa</s> is smooth, soft, high, and without an entrance.

children.text: na cāsya kiṃcinnistaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: There is no way out of it at all.

children.text: tatrāyaskīlānāṃ koṭyātikramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: There it must be crossed by means of the tips of iron spikes.

children.text: ślakṣṇaṃ parvatamatikramya ślakṣṇā nāma nadī grāhamakarākulā ||
children.translated_text: After crossing Mount <s>Ślakṣṇa</s>, there is a river named <s>Ślakṣṇā</s>, thronged with grāhas and makaras.

children.text: saṃvṛtā ca sā nadī ||
children.translated_text: And that river is enclosed.

children.text: tatra vetrapāśān baddhvā atikramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: There one must bind cane ropes and cross over.

children.text: sacet patati anayena vyasanamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: If he falls, he meets disaster from that danger.

children.text: ślakṣṇāṃ nadīmatikramya dhūmanetro nāma parvato dhūmāyate saṃdhūmāyate ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the river <s>Ślakṣṇā</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Dhūmanetra</s>, which smokes and smolders.

children.text: yena khalu tena dhūmena mṛgā vā pakṣiṇo vā spṛśyante pañcatvamāpadyante ||
children.translated_text: Any deer or birds that are touched by that smoke come to death.

children.text: dhūmanetraḥ parvata ucchrito mahāprapāto 'dvārakaśca ||
children.translated_text: The mountain <s>Dhūmanetra</s> is high, has a great precipice, and has no doorway.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa guhā paryeṣitavyā ||
children.translated_text: There that man must seek out a cave.

children.text: guhāṃ samanviṣya tenātra guhādvāramauṣadhibalena mantrabalena ca moktavyam ||
children.translated_text: Having found the cave, he must open the cave entrance there by the power of the herb and by the power of mantra.

children.text: sā ca khalu guhā āśīviṣaparipūrṇā tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: And that cave stands filled with venomous serpents.

children.text: te khalu āśīviṣā dṛṣṭiviṣā api sparśaviṣā api ||
children.translated_text: Those venomous serpents are poisonous by sight and poisonous by touch.

children.text: dhūmanetrasya parvatasyopariṣṭānmahadudakapalvalam ||
children.translated_text: Above <s>Dhūmanetra</s> mountain there is a great pool of water.

children.text: tasminnudakapalvale mahatyaśmaśilā ||
children.translated_text: In that pool of water there is a great stone slab.

children.text: tāṃ vīryabalenotpāṭya guhā ||
children.translated_text: After he has torn it up by the power of energy, there is the cave.

children.text: tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ saṃjīvanī nāmauṣadhī jyotīrasaśca maṇirdīpaprabhāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that cave are the medicinal herb named <s>Saṃjīvanī</s> and the jewel <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, shining like a lamp.

children.text: tāmauṣadhīṃ gṛhītvā saśīrṣapādaṃ samālabhya tāṃ cauṣadhīṃ gṛhītvā guhā praveṣṭavyā ||
children.translated_text: Having taken that herb, smeared himself from head to foot, and taken that herb, he must enter the cave.

children.text: auṣadhībalena mantrabalena auṣadhīprabhāvāccāśīviṣāḥ kāye na kramiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: By the power of the herb, by the power of mantra, and through the influence of the herb, the venomous serpents will not crawl over his body.

children.text: evaṃ hi tasmāt parvatānnistaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For in this way there will be a way out from that mountain.

children.text: dhūmanetraparvatamatikramya saptāśīviṣaparvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing <s>Dhūmanetra</s> mountain there are seven mountains of venomous serpents.

children.text: auṣadhībalena mantrabalena ca saptāśīviṣaparvatā atikramitavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The seven mountains of venomous serpents must be crossed by the power of the herb and by the power of mantra.

children.text: saptāśīviṣaparvatānatikramya saptāśīviṣanadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the seven mountains of venomous serpents there are seven rivers of venomous serpents.

children.text: tīkṣṇagandhā nāma tatrāśīviṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the venomous serpents are named <s>Tīkṣṇagandhā</s>.

children.text: tatra tena puruṣeṇa māṃsapeśyanveṣitavyā ||
children.translated_text: There that man must seek out pieces of meat.

children.text: tāsāmāśīviṣanadīnāṃ tīre śālmalīvanam ||
children.translated_text: On the banks of those rivers of venomous serpents there is a forest of śālmalī trees.

children.text: tataḥ śālmalīphalakaiḥ plavaṃ baddhvā māṃsapeśyā ātmānamācchādya adhiroḍhavyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after binding a raft with śālmalī planks, he must cover himself with pieces of meat and mount it.

children.text: tatasta āśīviṣā māṃsagandhena pārāt pāraṃ gamiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those venomous serpents, because of the smell of meat, will go from one bank to the other.

children.text: saptāśīviṣamatikramya mahān sudhāvadātaḥ parvataḥ uccaśca pragṛhītaśca ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the seven venomous-serpent rivers, there is a great mountain, white as lime, high and steep.

children.text: so 'dhiroḍhavyas tatra drakṣyasi mahāntaṃ sauvarṇabhūmiṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ puṣpaphalacchāyāvṛkṣopaśobhitam ||
children.translated_text: He must climb it. There you will see a great region of golden earth, adorned with trees that bear flowers, fruits, and shade.

children.text: rohitakāñ janapadān ṛddhāṃśca kṣemāṃśca subhikṣāṃśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṃśca ||
children.translated_text: You will see the <s>Rohitaka</s> districts, prosperous, secure, rich in food, and filled with many people and human beings.

children.text: rohitakaṃ ca mahānagaraṃ dvādaśayojanāyāmaṃ saptayojanavistṛtaṃ saptaprākāraparikṣiptaṃ dvāṣaṣṭidvāropaśobhitaṃ bhavanaśatasahasravirājitaṃ suviviktarathyāvīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: And there is the great city <s>Rohitaka</s>, twelve yojanas in length and seven yojanas in breadth, enclosed by seven ramparts, adorned with sixty-two gates, splendid with hundreds of thousands of buildings, and having well-laid-out roads, streets, squares, crossroads, and inner markets.

children.text: vīṇāvallikāmahatīsughoṣakaiḥ śrotrābhirāmaiśca gītadhvanibhiranuparataprayogaṃ nānāpaṇyasaṃvṛddhaṃ nityapramuditajanaughasaṃkulaṃ tridaśendropendrasadṛśodyānasabhāpuṣkariṇīsampannaṃ kādambahaṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākopaśobhitataḍāgaṃ rohitakaṃ mahārājādhyuṣitaṃ mahāpuruṣavaṇiṅniṣevitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rohitaka</s> is filled with uninterrupted performances of vīṇā, vallakī, mahatī, and sweet-sounding instruments, and with song-sounds pleasing to the ear; it thrives with many wares, is crowded with hosts of people who are always delighted, is endowed with gardens, assembly halls, and lotus ponds like those of <s>Tridaśendra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, has lakes adorned with kādamba, haṃsa, kāraṇḍava, and cakravāka birds, is inhabited by a great king, and is frequented by great men and merchants.

children.text: yatra maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ prativasati abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī dvīpāntaradvīpagamanavidhijño mahāsamudrayānapātrayāyī ||
children.translated_text: There the caravan leader <s>Magha</s> lives: handsome, good-looking, gracious, learned, eloquent, intelligent, wealthy, possessed of great riches and great enjoyments, with broad and extensive possessions, endowed with the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, knowing the methods for going from island to island, and a traveler by vessels over the great ocean.

children.text: sa te badaradvīpamahāpattanasya pravṛttimākhyāsyati nimittāni ca darśayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will tell you about the state of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> and will show you the signs.

children.text: yathoktaṃ ca vidhimanuṣṭhāsyasi na ca khedamāpatsyase ||
children.translated_text: You will follow the prescribed procedure and will not fall into weariness.

children.text: evaṃ mahāsārthavāha paramaduṣkarakāraka imāṃ sumerumalayamandarasadṛśīṃ dṛḍhāṃ pratijñāṃ nistariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Thus, great caravan leader, doer of what is supremely difficult, you will get through this firm vow, which is like <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, and <s>Mandara</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ ca mahāpratijñā śakrabrahmādīnāmapi duṣkarā prāgeva manuṣyabhūtānām ||
children.translated_text: And this great vow is difficult even for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the others, much more for beings who are human.

children.text: ityuktvā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, that deity disappeared right there.

children.text: atha supriyaḥ sārthavāhaḥ suptapratibuddho devatāvacanaṃ śrutvā paramavismayamāpannaścintayati nūnamanayā devatayā anekairevaṃvidhaiḥ paramaduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpayātrā sādhitapūrvā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, awakened from sleep, heard the deity's words, was filled with supreme wonder, and thought: "Surely this deity herself has previously accomplished the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many hundreds of thousands of supremely difficult deeds.

children.text: yadi tāvat sādhitā duṣkarakārikā iyaṃ devatā ||
children.translated_text: If, to begin with, it has been accomplished, then this deity is one who does what is difficult.

children.text: atha sādhyamānā dṛṣṭāḥ paramaduṣkarakārakāste manuṣyāḥ yairanekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpayātrā sādhitā ||
children.translated_text: Or, while it was being accomplished, she saw those human beings who did what was supremely difficult, by whom the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> was accomplished through many hundreds of thousands of difficulties.

children.text: atiduṣkaraṃ caitadasmābhiḥ karaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: This too is exceedingly difficult for us to do.

children.text: athavā yadyapyahaṃ lokahitārthe pratipadyeyam saphalo me pariśramaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Yet if I undertake it for the sake of the welfare of the world, my labor will be fruitful.

children.text: yathā anekairduṣkaraśatasahasrair badaradvīpamahāpattanayātrāṃ sādhayiṣyāmi paraṃ lokānugrahaṃ kariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: When I accomplish the journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many hundreds of thousands of difficulties, I shall perform supreme benefit for the world.

children.text: te 'pi manuṣyāḥ yairanekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpayātrā sādhitapūrvā ||
children.translated_text: Those human beings too, by whom the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> was previously accomplished through many hundreds of thousands of difficulties,

children.text: ahamapi manuṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I too am a human being.

children.text: taiḥ sādhitā ||
children.translated_text: It was accomplished by them.

children.text: kasmādahaṃ na sādhayiṣyāmītyanuvicintya supriyo mahāsārthavāho dṛḍhapratijño dṛḍhavīryaparākramo 'nikṣiptotsāha udārapuṇyavipākamaheśākhyo lokahitārthamabhyudgato yathopadiṣṭoddeśasmṛtiparigṛhīto dṛḍhapratijñāṃ samanusmṛtya mahatā vīryabalena ekākī advitīyavyavasāyo yathopadiṣṭāni pañcāntaradvīpaśatāni samatikrāmati ||
children.translated_text: Why should I not accomplish it?" Having reflected thus, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, firm in vow, firm in energy and heroic effort, with undiminished zeal, of great renown through the ripening of lofty merit, risen up for the welfare of the world, holding in memory the directions as they had been pointed out, remembering his firm vow, with great strength of energy, alone and with a resolve that had no second, crossed the five hundred intermediate islands as instructed.

children.text: sapta mahāparvatān sapta mahānadyo vistareṇa sarvāṇi saṃkaṭāni yathoktena vidhinā mūlakandaphalāhāro guṇavati phalake baddhvā paripūrṇairdvādaśabhirvarṣai rohitakaṃ mahānagaramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having traversed the seven great mountains, the seven great rivers, and all the difficult passages in full detail by the prescribed procedure, living on roots, bulbs, and fruits, and having fastened himself to a sturdy plank, after a full twelve years he reached the great city <s>Rohitaka</s>.

children.text: udyāne sthitvā anyatamaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate kaścidbhoḥ puruṣa asmin rohitake mahānagare magho nāma sārthavāhaḥ parivasati sa evamāha asti bhoḥ puruṣa ||
children.translated_text: Standing in a park, he addressed a certain man: "Good sir, does a caravan leader named <s>Magha</s> live in this great city <s>Rohitaka</s>?" He replied, "He does, good sir."

children.text: kiṃ tarhi mahāvyādhinā grastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "But he is afflicted with a great illness."

children.text: sthānametadvidyate yattenaivābādhena kālaṃ kariṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "It is possible that he will die from that very sickness."

children.text: atha supriyasya mahāsārthavāhasyaitadabhavat mā haiva magho mahāsārthavāho 'dṛṣṭa eva kālaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>: "Let not the great caravan leader <s>Magha</s> die before I have even seen him."

children.text: ko me vyapadeśaṃ kariṣyati tasya badaradvīpamahāpattanasya gamanāyeti viditvā tvaritatvaritam yena maghasya sārthavāhasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, "Who will give me directions for going to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>?", he went very, very quickly to the dwelling of the caravan leader <s>Magha</s>.

children.text: sa dvāre nivāryate na labhate praveśaṃ mahāsārthavāhadarśanāya ||
children.translated_text: At the door he was stopped, and he did not obtain entry in order to see the great caravan leader.

children.text: dharmatā khalu kuśalā bodhisattvāsteṣu teṣu śilpasthānakarmasthāneṣu ||
children.translated_text: Now it is the nature of skillful <s>bodhisattvas</s> (beings intent on awakening) to be skilled in those various crafts and fields of work.

children.text: tato vaidyasaṃjñāṃ ghoṣayitvā praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having announced himself under the designation of a physician, he entered.

children.text: adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāho 'riṣṭādhyāyeṣu viditavṛttāntaḥ maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ ṣaḍbhirmāsaiḥ kālaṃ kariṣyatīti viditvā supriyo mahāsārthavāho 'dhītya vaidyamatāni svayameva mūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyānyānulomikāni vyapadiśati sma vyādhivyupaśamārtham ||
children.translated_text: The great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, versed in the chapters on fatal signs, saw that the situation was this: the caravan leader <s>Magha</s> would die in six months. Knowing this, the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, having studied the doctrines of physicians, himself prescribed suitable medicines made from roots, tubers, leaves, flowers, and fruits for the calming of the disease.

children.text: paraṃ cainaṃ toṣayati citrākṣaravyañjanapadābhidhānaiḥ śāstrabaddhābhiḥ kathābhiḥ nānāśrutimanorathākhyāyikābhiḥ saṃrañjayati ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, he pleased him and delighted him with stories composed according to treatises, named with colorful letters, syllables, and words, and with many entertaining tales drawn from various learning.

children.text: dākṣyadākṣiṇyacāturyamādhuryopetamupasthānakarmaṇi satputra iva pitaraṃ bhaktyā gauraveṇa śuśrūṣate ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with competence, courtesy, cleverness, and sweetness in the work of attendance, he served him with devotion and respect, like a good son serving his father.

children.text: tato maghasya sārthavāhasya kṣemaṇīyataraṃ cābhūdyāpanīyataraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Magha</s> became more secure and more able to sustain life.

children.text: saṃjñā anena pratilabdhā ||
children.translated_text: He regained consciousness.

children.text: atha magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ pratilabdhasaṃjñaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat kuto bhavāñ jñānavijñānasampanno 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī paṭupracāraḥ sarvaśāstrajñaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ sarvakalābhijñaḥ sarvabhūtarutajña iṅgitajñaḥ kiṃ jātyā bhavān kiṃgotraḥ kena vā kāraṇena amanuṣyāvacaritaṃ deśamabhyāgataḥ evamuktaḥ supriyaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Magha</s>, having regained consciousness, said this to the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>: "Whence are you, sir, endowed with knowledge and discernment, handsome, pleasant to behold, pleasing, learned, articulate, intelligent, quick in action, knower of all <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), expert in all <s>śāstras</s>, acquainted with all arts, knower of the speech of all beings, and knower of gestures? What is your caste? What is your <s>gotra</s> (lineage)? For what reason have you come to a land frequented by nonhuman beings?" Thus addressed, the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> said, "Good, good, great caravan leader."

children.text: kāle 'smi mahāsārthavāhena jātikulagotrāgamanaprayojanaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "At the proper time I have been asked by the great caravan leader about my birth, family, <s>gotra</s> (lineage), coming, and purpose."

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāho maghāya sārthavāhāya jātikulagotrāgamanaprayojanaṃ vistareṇārocayati sma paraṃ cainaṃ vijñāpayati sārthavāhānubhāvādahaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanaṃ paśyeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> explained in detail to the caravan leader <s>Magha</s> his birth, family, <s>gotra</s> (lineage), coming, and purpose, and further petitioned him: "Through the caravan leader's favor, may I see the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>."

children.text: evamahaṃ syāt paripūrṇamanoratho nistīrṇadṛḍhapratijñaḥ sarvasattvamanorathaparipūrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "In this way my desire would be fulfilled; my firm vow would be carried through, and I would become one who fulfills the desires of all beings."

children.text: atha magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ supriyasya mahāsārthavāhasyāśrutapūrvāṃ parahitārthamabhyudyatāṃ dṛḍhapratijñāṃ śrutvā paramavismayajāto 'nimiṣadṛṣṭiḥ suciraṃ nirīkṣya supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat taruṇaśca bhavān dharmakāmaśca ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Magha</s>, hearing of the unprecedented firm vow of the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, raised up for the benefit of others, was filled with supreme wonder. Looking for a long time at the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> with unblinking eyes, he said this: "You are young, sir, and desirous of <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching)."

children.text: āścaryamamānuṣaparākramaṃ te paśyāmi yo nāma bhavāñ jambudvīpādamanuṣyāvacaritaṃ parvatasamudranadyottaraṇaṃ kṛtvā ihāgataḥ yatrāmanuṣyāḥ pralayaṃ gacchanti prāgeva manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I see marvelous, superhuman prowess in you, in that you have come here from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, having crossed mountains, oceans, and rivers not frequented by human beings, where nonhuman beings meet destruction, much more human beings."

children.text: devaṃ tadbhavantaṃ paśyāmi devānyatamaṃ vā manuṣyaveṣadhāriṇam ||
children.translated_text: "I regard you as a god, sir, or as some god wearing human guise."

children.text: na te kiṃciddustaramasādhyaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "For you there is nothing difficult to cross or impossible to accomplish."

children.text: api tu ahaṃ mahāvyādhinā grasto mumūrṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "But I am afflicted with a great illness and am about to die."

children.text: bhavāṃścāyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And you have arrived."

children.text: api tu ko bhavato 'rthe parahitārthe 'bhyudyatasyātmaparityāgamapi na kuryāt tena hi vatsa kṣipraṃ maṅgalapotaṃ samudānaya saṃvaraṃ cāropaya yadāvayoryātrāyanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "Yet who, for your sake, when you have undertaken the welfare of others, would not even give up himself? Therefore, child, quickly bring an auspicious boat and load the equipment; that will be the vehicle for our journey."

children.text: evaṃ sārthavāheti supriyo mahāsārthavāho maghāya mahāsārthavāhāya pratiśrutya maṅgalapotaṃ samudānīya saṃvaraṃ cāropya yena magho mahāsārthavāhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Very well, caravan leader," said the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>. Having promised the great caravan leader <s>Magha</s>, he brought an auspicious boat, had the equipment loaded, and went to the great caravan leader <s>Magha</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya maghaṃ sārthavāhamidamavocat deva samudānīto maṅgalapotaḥ saṃvaraṃ cāropitam yasyedānīṃ mahāsārthavāhaḥ kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to the caravan leader <s>Magha</s>: "Lord, the auspicious boat has been brought, and the equipment has been loaded. Let the great caravan leader now consider the proper time."

children.text: atha magho mahāsārthavāho badaradvīpamahāpattanagamanakṛtabuddhiḥ svajanabandhuvargaputradāramitrāmātyajñātisālohitaiḥ sabhṛtyavargeṇa ca rohitakarājñā ca nivāryamāṇo 'pi guṇavati phalake baddhvā āśu supriyasārthavāhasahāyo maṅgalapotamabhiruhya mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Magha</s>, the great caravan leader, having formed the intention of going to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, though he was being restrained by his own people, his relatives, his sons, wife, friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood-relations, together with his servants, and also by King <s>Rohitaka</s>, quickly fastened himself to a good plank, boarded the auspicious ship with the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> as his companion, and set out upon the great ocean.

children.text: atha magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ supriyasya mahāsārthavāhasya kathayati ahaṃ bāḍhaglāno na śakyāmi sthito gantum ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Magha</s>, the great caravan leader, said to <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, "I am severely ill; I cannot go standing up.

children.text: tadarhasi śayyāṃ kalpayitum yatrāhamapāśrito gamiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore please arrange a bed, on which I may travel while reclining."

children.text: api tu asmin mahāsamudre yāvadevaṃvidhāni nimittāni bhavanti udakasya varṇasaṃsthānāni ca mama nivedayitavyāni ||
children.translated_text: "Moreover, whenever signs of this kind arise in this great ocean, and also the colors and shapes of the water, they are to be reported to me."

children.text: yathā anekāni yojanaśatāni gatvā adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāha ekapāṇḍaraṃ pānīyam ||
children.translated_text: After they had gone many hundreds of yojanas, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, saw water of a single pale color.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā punarmaghāya sārthavāhāyārocayati yatkhalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāḥ ekapāṇḍaraṃ pānīyaṃ paśyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Having seen it, he reported to <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, "Great caravan leader, please know that I see water of a single pale color."

children.text: evamukte maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati naitanmahāsārthavāha ekapāṇḍaraṃ pānīyam ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, said, "Great caravan leader, this is not water of a single pale color.

children.text: api tu paśyasi tvaṃ dakṣiṇakena mahatsudhāparvatam yadidaṃ tasyaitadanubhāvena pānīyaṃ rañjitam ||
children.translated_text: Rather, do you see to the south a great mountain of lime? By its power this water has been colored.

children.text: yatraikaviṃśatidhātugotrāṇi yaṃ paktvā suvarṇarūpyavaiḍūryānyabhinirvartante yadeke jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā ratnānyādāya pratinivartante ||
children.translated_text: There are twenty-one families of minerals there; when they are smelted, gold, silver, and vaiḍūrya are produced, and from there some people of <s>Jāmbudvīpa</s> return after taking jewels.

children.text: idaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya prathamanimittam ||
children.translated_text: This is the first sign of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>."

children.text: punarapi gacchan paśyati supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ śastravarṇaṃ pānīyam ||
children.translated_text: Again, as he went on, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, saw weapon-colored water.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarmaghāya sārthavāhāyārocayati yat khalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāḥ śastravarṇaṃ pānīyaṃ dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Having seen it, he again reported to <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, "Great caravan leader, please know that weapon-colored water is visible."

children.text: maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati naitacchastravarṇaṃ pānīyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, said, "This is not weapon-colored water.

children.text: paśyasi tvaṃ dakṣiṇakeṇa mahacchastraparvatam ||
children.translated_text: Do you see to the south a great mountain of weapons?

children.text: tasyaitadanubhāvena pānīyaṃ rañjitam ||
children.translated_text: By its power this water has been colored.

children.text: atrāpyanekāni dhātugotrāṇi yaṃ paktvā suvarṇarūpyavaidūryasphaṭikānyabhinirvartante yadeke jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā ratnānyādāya pratinivartante ||
children.translated_text: Here too there are many families of minerals; when they are smelted, gold, silver, vaiḍūrya, and crystal are produced, and from there some people of <s>Jāmbudvīpa</s> return after taking jewels.

children.text: idaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya dvitīyaṃ nimittam ||
children.translated_text: This is the second sign of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>."

children.text: evaṃ lohaparvatāstāmraparvatā rūpyaparvatāḥ suvarṇaparvatāḥ sphaṭikaparvatā vaidūryaparvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way there were iron mountains, copper mountains, silver mountains, gold mountains, crystal mountains, and vaiḍūrya mountains.

children.text: adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāho nīlapītalohitāvadātaṃ pānīyam antarjale ca dīpārciṣaḥ paśyati dīpyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, saw water that was blue, yellow, red, and white, and in the water he saw lamp-flames blazing.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarmaghāya sārthavāhāyārocayati yatkhalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāḥ nīlapītalohitāvadātaṃ pānīyaṃ dṛśyate antarjale ca dīpārciṣo dīpyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen them, he again reported to <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, "Great caravan leader, please know that water that is blue, yellow, red, and white is visible, and lamp-flames are blazing in the water."

children.text: evamukte magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ kathayati naitanmahāsārthavāha nīlapītalohitāvadātaṃ pānīyam nāpyete dīpā iva dīpyante ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Magha</s>, the great caravan leader, said, "Great caravan leader, this is not water that is blue, yellow, red, and white, nor are these things blazing like lamps.

children.text: paśyasi tvaṃ dakṣiṇakena catūratnamayaṃ parvatam ||
children.translated_text: Do you see to the south a mountain made of four jewels?

children.text: tasyaitadanubhāvena pānīyaṃ rañjitam ||
children.translated_text: By its power this water has been colored.

children.text: ye 'pyete dīpā iva dīpyante ete 'ntargatā auṣadhyo dīpyante ||
children.translated_text: And those things that blaze like lamps are medicinal plants hidden within, blazing.

children.text: atrāpyanekāni dhātugotrāṇi yaṃ paktvā suvarṇarūpyavaidūryasphaṭikānyabhinirvartante yatraike jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā ratnānyādāya pratinivartante ||
children.translated_text: Here too there are many families of minerals; when they are smelted, gold, silver, vaiḍūrya, and crystal are produced, and from there some people of <s>Jāmbudvīpa</s> return after taking jewels.

children.text: idaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya daśamaṃ nimittam ||
children.translated_text: This is the tenth sign of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>.

children.text: api tu mahāsārthavāha iyantyevāhaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya daśa nimittāni jāne gamanaṃ prati ataḥ pareṇa na jāne ||
children.translated_text: But, great caravan leader, I know only this many, the ten signs of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, with regard to the journey; beyond this I do not know."

children.text: evamukte supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ kathayati kadā badaradvīpamahāpattanasya gamanāyānto bhaviṣyati evamukte maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati mayāpi supriya badaradvīpamahāpattanaṃ kārtsnena na dṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, said, "When will there be an end to the journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>?" When this was said, <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, said, "<s>Supriya</s>, I too have not seen the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> in its entirety.

children.text: api tu mayā śrutaṃ paurāṇānāṃ mahāsārthavāhānām antikājjīrṇānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ mahallakānām ito jalamapahāya paścimāṃ diśaṃ sthalena gamyate ||
children.translated_text: But I have heard from ancient great caravan leaders, aged, old, and elderly men, that from here, leaving the water, one goes westward by land."

children.text: tena caivamabhihitam maraṇāntikāccāsya vedanāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when he had said just this, pains like those at the point of death arose in him.

children.text: tataḥ supriyāya mahāsārthavāhāya kathayati maraṇāntikā me vedanāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he said to <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, "Pains like those at the point of death have arisen in me.

children.text: etattvaṃ maṅgalapotaṃ tīramupanīya vetrapāśaṃ baddhvā maccharīre śarīrapūjāṃ kuruṣva ||
children.translated_text: Bring this auspicious ship to the shore, tie a cane rope to my body, and perform the funeral honor for my body."

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhastaṃ maṅgalapotaṃ tīramupanīya vetrapāśaṃ badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, brought that auspicious ship to the shore and tied the cane rope.

children.text: atrāntare magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile <s>Magha</s>, the great caravan leader, passed away.

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāho maghaṃ sārthavāhaṃ kālagataṃ viditvā sthale utthāpya śarīre śarīrapūjaṃ kṛtvā cintayati maṅgalapotamāruhya yāsyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, knowing that <s>Magha</s>, the caravan leader, had passed away, lifted him onto the land, performed the funeral honor for his body, and thought, "I will board the auspicious ship and go."

children.text: sa ca poto vāyunā vetrapāśaṃ chittvā apahṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But that ship, driven by the wind, broke the cane rope and was carried away.

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaścatūratnamayasya parvatasya dakṣiṇena pārśvenāṭavyāṃ sthalena samprasthito mūlaphalāni bhakṣayamāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> set out overland through the wilderness on the southern side of the mountain made of four jewels, eating roots and fruits.

children.text: anekāni yojanāni gatvā adrākṣīt ślakṣṇaṃ parvatam anupūrvapravaṇamanupūrvaprāgbhāram ||
children.translated_text: After going many yojanas, he saw a smooth mountain, gradually sloping and gradually leaning forward.

children.text: na śakyate 'bhiroḍhum ||
children.translated_text: It could not be climbed.

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho madhunā pādau pralipyābhirūḍhaśca avatīrṇaśca anekāni yojanāni gatvā mūlaphalāhāro gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> smeared his feet with honey, climbed up and descended, and, after going many yojanas, continued on, living on roots and fruits.

children.text: sa tatra paśyati mahāntaṃ parvatamuccaṃ ca pragṛhītaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: There he saw a great mountain, high and steeply raised.

children.text: niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣamāṇo na labhate na cāsya kaścinniḥsaraṇavyapadeṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Searching for a way out, he did not find one, and there was no one to point out an exit for him.

children.text: tataścintāparaḥ śayitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, overcome with anxiety, he lay down.

children.text: tatra ca parvate nīlādo nāma yakṣaḥ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: On that mountain there lived a <s>yakṣa</s> named <s>Nīlāda</s>.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati ayaṃ bodhisattvo lokahitārthamudyataḥ parikliśyate yannvahamasya sāhāyyaṃ kalpayeyam ||
children.translated_text: He considered, "This <s>bodhisattva</s>, striving for the welfare of the world, is suffering hardship. What if I were to provide him assistance?"

children.text: idamanucintya supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat ito mahāsārthavāha pūrveṇa yojanaṃ gatvā trīṇi parvataśṛṅgāṇy anupūrvanimnānyanupūrvapravaṇānyanupūrvaprāgbhārāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Having reflected in this way, he said this to the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>: "From here, great caravan-leader, after going one yojana to the east, there are three mountain peaks, successively lower, successively sloping, and successively leaning forward.

children.text: tatra tvayā vetraśiṭām baddhvā atikramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: There you must fasten a cane rope and cross over."

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ suptaprabuddho vetraśiṭām baddhvā tāni parvataśṛṅgāṇyatikrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, waking from sleep, fastened a cane rope and crossed those mountain peaks.

children.text: bhūyaḥ samprasthito 'drākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sphaṭikaparvataṃ ślakṣṇaṃ nirālambamagamyaṃ manuṣyamātrasya ||
children.translated_text: Setting out again, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> saw a crystal mountain, smooth, without support, and inaccessible to an ordinary human being.

children.text: na cāsyopāyaṃ paśyati taṃ parvatamabhirohaṇāyeti viditvā cintāparo 'horātramavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing no means for climbing that mountain, he remained there anxious for a day and night.

children.text: tasmiṃśca parvate candraprabho nāma yakṣaḥ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: On that mountain there lived a <s>yakṣa</s> named <s>Candraprabha</s>.

children.text: sa cintāparaṃ sārthavāhaṃ viditvā lokahitārthamabhyudyataṃ mahāyānasamprasthitaṃ prasannacittaṃ copetyāśvāsayati na khalu mahāsārthavāhena viṣādaḥ karaṇīya iti ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that the caravan-leader was anxious, that he was intent on the welfare of the world, had set out on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and was of faithful mind, he approached and reassured him: "The great caravan-leader certainly must not despair."

children.text: pūrveṇa krośamātraṃ gatvā mahaccandanavanam ||
children.translated_text: "After going about a krośa to the east, there is a great sandalwood forest.

children.text: tasmiṃśca candanavane mahatyaśmaśilā ||
children.translated_text: In that sandalwood forest there is a great stone slab.

children.text: tāṃ vīryabalenotpāṭya guhāṃ drakṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: When you have torn it up by the power of strength and vigor, you will see a cave.

children.text: tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ prabhāsvarā nāmauṣadhī pañcaguṇopetā ||
children.translated_text: In that cave there is a medicine named <s>Prabhāsvarā</s>, endowed with five qualities.

children.text: tayā gṛhītayā nāsya kāye śastraṃ kramiṣyati amanuṣyāścāvatāraṃ na lapsyante balaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca saṃjanayati ālokaṃ ca karoti ||
children.translated_text: When it has been taken, no weapon will penetrate his body, nonhuman beings will gain no entrance, it produces strength and vigor, and it gives light.

children.text: tenālokena drakṣyasi catūratnamayaṃ sopānam ||
children.translated_text: By that light you will see a staircase made of four jewels.

children.text: tena sopānena sphaṭikaparvatamatikramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: By that staircase the crystal mountain must be crossed.

children.text: sphaṭikaparvatamatikrāntasya te prabhāsvarā auṣadhyantardhāsyati ||
children.translated_text: When you have crossed the crystal mountain, the medicine <s>Prabhāsvarā</s> will disappear.

children.text: tatra te na śocitavyaṃ na kranditavyaṃ na paridevitavyam ||
children.translated_text: At that you must not grieve, cry out, or lament."

children.text: atha candraprabho yakṣaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ samanuśāsya tatraivāntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Candraprabha</s>, having instructed the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, vanished right there.

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaścandraprabheṇa mahāyakṣeṇa samāśvāsya ādeśitamārgo yathoktena vidhinā sphaṭikaparvatamatikrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, reassured by the great <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Candraprabha</s> and shown the path, crossed the crystal mountain according to the stated method.

children.text: atikrāntasya cāsya prabhāsvarā auṣadhyantarhitā ||
children.translated_text: When he had crossed it, the medicine <s>Prabhāsvarā</s> disappeared.

children.text: bhūyaḥ samprasthito 'drākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sauvarṇaṃ mahānagaramārāmasampannaṃ puṣkariṇīsampannam ||
children.translated_text: Setting out again, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> saw a great golden city, furnished with parks and furnished with lotus ponds.

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho nagaradvāraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> went to the city gate.

children.text: yāvadbaddhaṃ nagaraṃ paśyati ||
children.translated_text: There he saw that the city was shut.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarudyānaṃ gatvā cintayati yadyapyahaṃ nagaramadrākṣam tadapi śūnyam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, he went to a garden and thought, "Although I have seen the city, still it is empty.

children.text: kadā badaradvīpasya mahāpattanasyāgamanāyādhvā bhaviṣyatīti viditvā śayitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When will there be a road for coming to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>?" Having understood this, he lay down.

children.text: atha sā pūrvadevatā supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ durmanasaṃ viditvā rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaya upasaṃkramya samāśvāsya utkarṣayati sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha nistīrṇāni te mahāsamudraparvatanadīkāntārāṇi manuṣyāmanuṣyāgamyāni ||
children.translated_text: Then that former deity, knowing that the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> was downcast, approached at daybreak, reassured him, and encouraged him: "Good, good, great caravan-leader. You have crossed great oceans, mountains, rivers, and wildernesses inaccessible to humans and nonhumans.

children.text: samprāpto 'si badaradvīpamahāpattanaṃ manuṣyāmanuṣyānavacaritaṃ maheśākhyapuruṣādhyuṣitam ||
children.translated_text: You have reached the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, untrodden by humans and nonhumans and inhabited by men of great power.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi na sāmpratamaprasādaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore no despondency should be felt now.

children.text: indriyāṇi ca gopayitavyāni cakṣurādīni kāyagatā smṛtirbhāvayitavyā ||
children.translated_text: The senses beginning with the eye must be guarded, and mindfulness directed to the body must be cultivated.

children.text: śvobhūte nagaradvāraṃ trikoṭayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Tomorrow the city gate must be knocked upon three times.

children.text: tataścatasraḥ kinnarakanyā nirgamiṣyanti abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāścāturyamādhuryasampannāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ paramarūpābhijātāḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā hasitaramitaparicāritanṛttagītavāditrakalāsvabhijñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then four <s>kinnara</s> maidens will come out, beautiful, lovely to behold, pleasing, endowed with skill and sweetness, complete in every limb and minor limb, born with supreme beauty, adorned with every ornament, and skilled in the arts of laughter, love-play, attendance, dancing, singing, and instrumental music.

children.text: tāstvāmatyarthamupalālayanti evaṃ ca vakṣyanti etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They will flatter you exceedingly and will say this: 'Come, great caravan-leader.

children.text: svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāha asmākam asvāminīnāṃ svāmī bhava apatikānāṃ patiralayanānāṃ layano 'dvīpānāṃ dvīpo 'trāṇānāṃ trāṇo 'śaraṇānāṃ śaraṇamaparāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Welcome, great caravan-leader. Be the master of us who have no master, the husband of us who have no husband, the resting-place of us who have no resting-place, the island of us who have no island, the protection of us who have no protection, the refuge of us who have no refuge, and the final resort of us who have no final resort.'"

children.text: imāni ca te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi śayanagṛhāṇyārāmaramaṇīyāni prabhūtāni ca jāmbudvīpakāni ratnāni tadyathā maṇayo muktā vaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpamaśmagarbhamusāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here for you are storehouses of food, storehouses of drink, storehouses of clothing, storehouses of beds, and delightful parks; and there are abundant jewels from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, namely gems, pearls, beryl, conch shell, stone, coral, silver, gold, aśmagarbha, musāragalva, lohitikā, and right-spiraled shells.

children.text: etāni ca te ratnāni ||
children.translated_text: And these are the jewels for you.

children.text: tvaṃ cāsmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva ||
children.translated_text: Sport with us, enjoy yourself, and let yourself be attended by us.

children.text: tatra te tāsu mātṛsaṃjñā upasthāpayitavyā bhaginīsaṃjñā duhitṛsaṃjñā upasthāpayitavyā ||
children.translated_text: There you must establish toward them the idea of mother; you must establish the idea of sister and the idea of daughter.

children.text: daśākuśalāḥ karmapathā vigarhitavyāḥ daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ saṃvarṇayitavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ten unwholesome <s>karmapathas</s> (paths of action) are to be censured, and the ten wholesome <s>karmapathas</s> are to be praised.

children.text: subahvapi te pralobhyamānena rāgasaṃjñā notpādayitavyā ||
children.translated_text: Even though you are very much being tempted, you must not produce any thought of passion.

children.text: sacedutpādayiṣyasi tatraivānayena vyasanamāpatsyase ||
children.translated_text: If you do produce it, you will fall into disaster from that very danger there.

children.text: sūpasthitasmṛtestava saphalaḥ śramo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: If your mindfulness is well established, your effort will bear fruit.

children.text: yadyapi te subhāṣitasyārghamaṇiṃ prayaccheyuḥ tatastvayā nipuṇaṃ praṣṭavyāḥ asya ratnasya bhaginyaḥ ko 'nubhāva iti ||
children.translated_text: Even if they should give you a precious jewel as the price of a well-spoken teaching, then you must carefully ask them, 'Sisters, what is the power of this jewel?'

children.text: evaṃ dvitīyaṃ kinnaranagaramanuprāptasyāṣṭau kinnarakanyā nirgamiṣyanti tāsāṃ pūrvikānāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, when you have reached the second kinnara city, eight kinnara maidens will come out, more beautiful than the former ones.

children.text: tatrāpi te eṣānupūrvī karaṇīyā ||
children.translated_text: There too this same procedure is to be followed by you.

children.text: yāvaccaturthakinnaranagaraprāptasya te dvātriṃśat kinnarakanyā nirgamiṣyanti tāsāṃ pūrvikānāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca darśanīyatarāśca prāsādikatarāścāpsarasaḥ pratispardhinyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Until, when you have reached the fourth kinnara city, thirty-two kinnara maidens will come out, more beautiful than the former ones, more lovely to behold, more gracious, rivaling apsarases.

children.text: śatasahasraśobhitā bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: They will be adorned with a hundred thousand splendors.

children.text: tatrāpi te eṣaivānupūrvī karaṇīyā ||
children.translated_text: There too this very same procedure is to be followed by you.

children.text: ityuktvā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that deity vanished right there.

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ pramuditamanāḥ sukhapratibuddhaḥ kālyamevotthāya sauvarṇaṃ kinnaranagaramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, joyful in mind and having awakened happily, rose at the very break of day and reached the golden kinnara city.

children.text: dvāramūlamupasaṃkramya trikoṭayati ||
children.translated_text: He approached the foot of the gate and knocked.

children.text: tataḥ supriyeṇa mahāsārthavāhena trikoṭite dvāre catasraḥ kinnarakanyā nirgatā abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāścāturyamādhuryasampannāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ paramarūpābhijātā hasitaramitaparicāritanṛttagītavāditrakalāsvabhijñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the gate had been knocked on by the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, four kinnara maidens came out, beautiful, lovely to behold, gracious, endowed with skill and sweetness, complete in every limb and minor limb, supremely noble in form, and expert in the arts of laughter, pleasure, attendance, dancing, singing, and instrumental music.

children.text: tā evamāhuḥ etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They said this: 'Let the great caravan leader come.'

children.text: svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāha ||
children.translated_text: Welcome, great caravan leader.

children.text: asmākam asvāminīnāṃ svāmī bhava apatīnāṃ patiralayanānāṃ layano 'dvīpānāṃ dvīpo 'śaraṇānāṃ śaraṇo 'trāṇānāṃ trāṇo 'parāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Be the master of us who have no master, the husband of us who have no husband, the refuge of us who have no refuge, the island of us who have no island, the shelter of us who have no shelter, the protector of us who have no protector, and the final resort of us who have no final resort.

children.text: imāni ca te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi śayanagṛhāṇyārāmaramaṇīyāni vanaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni ca ||
children.translated_text: And here for you are storehouses of food, storehouses of drink, storehouses of clothing, storehouses of beds, delightful parks, delightful groves, and delightful lotus ponds.

children.text: jāmbudvīpakāni ratnāni tadyathāmaṇayo muktā vaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartā etāni ca ||
children.translated_text: There are jewels from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, namely gems, pearls, beryl, conch shell, stone, coral, silver, gold, aśmagarbha, musāragalva, lohitikā, and right-spiraled shells; and these too are yours.

children.text: tvaṃ cāsmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva ||
children.translated_text: Sport with us, enjoy yourself, and let yourself be attended by us.

children.text: atha supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ sūpasthitasmṛtiṃ tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ sarvāṅgairanuparigṛhya sauvarṇaṃ kinnaranagaraṃ praveśya prāsādamabhiropya prajñapta evāsane niṣādayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those kinnara maidens, finding the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> with his mindfulness well established, received him with all their limbs, brought him into the golden kinnara city, led him up into a palace, and seated him on a prepared seat.

children.text: niṣaṇṇaḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho daśākuśalān karmapathān vigarhati daśa kuśalān karmapathān saṃvarṇayati subahvapi pralobhyamāno na śakyate skhalayitum ||
children.translated_text: Once seated, the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> censured the ten unwholesome <s>karmapathas</s> and praised the ten wholesome <s>karmapathas</s>; although he was being greatly tempted, he could not be made to stumble.

children.text: tuṣṭāśca tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ kathayanti āścaryam yatredānīṃ daharaśca bhavān dharmakāmaśca ||
children.translated_text: Pleased, those kinnara maidens said, 'It is marvelous that now, though you are young, sir, you are also desirous of <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching).

children.text: na ca kāmeṣu sajjase vā badhyase vā ||
children.translated_text: And you are neither attached nor bound among sensual pleasures.

children.text: prabhūtaiśca ratnaiśca pravārayanti ||
children.translated_text: And they invited him to accept abundant jewels.

children.text: dharmadeśanāvarjitāśca ekaṃ saubhāsinikaṃ ratnamanuprayacchanti ||
children.translated_text: Won over by his teaching of <s>dharma</s>, they gave him one saubhāsinika jewel.

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhastasya ratnasya prabhāvānveṣī kathayati asya ratnasya bhaginyaḥ ko 'nubhāva iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, seeking to know the power of that jewel, said, 'Sisters, what is the power of this jewel?'

children.text: tāḥ kathayanti yatkhalu sārthavāha jānīyāḥ tadeva poṣadhe pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnāta upoṣadhoṣita idaṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre āropya yojanasahasraṃ sāmantakena yo yenārthī bhavati hiraṇyena vā suvarṇena vā annena vā vastreṇa vā pānena vā alaṃkāraviśeṣeṇa vā dvipādena vā catuṣpādena vā yānena vā vāhanena vā dhanena vā dhānyena vā sa cittamutpādayatu vācaṃ ca niścārayatu ||
children.translated_text: They said, 'Caravan leader, you should know this: on the fifteenth day, on the fast day, after bathing your head and keeping the fast, set this jewel-gem on the top of a banner. Then, within a thousand yojanas all around, whoever has need of anything, whether silver, gold, food, clothing, drink, a special ornament, a two-footed creature, a four-footed creature, a cart, a mount, wealth, or grain, should produce the thought and utter the words.
