children.text: sahacittotpādād vāgniścāraṇena yathepsitāścopakaraṇaviśeṣā ākāśādavatariṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: As soon as the thought is produced and the words are uttered, the particular provisions desired will descend from the sky.

children.text: ayamasya ratnasyānubhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the power of this jewel.'

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛbhaginīduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya sauvarṇāt kinnaranagarāt pratiniṣkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, having instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened those kinnara maidens with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>, and having greeted them as mother, sister, and daughter, departed from the golden kinnara city.

children.text: adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāho rūpyamayaṃ kinnaranagaramārāmasampannaṃ vanasampannaṃ puṣkariṇīsampannam ||
children.translated_text: The great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> saw a silver city of kinnaras, endowed with parks, endowed with forests, and endowed with lotus ponds.

children.text: tatrāpi supriyeṇa sārthavāhena trikoṭite dvāre'ṣṭau kinnarakanyā nirgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too, when the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> had knocked three times at the gate, eight kinnara maidens came out.

children.text: tā apyevamāhuḥ etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They too said this: "Let the great caravan leader come."

children.text: svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāhāya ||
children.translated_text: "Welcome to the great caravan leader."

children.text: asmākamasvāmikānāṃ svāmī bhava pūrvavadyāvattābhirapi dharmadeśanāvarjitābhistadviśiṣṭataraṃ dvisāhasrayojanavarṣakaṃ maṇiratnamanupradattam ||
children.translated_text: "Be the master of us who have no master." As before, up to the point where, after they too had not been left without a teaching of <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching), a jewel superior to that, causing rain over two thousand yojanas, was given.

children.text: tatrāpi supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛbhaginīduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya rūpyamayāt kinnaranagarāt pratiniṣkrānto yāvat tṛtīyaṃ vaiḍūryamayaṃ kinnaranagaramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, having instructed those kinnara maidens with a discourse on <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching), having made them accept it, stirred them up, gladdened them, and conversed with them as with mothers, sisters, and daughters, departed from the silver city of kinnaras, until he reached a third city of kinnaras made of vaiḍūrya.

children.text: tatrāpi supriyeṇa sārthavāhena trikoṭite dvāre ṣoḍaśa kinnarakanyā nirgatāḥ tāsāṃ pūrvikānāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca prāsādikatarāśca ||
children.translated_text: There too, when the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> had knocked three times at the gate, sixteen kinnara maidens came out, more beautiful and more pleasing than the earlier ones.

children.text: tā api dharmadeśanāvarjitāstata eva viśiṣṭataraṃ saubhāsinikaṃ trisāhasrayojanikaṃ ratnamanuprayacchanti ||
children.translated_text: They too, not left without a teaching of <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching), offered him a <s>saubhāsinika</s> jewel, still more excellent than that one, measuring three thousand yojanas.

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhastasya ratnasya prabhāvānveṣī kathayati asya ratnasya bhaginyaḥ ko'nubhāva iti kinnarakanyāḥ kathayanti pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, inquiring into the power of that jewel, said, "Sisters, what is the power of this jewel?" The kinnara maidens replied as before.

children.text: supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛbhaginīduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya tṛtīyāt kinnaranagarāt pratiniṣkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, having instructed those kinnara maidens with a discourse on <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching), having made them accept it, stirred them up, gladdened them, and conversed with them as with mothers, sisters, and daughters, departed from the third city of kinnaras.

children.text: adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāhaścaturthaṃ catūratnamayaṃ kinnaranagaram ārāmodyānaprāsādadevakulapuṣkariṇītaḍāgasuvibhaktarathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇasuracitagandhojjvalaṃ nānāgītavāditayuvatimadhurasvaravajravaiḍūryaśātakumbhamayaprākāratoraṇopaśobhitam ||
children.translated_text: The great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> saw a fourth city of kinnaras made of four jewels: it had parks, pleasure groves, mansions, temples, lotus ponds, and tanks; its roads, streets, crossroads, squares, and market places were well laid out; it was bright with arranged perfumes, sweet with various songs, music, and the voices of young women, and adorned with ramparts and gateways made of diamond, vaiḍūrya, and gold.

children.text: dvāraṃ trirākoṭayati ||
children.translated_text: He knocked three times at the gate.

children.text: tataḥ supriyeṇa sārthavāhena trirākoṭite dvāre dvātriṃśat kinnarakanyā nirgatāḥ tāsāṃ pūrvikāṇāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca darśanīyatarāścāpsarasaḥ pratispardhinyaḥ śatasahasraśobhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> had knocked three times at the gate, thirty-two kinnara maidens came out, more beautiful and more lovely to behold than the former ones, rivaling apsarases and adorned with a hundred thousand splendors.

children.text: tā apyevamāhuḥ etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They too said this: "Let the great caravan leader come."

children.text: svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāhāya ||
children.translated_text: "Welcome to the great caravan leader."

children.text: asmākam asvāmikānāṃ svāmī bhava apatīnāṃ patir alayanānāṃ layano 'dvīpānāṃ dvīpo 'śaraṇānāṃ śaraṇo 'trāṇānāṃ trāṇo 'parāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Be the master of us who have no master, the husband of us who have no husband, the abode of us who have no abode, the island of us who have no island, the refuge of us who have no refuge, the protection of us who have no protection, and the final resort of us who have no final resort."

children.text: imāni ca te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi śayanagṛhāṇyārāmaramaṇīyāni vanaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni ||
children.translated_text: "And these are your houses of food, houses of drink, houses of clothing, and houses of beds, lovely with parks, lovely with forests, and lovely with lotus ponds."

children.text: prabhūtāni ca jāmbudvīpakāni ratnāni tadyathā maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajataṃ jātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And there are abundant jewels from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, namely gems, pearls, vaiḍūrya, conch, stone, coral, silver, gold, aśmagarbha, musāragalva, lohitikā, and right-spiraling shells."

children.text: etāni ca te vayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "These are yours, and so are we."

children.text: asmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva ||
children.translated_text: "Sport with us, enjoy yourself, and let us attend upon you."

children.text: tatrāpi supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sūpasthitasmṛtistāḥ kinnarakanyā vividhairdharmapadavyañjanaiḥ paritoṣayāmāsa ||
children.translated_text: There too the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s>, his mindfulness well established, delighted those kinnara maidens with various words and expressions of <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching).

children.text: tuṣṭāśca tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ sarvāṅgairanuparigṛhya catūratnamayaṃ kinnaranagaramanupraveśya prāsādamabhiropya prajñapta evāsane niṣādayanti ||
children.translated_text: Pleased, those kinnara maidens took hold of the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> with all their limbs, led him into the city of kinnaras made of four jewels, brought him up into a mansion, and seated him on the prepared seat.

children.text: niṣaṇṇaḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho daśākuśalān karmapathān vigarhati daśa kuśalān karmapathān saṃvarṇayati subahvapi pralobhyamāno na śakyate skhalayitum ||
children.translated_text: Seated there, the great caravan leader <s>Supriya</s> condemned the ten unwholesome paths of action and praised the ten wholesome paths of action; though he was much tempted, he could not be made to stumble.

children.text: tuṣṭāśca tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ kathayanti āścaryam yatredānīṃ daharaśca bhavān dharmakāmaśca ||
children.translated_text: Pleased, those kinnara maidens said, "It is wonderful that now, though you are young, you are also one who loves <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching)."

children.text: na ca kāmeṣu sajjase vā badhyase vā ||
children.translated_text: "And you neither cling to sensual pleasures nor become bound by them."

children.text: prabhūtaiśca ratnaiḥ pravārayanti ||
children.translated_text: They invited him with abundant jewels.

children.text: tā api dharmadeśanāvarjitāḥ saubhāsinikaṃ jāmbudvīpapradhānam anargheyamūlyam anantaguṇaprabhāvaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattane sarvasvabhūtaṃ ratnamanuprayacchanti ||
children.translated_text: They too, not left without a teaching of <s>dharma</s> (the Buddhist teaching), offered him a <s>saubhāsinika</s> jewel, foremost in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, priceless, of endless qualities and power, and constituting all the wealth in the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ ca kathayanti idamasmākaṃ mahāsārthavāha maṇiratnaṃ badareṇa bhrātrā kinnararājñā anupradattam asmin badaradvīpamahāpattane cihnabhūtamālakṣyabhūtaṃ maṇḍanabhūtaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Great caravan leader, this jewel of ours was given by our brother <s>Badara</s>, king of the kinnaras. In this great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> it serves as a sign, a distinguishing mark, and an ornament."

children.text: tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ kathayati asya ratnasya ko 'nubhāva iti tāḥ kathayanti yatkhalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāḥ idaṃ maṇiratnaṃ tadeva poṣadhoṣito dhvajāgre baddhvā āropya kṛtsne jambudvīpe ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ karaṇīyam śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpanivāsinaḥ strīmanuṣyāḥ yuṣmākam yo yenārthī upakaraṇaviśeṣeṇa hiraṇyena vā suvarṇena vā ratnena vā annena vā pānena vā vastreṇa vā bhojanena vā alaṃkāraviśeṣeṇa vā dvipadena vā catuṣpadena vā vāhanena vā yānena vā dhanena vā dhānyena vā sa cittamutpādayatu vacanaṃ ca niścārayatu ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, said, "What is the power of this jewel?" They said, "Know, great caravan leader: after this jewel has been proclaimed on the <s>poṣadha</s> day, it should be tied to the top of a banner and raised, and a bell proclamation should be made throughout all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>: 'Let the women and men dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> hear. Whatever each of you needs by way of special equipment, whether silver, gold, jewels, food, drink, clothing, meals, special ornaments, bipeds, quadrupeds, vehicles, conveyances, wealth, or grain, let him form the thought and utter the words.'"

children.text: sahacittotpādādvāgniścāraṇena ca yathepsitāścopakaraṇaviśeṣā asya ratnasyānubhāvādākāśādavatariṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: "As soon as the thought is formed and the words are uttered, the desired special equipment will descend from the sky through the power of this jewel."

children.text: ayaṃ tu prativiśeṣaḥ yāni cāsya lokasya bhavanti mahābhayāni tadyathā rājato vā caurato vā agnito vā udakato vā manuṣyato vā amanuṣyato vā siṃhato vā vyāghrato vā dvipatarakṣuto vā yakṣarākṣasapretapiśācakumbhāṇḍapūtanakaṭapūtanato vā ītayopadravo vā upasargo vā anāvṛṣṭirvā durbhikṣabhayāni vā asminnucchrite ratnaviśeṣe ima ītayopadravā na bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: "And this is its further distinction: whatever great dangers exist for this world, namely from kings, thieves, fire, water, human beings, nonhuman beings, lions, tigers, elephants or bears, or from yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas, or whatever calamity, affliction, disaster, drought, or fear of famine there may be, when this special jewel has been raised, these calamities and afflictions will not occur."

children.text: ityuktvā tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ saṃrādhayāmāsuḥ sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha nistīrṇāni mahāsamudraparvatanadīkāntārāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, those kinnara maidens honored <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader: "Good, good, great caravan leader. The great oceans, mountains, rivers, and wildernesses have been crossed.

children.text: pūritā te dṛḍhasupratijñā ||
children.translated_text: Your firm and excellent vow has been fulfilled.

children.text: saphalīkṛtā te śraddhā ||
children.translated_text: Your faith has been made fruitful.

children.text: te gopitānīndriyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Your senses have been guarded.

children.text: sādhitā badaradvīpamahāpattanayātrā ||
children.translated_text: The journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> has been accomplished.

children.text: adhigataṃ te sarvajanamanorathasampādakaṃ jambudvīpapradhānaṃ ratnaviśeṣam ||
children.translated_text: You have obtained the foremost special jewel of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, which fulfills the desires of all people.

children.text: api tu yena tvaṃ pathenāgataḥ amanuṣyāstāvat pralayaṃ gaccheyuḥ prāgeva manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But on the path by which you came, nonhuman beings would meet destruction, much more human beings.

children.text: anyadeva vayaṃ sanmārgaṃ vyapadekṣyāmaḥ kṣipraṃ vārāṇasīgamanāya ||
children.translated_text: We will indicate a different good path for going quickly to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: tacchṛṇu manasi kuru bhāṣiṣyāmaḥ itaḥ paścime digbhāge sapta parvatānatikramya mahāparvata uccaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Listen to this and keep it in mind; we shall speak. From here, in the western quarter, after crossing seven mountains, there is a high great mountain.

children.text: tasmin parvate lohitākṣo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati raudraḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On that mountain dwells a rākṣasa named <s>Lohitākṣa</s>, fierce and taking the lives of others.

children.text: sa ca parvato 'manuṣyāvacaritaḥ kṛṣṇamandhakāraṃ savisphuliṅgaṃ vāyuṃ mokṣayati ||
children.translated_text: That mountain is frequented by nonhuman beings and releases a wind that is black darkness and full of sparks.

children.text: tatra te etadeva ratnaṃ dhvajāgre 'varopayitvā gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: There you must go after lowering this very jewel onto the top of the banner.

children.text: ratnaprabhāvācca te ītayo vilayaṃ gamiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: By the power of the jewel, those calamities will disappear.

children.text: mahāparvatamatikramya aparaparvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing the great mountain, there is another mountain.

children.text: tasmin parvate 'gnimukho nāgaḥ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: On that mountain dwells a nāga named <s>Agnimukha</s>.

children.text: sa tava gandhamāghrāya sapta rātriṃdivasānyaśaniṃ pātayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Having smelled your scent, he will cause thunderbolts to fall for seven days and nights.

children.text: tatra ratnaguhāṃ samanviṣya praveṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: There you must search out and enter a jewel cave.

children.text: saptarātrasya cātyayādduṣṭanāgaḥ svapiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: After seven nights have passed, the wicked nāga will fall asleep.

children.text: śayite duṣṭanāge parvatamadhiroḍhavyam ||
children.translated_text: When the wicked nāga is asleep, the mountain must be climbed.

children.text: tatra drakṣyasi samaṃ bhūmipradeśamakṛṣṭoptaṃ ca taṇḍulaphalaśālim akaṇakamatuṣaṃ śuciṃ niṣpūtigandhikaṃ caturaṅgulaparyavanaddham ||
children.translated_text: There you will see a level stretch of ground, bearing rice-grain fruit without being ploughed or sown, without awns or husks, pure, free from bad smell, and wrapped around to the measure of four finger-breadths.

children.text: yastamaṣṭamyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ vā bālāho'śvarājaḥ paribhujya sukhī arogo balavān prīṇitendriyaḥ pūrvakāyamabhyunnamayyodānamudānayati kaḥ pāragāmī kaḥ pāragāmī kaṃ pāraṃ nayāmi svastikṣemābhyāṃ jambudvīpamanuprāpayāmi sa tvayopasaṃkramya idaṃ syādvacanīyam ahaṃ pāragāmī māṃ pāraṃ naya māṃ svastikṣemābhyāṃ vārāṇasīmanuprāpaya ||
children.translated_text: After eating that on the eighth or fifteenth lunar day, <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king, happy, healthy, strong, and with his senses satisfied, raises the front part of his body and utters this solemn utterance: 'Who is going across? Who is going across? Whom shall I carry across and bring safely and securely to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?' You should approach him and say these words: 'I am going across. Carry me across. Bring me safely and securely to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.'"

children.text: atha sa supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya yathoddiṣṭena mārgeṇa yathoktena vidhinā anupūrveṇa taṃ bhūmipradeśamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, instructed, urged, encouraged, and delighted those kinnara maidens with a discourse in accordance with <s>dharma</s> (the teaching), exchanged friendly words with them as with mothers and daughters, and by the indicated path and the stated method, step by step, reached that stretch of ground.

children.text: sa ca bālāho'śvarājaścarannevamāha kaḥ pāragāmī kaḥ pāragāmī kaṃ pāraṃ nayāmi svastikṣemābhyāṃ jambudvīpamanuprāpayāmi tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho yena bālāho 'śvarājastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king, while roaming about, said in this way: "Who is going across? Who is going across? Whom shall I carry across and bring safely and securely to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?" Then <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, approached <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king.

children.text: upasaṃkramya ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bālāho 'śvarājastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bālāhamaśvarājamidamavocat ahaṃ pāragāmī ahaṃ pāragāmī naya mām ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king, and said this to <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king: "I am going across. I am going across. Carry me.

children.text: svastikṣemābhyāṃ vārāṇasīmanuprāpaya ||
children.translated_text: Bring me safely and securely to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>."

children.text: evamukte bālāho 'śvarājaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat na te mahāsārthavāha mama pṛṣṭhādhirūḍhena diśo nāvalokayitavyāḥ nimīlitākṣeṇa te stheyam ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king, said this to <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader: "Great caravan leader, when you have mounted on my back, you must not look toward the directions. You must remain with your eyes closed."

children.text: ityuktvā bālāho'śvarājaḥ pṛṣṭhamupanāmayati ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Bālāha</s>, the horse-king, lowered his back.

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāho bālāhasyāśvarājasya pṛṣṭhamadhiruhya yathānuśiṣṭo 'lpaiśca kṣaṇalavamuhūrtairvārāṇasīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, mounted the back of <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, and, as he had been instructed, reached <s>Vārāṇasī</s> in a few instants, moments, and muhūrtas.

children.text: sva udyāne 'vataritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He alighted in his own garden.

children.text: avatīrya supriyo mahāsārthavāho bālāhāśvarājapṛṣṭhād bālāhāśvarājaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya pādābhivandanaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Having descended from the back of <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, circumambulated <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, three times and bowed down at his feet.

children.text: tato bālāho 'śvarājaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ saṃrādhayāmāsa sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, congratulated <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader: "Good, good, great caravan leader.

children.text: nistīrṇāni te mahāsamudraparvatanadīkāntārāṇi ||
children.translated_text: You have crossed the great oceans, mountains, rivers, and wildernesses.

children.text: pūritā te dṛḍhapratijñā ||
children.translated_text: Your firm vow has been fulfilled.

children.text: saphalīkṛtaste 'dhvā ||
children.translated_text: Your journey has been made fruitful.

children.text: gopitānīndriyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Your senses have been guarded.

children.text: sādhitā te badaradvīpamahāpattanayātrā ||
children.translated_text: Your journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> has been accomplished.

children.text: adhigataste sarvajanamanorathasampādako jambudvīpasya pradhāno ratnaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You have obtained the chief special jewel of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, which fulfills the wishes of all people.

children.text: evaṃ hi parahitārthamabhyudyatāḥ kurvanti sattvaviśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For beings of special quality who have risen up for the welfare of others act in just this way."

children.text: ityuktvā bālāho 'śvarājaḥ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, departed.

children.text: athāciraprakrānte bālāhe 'śvarājani supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ svagṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, not long after <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, had departed, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, entered his own house.

children.text: aśrauṣurvārāṇasīnivāsinaḥ paurā brahmadattaśca kāśirājaḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ pūrṇena varṣaśatena saṃsiddhayātraḥ pūrṇamanorathaḥ svagṛhamanuprāpta iti ||
children.translated_text: The citizens living in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, and <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, heard: "<s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, after a full hundred years, has completed his journey, fulfilled his wish, and returned to his own home."

children.text: śrutvā ca punarbrahmadattaḥ kāśirāja ānanditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when he heard this, <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, was delighted.

children.text: pauravargaḥ supriyaṃ sārthavāhaṃ saṃrādhayāmāsa ||
children.translated_text: The body of citizens congratulated <s>Supriya</s>, the caravan leader.

children.text: aśrauṣīt tat pūrvakaṃ caurasahasramanyaśca jano dhanārthī supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ saṃsiddhayātraḥ paripūrṇamanoratha āgata iti ||
children.translated_text: That former thousand thieves and other people seeking wealth heard: "<s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, has completed his journey, fulfilled his wish, and come back."

children.text: srutvā ca punarupasaṃkramya supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocan parikṣīṇadhanāḥ sma iti ||
children.translated_text: And when they heard this, they approached <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, and said this: "Our wealth is exhausted."

children.text: evamukte mahāsārthavāhastān sarvān maitreṇa cakṣuṣā vyavalokya vijñāpayati gacchantu bhavantaḥ svakasvakeṣu vijiteṣu ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, the great caravan leader looked upon them all with eyes of loving-kindness and informed them: "Go, sirs, to your own respective territories.

children.text: yo yenārthī upakaraṇaviśeṣeṇa bhavati sa tasyārthe cittamutpādayatu vācaṃ ca niścārayatu ||
children.translated_text: Whatever particular kind of resource anyone needs, let him direct his mind toward that object and utter the words."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, they departed again.

children.text: atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhastadeva poṣadhe pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnāta upoṣadhoṣito yattatprathamalabdhaṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre āropya vācaṃ ca niścārayati yojanasahasrasāmantakena yathepsitāni sattvānāmupakaraṇānyutpadyante sahābhidhānācca yo yenārthī tasya tadvarṣaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then, on that very <s>poṣadha</s> day, the fifteenth, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, having bathed his head and observed the fast, raised on the top of a banner the jewel-gem that he had first obtained and uttered these words: "Within a thousand yojanas around, let the desired resources of beings arise; and immediately upon their being named, whatever anyone needs, let that rain down for him."

children.text: tataḥ paripūrṇamanorathāste sattvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those beings had their wishes completely fulfilled.

children.text: taccaurasahasraṃ supriyeṇa mahāsārthavāhena daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That thousand thieves was established by <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, in the ten wholesome paths of action.

children.text: atrāntarāt kālagate brahmadatte kāśirājani paurāmātyaiḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho rājābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, when <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, had died, <s>Supriya</s>, the great caravan leader, was consecrated with the royal consecration by the citizens and ministers.

children.text: mahābhiṣiktena supriyeṇa mahārājñā dvitīyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre āropya pūrvavidhinā dviyojanasahasrasāmantakena yathepsitāni sattvānāmupakaraṇānyutpadyantāmiti sahābhidhānācca yo yenārthī tasya tadvarṣati ||
children.translated_text: After <s>Supriya</s> had been consecrated as great king, he raised the second jewel-gem on the top of a banner and, by the former procedure, declared: "Within two thousand yojanas around, let the desired resources of beings arise." And immediately upon their being named, whatever anyone needed rained down for him.

children.text: tṛtīyena maṇiratnena yathoktena vidhinā dhvajāgrocchritena yathepsitopakaraṇaviśeṣavarṣaṇāni sampannāni ||
children.translated_text: With the third jewel-gem, raised on the top of the banner according to the stated procedure, rains of the particular resources desired were brought about.

children.text: evaṃ triyojanasahasrasāmantakenopakaraṇaiḥ strīmanuṣyāḥ saṃtarpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, within three thousand yojanas around, women and men were satisfied with resources.

children.text: tato 'nupūrveṇa jambudvīpaiśvaryabhūtena supriyeṇa mahārājñā tadeva poṣadhe pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnātenopoṣadhoṣitena kṛtsne jambudvīpe ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā upakaraṇotpannābhilāṣiṇāṃ strīmanuṣyāṇāṃ jambudvīpanivāsinām yanmaṇiratnaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasarvasvabhūtam yathepsitam sarvopakaraṇavarṣiṇaṃ dhvajāgre āropayāmāsa ||
children.translated_text: Then, in due course, when the great king <s>Supriya</s> had become lord of the sovereignty of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, on that very <s>poṣadha</s> day, the fifteenth, having bathed his head and observed the fast, he had a bell proclamation made throughout all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. For the women and men living in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who desired the arising of resources, he raised on the top of a banner the jewel-gem that was the whole wealth of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, the foremost jewel that rained every resource desired.

children.text: samanantaraṃ dhvajāgrāvaropite tasmiñ jambudvīpapradhānamaṇiratne kṛtsno jambudvīpanivāsī mahājanakāyo yathepsitairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ saṃtarpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Immediately, when that foremost jewel-gem of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> had been mounted on the top of the banner, the whole great mass of people living in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was satisfied with the particular resources they desired.

children.text: upakaraṇasaṃtarpitaśca jambudvīpanivāsī janakāyaḥ supriyeṇa rājñā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the mass of people living in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, satisfied with resources, was established by King <s>Supriya</s> in the ten wholesome paths of action.

children.text: tato jyeṣṭhaṃ kumāraṃ rājyaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpya rājarṣibrahmacaryaṃ caritvā caturo brāhmān vihārān bhāvayitvā kāmeṣu kāmacchandaṃ prahāya tadbahulavihārī brahmalokasabhāgatāyāṃ copapanno mahābrahmā saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after installing his eldest prince in the rule, sovereignty, and lordship of the kingdom, he practiced the celibate conduct of a royal sage, cultivated the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes), abandoned desire for sensual pleasures, lived mostly in that state, and was reborn in fellowship with the <s>Brahmaloka</s>; he became <s>Mahābrahmā</s>.

children.text: bhagavānāha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau supriyo nāma mahāsārthavāhaḥ ahameva tena kālena tena samayena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ vartitavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? The one who was then the great caravan leader named <s>Supriya</s> was I myself; at that time, on that occasion, I was engaged in bodhisattva conduct.

children.text: yattaccaurasahasram etadeva bhikṣusahasram ||
children.translated_text: That thousand thieves is this very thousand monks.

children.text: yā sā pūrvadevatā kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddho bodhisattvabhūtaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: That former deity was <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, when he was in the state of a bodhisattva at that time, on that occasion."

children.text: yaścāsau magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ eṣa eva śāriputro bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the one who was <s>Magha</s>, the great caravan leader, was this very monk <s>Śāriputra</s> at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: yaścāsau nīlādo nāma mahāyakṣaḥ eṣa evānando bhikṣustena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the one who was the great yakṣa named <s>Nīlāda</s> was this very monk <s>Ānanda</s> at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: yaścāsau candraprabho yakṣaḥ eṣa evāniruddho bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the one who was the yakṣa <s>Candraprabha</s> was this very monk <s>Aniruddha</s> at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: yaścāsau lohitākṣo nāma mahāyakṣaḥ sa eṣa eva devadattastena kalena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the one who was the great yakṣa named <s>Lohitākṣa</s> was this very <s>Devadatta</s> at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: yaścāsau agnimukho nāma nāgaḥ eṣa eva māraḥ pāpīyān sa tena kalena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the one who was the nāga named <s>Agnimukha</s> was this very <s>Māra Pāpīyān</s> at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: yaścāsau bālāho 'śvarājaḥ maitreyo bodhisattvastena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the one who was <s>Bālāha</s>, the king of horses, was <s>Maitreya</s> the bodhisattva at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: tadā tāvanmayā bhikṣavo dṛḍhapratijñena pratijñāpūraṇārthaṃ saptavārāṃścaurasahasrāt sārthaḥ paritrātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, monks, at that time, firm in my vow, for the sake of fulfilling the vow, I rescued the caravan seven times from a thousand thieves.

children.text: aparituṣṭāṃśca caurān viditvā dṛḍhapratijñā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: And when I knew that the thieves were not satisfied, a firm vow was made.

children.text: kṛtvā cānekairduṣkaraśatasahasrair badaradvīpamahāpattanasya yātrāṃ sādhayitvā caurasahasrapramukhaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jambudvīpaṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made it, and having accomplished the journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds, I satisfied the whole of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, headed by the thousand thieves, with wealth and established them in the ten wholesome paths of action.

children.text: idānīmapi mayā anekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairanuttaraṃ jñānamadhigamya maitrāyatā karuṇayā saptakṛtvaścaurasahasrasakāśāt sārthaḥ paritrātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even now, after attaining unsurpassed knowledge through many hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds, I have, with loving-kindness and compassion, rescued the caravan seven times from the presence of a thousand thieves.

children.text: aparituṣṭaṃ ca caurasahasraṃ viditvā yāvadāptaṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā atyantaniṣṭhe 'nuttare yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And knowing that the thousand thieves were not satisfied, I satisfied them with as much wealth as had been obtained and established them in the absolutely final, unsurpassed security from bondage, nirvāṇa.

children.text: anekāni ca devamanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi yakṣarākṣasapretapiśācakumbhāṇḍapūtanakaṭapūtanakoṭiśatasahasrāṇi śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni ||
children.translated_text: And many hundreds of thousands of gods and humans, and hundreds of thousands of crores of yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas, were established in going for refuge and in the training precepts.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 9
śrāvastyāṃ nidānam ||
children.translated_text: The occasion was at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena bhadraṃkare nagare ṣaḍ janā mahāpuṇyāḥ prativasanti meṇḍhako gṛhapatir meṇḍhakapatnī meṇḍhakaputro meṇḍhakasnuṣā meṇḍhakadāso meṇḍhakadāsī ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> there lived six people of great merit: the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant, and <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant.

children.text: kathaṃ meṇḍhako gṛhapatirjñāto mahāpuṇyaḥ sa yadi riktakāni kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi paśyati sahadarśanādeva pūryante ||
children.translated_text: How was the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> known as one of great merit? If he saw treasuries and granaries that were empty, at the very sight they became full.

children.text: evaṃ meṇḍhako gṛhapatirjñāto mahāpuṇyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> was known as one of great merit.

children.text: kathaṃ meṇḍhakapatnī sā ekasyārthāya sthālikāṃ sādhayati śatāni sahasrāṇi ca bhuñjate ||
children.translated_text: How was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife so? She prepares a cooking pot for the sake of one person, and hundreds and thousands eat.

children.text: evaṃ meṇḍhakapatnī ||
children.translated_text: Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife.

children.text: kathaṃ meṇḍhakaputraḥ tasya pañcaśatiko nakulako kaṭyāṃ baddhastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: How was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son so? A five-hundred-coin mongoose-purse remained tied at his waist.

children.text: sa yadi śataṃ sahasraṃ vā parityajati tadā pūrṇa eva tiṣṭhati na parikṣīyate ||
children.translated_text: If he gave away a hundred or a thousand, then it remained full and was not depleted.

children.text: evaṃ meṇḍhakaputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son.

children.text: kathaṃ meṇḍhakasnuṣā sā ekasyārthāya gandhaṃ sampādayati śatasahasrasya paryāptirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: How was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law so? She prepares perfume for the sake of one person, and it is sufficient for a hundred thousand.

children.text: evaṃ meṇḍhakasnuṣā ||
children.translated_text: Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law.

children.text: kathaṃ meṇḍhakadāsaḥ sa yadaikaṃ halasīraṃ kṛṣati tadā sapta sīrāḥ kṛṣṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: How was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant so? When he ploughs one furrow with the plough, seven furrows have been ploughed.

children.text: evaṃ meṇḍhakadāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant.

children.text: kathaṃ meṇḍhakadāsī mahāpuṇyā sā yadaikaṃ vastu rakṣati tatsaptaguṇaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: How was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant one of great merit? When she guards one property, it becomes sevenfold.

children.text: yadā ekamātraṃ pratijāgarti tadā sapta mātrāḥ saṃpadyante ||
children.translated_text: When she tends just one measure, seven measures are produced.

children.text: evaṃ meṇḍhakadāsī mahāpuṇyā ||
children.translated_text: Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant one of great merit.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgavipratihīnānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātrestrirdivasasya ṣaṭkṛtvo rātriṃdivasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kamahamapāyamārgādvyutthāpya svargaphale mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanupradadyām ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed the nature of the blessed Buddhas, who are greatly compassionate, who have crossed the four floods, whose soles are well established in the four bases of supernatural power, who have long been practiced in the four means of gathering disciples, who are not deficient in the five factors, who have passed beyond the five destinies, who are endowed with the six factors, who have fulfilled the six perfections, who are rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, who teach the eightfold path, who are skilled in the nine successive attainments, who are strong with the strength of the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and who are distinguished beyond those who rule over ten hundreds, that three times in the night and three times in the day, six times in a day and night, they survey the world with the Buddha-eye, and knowledge and vision arise: Who is declining? Who is prospering? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into hardship, danger, and distress? Who slopes toward the lower realms? Who inclines toward the lower realms? Who is weighted toward the lower realms? Whom shall I raise up from the path to the lower realms and establish in the fruit of heaven and in liberation? To whom, sunk in the mud of sensual desire, shall I extend a helping hand?

children.text: kamāryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayāmi kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya pakvāni vimocayeyam kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣurviśodhayeyam ||
children.translated_text: Whom, deprived of noble wealth, shall I establish in the lordship and sovereignty of noble wealth? Whose unplanted roots of goodness shall I plant? Whose planted roots shall I mature? Whose matured roots shall I liberate? Whose eyes, covered over by a mass of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: apyevātikramedvelāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the ocean, abode of makaras, might pass beyond its shore;

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velāmatikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha would not pass beyond the proper time for those to be trained, dear as calves.

children.text: sarvajñasaṃtānanivāsinī hi kāruṇyadhenur mṛgayatyakhinnā
children.translated_text: For the milk-cow of compassion, dwelling in the continuum of the Omniscient One, tirelessly seeks out

children.text: vaineyavatsān bhavadurganaṣṭān vatsān praṇaṣṭāniva vatsalā gauḥ ||
children.translated_text: the calves to be trained, lost in the difficult wilderness of becoming, like an affectionate cow seeking her calves that have strayed.

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati ayaṃ meṇḍhako gṛhapatiḥ saparivāro bhadraṃkare nagare prativasati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> perceived: "This householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, together with his household, lives in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: tasya vaineyakālaṃ pakvamiva gaṇḍaṃ śastrābhinipātamavekṣate ||
children.translated_text: For him the time for training has ripened, like an abscess awaiting the fall of the knife.

children.text: yannvahaṃ bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikām careyam ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to go on tour through the districts of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>?"

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate gaccha tvamānanda bhikṣūṇāmārocaya tathāgato bhikṣavo bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, announce to the monks: 'Monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will go on tour through the districts of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cartum sa cīvarakāṇi pratigṛhṇātu iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you is able to go on tour through the districts of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> together with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take up his robes.'"

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati tathāgata āyuṣmanto bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and announced to the monks: "Venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will go on tour through the districts of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caritum sa cīvarakāṇi pratigṛhṇātu iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you is able to go on tour through the districts of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> together with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take up his robes."

children.text: evamāyuṣmanniti te bhikṣava āyuṣmata ānandasya pratiśrutya pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchanti ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, venerable sir," those monks replied to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and they went along following one after another.

children.text: atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāraḥ vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭrigaṇaparivāraḥ haṃsarāja iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇa iva pakṣigaṇaparivṛtaḥ vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ deśika ivādhvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva paurajanaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaḥ cakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ candra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛtaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpākṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛtaḥ dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛtaḥ vemacitrir ivāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛtaḥ brahmeva brahmakāyikaparivṛtaḥ stimita iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jalanidhiḥ vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntairindriyair asaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇair aśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātro daśabhirbalaiścaturbhirvaiśāradyaistribhiḥ smṛtyupasthānairmahākaruṇayā ca ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, tamed and surrounded by the tamed, peaceful and surrounded by the peaceful, liberated and surrounded by the liberated, confident and surrounded by the confident, disciplined and surrounded by the disciplined, an arhat surrounded by arhats, free from passion and surrounded by those free from passion, pleasing and surrounded by the pleasing; like a bull surrounded by a herd of cows, like a lion surrounded by a troop of fanged beasts, like a royal swan surrounded by a flock of swans, like <s>Suparṇa</s> surrounded by birds, like a brahmin surrounded by pupils, like a skilled physician surrounded by the sick, like a hero surrounded by warriors, like a guide surrounded by travelers, like a caravan leader surrounded by merchants, like a guildmaster surrounded by townspeople, like a king of a fortress surrounded by ministers, like a wheel-turning king surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by gandharvas, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by kumbhāṇḍas, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by nāgas, like <s>Dhanada</s> surrounded by yakṣas, like <s>Vemacitra</s> surrounded by asuras, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by the thirty gods, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by the gods of <s>Brahmā</s>'s retinue; like a still ocean, like an ocean filled with water, like an elephant lord free from rut, with his senses well tamed, with the course of his deportment unshaken, his body resplendent with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks, endowed with the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three establishments of mindfulness, and great compassion;

children.text: evamanekaguṇagaṇasamanvāgato buddho bhagavāñ janapadacārikayā bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus the Buddha, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, endowed with such a multitude of qualities, set out on a tour through the country toward the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: yadā bhagavatā śrāvastyāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitam nirbhartsitā ānanditā devamanuṣyāḥ toṣitāni sajjanahṛdayāni tadā bhagnaprabhāvāstīrthyāḥ pratyantān saṃśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had displayed the great miracle at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, had rebuked and gladdened gods and humans, and had satisfied the hearts of good people, the tīrthikas (sectarian teachers), their influence broken, had taken refuge in the border regions.

children.text: tataḥ kecidbhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ gatvā avasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then some of them went to the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> and settled there.

children.text: taiḥ śrutaṃ śramaṇagautama āgacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: They heard, "The śramaṇa <s>Gautama</s> is coming."

children.text: śrutvā ca punarvyathitāste parasparaṃ kathayanti pūrvaṃ tāvadvayaṃ śramaṇena gautamena madhyadeśānnirvāsitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when they heard it, they were disturbed and said to one another, "First we were driven out of the Middle Country by the śramaṇa <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: sa yadīhāgamiṣyati niyatamito 'pi nirvāsayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: If he comes here, he will certainly drive us out from here as well.

children.text: tadupāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a plan must be devised."

children.text: te kulopakaraṇaśālā upasaṃkramya kathayanti dharmalābho dharmalābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They approached the houses of their lay supporters and said, "A gain in <s>dharma</s>! A gain in <s>dharma</s>!"

children.text: te kathayanti kimidam avalokitā gamiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They said, "What is this? We will look into it and go."

children.text: kasyārthāya dṛṣṭā asmābhiryuṣmākaṃ saṃpattiḥ yāvadvipattiṃ na paśyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "For what purpose have we seen your prosperity, if we do not also see your misfortune?"

children.text: āryakāḥ asmākaṃ vipattirbhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Noble ones, will there be misfortune for us?"

children.text: bhavantaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ kṣurāśaniṃ pātayannanekā aputrikā apatikāśca kurvannāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: "Gentlemen, the śramaṇa <s>Gautama</s> is coming, dropping a razor-like thunderbolt and making many women childless and husbandless."

children.text: āryāḥ yadyevam yasminneva kāle sthātavyaṃ tasminneva kāle 'smākaṃ parityāgas kriyate ||
children.translated_text: "Noble ones, if this is so, then at the very time when you ought to remain, you are abandoning us."

children.text: tiṣṭhata na gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: "Stay; do not go."

children.text: te kathayanti kiṃ vayaṃ na tiṣṭhāmaḥ na yūyamasmākaṃ śroṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Do we not stay? But you will not listen to us."

children.text: āryāḥ kathayata śroṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Noble ones, speak; we will listen."

children.text: te kathayanti bhadraṃkarasāmantakena sarvajanakāyamudvāsya bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ pravāsayata ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Evacuate the whole body of people from the vicinity of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> and send them into exile from the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: śādvalāni kṛṣata ||
children.translated_text: Plough up the grassy places.

children.text: sthaṇḍilāni pātayata ||
children.translated_text: Break down the dry resting grounds.

children.text: puṣpaphalavṛkṣaṃ chedayata ||
children.translated_text: Cut down the trees with flowers and fruit.

children.text: pānīyāni viṣeṇa dūṣayata ||
children.translated_text: Spoil the drinking waters with poison."

children.text: te kathayanti āryāḥ tiṣṭhata sarvamanutiṣṭhāma iti ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Noble ones, stay; we will carry out everything."

children.text: te 'vasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They remained there.

children.text: tatastairbhadraṃkaranagarasāmantakena sarvo janakāya udvāsya bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ pravāsitaḥ śādvalāni kṛṣṭāni sthaṇḍilāni pātitāni puṣpaphalavṛkṣāśchinnāḥ pānīyāni viṣadūṣitāni ||
children.translated_text: Then by those in the environs of the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>, the whole body of people was driven out and the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> was emptied; the grassy places were ploughed up, the level spaces were knocked down, the flowering and fruit-bearing trees were cut down, and the waters were poisoned.

children.text: tataḥ śakro devendraḥ saṃlakṣayati na mama pratirūpam yadahaṃ bhagavato 'satkāramadhyupekṣeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, reflected, "It is not fitting for me to overlook a failure of honor toward the Blessed One.

children.text: yena nāma bhagavatā tribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyairanekair duṣkaraśatasahasraiḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūryānuttarajñānamadhigatam sa nāma bhagavān sarvalokaprativiśiṣṭaḥ sarvavādavijayī śūnye janapade cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For the Blessed One, who over three incalculable kalpas fulfilled the six perfections by many hundreds of thousands of hardships and attained unsurpassed knowledge, that Blessed One, distinguished above the whole world and victorious over all doctrines, will now wander on his journey through an empty countryside.

children.text: yannvahaṃ bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya sukhasparśārthāya autsukyamāpadyeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: So then, for the sake of pleasant contact for the Blessed One together with the community of his disciples, I should bestir myself."

children.text: tena vātabalāhakānāṃ devaputrāṇāmājñā dattā gacchata bhadraṃkaranagarasāmantakena viṣapānīyāni śoṣayata iti ||
children.translated_text: He gave an order to the divine sons of the wind-clouds: "Go, and in the environs of the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> dry up the poisoned waters."

children.text: varṣabalāhakānāṃ devaputrāṇāmājñā dattā aṣṭāṅgopetasya pānīyasyāpūryateti ||
children.translated_text: He gave an order to the divine sons of the rain-clouds: "Fill them with water endowed with the eight qualities."

children.text: cāturmahārājikā devā uktāḥ yūyaṃ bhadraṃkarāṇāṃ janapadānāṃ vāsayateti ||
children.translated_text: The gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven were told, "You are to make the districts of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> inhabited."

children.text: tato vātabalāhakair devaputrairviṣadūṣitāni pānīyāni śoṣitāni varṣabalāhakaistānyeva kūpodapānavāpīsarastaḍāgānyaṣṭāṅgopetasya pānīyasya pūritāni ||
children.translated_text: Then the poisoned waters were dried up by the divine sons of the wind-clouds, and by the rain-clouds those very wells, water-holes, reservoirs, lakes, and ponds were filled with water endowed with the eight qualities.

children.text: cāturmahārājikairdevair bhadraṃkaranagarasāmantakaṃ sarvamāvāsitam ||
children.translated_text: By the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods the whole region around the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> was made inhabited.

children.text: janapadā ṛddhāḥ sphītāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The districts became rich and flourishing.

children.text: tīrthyair nagarajanakāyasametair avacarakāḥ preṣitāḥ gatvā paśyata kīdṛśā janapadā iti ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics, together with the body of citizens, sent out scouts, saying, "Go and see what the districts are like."

children.text: te gatāḥ paśyantyatiśayena janapadān ṛddhān sphītān ||
children.translated_text: They went and saw that the districts were exceedingly rich and flourishing.

children.text: tata āgatya kathayanti bhavantaḥ na kadācidasmābhirevaṃrūpā janapadā ṛddhāḥ sphītā dṛṣṭapūrvā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then they came back and said, "Sirs, never before have we seen districts so rich and flourishing."

children.text: tīrthyāḥ kathayanti bhavantaḥ vo yastāvadacetanān bhāvānanvāvartayati sa yuṣmānnānvāvartayiṣyatīti kuta etat sarvathā avalokitā bhavantaḥ apaścimaṃ vo darśanam gacchāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics said, "Sirs, if he can make even insentient things follow after him, will he not make you follow after him? How can this be otherwise? Sirs, you have been thoroughly seen through; this is your last sight of us. We are going."

children.text: te kathayanti āryāḥ tiṣṭhata kim yuṣmākaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ karoti so 'pi pravrajitaḥ yūyamapi pravrajitā bhikṣācarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Noble ones, stay. What can the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> do for you? He too is a renunciant, and you too are renunciants, living by alms.

children.text: kimasau yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣāṃ cariṣyatīti tīrthyāḥ kathayanti samayena tiṣṭhāmo yadi yūyaṃ kriyākāraṃ kuruta na kenacicchramaṇaṃ gautamaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Will he go begging alms for you?" The non-Buddhist ascetics said, "We shall stay on one condition: if you make an agreement that no one is to approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> to see him.

children.text: ya upasaṃkrāmati sa ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇo daṇḍya iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever approaches him is to be fined sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>."

children.text: taiḥ pratijñātaṃ kriyākāraśca kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They agreed, and the formal compact was made.

children.text: tato janapadacārikāṃ caran bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, while wandering on his tour through the districts, he arrived at the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: bhadraṃkare nagare viharati dakṣiṇāyatane ||
children.translated_text: He stayed in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>, at the southern sanctuary.

children.text: tena khalu samayena kapilavastuno brāhmaṇadārikā bhadraṃkare nagare pariṇītā ||
children.translated_text: At that time a brahmin girl from <s>Kapilavastu</s> had been married in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.

children.text: tayā prākārasthayā bhagavānandhakāre dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Standing on the rampart, she saw the Blessed One in the darkness.

children.text: sā saṃlakṣayati ayaṃ bhagavāñ śākyakulanandanaḥ śākyakulādrājyamapahāya pravrajitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She reflected, "This is the Blessed One, the delight of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, who left the kingdom of the <s>Śākya</s> clan and went forth.

children.text: sa idānīmandhakāre tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Now he is standing in the darkness.

children.text: yadyatra sopānaṃ syāt ahaṃ pradīpamādāyāvatareyamiti ||
children.translated_text: If there were a staircase here, I would take a lamp and go down."

children.text: tato bhagavatā tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya sopānaṃ nirmitam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing her thought with his mind, created a staircase for her.

children.text: tato hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditā pradīpamādāya sopānenāvatīrya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntā ||
children.translated_text: Then, thrilled, satisfied, and delighted, she took a lamp, descended by the staircase, and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ purastāt pradīpaṃ sthāpayitvā pādau śirasā vanditvā niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, she set the lamp before the Blessed One, bowed her head to his feet, and sat down to hear the <s>dharma</s> (teaching).

children.text: tato bhagavatā tasyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī pūrvavadyāvaccharaṇagatāmabhiprasannāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature, taught in such a way that she realized the four noble truths; as before, up to the point that she went for refuge and became full of faith.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstāṃ dārikāmidamavocat ehi tvaṃ dārike yena meṇḍhako gṛhapatistenopasaṃkrama upasaṃkramyaivaṃ madvacanādārogyāpaya evaṃ ca vada gṛhapate tvāmuddiśyāhamihāgataḥ tvaṃ ca dvāraṃ baddhvā sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said this to that girl: "Come, girl, go to the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>. Having approached him, ask after his health in my words, and say this: 'Householder, I have come here on your account, while you stand with your door shut.

children.text: yuktametadevamatitheḥ pratipattum yathā tvam pratipanna iti yadi kathayati gaṇena kriyākāraḥ kṛta iti vaktavyas tava putrasya pañcaśatiko nakulakaḥ kaṭyāṃ baddhastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Is it fitting to treat a guest in just the way you have done?' If he says, 'The group has made a compact,' you should say, 'Your son's five-hundred-valued mongoose-purse is standing tied at his waist.

children.text: sa yadi śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā vyayīkaroti pūryata eva na parikṣīyate ||
children.translated_text: If he spends a hundred or a thousand, it is replenished and does not become exhausted.

children.text: na śaknoṣi ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇaṃ dattvā āgantumiti evaṃ bhadanteti sā dārikā bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya samprasthitā ||
children.translated_text: Can you not come after paying sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>?'" "So be it, venerable sir," that girl replied to the Blessed One, and she set out.

children.text: yathāparijñātaiva kenacideva meṇḍhakasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: Just as she had understood, by some means she went to the presence of the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>.

children.text: gatvā ca kathayati gṛhapate bhagavāṃsta ārogyayati ||
children.translated_text: Having gone, she said, "Householder, the Blessed One asks after your health."

children.text: sa kathayati vande buddhaṃ bhagavantam ||
children.translated_text: He said, "I bow to the Buddha, the Blessed One."

children.text: gṛhapate bhagavānevamāha tvāmevāhamuddiśyāgataḥ tvaṃ ca dvāraṃ baddhvā avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Householder, the Blessed One says this: 'I have come on your account alone, while you stand with your door shut.'"

children.text: yuktametadevamatitheḥ pratipattum yathā tvaṃ pratipanna iti sa kathayati dārike gaṇena kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ na kenacicchramaṇaṃ gautamaṃ darśanāya upasaṃkramitavyam ||
children.translated_text: "It is proper for such a guest to be honored just as you have honored him." He says, "Girl, a formal agreement has been made by the assembly: no one is to approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> to see him.

children.text: ya upasaṃkrāmati sa gaṇena ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇo daṇḍya iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever approaches him is to be fined sixty kārṣāpaṇas by the assembly."

children.text: gṛhapate bhagavān kathayati tava putrasya pañcaśatiko nakulakaḥ kaṭyāṃ baddhastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: "Householder, the Blessed One says, 'A mongoose worth five hundred is tied at your son's waist.

children.text: sa yadi śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā vyayīkaroti pūryata eva na parikṣīyate ||
children.translated_text: If he spends a hundred or even a thousand, it is filled up again and is not depleted.

children.text: na śaknoṣi tvaṃ ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇaṃ dattvā āgantumiti sa saṃlakṣayati na kaścidetajjānīte ||
children.translated_text: Can you not come after paying sixty kārṣāpaṇas?'" He reflects, "No one knows this.

children.text: nūnaṃ sarvajñaḥ sa bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: Surely that Blessed One is omniscient.

children.text: gacchāmīti ||
children.translated_text: I will go."

children.text: sa ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇān dvāre sthāpayitvā brāhmaṇadārikopadiṣṭena sopānenāvatīrya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He placed sixty kārṣāpaṇas at the gate, descended by the stairway pointed out by the brahmin girl, and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the Dharma.

children.text: tato bhagavatā meṇḍhakasya gṛhapaterāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā meṇḍhakena gṛhapatinā yāvacchrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature of <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder, gave such a teaching of Dharma that led to the realization of the four noble truths, and, on hearing it, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder realized the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ kathayati bhagavan kimeṣo 'pi bhadraṃkaranagaranivāsī janakāya evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhīti bhagavānāha gṛhapate tvāmāgamya bhūyasā sarva eva janakāyo lābhīti ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the truth, he said, "Blessed One, is this body of people living in the city of <s>Bhadrakara</s> also capable of obtaining such dharmas?" The Blessed One said, "Householder, because of you, almost the whole body of people will obtain them."

children.text: tato meṇḍhako gṛhapatirbhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: svagṛhaṃ gatvā nagaramadhye kārṣāpaṇānāṃ rāśiṃ vyavasthāpya gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: After going to his own house, he arranged a heap of kārṣāpaṇas in the middle of the city and spoke a verse:

children.text: yo draṣṭumicchati jinaṃ jitarāgadoṣaṃ nirbandhamapratisamaṃ karuṇāvadātam
children.translated_text: "Whoever wishes to see the <s>Jina</s>, whose passion and hatred are conquered, unbound, unequaled, bright with compassion,

children.text: so 'niścareṇa hṛdayena suniścitena kṣipraṃ prayātu dhanamasya mayā pradeyam
children.translated_text: let him go quickly, with an unwavering and firmly resolved heart; his money is to be given by me."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke.

children.text: janakāyaḥ kathayati gṛhapate śreyaḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya darśanam sa kathayati śreyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The people said, "Householder, is seeing the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> a good thing?" He said, "It is good."

children.text: te kathayanti yadyevam gaṇenaivaṃ kriyākāraḥ kṛto gaṇa eva udghāṭayatu ||
children.translated_text: They said, "If so, since the assembly made this formal agreement, let the assembly itself abolish it."

children.text: ko 'tra virodhas te kriyākāramudghāṭya nirgantumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What opposition is there in this?" After abolishing the formal agreement, they began to go out.

children.text: tataḥ parasparaṃ saṃghaṭṭanena na śaknuvanti nirgantumiti vajrapāṇinā yakṣeṇa vineyajanānukampayā vajraḥ kṣiptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, because they were jostling one another and could not get out, the yakṣa <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, out of compassion for those to be trained, hurled his thunderbolt.

children.text: prākārasya khaṇḍaḥ patitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A section of the rampart fell down.

children.text: anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi nirgatāni kānicit kutūhalajātāni kānicit pūrvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni ||
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of living beings went out, some prompted by curiosity, some urged on by previous roots of merit.

children.text: te gatvā bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purato niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They went, bowed at the Blessed One's feet, and sat down before him.

children.text: yāvadbhagavataḥ sāmantakena parṣat saṃnipatitā ||
children.translated_text: At length an assembly gathered around the Blessed One.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstāṃ parṣadamabhyavagāhya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣadyānekasattvasaṃtānakuśalamūlasamāropikāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān yām śrutvā kaiścicchrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered that assembly and sat before the community of monks on the prepared seat, gave a teaching of Dharma that planted roots of merit in the continuities of many beings. Having heard it, some realized the fruit of stream-entry and some undertook refuge and the training precepts.

children.text: bhagavato 'ciraṃ dharmaṃ deśayato bhojanakālo 'tikrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While the Blessed One was teaching the Dharma, before long the meal time passed.

children.text: meṇḍhako gṛhapatiḥ kathayati bhagavan bhaktakṛtyaṃ kriyatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder said, "Blessed One, let the meal service be performed."

children.text: bhagavānāha gṛhapate bhojanakālo 'tikrānta iti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Householder, the meal time has passed."

children.text: sa kathayati bhagavan kimakāle kalpate bhagavānāha ghṛtaguḍaśarkarāpānakāni ceti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Blessed One, what is allowable at the improper time?" The Blessed One said, "Ghee, molasses, sugar, and drinks."

children.text: tato meṇḍhakena gṛhapatinā śilpina āhūya uktāḥ bhagavato 'kālakhādyakāni śīghraṃ sajjīkuruteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder summoned craftsmen and said, "Quickly prepare non-mealtime foods for the Blessed One."

children.text: tairakālakāni sajjīkṛtāni ||
children.translated_text: They prepared the allowable non-mealtime items.

children.text: tato meṇḍhakena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'kālakhādyakairakālapānakaiśca saṃtarpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with non-mealtime foods and non-mealtime drinks.

children.text: tato bhagavān meṇḍhakaṃ gṛhapatiṃ saparivāraṃ satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ karvaṭanivāsinaṃ janakāyam yathābhavyatayā vinīya prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having established <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder together with his retinue in the truths and having disciplined the people living in the market town according to their capacity, departed.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 10

bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kiṃ bhadanta meṇḍhakena meṇḍhakapatnyā meṇḍhakaputreṇa meṇḍhakasnuṣayā meṇḍhakadāsena meṇḍhakadāsyā karma kṛtam yena ṣaḍabhijñātā mahāpuṇyāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ bhagavato 'ntike satyāni dṛṣṭāni bhagavāṃścaibhirārāgito na virāgita iti bhagavānāha ebhireva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni ||
children.translated_text: The monks, having become doubtful, asked the Blessed One, the Buddha who cuts off all doubts, "Venerable sir, what karma was done by <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant, and <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant, such that they became possessed of the six superknowledges and great merit, saw the truths in the presence of the Blessed One, and pleased the Blessed One rather than displeased him?" The Blessed One said, "Monks, these very people performed and accumulated deeds, gathered the requisites, matured the conditions, and made them present like a flood; they were inevitably to come about."

children.text: ebhiḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: By these actions deeds have been done and accumulated; who else will experience them? No, monks, deeds that have been done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds that have been done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish, even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: when they have obtained the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsampannamakhilamakaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: Monks, in the past, in a former time, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled a kingdom that was rich, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, crowded with many people and human beings, free from sedition, quarrels, riots, uproars, thieves, and disease, endowed with rice, sugarcane, cows, and buffaloes, whole and without thorns.

children.text: ekaputramiva rājyaṃ pālayati ||
children.translated_text: He protected the kingdom as if it were an only son.

children.text: tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ naimittikairdvādaśavarṣikā anāvṛṣṭirvyākṛtā ||
children.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the diviners predicted a twelve-year drought.

children.text: trividhaṃ durbhikṣaṃ bhaviṣyati cañcu śvetāsthi śalākāvṛtti ca ||
children.translated_text: There would be a threefold famine: <s>cañcu</s>, <s>śvetāsthi</s>, and <s>śalākāvṛtti</s>.

children.text: tatra cañcu ucyate samudgake tasmin manuṣyā bījāni prakṣipya anāgate sattvāpekṣayā sthāpayanti mṛtānām anena te bījakāyaṃ kariṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>cañcu</s> is so called: in that little box people put seeds and set them aside out of concern for beings yet to come, thinking, 'With this they will make a seed-body for the dead.'

children.text: idaṃ samudgakaṃ baddhvā cañcu ucyate ||
children.translated_text: When this little box has been tied up, it is called <s>cañcu</s>.

children.text: śvetāsthi nāma durbhikṣam tasmin kāle manuṣyā asthīnyupasaṃhṛtya tāvat kvāthayanti yāvat tānyasthīni śvetāni saṃvṛttānīti ||
children.translated_text: The famine called <s>śvetāsthi</s> is this: at that time people collect bones and boil them until those bones have become white.

children.text: tatastatkvāthaṃ pibanti ||
children.translated_text: Then they drink that broth.

children.text: idaṃ śvetāsthi durbhikṣamityucyate ||
children.translated_text: This is called the <s>śvetāsthi</s> famine.

children.text: śalākāvṛttir nāma tasmin kāle manuṣyāḥ khalu bilebhyo dhānyaguḍakāni śalākayā ākṛṣya bahūdakasthālyāṃ kvāthayitvā pibanti ||
children.translated_text: The one called <s>śalākāvṛtti</s> is this: at that time people draw little grain pellets out of holes with a stick, boil them in a pot full of water, and drink them.

children.text: iyaṃ śalākāsambaddhatvācchalākāvṛttirityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because it is connected with a stick, this is called <s>śalākāvṛtti</s>.

children.text: tato rājñā brahmadattena vārāṇasyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam śṛṇvantu bhavanto vārāṇasīnivāsinaḥ paurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s> had a bell proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Let the citizens living in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> hear, sirs.

children.text: naimittikairdvādaśavarṣikā anāvṛṣṭirvyākṛtā śalākāvṛtti durbhikṣaṃ cañcu śvetāsthi ca ||
children.translated_text: The diviners have predicted a twelve-year drought and the famines called <s>śalākāvṛtti</s>, <s>cañcu</s>, and <s>śvetāsthi</s>.

children.text: yeṣāṃ vo dvādaśavarṣikaṃ bhaktamasti taiḥ sthātavyam ||
children.translated_text: Those of you who have food for twelve years should remain.

children.text: yeṣāṃ nāsti te yatheṣṭaṃ gacchantu ||
children.translated_text: Those who do not have it may go wherever they wish.

children.text: vigatadurbhikṣabhayāḥ subhikṣe punarapyupāgamiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: When the fear of famine has passed, they will come back again in a time of plenty.'

children.text: tasmiṃśca samaye vārāṇasyāmanyatamo gṛhapatirāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaparivāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there was a certain householder, wealthy, possessing great riches and great enjoyments, with an extensive retinue.

children.text: tena koṣṭhāgārika āhūya uktaḥ bhoḥ puruṣa bhaviṣyati me saparivārāṇāṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi bhaktamiti sa kathayati ārya bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: He summoned his steward and said, 'Sir, will there be food for me and my retinue for twelve years?' He replied, 'Noble sir, there will be.'

children.text: sa tatraivāvasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He remained right there.

children.text: samanantarānubaddhaṃ caitat durbhikṣam ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after that, this famine followed on continuously.

children.text: tasya kośakoṣṭhāgārāḥ parikṣīṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: His treasuries and granaries were exhausted.

children.text: sarvaśca parijanaḥ kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: All his attendants had died.

children.text: ātmanā ṣaṣṭho vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He remained with himself as the sixth.

children.text: tatastena gṛhapatinā kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi śodhayitvā dhānyaprastha upasaṃhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that householder cleared out the treasuries and granaries, and a prastha of grain was gathered.

children.text: so 'sya patnyā sthālyāṃ prakṣipya sādhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His wife put it in a cooking pot and cooked it.

children.text: asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya ||
children.translated_text: When Buddhas have not arisen, pratyekabuddhas arise in the world, compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, taking beds and food in remote places, the sole recipients of gifts for the world.

children.text: yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain pratyekabuddha, wandering on a circuit through the countryside, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: sa pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya vārāṇasīṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the forenoon he dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms.

children.text: sa ca gṛhapatirātmanā ṣaṣṭho 'vasthito bhoktum ||
children.translated_text: That householder, with himself as the sixth, was about to eat.

children.text: sa ca pratyekabuddho 'nupūrveṇa piṇḍapātamaṭaṃs tasya gṛhapater niveśanamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That pratyekabuddha, going for alms in order, reached the dwelling of that householder.

children.text: sa tena gṛhapatinā dṛṣṭaścittaprāsādikaḥ kāyaprāsādikaśca ||
children.translated_text: That householder saw him, inspiring serenity in mind and inspiring serenity in body.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ saṃlakṣayati etadapyahaṃ parityajya niyataṃ prāṇairviyokṣye yannvahaṃ svapratyaṃśamasmai pravrajitāya dadyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he reflected, 'Even after giving up this too, I shall certainly be separated from my life. What if I were to give my own share to this renunciant?'

children.text: tena bhāryā abhihitā bhadre yo mama pratyaṃśastamahamasmai pravrajitāyānuprayacchāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He said to his wife, 'Good woman, I am giving my share to this renunciant.'

children.text: sā saṃlakṣayati mama svāmī na paribhuṅkte kathamahaṃ paribhokṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: She reflected, 'My husband does not eat; how can I eat?'

children.text: sā kathayati āryaputra ahamapi pratyaṃśamasmai prayacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: She said, 'Noble son, I too give my share to him.'

children.text: evaṃ putreṇa snuṣayā dāsena dāsyā ca vicārya svasvapratyaṃśāḥ parityaktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, the son, the daughter-in-law, the male slave, and the female slave considered the matter and gave up their own respective shares.

children.text: tatastaiḥ sarvaiḥ sambhūya pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then all of them together honored the pratyekabuddha with the lump of alms.

children.text: kāyikī teṣāṃ mahātmanāṃ dharmadeśanā na vācikī ||
children.translated_text: For those great beings, the teaching of dharma is bodily, not verbal.

children.text: sa vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarāja upari vihāyasamudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like a king of geese with wings spread, he rose up into the sky above and began to perform miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and illuminating.

children.text: āśu pṛthagjanāvarjanakarī ṛddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Supernatural power swiftly wins over ordinary people.

children.text: te mūlanikṛttā iva drumāḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They fell at his feet like trees cut off at the root and began to make a vow.

children.text: gṛhapatiḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadi riktakāni kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi sahadarśanānme pūrṇāni syur evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The householder began to make an aspiration: "Since I have rendered service to such a true recipient of gifts, by this root of merit may my empty treasuries and granaries become full as soon as I see them; may I become one who obtains such dharmas; and, even more especially, may I please the Teacher, not displease him."

children.text: patnī praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhā yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekasyārthāya sthālīṃ paceyam sā śatenāpi paribhujyeta sahasreṇāpi na parikṣayaṃ gacchet yāvanmayā prayogo 'pratipraśrabdhaḥ ityevaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhinī syām prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
