children.translated_text: His wife began to make an aspiration: "Since I have rendered service to such a true recipient of gifts, by this root of merit, if I cook a pot for the sake of one person, may it be enjoyed even by a hundred, even by a thousand, and not be exhausted so long as my effort has not ceased. May I become one who obtains such dharmas, and, even more especially, may I please the Teacher, not displease him."

children.text: putraḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdho yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena pañcaśatiko nakulakaḥ kaṭyāmuparibaddhastiṣṭhet yadi ca śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā tato vyayaṃ kuryāt pūrṇa eva tiṣṭhet mā parikṣayaṃ gacchet evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The son began to make an aspiration: "Since I have rendered service to such a true recipient of gifts, by this root of merit may a five-hundred-valued mongoose-purse stand tied at my waist; and if one should spend a hundred or a thousand from it, may it remain full and not become exhausted. May I become one who obtains such dharmas, and, even more especially, may I please the Teacher, not displease him."

children.text: snuṣā praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhā yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekasya gandham yojayeyam śataṃ vā gandhaṃ ghrāsyati taṃ na ca parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuryāvanmayā apratipraśrabdham evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhinī syām prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The daughter-in-law began to make an aspiration: "Since I have rendered service to such a true recipient of gifts, by this root of merit, if I prepare fragrance for one person, may a hundred smell that fragrance, and may it not become exhausted so long as I have not stopped. May I become one who obtains such dharmas, and, even more especially, may I please the Teacher, not displease him."

children.text: dāsaḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekahalasīraṃ kṛṣeyam sapta sīrāḥ kṛṣṭāḥ syuḥ evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ ca lābhī syāṃ prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The male servant began to make an aspiration: "Since I have rendered service to such a true recipient of gifts, by this root of merit, if I plow one plow-strip, may seven strips be plowed. May I become one who obtains such dharmas, and, even more especially, may I please the Teacher, not displease him."

children.text: dāsī praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekāṃ mātrāmārabheyam sapta mātrāḥ saṃpadyeran evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ ca lābhinī syāṃ prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The female servant began to make an aspiration: "Since service has been rendered to such a true recipient of gifts, by this root of merit, if I begin with one measure, may seven measures be produced. May I become one who obtains such dharmas, and, even more especially, may I please the Teacher, not displease him."

children.text: taiścaivaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Thus they made their aspirations.

children.text: sa ca mahātmā pratyekabuddhasteṣāmanukampayā ṛddhyā upari vihāyasā rājakulasyopariṣṭāt samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that great-souled pratyekabuddha, out of compassion for them, set out through the sky by supernormal power, passing above the royal palace.

children.text: tena khalu samayena rājā brahmadatta upariprāsādatalagatastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: At that time King <s>Brahmadatta</s> was standing on the upper terrace of the palace.

children.text: tasya ṛddhyā gacchato rājño brahmadattasyopari chāyā nipatitā ||
children.translated_text: As he went by supernormal power, his shadow fell above King <s>Brahmadatta</s>.

children.text: sa ūrdhvamukho nirīkṣitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king began to look upward.

children.text: paśyati taṃ pratyekabuddham ||
children.translated_text: He saw that pratyekabuddha.

children.text: tasyaitadabhavat kasyāpyanena mahātmanā ṛddhimahālāṅgalairdāridryamūlānyutpāṭitāni ||
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "By this great-souled one, with the great ploughs of supernormal power, the roots of someone's poverty have been uprooted."

children.text: balavatī āśā ||
children.translated_text: Powerful indeed was the aspiration.

children.text: tato 'sau gṛhapatiḥ kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi pratyavekṣitumārabdho yāvatpūrṇāni paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Then that householder began to inspect his treasuries and granaries, and he saw that they were full.

children.text: sa patnīmāmantrayate mama tāvat praṇidhānaṃ pūrṇam yuṣmākamapīdānīṃ paśyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: He addressed his wife: "My aspiration, at least, has been fulfilled. Now let us see about yours as well."

children.text: tato dāsyā dhānyānāmekāṃ mātrāmārabdhvā parikarmayitum sapta mātrāḥ sampannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the female servant began to process one measure of grain, seven measures were produced.

children.text: patnyā ekasyārthāya sthālī sādhitā sarvais taiḥ paribhuktaṃ tathaivāvasthitā prātiveśyairanekaiśca prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ paribhuktam tathaivāvasthitā ||
children.translated_text: The wife prepared a pot for the sake of one person; all of them ate from it, and it remained just as before. The neighbors and many hundreds of thousands of living beings ate from it, and it remained just as before.

children.text: tathaiva putrasya snuṣāyā dāsasya praṇidhiḥ siddhā ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, the aspirations of the son, the daughter-in-law, and the male servant were fulfilled.

children.text: tato gṛhapatinā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritaṃ vārāṇasyām yo bhavanto 'nnenārthī sa āgacchatu iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder had a bell proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: "Good people, whoever has need of food, let him come."

children.text: vārāṇasyāmuccaśabdo mahāśabdo jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> a loud noise, a great noise, arose.

children.text: rājñā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: The king heard it.

children.text: kathayati kimeṣa bhavanta uccaśabdo mahāśabda iti amātyaiḥ samākhyātam deva amukena gṛhapatinā kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi udghāṭitānīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Good people, what is this loud noise, this great noise?" The ministers explained, "Your Majesty, such-and-such a householder has opened his treasuries and granaries."

children.text: rājā tamāhūya kathayati yadā eva lokaḥ kālagataḥ tadā tvayā kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇyudghāṭitānīti ||
children.translated_text: The king summoned him and said, "Only when the people had already perished did you open your treasuries and granaries?"

children.text: deva kasya kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇyudghāṭitāni api tu adyaiva me bījamuptamadyaiva phaladāyakamiti ||
children.translated_text: "Your Majesty, whose treasuries and granaries have been opened? Rather, today my seed was sown, and today it gives fruit."

children.text: rājā pṛcchati yathā katham sa etat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati ||
children.translated_text: The king asked, "How is that?" He reported the whole matter in detail.

children.text: rājā kathayati gṛhapate tvayā asau mahātmā piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ deva mayaiva pratipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "Householder, was that great-souled one satisfied with alms by you?" "Your Majesty, he was satisfied by me myself."

children.text: so 'bhiprasanno gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Deeply pleased, he spoke a verse:

children.text: aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam
children.translated_text: "Ah, a field made of virtues, free from all faults,

children.text: yatroptaṃ bījamadyaiva adyaiva phaladāyakam
children.translated_text: where a seed sown today gives fruit today itself."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau gṛhapatirgṛhapatipatnī gṛhapatiputro gṛhapatisnuṣā gṛhapatidāso gṛhapatidāsī ayameva meṇḍhako gṛhapatir meṇḍhakapatnī meṇḍhakaputro meṇḍhakasnuṣā meṇḍhakadāso meṇḍhakadāsī ca ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? That householder, the householder's wife, the householder's son, the householder's daughter-in-law, the householder's male servant, and the householder's female servant were precisely this <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant, and <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant.

children.text: yadebhiḥ pratyekabuddhe kārān kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam tasya karmaṇo vipākena ṣaḍ mahāpuṇyā jātāḥ mamāntike dṛṣṭasatyāni ||
children.translated_text: Because they rendered honors to the pratyekabuddha and made their vow, by the ripening of that karma they were born as six persons of great merit and saw the truths in my presence.

children.text: ahaṃ caibhiḥ pratyekabuddhakoṭiśatasahasrebhyaḥ prativiśiṣṭaḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And I, a teacher more excellent than hundreds of thousands of crores of pratyekabuddhas, was pleased by them, not displeased.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntaśuklaḥ vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, the result of deeds that are entirely black is entirely black; of deeds that are entirely white, entirely white; and of mixed deeds, mixed.

children.text: tasmāttarhi evaṃ śikṣitavyam yadekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you should train in this way: having rejected deeds that are entirely black, and mixed ones as well, effort should be made only in deeds that are entirely white.

children.text: ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, you should train.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 11
evaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard.

children.text: ekasmin samaye bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrairdhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairdevair nāgairasurairyakṣairgaruḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragairiti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavāñ jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vaiśālyāṃ viharati sma markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām ||
children.translated_text: At one time the Blessed One, honored, respected, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, citizens, guildmasters, caravan leaders, gods, nāgas, asuras, yakṣas, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus revered by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known, of great merit, a receiver of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was staying with the community of disciples at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, on the bank of the <s>Markaṭahrada</s>, in the <s>Kūṭāgāraśālā</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena vaiśālikā licchavaya idamevaṃrūpaṃ kriyākāramakārṣuḥ pañcadaśyāṃ bhavantaḥ pakṣasya aṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ ca prāṇino hantavyā yatkāraṇameyurmanuṣyā māṃsamanveṣanta iti ||
children.translated_text: At that time the <s>Licchavis</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s> made a rule of this kind: 'Sirs, on the fifteenth day of the fortnight, and on the eighth and fourteenth as well, living beings are to be killed, because people come looking for meat.'

children.text: tena khalu samayena anyatamo goghātako mahāntaṃ vṛṣabhamādāya nagarānniṣkramati praghātayitum ||
children.translated_text: At that time a certain cattle-butcher took a great bull and went out from the city in order to kill it.

children.text: tamenaṃ mahājanakāyaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddho māṃsārthī kathayati śīghramenaṃ vṛṣaṃ ghātaya vayaṃ māṃsenārthina iti ||
children.translated_text: A great crowd of people, wanting meat, followed him from behind and said, 'Quickly kill this bull. We need meat.'

children.text: sa kathayati evaṃ kariṣyāmi kiṃtu muhūrtamudīkṣadhvamiti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'I will do so, but wait a moment.'

children.text: tato vṛṣa īdṛśamanāryaṃ vaco duruktaṃ śrutvā bhītastrastaḥ saṃvigna āhṛṣṭaromakūpa itaścāmutaśca saṃbhrānto nirīkṣate cintayati ca ko māṃ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptamatrāṇamaśaraṇamiṣṭena jīvitenācchādayediti ||
children.translated_text: Then the bull, having heard such ignoble and harshly spoken words, was frightened, terrified, and agitated, the pores of his hair bristling; confused, he looked this way and that, and thought, 'Who could protect me, fallen into this painful, cramped, and constricted danger, without protection and without refuge, together with my beloved life?'

children.text: sa caivaṃ vihvalavadanastrāṇānveṣī tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: And he stood there with a distressed face, looking for protection.

children.text: bhagavāṃśca pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, in the forenoon, dressed himself, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms.

children.text: athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam ||
children.translated_text: Then the bull saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body shining with the eighty minor signs, adorned with a fathom-wide halo, with a radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: sahadarśanaiścāsya bhagavato 'ntike cittamabhiprasannam ||
children.translated_text: At the very sight of him, the bull's mind became serenely confident toward the Blessed One.

children.text: prasannacittaśca saṃlakṣayati prāsādiko 'yaṃ sattvaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With a serene mind he considered, 'This distinguished being is inspiring in appearance.

children.text: śakṣyatyeṣo mama prāṇaparitrāṇaṃ kartum ||
children.translated_text: He will be able to save my life.

children.text: yannvahamenamupasaṃkrameyamiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to approach him?'

children.text: atha sa vṛṣo bhagavatyavekṣāvān pratibaddhacitta eṣo me śaraṇamiti sahasaiva tāni dṛḍhāni varatrakāṇi bandhanāni chittvā pradhāvan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that bull, looking toward the Blessed One, his mind attached to him and thinking, 'This is my refuge,' suddenly broke those firm rope bonds and, running forward, approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramyobhābhyāṃ jānubhyāṃ bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya pādau jihvayā nileḍhumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he fell on both knees at the Blessed One's feet and began to lick his feet with his tongue.

children.text: sa cāsya raudrakarmā goghātakaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddha eva śastravyagrahastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that cattle-butcher of cruel deeds kept following him from behind, his hand occupied with a weapon.

children.text: tato bhagavāṃstaṃ raudrakarmāṇaṃ goghātakamidamavocat kuruṣva tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa anena govṛṣabheṇa sārdhaṃ sātmyam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said this to that cattle-butcher of cruel deeds: 'Good man, make an accommodation with this bull.

children.text: jīvitenāchādayeti ||
children.translated_text: Spare him his life.'

children.text: sa kathayati nāhaṃ bhadanta prabhavāmyenaṃ jīvitenāchādayitum ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'Venerable sir, I am not able to spare his life.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ mayā eṣa bahunā mūlyena krītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? I bought him for a high price.

children.text: putradāraṃ ca me bahu poṣitavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: And I have many children and a wife to support.'

children.text: bhagavānāha yadi mūlyaṃ dīyate pratimuñcasīti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'If the price is given, will you release him?'

children.text: sa kathayati pratimokṣyāmi bhagavanniti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'I will release him, Blessed One.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃllaukikacittamutpādayati aho bata śakro devendrastrīṇi kārṣāpaṇasahasrāṇyādāyāgacchediti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One produced a worldly thought: 'Ah, may <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, come bringing three thousand kārṣāpaṇas.'

children.text: sahacittotpādādbhagavataḥ śakro devendraḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasratrayamādāya bhagavataḥ purastādasthāt ||
children.translated_text: As soon as the Blessed One's thought arose, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, took three thousand kārṣāpaṇas and stood before the Blessed One.

children.text: atha bhagavāñśakraṃ devendramidamavocat anuprayaccha kauśika asya goghātakasya triguṇaṃ mūlyam ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'Give, <s>Kauśika</s>, to this cattle-butcher the threefold price.'

children.text: adācchakro devendrastasya goghātakasya kārṣāpaṇatrayasahasraṃ vṛṣamūlyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, gave three thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> to that cow-killer as the price of the bull.

children.text: atha goghātakaḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasratrayaṃ vṛṣamūlyaṃ gṛhītvā hṛṣṭastuṣṭaḥ pramudito bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā taṃ govṛṣaṃ bandhanānmuktvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the cow-killer, having taken the three thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> as the bull's price, joyful, satisfied, and delighted, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet, released that bull from bondage, and departed.

children.text: śakro devendro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā tatraivāntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and vanished right there.

children.text: atha govṛṣo gatapratyāgataprāṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā bhagavatyabhiprasanno bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddho bhagavato mukhaṃ vyavalokayamāno 'sthāt ||
children.translated_text: Then the bull, whose life had gone and returned, became even more deeply serene toward the Blessed One; having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, he followed close behind him and stood looking at the Blessed One's face.

children.text: atha bhagavān smitamakārṣīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One smiled.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātāḥ puṣparāgapadmarāgavajravaiḍūryamusāragalvārkalohitakādakṣiṇāvartaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavarṇā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: It is the rule that, when the buddhas, the blessed ones, reveal a smile, then rays colored blue, yellow, red, and white, and colored like <s>puṣparāga</s>, <s>padmarāga</s>, diamond, beryl, <s>musāragalva</s>, sunlight, red arsenic, right-turning conch, stone, coral, gold, and silver issue from their mouth: some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastādgacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvamutpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaparyantān narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣṇībhūtvā nipatanti ||
children.translated_text: Those that go downward reach the hells ending with <s>Sañjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall after becoming cool, and in the cold hells they fall after becoming warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante ||
children.translated_text: Through this the particular torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣāmevaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ āhosvidanyatropapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: They think, 'Sirs, have we passed away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati ||
children.translated_text: In order to produce serenity in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃ bhavati na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ nāpyanyatropapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that emanation, they think, 'Indeed, sirs, we have not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tvayamapūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti ||
children.translated_text: Rather, this is a being never seen before; through his power our particular torments have subsided.'

children.text: te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya tannarakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Having made their minds deeply serene toward the emanation, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭādgacchanti tāścāturmahārājakāyikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānabṛhānatapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhaparyantān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyudghoṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: Those that go upward reach the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> class, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and the gods as far as <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, and proclaim, 'Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self.'

children.text: gāthādvayaṃ bhāṣante ||
children.translated_text: They speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: Begin; go forth; apply yourselves in the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned birth and <s>saṃsāra</s> (wandering rebirth), will make an end of suffering.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, after wandering through the three-thousand great-thousand world system, follow the Blessed One himself, close behind him.

children.text: tadyadi bhagavānatītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastādantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyāmantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear in his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (departed spirit), they disappear in his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunorantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear in his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a powerful wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyāmantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear in his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict a disciple's awakening, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyāmantardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict an individual buddha's awakening, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft).

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyāmantarhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times and disappeared in the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with his hands joined in reverence, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A cluster, variegated with thousands of many kinds of colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around were illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises.

children.text: gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: And he speaks a verse:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: Buddhas, free from agitation, with dejection and pride abandoned, being the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s> who have conquered their enemies do not show without cause a smile white as conch and lotus fiber.'

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīrabuddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇajinendrakāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Having himself understood it at that very moment with steadfast wisdom, for the listeners who long for the Jina, the lord of ascetics,

children.text: dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, with firm, excellent, auspicious words remove the doubt that has arisen.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The protectors, the perfectly awakened ones, steady as the king of salt-water mountains, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ
children.translated_text: The crowds of people wish to hear the matter for the sake of which those steadfast ones show a smile.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhagavānāha evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, do not reveal a smile without cause and condition.

children.text: dṛṣṭaste ānanda ayaṃ govṛṣaḥ dṛṣṭo bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, have you seen this bull?" "I have seen it, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda govṛṣastathāgatasyāntike prasannacittaḥ saptame divase kālaṃ kṛtvā cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, this bull, with a mind made serene in the presence of the Tathāgata, will die on the seventh day and be reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.

children.text: vaiśravaṇasya mahārājasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will become a son of the great king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: tataścyutvā trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: After passing away from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: śakrasya devendrasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will become a son of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: tataścyutvā yāmeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: After passing away from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Yāma</s> gods.

children.text: yāmasya devasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will become a son of the god <s>Yāma</s>.

children.text: tataścyutvā tuṣiteṣu deveṣūpapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: After passing away from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods.

children.text: sa tuṣitasya devasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will become a son of the god <s>Tuṣita</s>.

children.text: tataścyutvā nirmāṇaratiṣu deveṣūpapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: After passing away from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods.

children.text: sunirmitasya devaputrasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will become a son of the divine prince <s>Sunirmita</s>.

children.text: tataścyutvā parinirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣūpapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: After passing away from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Parinirmitavaśavartin</s> gods.

children.text: vaśavartino devaputrasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will become a son of the divine prince <s>Vaśavartin</s>.

children.text: tadanayā saṃtatyā navanavatikalpasahasrāṇi vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Through that continuity he will not go to a state of ruin for ninety-nine thousand kalpas.

children.text: tataḥ kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu divyaṃ sukhamanubhūya paścime bhave paścime nikete samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe manuṣyatvaṃ pratilabhya rājā bhaviṣyati aśokavarṇo nāma cakravartī caturarṇavāntavijetā dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after experiencing divine happiness among the desire-realm gods, in his final existence, final abode, final body, and final attainment of an individual life, he will obtain human birth and become a king named <s>Aśokavarṇa</s>, a universal monarch, conqueror as far as the four oceans, righteous, a king of dharma, and endowed with the seven jewels.

children.text: tasyemānyevaṃrūpāṇi sapta ratnāni bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: He will have these seven jewels of such a kind:

children.text: tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam ||
children.translated_text: namely the jewel of the wheel, the jewel of the elephant, the jewel of the horse, the jewel of the gem, the jewel of the woman, the jewel of the householder, and the jewel of the counselor as the seventh.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: He will have a full thousand sons, brave, heroic, beautiful in their noble limbs, and crushers of hostile armies.

children.text: imāmeva samudraparyantāṃ mahāpṛthivīmakhilām akaṇṭakām anutpīḍām adaṇḍenāśastreṇa dharmyeṇa samayenābhinirjitya adhyāvatsyati ||
children.translated_text: Having conquered this entire great earth as far as the ocean, whole, free from thorns and oppression, without the rod and without weapons, by a righteous settlement, he will dwell over it.

children.text: so 'pareṇa samayena dānāni dattvā cakravartirājyamapahāya keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajya pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkariṣyati aśokavarṇo nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: At a later time, after giving gifts, abandoning the sovereignty of a universal monarch, shaving off his hair and beard, putting on saffron robes, and going forth properly in faith from home to homelessness, he will realize pratyekabodhi; he will become a pratyekabuddha named <s>Aśokavarṇa</s>."

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha kiṃ bhadanta anena govṛṣeṇa karma kṛtam yena tiryagyonāvupapannaḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam yena divyamānuṣasukhamanubhūya pratyekāṃ bodhimadhigamiṣyati bhagavānāha anenaiva ānanda govṛṣeṇa karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni ||
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with hands joined in reverence, asked the Blessed One, "Venerable sir, what karma was done by this bull, so that he was born in an animal womb? What karma was done, so that after experiencing divine and human happiness he will attain pratyekabodhi?" The Blessed One said, "<s>Ānanda</s>, this very bull performed and accumulated deeds, gathered the requisites, matured the conditions, and made them present like a flood; they were inevitably to come about.

children.text: govṛṣeṇa karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na hyānanda karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāśubhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Deeds have been done and accumulated by the bull; who else will experience them? For, <s>Ānanda</s>, deeds that have been done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds that have been done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatairapi
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish, even through hundreds of kalpas;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: when they have obtained the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvamānanda atīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, in the past, in a former time, ninety-one kalpas ago, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Vipaśyī</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One.

children.text: sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīmupaniśritya viharati anyatamasmin vanaṣaṇḍe ||
children.translated_text: He was dwelling near the capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>, in a certain forest grove.

children.text: tasya nātidūre ṣaṣṭibhikṣavaḥ prativasantyāraṇyakāḥ piṇḍapātikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not far from him there lived sixty monks, forest-dwellers and almsmen.

children.text: sarve ca vītarāgā vigatadveṣā vigatamohā yāvat pañcamātrāṇi dhūrtakaśatāni tena tenāhiṇḍyamānāni taṃ pradeśamanuprāptāni ||
children.translated_text: All were free from passion, free from hatred, and free from delusion. Then as many as five hundred rogues, wandering here and there, reached that region.

children.text: teṣāmetadabhavat ete hi pravrajitā mahātmāna īdṛśeṣu sthāneṣvabhiramante ||
children.translated_text: They thought, "These renunciants are surely great beings; they delight in places such as this.

children.text: yadyeṣāṃ jīvitopacchedaṃ na kariṣyāmaḥ na bhūya etasmin pradeśe svasthairvihartavyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: If we do not cut off their lives, we will no longer be able to live at ease in this region.

children.text: yadyapyete mahātmānaḥ sarvasattvahitodayapravṛttā na pareṣāmārocayiṣyanti tathāpyeṣāṃ pradhānapuruṣā upasaṃkramiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Although these great beings, intent on the welfare and benefit of all beings, will not report us to others, nevertheless the chief men will approach them.

children.text: te 'smākaṃ rājñaḥ samarpayiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: They will hand us over to the king.

children.text: tatrāsmābhiścārakāvaruddhairmartavyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: There we will die, shut up in prison."

children.text: kathamatra pratipattavyamiti ekastatraiva nirghṛṇahṛdayastyaktaparalokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'How is one to proceed in this matter?' There, one among them, ruthless-hearted and having abandoned concern for the next world,

children.text: sa kathayati aghātayitvā etān kutaḥ kṣema iti taiste jīvitādvyaparopitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, 'Without killing these people, how can there be safety?' And by them those people were deprived of life.

children.text: te caitatkarma kṛtvā pāpakamakuśalam ekanavatikalpān apāyeṣūpapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done this evil, unwholesome deed, they were reborn in the bad destinies for ninety-one eons.

children.text: yadbhūyasā tu narakeṣu tiryagyonau upapannāśca santo nityaṃ śastreṇa praghātitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the most part they were reborn in hells and in the animal womb, and, when they existed there, they were constantly struck down by weapons.

children.text: tatra yo 'sau caurasteṣāṃ samādāpakaḥ sa evāyaṃ govṛṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, the thief who was their instigator is this very bull.

children.text: tasya karmaṇo vipākena iyantaṃ kālaṃ na kadācit sugatau upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the result of that deed, for all this time he has never once been reborn in a good destiny.

children.text: yatpunaridānīṃ mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditam tasya karmaṇo vipākena divyaṃ mānuṣaṃ sukhamanubhūya pratyekāṃ bodhimadhigamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But now he has made his mind serene in my presence; as the result of that deed, after experiencing divine and human happiness, he will attain <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening).

children.text: evaṃ hi ānanda tathāgatānāṃ cittaprasādo 'pyacintyavipākaḥ kiṃ punaḥ praṇidhānam ||
children.translated_text: For thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, even serenity of mind toward the <s>Tathāgatas</s> has an inconceivable result; how much more, then, a vow.

children.text: tasmāttarhi ānanda evaṃ śikṣitavyam yatstokastokaṃ muhūrtamuhūrtamantato 'cchaṭāsaṃghātamātramapi tathāgatamākārataḥ samanusmariṣyāmītyevaṃ te ānanda śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, one should train in this way: 'Little by little, moment by moment, even for as much as the snap of the fingers, I shall recollect the <s>Tathāgata</s> by his form.' Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should train.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyānandyānumodya bhikṣūṇāṃ purastādgāthā bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, rejoicing in and approving the Blessed One's speech, recited verses before the monks:

children.text: aho nāthasya kāruṇyaṃ sarvajñasya hitaiṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, the compassion of the Protector, the omniscient one who seeks beings' welfare,

children.text: sukṛtenaiva vātsalyam yasyedṛśamahādbhutam ||
children.translated_text: whose affection, because of merit alone, is such a great wonder.

children.text: āpanno hi paraṃ kṛcchraṃ govṛṣo yena mocitaḥ
children.translated_text: For the bull, fallen into the utmost distress, was released by him,

children.text: vyākṛtaśca bhave divye pratyekaśca jino hyasau
children.translated_text: and he was prophesied to a divine existence; indeed he will be a solitary jina.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what had been spoken.

children.text: Chapter 12

sa bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrairdhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairdevair nāgairyakṣairasurairgaruḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragairiti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavāñjñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho divyānāṃ mānuṣyāṇāṃ ca bhagavānanupalipto viharati padmapatramivāmbhasā ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One was staying at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas. Thus the Buddha, the Blessed One, worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines for the sick, together with the community of disciples, dwelt unstained by things divine and human, like a lotus leaf by water.

children.text: tena khalu samayena rājagṛhe nagare ṣaṭ pūrṇādyāḥ śāstāro 'sarvajñāḥ sarvajñamāninaḥ prativasanti sma ||
children.translated_text: At that time in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> there lived the six teachers beginning with <s>Pūrṇa</s>, not omniscient but thinking themselves omniscient.

children.text: tadyathā pūrṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ maskarī gośālīputraḥ saṃjayī vairaṭṭīputraḥ ajitaḥ keśakambalaḥ kakudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ nirgrantho jñātiputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: They were, namely, <s>Pūrṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Saṃjayin Vairaṭṭīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s>.

children.text: atha ṣaṇṇāṃ pūrṇādīnāṃ tīrthyānāṃ kutūhalaśālāyāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām ayam evaṃrūpo 'bhūd antarākathāsamudāhāraḥ yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran yadā śramaṇo gautamo loke 'nutpannas tadā vayaṃ satkṛtāścābhūvan gurukṛtāśca mānitāśca pūjitāśca rājñāṃ rājamātrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ naigamānāṃ jānapadānāṃ śreṣṭhināṃ sārthavāhānām lābhinaścābhūvaṃścīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the six heterodox teachers beginning with <s>Pūrṇa</s> had sat down and gathered together in the debating hall, this sort of conversation arose among them: 'Sirs, you should know this: when the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> had not arisen in the world, we were honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, brahmins, householders, townsmen, country people, merchants, and caravan leaders, and we received robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines for the sick.

children.text: yadā tu śramaṇo gautamo loke utpannaḥ tadā śramaṇo gautamaḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājñāṃ rājamātrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ janapadānāṃ dhanināṃ śreṣṭhināṃ sārthavāhānām lābhī ca śramaṇo gautamaḥ saśrāvakasaṃghaścīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām ||
children.translated_text: But when the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> arose in the world, then the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> was honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, brahmins, householders, country people, wealthy men, merchants, and caravan leaders, and the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>, together with his community of disciples, received robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines for the sick.

children.text: asmākaṃ ca lābhasatkāraḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ samucchinnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And our gain and honor have been completely cut off in every way.

children.text: vayaṃ sma ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We are endowed with supernatural power and profess knowledge.

children.text: śramaṇo 'pi gautama ṛddhimāñjñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte ||
children.translated_text: The renunciant <s>Gautama</s> too declares himself to be endowed with supernatural power and to profess knowledge.

children.text: arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: It is proper for one who professes knowledge to display, together with another who professes knowledge, a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautamo 'nuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ dve ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, we will display two.

children.text: dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ catvāri ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays two, we will display four.

children.text: catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayamaṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays four, we will display eight.

children.text: aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, we will display sixteen.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ taddviguṇaṃ tattriguṇaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, we will display thirty-two; and as far as the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, we will display twice that and three times that.

children.text: upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu vayamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> come halfway along the road, and we too will go halfway along the road.

children.text: tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: There let us have, together with the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>, a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.'

children.text: atha mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhavat asakṛdasakṛnmayā śramaṇasya gautamasya parākrāntam na ca kadācidavatāro labdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One thought, 'Again and again I have made an effort against the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>, and never have I found an opening.

children.text: yannvahaṃ tīrthyānāṃ prahareyam ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to strike at the heterodox teachers?'

children.text: iti viditvā pūraṇavadātmānamabhinirmāya upari vihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā maskariṇaṃ gośālīputramāmantrayate yatkhalu maskariñjānīyā aham ṛddhimāñjñānavādī śramaṇo gautama ṛddhimāñjñānavādītyātmānaṃ parijānīte ||
children.translated_text: Having understood this, he fashioned himself in the form of <s>Pūraṇa</s>, rose upward into the sky, performed miracles of blazing, burning, raining, and flashing, and addressed <s>Maskarin Gośālīputra</s>: "Know this, <s>Maskarin</s>: I am possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernormal power) and claim knowledge. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> recognizes himself as possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and as a claimant of knowledge."

children.text: arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: A claimant of knowledge ought to display, together with a claimant of knowledge, a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati ahaṃ dve ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>, I will display two.

children.text: dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahaṃ catvāri ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, I will display four.

children.text: catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahamaṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, I will display eight.

children.text: aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahaṃ ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, I will display sixteen.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ taddviguṇamuttaraṃ manuṣyadharmam ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, I will display thirty-two; however many superhuman miracles of <s>ṛddhi</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, we will display twice as many further superhuman miracles of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu ahamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come half the way; I too will go half the way.

children.text: tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: There let there be for us, together with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: atha mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhavat asakṛdasakṛnmayā śramaṇasya gautamasya parākrāntam na ca kadācidavatāro labdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: "Again and again I have exerted myself against the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, but I have never obtained an opening."

children.text: yannvahaṃ tīrthyānāṃ prahareyam ||
children.translated_text: "What if I were to strike at the rival ascetics?"

children.text: iti viditvā maskarivadātmānamabhinirmāya upari vihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavidyotanavarṣaṇaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā saṃjayinaṃ vairaṭṭīputramāmantrayate yatkhalu saṃjayiñ jānīyā aham ṛddhimāñjñānavādī śramaṇo gautama ṛddhimāñ jñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte ||
children.translated_text: Having understood this, he fashioned himself in the form of <s>Maskarin</s>, rose upward into the sky, performed miracles of blazing, burning, flashing, and raining, and addressed <s>Saṃjayin Vairaṭṭīputra</s>: "Know this, <s>Saṃjayin</s>: I am possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and claim knowledge. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> declares himself to be possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and a claimant of knowledge."

children.text: arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: A claimant of knowledge ought to display, together with a claimant of knowledge, a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati ahaṃ dve ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>, I will display two.

children.text: dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahaṃ catvāri ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, I will display four.

children.text: catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahamaṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, I will display eight.

children.text: aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahaṃ ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, I will display sixteen.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ ahaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati ahaṃ taddviguṇamuttaraṃ manuṣyadharmaprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, I will display thirty-two; however many superhuman miracles of <s>ṛddhi</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, I will display twice as many further superhuman miracles.

children.text: upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu ahamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come half the way; I too will go half the way.

children.text: tatra me bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: There let there be for me, together with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: evamanyonyaṃ sarve viheṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way they were all harassed by one another.

children.text: ekaika evamāharddherlābhī nāhamiti ||
children.translated_text: Each one said, "He has obtained <s>ṛddhi</s>; I have not."

children.text: pūraṇādyāḥ ṣaṭ śāstāraḥ sarvajñajñānino yena rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastenopasaṃkrāman ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the others, the six teachers, claimants to omniscient knowledge, approached the Magadhan king <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāramidamavocan yatkhalu deva jānīyā vayam ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they said this to the Magadhan king <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>: "Know this, Your Majesty: we are possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and claim knowledge."

children.text: śramaṇo 'pi gautama ṛddhimāñjñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte ||
children.translated_text: "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> also declares himself to be possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and a claimant of knowledge."

children.text: arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: A claimant of knowledge ought to display, together with a claimant of knowledge, a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ dve ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>, we will display two.

children.text: dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ catvāri ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, we will display four.

children.text: catvāri śramaṇo gautamo vayamaṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, we will display eight.

children.text: aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, we will display sixteen.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ taddviguṇaṃ tattriguṇam ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, we will display thirty-two; however many superhuman miracles of <s>ṛddhi</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, we will display twice and three times as many miracles of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu vayamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come half the way; we too will go half the way.

children.text: tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: There let it be for us, together with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, to display a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: evamukte rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastīrthyānidamavocat yūyamapi śavā bhūtvā bhagavatā sārdham ṛddhiṃ prārabhadhve atha pūraṇādyāḥ ṣaṭ śāstāro 'sarvajñāḥ sarvajñajñānino 'rdhamārge rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ vijñāpayanti vayaṃ smo deva ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Magadhan king <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> said this to the rival ascetics: "You too, having become as corpses, are beginning a contest of <s>ṛddhi</s> with the Blessed One?" Then <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the others, the six teachers, not omniscient but claimants to omniscient knowledge, informed the Magadhan king <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> halfway along the road: "Your Majesty, we are possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and claim knowledge."

children.text: śramaṇo 'pi gautama ṛddhimāñjñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte ||
children.translated_text: "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> also declares himself to be possessed of <s>ṛddhi</s> and a claimant of knowledge."

children.text: arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: A claimant of knowledge ought to display, together with a claimant of knowledge, a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>.

children.text: yāvat tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: And so on, up to: "There let it be for us, together with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, to display a superhuman miracle of <s>ṛddhi</s>."

children.text: evamukte rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastāṃstīrthikaparivrājakānidamavocat yadyevaṃ trirapyetamarthaṃ vijñāpayiṣyatha nirviṣayān vaḥ kariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> said this to those tīrthika wanderers: "If you inform me of this matter even three times, I will make you without a domain."

children.text: atha tīrthyānāmetadabhavat ayaṃ rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya śrāvakaḥ bimbisārastiṣṭhatu ||
children.translated_text: Then the tīrthikas thought, "This King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> is a disciple of the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>. Let <s>Bimbisāra</s> be."

children.text: rājā prasenajit kauśalo madhyasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> is neutral.

children.text: yadā śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrāvastīṃ gamiṣyati tatra vayaṃ gatvā śramaṇaṃ gautamamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihārye āhvayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "When the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> goes to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, we will go there and challenge the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> to a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity."

children.text: ityuktvā prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, they departed.

children.text: atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro 'nyatamaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa kṣipram ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> addressed a certain man: "Go quickly, good man.

children.text: bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojaya yatrāhamadhiruhya bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi paryupāsanāyai ||
children.translated_text: Yoke an excellent vehicle, in which I shall mount and approach the Blessed One to see him and to attend upon him."

children.text: evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājño māgadhasya śreṇyasya bimbisārasya pratiśrutya kṣipraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojayitvā yena rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, Your Majesty," that man replied to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>; and, having quickly yoked an excellent vehicle, he approached King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāramidamavocat yuktaṃ devasya bhadraṃ yānaṃ yasyedānīṃ devaḥ kālaṃ manyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>: "Your Majesty's excellent vehicle is ready. Let Your Majesty now think it time."

children.text: atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhadraṃ yānamabhiruhya rājagṛhānniryāti bhagavato 'ntikaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> mounted the excellent vehicle and set out from <s>Rājagṛha</s> toward the Blessed One, to approach the Blessed One in order to see him and attend upon him.

children.text: tasya yāvatī yānasya bhūmistāvadyānena gatvā yānādavatīrya padbhyāmevārāmaṃ prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: As far as there was ground fit for a vehicle, he went by vehicle; then, descending from the vehicle, he entered the park on foot.

children.text: antarā rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavantamadrākṣīt ||
children.translated_text: On the way King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> saw the Blessed One.

children.text: tadantarā pañca kakudānyapanīya tadyathā uṣṇīṣaṃ chatraṃ khaḍgamaṇiṃ vālavyajanaṃ citre copānahau sa pañca kakudānyapanīya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon, after removing the five royal insignia, namely the turban, the parasol, the jeweled sword, the yak-tail fan, and the patterned sandals, having removed those five royal insignia, he approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached and bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet, he sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ viditvā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> was seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed him, made him take up the teaching, encouraged him, and gladdened him with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: After instructing him, making him take it up, encouraging him, and gladdening him in many ways with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>, he became silent.

children.text: atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavantamabhyānandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, rejoicing in and approving the Blessed One's words, bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: atha bhagavata etadabhavat kutra pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇinām devatā bhagavata ārocayanti śrutapūrvaṃ bhadanta pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇināmiti ||
children.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: "Where did the former perfectly awakened Buddhas display the great miracle for the welfare of living beings?" Deities informed the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, we have heard that the former perfectly awakened Buddhas displayed the great miracle for the welfare of living beings."

children.text: bhagavato jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate śrāvastyāṃ pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇināmiti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One's knowledge and vision arose: "At <s>Śrāvastī</s> the former perfectly awakened Buddhas displayed the great miracle for the welfare of living beings."

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate gaccha tvamānanda bhikṣūṇāmārocaya ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce this to the monks.

children.text: tathāgataḥ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> will wander on tour through the countries of <s>Kosala</s>.

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cartum sa cīvarakāṇi dhāvatu sīvyatu rañjayatu ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you is able to wander on tour with the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the countries of <s>Kosala</s>, let him wash, sew, and dye his robes."

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati bhagavānāyuṣmantaḥ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, venerable sir," venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One, and he announced to the monks: "Venerable ones, the Blessed One will wander on tour through the countries of <s>Kosala</s>.

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caritum sa cīvarāṇi dhāvatu sīvyatu rañjayatu iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you is able to wander on tour with the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the countries of <s>Kosala</s>, let him wash, sew, and dye his robes."

children.text: te bhikṣava āyuṣmata ānandasya pratyaśrauṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those monks assented to venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gaja iva kalabhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭrigaṇaparivṛto rājahaṃsa iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto deśika ivādhvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva pauragaṇaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaścakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaścandra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpākṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛto dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto vemacitra ivāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛto brahmeva brahmakāyikagaṇaparivṛtaḥ stimita iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntairindriyair asaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro 'nekairāveṇikairbuddhadharmairmahatā bhikṣusaṃghena ca puraskṛto yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, tamed and with a tamed retinue, peaceful and with a peaceful retinue, liberated and with a liberated retinue, reassured and with a reassured retinue, disciplined and with a disciplined retinue, an arhat and with a retinue of arhats, free from passion and with a retinue free from passion, gracious in appearance and with a gracious retinue; surrounded like a bull by a herd of cows, like an elephant by a herd of young elephants, like a lion by a troop of fanged beasts, like a royal swan by a flock of swans, like <s>Suparṇī</s> by flocks of birds, like a brahmin by a group of pupils, like a good physician by a group of the sick, like a hero by a band of warriors, like a guide by travelers on the road, like a caravan leader by a group of merchants, like a guild-master by townspeople, like a king of a fortress by ministers, like a universal monarch by a thousand sons, like the moon by hosts of stars, like the sun by a thousand rays, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> by hosts of kumbhāṇḍas, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> by hosts of nāgas, like <s>Dhanada</s> by hosts of yakṣas, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> by hosts of gandharvas, like <s>Vemacitra</s> by hosts of asuras, like <s>Śakra</s> by the hosts of the Thirty-three, like <s>Brahmā</s> by hosts of Brahmā's retinue; still as the ocean, full of water as a rain cloud, free from rut like a lordly elephant, his sense faculties well tamed, his course and deportment unagitated, honored by many distinctive buddha-qualities and by a great community of monks, set out on tour toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: anekaiśca devatāśatasahasrairanugamyamāno 'nupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: Followed by many hundreds of thousands of deities, and traveling on his tour by stages, he reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He stayed at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: aśrauṣustīrthyāḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrāvastīṃ gata iti ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics heard, "The renunciant <s>Gautama</s> has gone to <s>Śrāvastī</s>."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ śrāvastīṃ samprasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when they had heard this, they too set out for <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: te śrāvastīṃ gatvā rājānaṃ prasenajitkauśalamidamavocan yatkhalu deva jānīthā vayam ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They went to <s>Śrāvastī</s> and said this to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>: "Your Majesty should know this: we are endowed with supernatural power and profess knowledge.

children.text: śramaṇo gautama ṛddhimāñ jñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte ||
children.translated_text: The renunciant <s>Gautama</s> declares himself to be endowed with supernatural power and to profess knowledge.

children.text: arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharma ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: It is fitting that one who professes knowledge should display, together with one who professes knowledge, a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ dve ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, we will display two.

children.text: dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ catvāri ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays two, we will display four.

children.text: catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayamaṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays four, we will display eight.

children.text: aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, we will display sixteen.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ vayaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ taddviguṇaṃ tattriguṇamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, we will display thirty-two; and as far as the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> displays a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, we will display, in supernatural miracles beyond ordinary human capacity, twice that and three times that.

children.text: upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu vayamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> come halfway along the road, and we too will go halfway along the road.

children.text: tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: There let us have a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity together with the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: evamukte rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat āgamayantu tāvadbhavanto yāvadahaṃ bhagavantamavalokayāmi ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> said this to the non-Buddhist ascetics: "Gentlemen, wait for a while, until I go and see the Blessed One."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo 'nyatamaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> addressed a certain man: "Go, my good man.

children.text: kṣipraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojaya ||
children.translated_text: Quickly harness a fine vehicle.

children.text: ahamabhiruhya adyaiva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi paryupāsanāyai ||
children.translated_text: I shall mount it and today itself approach the Blessed One to see him and attend upon him."

children.text: evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya pratiśrutya kṣipraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojayitvā yena rājā prasenajit kauśalastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, Your Majesty," that man replied to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>. After quickly harnessing a fine vehicle, he approached King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocat yuktaṃ devasya bhadraṃ yānaṃ yasyedānīṃ devaḥ kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>: "Your Majesty's fine vehicle is harnessed; let Your Majesty now think it is time."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhadraṃ yānamabhiruhya śrāvastyā niryāti bhagavato 'ntikaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya upasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> mounted the fine vehicle and departed from <s>Śrāvastī</s> to approach the Blessed One, to see the Blessed One and attend upon him.

children.text: tasya yāvatī yānasya bhūmistāvadyānena gatvā yānādavatīrya pādābhyāmeva ārāmaṃ praviśya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He went by vehicle as far as the ground was suitable for the vehicle, then descended from the vehicle, entered the park on foot, and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantamidamavocat ime bhadanta tīrthyā bhagavantamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryeṇāhvayante ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, these non-Buddhist ascetics challenge the Blessed One to a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: vidarśayatu bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed One display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity for the welfare of living beings.

children.text: nirbhartsayatu bhagavāṃstīrthyān ||
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed One rebuke the non-Buddhist ascetics.

children.text: nandayatu devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: Let him gladden gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: Let him satisfy the hearts and minds of good people."

children.text: evamukte bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocat nāhaṃ mahārāja evaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi evam yūyaṃ bhikṣava āgatāgatānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayateti ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "Great king, I do not teach the Dharma to the disciples in this way: 'Monks, display to the brahmins and householders who come and go a miracle of supernatural power beyond human capacity.'"

children.text: api tu ahamevaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi praticchannakalyāṇā bhikṣavo viharata vivṛtapāpā iti ||
children.translated_text: Rather, I teach the Dharma to the disciples in this way: "Monks, live with your good qualities concealed and your faults laid open."

children.text: dvirapi trirapi rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantamidamavocat vidarśayatu bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: A second and a third time King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One display a miracle of supernatural power beyond human capacity, for the welfare of living beings.

children.text: nirbhartsayatu tīrthyān ||
children.translated_text: Let him rebuke the heterodox teachers.

children.text: nandayatu bhagavān devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed One gladden gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: Let him satisfy the hearts and minds of good people."

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jīvatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyamāṇānām yāpayatām yaduta daśāvaśyakaraṇīyāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, while they are living, staying, remaining, and passing their lives, that there are ten things that must necessarily be done.

children.text: na tāvadbuddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvānti yāvanna buddho buddhaṃ vyākaroti yāvanna dvitīyena sattvenāparivartyamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpāditaṃ bhavati sarvabuddhavaineyā vinītā bhavanti tribhāga āyuṣa utsṛṣṭo bhavati sīmābandhaḥ kṛto bhavati śrāvakayugamagratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ bhavati sāṃkāśye nagare devatāvataraṇaṃ vidarśitaṃ bhavati anavatapte mahāsarasi śrāvakaiḥ sārdhaṃ pūrvikā karmaplotirvyākṛtā bhavati mātāpitarau satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau bhavataḥ śrāvastyāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Buddhas, Blessed Ones, do not pass into <s>parinirvana</s> until a Buddha has prophesied a Buddha, until a second being has raised a mind irreversible toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, until all those to be trained by a Buddha have been trained, until a third part of the lifespan has been relinquished, until the boundary has been established, until the pair of disciples has been appointed to foremost rank, until the descent of the deities has been displayed in the city of <s>Samkasya</s>, until the former mass of karma has been prophesied together with the disciples at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, until his mother and father have been established in the truths, and until the great miracle has been displayed at <s>Sravasti</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavata etadabhavat avaśyakaraṇīyametattathāgateneti viditvā rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamāmantrayate gaccha tvaṃ mahārāja ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One: "This is something that must necessarily be done by the <s>Tathagata</s>." Knowing this, he addressed King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "Go, great king.

children.text: itaḥ saptame divase tathāgato mahājanapratyakṣamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day from now the <s>Tathagata</s> will display, in the sight of a great crowd, a miracle of supernatural power beyond human capacity, for the welfare of living beings."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantamidamavocat yadi bhagavānanujānīyāt ahaṃ bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ kārayeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> said this to the Blessed One: "If the Blessed One permits it, I shall have a pavilion for the Blessed One's miracle constructed."

children.text: atha bhagavata etadabhavat katarasmin pradeśe pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇināmiti devatā bhagavata ārocayanti antarā bhadanta śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanamatrāntarāt pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One: "In what place did the former perfectly awakened Buddhas display the great miracle for the welfare of living beings?" The deities informed the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, between <s>Sravasti</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>, in that interval, the former perfectly awakened Buddhas displayed the great miracle for the welfare of living beings."

children.text: bhagavato 'pi jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate antarā ca śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanamatrāntarāt pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge and vision also arose for the Blessed One: "Between <s>Sravasti</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>, in that interval, the former perfectly awakened Buddhas displayed the great miracle for the welfare of living beings."
