children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One accepted King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>'s request by silence.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavantamidamavocat katamasmin bhadanta pradeśe prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ kārayāmi antarā ca mahārāja śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanam ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, knowing that the Blessed One had accepted by silence, said this to the Blessed One: "In what place, venerable sir, shall I have the miracle pavilion constructed?" "Between <s>Sravasti</s>, great king, and <s>Jetavana</s>."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, rejoicing in and approving the Blessed One's words, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran itaḥ saptame divase bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> said this to the heterodox teachers: "Sirs, you should know this: on the seventh day from now the Blessed One will display a miracle of supernatural power beyond human capacity."

children.text: atha tīrthyānāmetadabhavat kiṃ punaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ saptabhirdivasairanadhigatamadhigamiṣyati atha vā niṣpalāyiṣyati atha vā pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmas teṣāmetadabhavat na hyeva śramaṇo gautamo niṣpalāyiṣyati nāpyanadhigatamadhigamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the heterodox teachers: "What then? Will the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> attain in seven days what he has not attained? Or will he run away? Or does he intend to search for supporters?" This occurred to them: "Certainly the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> will not run away, nor will he attain what he has not attained.

children.text: nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> intends to search for supporters.

children.text: vayamapi tāvat pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We too, then, will search for supporters."

children.text: iti viditvā raktākṣo nāma parivrājaka indrajālābhijñaḥ sa āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having understood this, a wandering ascetic named <s>Raktaksa</s>, skilled in illusion, was summoned.

children.text: raktākṣasya parivrājakasyaitat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayanti evaṃ cāhur yatkhalu raktākṣa jānīyāḥ śramaṇo gautamo 'smābhirṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They explained this matter in detail to the wandering ascetic <s>Raktaksa</s>, and said this: "<s>Raktaksa</s>, you should know this: the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged by us in supernatural power.

children.text: sa kathayati itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He says, 'On the seventh day from now I shall display a miracle of supernatural power beyond human capacity.'

children.text: nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> intends to search for supporters.

children.text: tvamapi tāvat sabrahmacāriṇāṃ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kuruṣva ||
children.translated_text: You too, then, search for supporters among your fellow celibates."

children.text: tena tatheti pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: He agreed, saying, "So be it."

children.text: atha raktākṣaḥ parivrājako yena nānātīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakās tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the wandering ascetic <s>Raktaksa</s> approached the ascetics, brahmins, carakas, and wandering mendicants belonging to various heterodox sects.

children.text: upasaṃkramya nānātīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakānām etatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati evaṃ cāha yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran śramaṇo gautamo 'smābhirṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached the many Tīrthika ascetics, brahmins, Carakas, and wandering mendicants, he reported this matter to them in detail and said: "Sirs, you should know that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been summoned by us through supernatural power."

children.text: sa kathayati itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He says, "On the seventh day from now I shall display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity."

children.text: nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek supporters.

children.text: bhavadbhirapi brahmacāriṇāṃ sāhāyyaṃ karaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: You too must give help to your fellow celibates.

children.text: saptame divase yuṣmābhirbahiḥ śrāvastyā nirgantavyam ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day you must go out beyond <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: taistatheti pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: They agreed, saying, "So be it."

children.text: athānyatamasmin parvate pañcamātrāṇi ṛṣiśatāni prativasanti ||
children.translated_text: Now on a certain mountain there lived about five hundred seers.

children.text: atha raktākṣaḥ parivrājako yena te ṛṣayastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the wandering mendicant <s>Raktākṣa</s> approached those seers.

children.text: upasaṃkramya teṣāmetatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati evaṃ cāha yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran śramaṇo gautama ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached them, he reported this matter to them in detail and said: "Sirs, you should know that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been summoned by supernatural power."

children.text: sa kathayati itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He says, "On the seventh day from now I shall display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity."

children.text: nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek supporters.

children.text: bhavadbhirapi sabrahmacāriṇāṃ sāhāyyaṃ karaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: You too must give help to your fellow celibates.

children.text: saptame divase yuṣmābhiḥ śrāvastīmāgantavyam ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day you must come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: taistatheti pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: They agreed, saying, "So be it."

children.text: tena khalu samayena subhadro nāma parivrājakaḥ pañcābhijñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time there was a wandering mendicant named <s>Subhadra</s>, possessed of the five superknowledges.

children.text: tasya kuśinagaryāmāvasatho 'navatapte mahāsarasi divā vihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: His residence was in <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, and his daytime resort was at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

children.text: atha raktākṣaḥ parivrājako yena subhadraḥ parivrājakastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the wandering mendicant <s>Raktākṣa</s> approached the wandering mendicant <s>Subhadra</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya etatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati evaṃ cāha yatkhalu subhadra jānīyāḥ śramaṇo gautamo 'smābhir ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached him, he reported this matter in detail and said: "<s>Subhadra</s>, you should know that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been summoned by us through supernatural power."

children.text: sa kathayati itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He says, "On the seventh day from now I shall display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity."

children.text: nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek supporters.

children.text: tvayā sabrahmacāriṇāṃ sāhāyyaṃ karaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: You must give help to your fellow celibates.

children.text: saptame divase tvayā śrāvastīmāgantavyam ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day you must come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: subhadreṇābhihitam na śobhanaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kṛtam yadyuṣmābhiḥ śramaṇo gautamo ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> said, "What you have done is not good, if you have summoned the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> by supernatural power."

children.text: tatkasya hetor mama tāvat kuśinagaryāmāvāso 'navatapte mahāsarasi divā vihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For my residence is in <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, and my daytime resort is at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

children.text: śramaṇasya gautamasya śāriputro nāma śiṣyastasya cundo nāma śrāmaṇerakastasyāpi tatraivānavatapte mahāsarasi divā vihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has a disciple named <s>Śāriputra</s>; he has a novice named <s>Cunda</s>, and he too has his daytime resort there at the same great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

children.text: na tathānavataptakāyikā devatā api kārān kartavyān manyante yathā tasya ||
children.translated_text: The deities belonging to <s>Anavatapta</s> do not think honors should be paid even to me as they do to him.

children.text: eko 'yaṃ samayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There was one such occasion.

children.text: ihāhaṃ kuśinagarīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā piṇḍapātamādāya anavataptaṃ mahāsarasaṃ gacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: Here, after going for alms in <s>Kuśinagarī</s> and taking my almsfood, I go to the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

children.text: tasya mamānavataptakāyikā devatā anavataptānmahāsarasaḥ pānīyamuddhṛtya ekānte na prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: For me, the deities belonging to <s>Anavatapta</s> do not draw water from the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> and give it to me apart.

children.text: cundaḥ śramaṇoddeśaḥ pāṃśukūlānyādāyānavataptaṃ mahāsaro gacchati ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Cunda</s>, the novice monk, takes rag-robes and goes to the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>.

children.text: tasyānavataptakāyikā devatā pāṃśukūlāni dhāvayitvā tena pānīyenātmānaṃ siñcati ||
children.translated_text: For him, the deities belonging to <s>Anavatapta</s> wash the rag-robes and sprinkle themselves with that water.

children.text: yasya tāvadvayaṃ śiṣyapratiśiṣyakayāpi na tulyāḥ sa yuṣmābhiruttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryeṇāhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since we are not equal even to his disciple's disciple, you have summoned him to a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: na śobhanaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kṛtam yacchramaṇo gautamo ṛddhiprātihāryeṇāhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What you have done is not good, that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been summoned to a miracle of supernatural power."

children.text: evamahaṃ jāne yathā maharddhikaḥ śramaṇo gautamo mahānubhāva iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus I know that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is of great supernatural power and great majesty."

children.text: raktākṣeṇābhihitaṃ tvaṃ tāvacchramaṇasya gautamasya pakṣaṃ vadasi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Raktākṣa</s> said, "For your part, you are speaking in favor of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: tvayā tāvanna gantavyam ||
children.translated_text: You, at least, must not go.

children.text: subhadreṇābhihitam naiva gamiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> said, "Indeed, I shall not go."

children.text: atha rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya kālo nāmnā bhrātā abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> had a brother named <s>Kāla</s>, handsome, lovely to see, gracious, faithful, good, and noble-minded.

children.text: sa rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya niveśanadvāreṇābhiniṣkrāmati ||
children.translated_text: He was going out through the gate of the residence of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>.

children.text: anyatamayā cāvaruddhikayā prāsādatalagatayā rājakumāraṃ dṛṣṭvā sragdāmaṃ kṣiptam ||
children.translated_text: A certain woman kept in seclusion, standing on the palace roof, saw the prince and threw down a wreath of flowers.

children.text: tat tasyopari nipatitam ||
children.translated_text: It fell upon him.

children.text: mitrārimadhyamo lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The world consists of friends, enemies, and those in between.

children.text: tai rājñe niveditaṃ yatkhalu deva jānīthāḥ kālena devasyāntaḥpuraṃ prārthitam ||
children.translated_text: They reported to the king, "Your Majesty, you should know that <s>Kāla</s> has desired Your Majesty's inner apartments."

children.text: rājā prasenajit kauśalaścaṇḍo rabhasaḥ karkaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> was fierce, violent, and harsh.

children.text: tenāparīkṣya pauruṣeyāṇāmājñā dattā gacchantu bhavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without investigating, he gave an order to his men: "Go, sirs."

children.text: śīghraṃ kālasya hastapādāṃś chindantu ||
children.translated_text: Quickly cut off <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet.

children.text: evaṃ deveti pauruṣeyai rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya pratiśrutya kālasya vīthīmadhye hastapādāśchinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, Your Majesty," the men replied to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, and in the middle of the street they cut off <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet.

children.text: sa ārtasvaraṃ krandate duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāmamanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate ||
children.translated_text: He cried out with a pained voice, experiencing painful, intense, sharp, bitter, and disagreeable feeling.

children.text: kālaṃ rājakumāraṃ dṛṣṭvā mahājanakāyo vikroṣṭumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing Prince <s>Kāla</s>, a great crowd of people began to cry out.

children.text: pūraṇādayaśca nirgranthāstaṃ pradeśamanuprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the Nirgranthas beginning with <s>Pūrṇa</s> reached that place.

children.text: kālasya jñātibhirabhihitam etamāryāḥ kālaṃ rājakumāraṃ satyābhiyācanayā yathāpaurāṇaṃ kurudhvamiti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāla</s>'s relatives said, "Noble ones, restore Prince <s>Kāla</s> as he was before by an appeal to truth."

children.text: pūraṇenābhihitam eṣa śramaṇasya gautamasya śrāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūraṇa</s> said, "This man is a disciple of the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: śramaṇadharmeṇa gautamo yathāpaurāṇaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Gautama</s> will restore him as he was before by the <s>dharma</s> of renunciants."

children.text: atha kālasya rājakumārasyaitadabhavat kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaṃ māṃ bhagavān na samanvāharatīti viditvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to Prince <s>Kāla</s>: "The Blessed One has not turned his attention to me, though I have fallen into painful, cramped, and constricted distress." Knowing this, he spoke a verse:

children.text: imāmavasthāṃ mama lokanātho na vetti saṃbādhagatasya kasmāt
children.translated_text: "Why does the Lord of the world not know this condition of mine, afflicted as I am and fallen into distress?

children.text: namo 'stu tasmai vigatajvarāya sarveṣu bhūteṣvanukampakāya ||
children.translated_text: Homage to him who is free from fever, who has compassion for all beings."

children.text: asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are by nature not forgetful.

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma gaccha tvamānanda saṃghāṭimādāya anyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścācchramaṇena yena kālo rājabhrātā tenopasaṃkrāma ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>. Take the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, and, with a certain monk as your attendant, approach <s>Kāla</s>, the king's brother.

children.text: upasaṃkramya kālasya rājakumārasya hastapādān yathāsthāne sthāpayitvā evaṃ vada ye kecit sattvā apadā vā dvipadā vā bahupadā vā arūpiṇo vā rūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino vā nāsaṃjñinaḥ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhasteṣāṃ sattvānāmagra ākhyāyate ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, set Prince <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet in their proper places and say this: 'Whatever beings there are, footless, two-footed, or many-footed, formless or possessed of form, percipient, non-percipient, neither percipient nor non-percipient, among those beings the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, is declared foremost.

children.text: ye kecid dharmā asaṃskṛtā vā saṃskṛtā vā virāgo dharmasteṣāmagra ākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharmas</s> there are, unconditioned or conditioned, the <s>dharma</s> of dispassion is declared foremost among them.

children.text: anena satyena satyavākyena tava śarīram yathāpaurāṇaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: By this truth, by this truthful utterance, may your body be as it was before.'"

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya saṃghāṭīmādāyānyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścācchramaṇena yena rājabhrātā kālastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, venerable sir," venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One. Taking the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, and with a certain monk as his attendant, he approached <s>Kāla</s>, the king's brother.

children.text: upasaṃkramya kālasya rājakumārasya hastapādān yathāsthāne sthāpayitvā evamāha ye kecit sattvā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuṣpadā vā bahupadā vā yāvannaivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñinaḥ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhasteṣāṃ sattvānāmagra ākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he set Prince <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet in their proper places and said this: "Whatever beings there are, footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed, up to those who are neither percipient nor non-percipient, among those beings the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, is declared foremost.

children.text: ye keciddharmāḥ saṃskṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā virāgo dharmasteṣāmagra ākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharmas</s> there are, conditioned or unconditioned, the <s>dharma</s> of dispassion is declared foremost among them.

children.text: ye kecit saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā parṣado vā tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghasteṣāmagra ākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever communities, groups, associations, or assemblies there are, the community of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples is declared foremost among them.

children.text: anena satyena satyavākyena tava śarīram yathāpaurāṇaṃ bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: By this truth, by this truthful utterance, may your body become as it was before."

children.text: sahābhidhānāt kālasya rājakumārasya śarīram yathāpaurāṇaṃ saṃvṛttam yathāpi tatra buddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: At the very utterance, Prince <s>Kāla</s>'s body became as it had been before, just as it did there through the Buddha's buddha-power and the deities' divine power.

children.text: kālena kumāreṇa tenaiva saṃvegena anāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ṛddhiścāpi nirhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Through that very spiritual shock, Prince <s>Kāla</s> realized the fruit of non-returning, and he also brought forth supernatural power.

children.text: tena bhagavata ārāmo niryātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He dedicated a park to the Blessed One.

children.text: sa bhagavata upasthānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to attend upon the Blessed One.

children.text: yatrāsya śarīraṃ gaṇḍagaṇḍaṃ kṛtaṃ tasya gaṇḍaka ārāmika iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Because his body had been made lump upon lump, from that he came to be known as <s>Gaṇḍaka Ārāmika</s>.

children.text: atha rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sa pravāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> offered him every requisite.

children.text: kālenābhihitam na mama tvayā prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāla</s> said, "I have no need of anything from you.

children.text: bhagavata evopasthānaṃ kariṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: I shall attend upon the Blessed One alone."

children.text: rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena antarā ca śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanamatrāntarādbhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapaḥ kāritaḥ śatasahasrahastacaturṇāṃ maṇḍapo vitataḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> had a miracle pavilion made for the Blessed One in the interval between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>; a pavilion measuring a hundred thousand cubits on each of its four sides was spread out.

children.text: bhagavataḥ siṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptam ||
children.translated_text: A lion-throne was prepared for the Blessed One.

children.text: anyatīrthikaśrāvakairapi pūrṇādīnāṃ nirgranthānāṃ pratyekapratyekamaṇḍapaḥ kāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The disciples of the other sectarians also had separate pavilions made for the naked ascetics, beginning with <s>Pūrṇa</s>, each one individually.

children.text: rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena saptame divase yāvajjetavanaṃ yāvacca bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapo 'ntarāt sarvo 'sau pradeśo 'pagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhalyo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> had that whole region, from <s>Jetavana</s> as far as the Blessed One's miracle pavilion, cleared of stones, gravel, and potsherds.

children.text: dhūpacūrṇāndhakāraḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was made dark with clouds of incense powder.

children.text: chatradhvajapatākāgandhodakapariṣikto nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇo ramaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was delightful, adorned with parasols, banners, and flags, sprinkled with scented water, and strewn with various flowers.

children.text: antarāntarā ca puṣpamaṇḍapāḥ sajjīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And at intervals flower pavilions were made ready.

children.text: atha bhagavān saptame divase pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, the Blessed One dressed in the forenoon, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.

children.text: śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratiśrāmya bahirvihārasya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ pratisaṃlayanāya ||
children.translated_text: After walking for alms in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, when he had completed the business of his meal and returned from the alms-round after eating, he put away his bowl and robe, washed his feet outside the monastery, and entered the monastery for seclusion.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo 'nekaśataparivāro 'nekasahasraparivāro 'nekaśatasahasraparivāro yena bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, surrounded by many hundreds, many thousands, and many hundreds of thousands, approached the Blessed One's miracle pavilion.

children.text: upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: tīrthyā api mahājanakāyaparivṛtā yena maṇḍapastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sectarians too, surrounded by a great mass of people, approached the pavilion.

children.text: upasaṃkramya pratyekapratyekasminnāsane niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they sat down each on his own seat.

children.text: niṣadya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocan yatkhalu deva jānīyā ete vayamāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After sitting down, they said this to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>: "Your Majesty should certainly know this: here we have come.

children.text: kutra etarhi śramaṇo gautamas tena bhavanto muhūrtamāgamayata ||
children.translated_text: Where now is the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>?" "Then, gentlemen, wait a moment."

children.text: eṣa idānīṃ bhagavānadhigamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One will now know this.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśala uttaraṃ māṇavamāmantrayate ehi tvamuttara yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāma ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> addressed the young brahmin <s>Uttara</s>: "Come, <s>Uttara</s>; go to where the Blessed One is.

children.text: upasaṃkramyāsmākaṃ vacanena bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛccha alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca anavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, bow with your head to the Blessed One's feet on our behalf, and ask whether he has little illness, little affliction, rises lightly, travels well, has strength, happiness, blamelessness, and dwells at ease.

children.text: evaṃ ca vada rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśala evamāha ime bhadanta tīrthyā āgatā yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: And say this: 'Venerable sir, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> says: These non-Buddhist ascetics have arrived, venerable sir; let the Blessed One now consider what time it is.'"

children.text: evaṃ devetyuttaro māṇavo rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya pratiśrutya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, Your Majesty," the young brahmin <s>Uttara</s> replied to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>, and he approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he exchanged with the Blessed One various friendly, cordial, and pleasing words face to face, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇa uttaro māṇavo bhagavantamidamavocat rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśalo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandate alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchati alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca anavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, the young brahmin <s>Uttara</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> bows with his head to the Blessed One's feet and asks whether he has little illness, little affliction, rises lightly, travels well, has strength, happiness, blamelessness, and dwells at ease.

children.text: sukhī bhavatu māṇava rājā prasenajit kauśalastvaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "May King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> be happy, young brahmin, and you too.

children.text: rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśala evamāha ime bhadanta tīrthyā āgatā yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Venerable sir, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> says this: 'These non-Buddhist ascetics have arrived, venerable sir; let the Blessed One now consider what time it is.'"

children.text: evamukte bhagavānuttaraṃ māṇavamidamavocat māṇava eṣo 'hamadyāgacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the young brahmin <s>Uttara</s>: "Young brahmin, here I come today."

children.text: bhagavatā tathādhiṣṭhito yathottaro māṇavastat evoparivihāyasā prakrāntaḥ yena rājā prasenajit kauśalastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One made such a determination that the young brahmin <s>Uttara</s> departed from that very place through the air above and approached King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>.

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā prasenajit kauśala uttaraṃ māṇavakamupari vihāyasā āgacchantam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> saw the young brahmin <s>Uttara</s> coming through the air above.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punastīrthyānidamavocat vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he then said this to the non-Buddhist ascetics: "The Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: yūyamapi vidarśayata ||
children.translated_text: You too should display one."

children.text: tīrthyāḥ kathayanti mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics said: "A great mass of people has gathered here, Your Majesty.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kenaitad vidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena atha bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte 'rgaḍacchidreṇārciṣo nirgatya bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍape nipatitāḥ sarvaśca prātihāryamaṇḍapaḥ prajvalitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How will you know by whom this was displayed, by us or by the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>?" Then the Blessed One entered such a samādhi (meditative absorption) that, while his mind was concentrated, flames came out through the aperture of the door-bar and fell upon the Blessed One's miracle pavilion, and the whole miracle pavilion blazed up.

children.text: adrākṣustīrthyā bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ prajvalitam dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocan eṣa idānīṃ mahārāja śramaṇasya gautamasya prātihāryamaṇḍapaḥ prajvalitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics saw the Blessed One's miracle pavilion blazing; and, seeing it, they then said this to <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s>: "Now, Your Majesty, this miracle pavilion of the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> is blazing.

children.text: gaccha idānīṃ nirvāpaya ||
children.translated_text: Go now and extinguish it."

children.text: atha so 'gniraspṛṣṭa eva vāriṇā sarvaprātihāryamaṇḍapam adagdhvā svayameva nirvṛto yathāpi tadbuddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Then that fire, without being touched by water and without burning the entire miracle pavilion, went out by itself, just as happens through a Buddha's buddha-power and through the deities' divine power.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> said this to the non-Buddhist ascetics: "The Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: yūyamapi vidarśayata ||
children.translated_text: You too should display one."

children.text: tīrthyāḥ kathayanti mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics said: "A great mass of people has gathered here, Your Majesty.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena bhagavatā kanakamarīcikāvabhāsā utsṛṣṭāḥ yena sarvaloka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: How will you know by whom this was displayed, by us or by the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>?" Golden-ray splendors were emitted by the Blessed One, by which the whole world was pervaded with a lofty radiance.

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ sarvalokamudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> saw that the whole world was pervaded with a lofty radiance.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punastīrthyānāmantrayate vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: Having seen it, he then addressed the non-Buddhist ascetics: "The Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: yūyamapi vidarśayata ||
children.translated_text: You too should display one."

children.text: tīrthyāḥ kathayanti mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics said: "A great mass of people has gathered here, Your Majesty.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena ||
children.translated_text: How will you know by whom this was displayed, by us or by the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>?"

children.text: gaṇḍakenārāmikenottarakauravād dvīpāt karṇikāravṛkṣamādāya bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapasyāgrataḥ sthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The park attendant <s>Gaṇḍaka</s> brought a karṇikāra tree from the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s> and set it in front of the Blessed One's miracle pavilion.

children.text: ratnakenāpyārāmikena gandhamādanādaśokavṛkṣamānīya bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapasya pṛṣṭhataḥ sthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The park attendant <s>Ratnaka</s> also brought an aśoka tree from <s>Gandhamādana</s> and set it behind the Blessed One's miracle pavilion.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśala</s> said this to the non-Buddhist ascetics: "The Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: yūyamapi vidarśayata ||
children.translated_text: You too should display one."

children.text: tīrthyāḥ kathayanti mahājanakāyo 'tra saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics said: "A great mass of people has gathered here.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena bhagavatā sābhisaṃskāreṇa pṛthivyāṃ pādau nyastau ||
children.translated_text: How will you know by whom this was displayed, by us or by the renunciant <s>Gautama</s>?" The Blessed One deliberately set his feet upon the earth.

children.text: mahāpṛthivīcālaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A great earthquake occurred.

children.text: ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturiyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ kampati prakampati samprakampati ||
children.translated_text: This <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra-lokadhātu</s> (three-thousand great-thousand world-system), this great earth, quaked in six ways: it shook, shook strongly, and shook all around.

children.text: calati saṃcalati saṃpracalati ||
children.translated_text: It moved, moved strongly, and moved all around.

children.text: vyathati saṃvyathati saṃpravyathati ||
children.translated_text: It trembled, trembled strongly, and trembled all around.

children.text: pūrvāvanamati paścimonnamati ||
children.translated_text: The eastern side sank downward, and the western side rose upward.

children.text: pūrvonnamati paścimāvanamati ||
children.translated_text: The eastern side rose upward, and the western side sank downward.

children.text: dakṣiṇonnamati uttarāvanamati ||
children.translated_text: The southern side rose upward, and the northern side sank downward.

children.text: uttaronnamati dakṣiṇāvanamati ||
children.translated_text: The northern side rose upward, and the southern side sank downward.

children.text: madhye unnamati ante 'vanamati ||
children.translated_text: It rose upward in the middle and sank downward at the ends.

children.text: madhye 'vanamati ante unnamati ||
children.translated_text: It sank downward in the middle and rose upward at the ends.

children.text: imau sūryacandramasau bhāsatastapato virocataḥ ||
children.translated_text: These two, the sun and the moon, shone, gave heat, and blazed.

children.text: vicitrāṇi ca āścaryādbhutāni prādurbhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: And various marvelous and wonderful things appeared.

children.text: gaganatalasthā devatā bhagavata upariṣṭāddivyānyutpalāni kṣipanti padmāni kumudāni puṇḍarīkānyagarucūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni tamālapatrāṇi divyāni māndārakāṇi puṣpāṇi kṣipanti divyāni ca vāditrāṇi saṃpravādayanti cailavikṣepaṃ cākārṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Deities standing in the expanse of the sky scattered celestial blue lotuses over the Blessed One, lotuses, water lilies, white lotuses, powders of aloe, sandalwood, and tagara, tamala leaves, and celestial mandaraka flowers; they played celestial instruments and made a tossing of cloths.

children.text: atha teṣām ṛṣīṇāmetadabhavat kimarthaṃ mahāpṛthivīcālaḥ saṃvṛtta iti ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to those seers: "For what reason has a great earthquake taken place?"

children.text: teṣāmetadabhavat nūnamasmākaṃ sabrahmacāribhiḥ śramaṇo gautamo ṛddhyā āhūto bhaviṣyatīti viditvā pañca ṛṣiśatāni śrāvastīṃ samprasthitāni ||
children.translated_text: They thought, "Surely the renunciant <s>Gautama</s> has been summoned by our fellow practitioners through supernatural power." Knowing this, five hundred seers set out for <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: teṣāmāgacchatāṃ bhagavatā ekāyano mārgo 'dhiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For them as they came, the Blessed One established a single path.

children.text: adrākṣuste ṛṣayo bhagavantaṃ dūrādeva dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ mūrtimantamiva dharmaṃ havyāvasiktamiva hutavahaṃ kāñcanabhājanasthamiva pradīpaṃ jaṅgamamiva suvarṇaparvataṃ nānāratnavicitramiva suvarṇarūpaṃ sphuṭapaṭumahāvimalaviśuddhabuddhiṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantam ||
children.translated_text: Those seers saw the Blessed One from far away, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person: the Buddha, the Blessed One, like <s>dharma</s> embodied, like a fire fed with oblations, like a lamp placed in a golden vessel, like a moving mountain of gold, like a golden image adorned with many kinds of jewels, clear, sharp, great, stainless, pure in understanding.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punar na tathā dvādaśavarṣe 'bhyastaśamatho yogācārasya cittasya kalyatāṃ janayati aputrasya vā putraḥ pratilambho daridrasya vā nidhidarśanaṃ rājyābhinandino vā rājyābhiṣeko yathā tatprathamataḥ pūrvabuddhāropitakuśalamūlānāṃ tatprathamato buddhadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: And when they saw him, neither calm practiced for twelve years produces such readiness in the mind of a practitioner of yoga, nor the obtaining of a son for one without a son, nor the sight of a treasure for a poor man, nor the royal consecration for one who delights in kingship, as did that first sight of the Buddha at that first moment for those whose roots of merit had been planted under former Buddhas.

children.text: atha te ṛṣayo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those seers approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads to the Blessed One's feet and stood to one side.

children.text: ekāntasthitāste ṛṣayo bhagavantamidamavocan labhemahi vayaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam ||
children.translated_text: Standing to one side, those seers said this to the Blessed One: "May we obtain, venerable sir, going forth, ordination, and the state of monks in the well-proclaimed <s>dharma-vinaya</s>.

children.text: carema vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntike pravrajya brahmacaryam ||
children.translated_text: Having gone forth in the presence of the Blessed One, may we practice the holy life."

children.text: te bhagavatā brāhmeṇa svareṇāhūtāḥ eta bhikṣavaścarata brahmacaryam ||
children.translated_text: They were summoned by the Blessed One in a Brahma-like voice: "Come, monks; practice the holy life."

children.text: sahābhidhānānmuṇḍāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtāḥ pātrakaravyagrahastāḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśravo varṣaśatopasaṃpannasya bhikṣorīryāpathenāvasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the very utterance, they became shaven, clothed in saṃghāṭī robes, with bowls and vessels in hand; their hair and beards looked as if they had been removed seven days before, and they stood in the deportment of a monk ordained for a hundred years.

children.text: ehīti coktāśca tathāgatena muṇḍāśca saṃghāṭiparītadehāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when they had been told, "Come," by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they were shaven, their bodies wrapped in saṃghāṭī robes.

children.text: sadyaḥ praśāntendriyā eva tasthurevaṃ sthitā buddhamanorathena ||
children.translated_text: Immediately they stood with their faculties calmed; thus they stood through the Buddha's intention.

children.text: atha bhagavān divyamānuṣyeṇa pūjāsatkāreṇa satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rhannarhatparivāraḥ saptabhiśca nikāyaiḥ saṃpuraskṛto mahatā ca janaughena yena prātihāryamaṇḍapastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, honored, revered, respected, and worshiped with divine and human worship and service, an arhat with a retinue of arhats, escorted by the seven companies and by a great flood of people, approached the miracle pavilion.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared in front of the community of monks.

children.text: bhagavataḥ kāyādraśmayo nirgatya sarvaṃ prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ suvarṇavarṇāvabhāsaṃ kṛtavatyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rays issued from the Blessed One's body and made the entire miracle pavilion shine with a golden color.

children.text: atha lūhasudatto gṛhapatirutthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Lūhasudatta</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, raised his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One remain at ease.

children.text: ahaṃ tīrthyaiḥ sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall display, together with the non-Buddhist ascetics, a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: nirbhartsayiṣyāmi tīrthyān ||
children.translated_text: I shall rebuke the non-Buddhist ascetics.

children.text: saha dharmeṇa nandayiṣyāmi devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: In accordance with the <s>dharma</s>, I shall gladden gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayiṣyāmi sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: I shall satisfy the hearts and minds of good people."

children.text: na tvaṃ gṛhapate ebhir ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ api tvahaṃ tīrthyaiḥ ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Householder, you were not summoned by these people through supernatural power; rather, I was summoned by the non-Buddhist ascetics through supernatural power.

children.text: ahamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: sthānametadvidyate yattīrthyā evaṃ vadeyuḥ nāsti śramaṇasya gautamasyottare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: It is possible that the non-Buddhist ascetics would say this: 'The renunciant <s>Gautama</s> has no miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: śrāvakasyaiṣā gṛhiṇo 'vadātavasanasya ṛddhiriti ||
children.translated_text: This is the supernatural power of a disciple, a householder dressed in white garments.'

children.text: niṣīda tvaṃ gṛhapate yathāsvake āsane ||
children.translated_text: Sit down, householder, on your own seat."

children.text: niṣaṇṇo lūhasudatto gṛhapatiryathāsvake āsane ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Lūhasudatta</s> sat down on his own seat.

children.text: yathā lūhasudatto gṛhapatirevaṃ kālo rājabhrātā rambhaka ārāmikaḥ ṛddhilamātā upāsikā śramaṇoddeśikā cundaḥ śramaṇoddeśaḥ utpalavarṇā bhikṣuṇī ||
children.translated_text: Just as the householder <s>Lūhasudatta</s> did, so too did <s>Kāla</s> the king's brother, <s>Rambhaka</s> the monastery attendant, <s>Ṛddhilamātā</s> the laywoman, the trainee nun, <s>Cunda</s> the novice, and <s>Utpalavarṇā</s> the nun.

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, raised his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One remain at ease.

children.text: ahaṃ tīrthyaiḥ sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall display, together with the non-Buddhist ascetics, a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity.

children.text: tīrthyān nigṛhniṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall subdue the non-Buddhist ascetics."

children.text: saha dharmeṇa nandayiṣyāmi devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: Together with the Dharma I shall delight gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayiṣyāmi sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: I shall satisfy the minds and hearts of good people.

children.text: pratibalastvaṃ maudgalyāyana tīrthyān sahadharmeṇa nigṛhītum ||
children.translated_text: You are capable, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, of subduing the Tīrthikas in accordance with the Dharma.

children.text: api tu na tvaṃ tīrthyair ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But you were not the one summoned by the Tīrthikas through supernatural power.

children.text: ahameṣāmuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: I shall display among them a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, for the welfare of living beings.

children.text: nirbhartsayiṣyāmi tīrthyān ||
children.translated_text: I shall rebuke the Tīrthikas.

children.text: nandayiṣyāmi devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: I shall delight gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayiṣyāmi sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: I shall satisfy the minds and hearts of good people.

children.text: niṣīda tvaṃ maudgalyāyana yathāsvake āsane ||
children.translated_text: Sit, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, on your own seat.

children.text: niṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yathāsvake āsane ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> sat down on his own seat.

children.text: tatra bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamāmantrayate ko mahārāja tathāgatamadhyeṣate uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat ahaṃ bhadanta bhagavantamadhyeṣe uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "Who, great king, requests the <s>Tathāgata</s> to display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, for the welfare of living beings?" Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, I request the Blessed One to display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity."

children.text: bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam vidarśayatu hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: May the Blessed One display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, for the welfare of living beings.

children.text: nirbhartsayatu tīrthyān ||
children.translated_text: May he rebuke the Tīrthikas.

children.text: nandayatu devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: May he delight gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: May he satisfy the minds and hearts of good people.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte svasminnāsane 'ntarhitaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya caturvidhamīryāpathaṃ kalpayati tadyathā caṅkramyate tiṣṭhati niṣīdati śayyāṃ kalpayati ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One entered such a state of concentration that, with his mind concentrated, he disappeared from his own seat, rose upward into the sky in the eastern direction, and performed the four postures, namely walking, standing, sitting, and lying down.

children.text: tejodhātumapi sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: He also entered the fire element.

children.text: tejodhātusamāpannasya buddhasya bhagavato vividhānyarcīṃṣi kāyānniścaranti tadyathā nīlapītāni lohitānyavadātāni mañjiṣṭhāni sphaṭikavarṇāni ||
children.translated_text: When the Buddha, the Blessed One, had entered the fire element, various flames issued from his body, namely blue, yellow, red, white, madder-colored, and crystal-colored.

children.text: anekānyapi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayati ||
children.translated_text: He displayed many other miracles as well.

children.text: adhaḥkāyaṃ prajvālayati uparimāt kāyācchītalā vāridhārāḥ syandante ||
children.translated_text: He set the lower part of his body ablaze, while cool streams of water flowed from the upper part of his body.

children.text: yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśīti caturdiśaṃ caturvidham ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśya tān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As in the eastern direction, so also in the southern direction and the other directions: having displayed the fourfold miracle of supernatural power in the four directions, he withdrew those magical formations and sat down on the prepared seat itself.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocat iyaṃ mahārāja tathāgatasya sarvaśrāvakasādhāraṇā ṛddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After sitting down, the Blessed One said this to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "This, great king, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supernatural power, common to all disciples."

children.text: tatra bhagavān dvirapi rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamāmantrayate ko mahārāja tathāgatamadhyeṣate 'sādhāraṇāyām ṛddhyāmuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat ahaṃ bhadanta bhagavantamadhyeṣe 'sādhāraṇāyām ṛddhyāmuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "Who, great king, requests the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with a supernatural power not shared by others, to display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, for the welfare of living beings?" Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, I request the Blessed One, with a supernatural power not shared by others, to display a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacity, for the welfare of living beings."

children.text: nirbhartsayatu tīrthyān ||
children.translated_text: May he rebuke the Tīrthikas.

children.text: nandayatu devamanuṣyān ||
children.translated_text: May he delight gods and humans.

children.text: toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: May he satisfy the minds and hearts of good people.

children.text: bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: A mundane thought was produced by the Blessed One.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatām yadi laukikaṃ cittamutpādayanti antaśaḥ kuntapipīliko 'pi prāṇī bhagavataḥ cetasi cittamājānanti ||
children.translated_text: For this indeed is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones: if they produce a mundane thought, then even a living creature as small as a kuntapipīlikā knows the thought in the Blessed One's mind.

children.text: atha lokottaracittamutpādayanti tatrāgatirbhavati pratyekabuddhānāmapi kaḥ punarvādaḥ śrāvakāṇām atha śakrabrahmādīnāṃ devānāmetadabhavat kimarthaṃ bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam teṣāmetadabhavat śrāvastyāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitukāmo hitāya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: But when they produce a supramundane thought, there is no access to it even for pratyekabuddhas, how much less for disciples. Then the gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> thought: "For what reason has the Blessed One produced a mundane thought?" They thought: "He wishes to display the great miracle at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, for the welfare of living beings."

children.text: atha śakrabrahmādayo devā anekāni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi bhagavataścetasā cittamājñāya tadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ saṃkuñcitaṃ vā bāhuṃ prasārayet prasāritaṃ vā saṃkuñcayet evameva śakrabrahmādayo devā anekāni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi ca devaloke 'ntarhitāni bhagavataḥ puratastasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of deities, having known the thought in the Blessed One's mind, just as a strong man might extend a bent arm or bend an extended arm, in just the same way disappeared from the world of the gods and stood before the Blessed One.

children.text: atha brahmādayo devā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> circumambulated the Blessed One three times, bowed their heads to the Blessed One's feet, and sat down close to his right side.

children.text: śakrādayo devā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> circumambulated the Blessed One three times, bowed their heads to the Blessed One's feet, and sat down close to his left side.

children.text: nandopanandābhyāṃ nāgarājābhyāṃ bhagavata upanāmitaṃ nirmitaṃ sahasrapatraṃ śakaṭacakramātraṃ sarvasauvarṇaṃ ratnadaṇḍaṃ padmam ||
children.translated_text: The nāga kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> offered to the Blessed One a magically created lotus, with a thousand petals, as large as a cart wheel, entirely golden, and with a jewel stalk.

children.text: bhagavāṃśca padmakarṇikāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya padmasyopari padmaṃ nirmitam ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One, seated on the pericarp of a lotus, folded his legs, set his body upright, established mindfulness before him, and manifested a lotus above the lotus.

children.text: tatrāpi bhagavān paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On that one too the Blessed One was seated cross-legged.

children.text: evamagrataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way there were lotuses in front, behind, and at the sides.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavatā buddhapiṇḍī nirmitā yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanamupādāya buddhā bhagavanto parṣannirmitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the Blessed One created a mass of Buddhas; up to the realm of <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, were manifested for the assembly.

children.text: kecidbuddhanirmāṇāścaṅkramyante kecit tiṣṭhanti kecinniṣīdanti kecicchāyāṃ kalpayanti tejodhātumapi samāpadyante jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Some Buddha-emanations walked back and forth, some stood, some sat, some cast shade, and some entered the fire element, performing miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and flashing light.

children.text: anye praśnān pṛcchanti anye visarjayanti ||
children.translated_text: Some asked questions; others answered them.

children.text: gāthādvayaṃ bhāṣante
children.translated_text: They spoke two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Set out, go forth; apply yourselves in the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this dharma and vinaya

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring suffering to an end."

children.text: bhagavatā tathā adhiṣṭhitam yathā sarvaloko 'nāvṛtamadrākṣīdbuddhāvataṃsakaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanamupādāya antato bāladārakā api yathāpi tadbuddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One made such a determination that the whole world saw the ornament of Buddhas unobstructed, up to the realm of <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, even to the youngest children, by that Buddha's Buddha-power and by the deities' divine power.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma tāvat pratigṛhṇīta bhikṣavo 'nupūrve sthitāyā buddhapiṇḍyā nimittam ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, now take hold of the sign of the row of Buddhas standing in succession.

children.text: ekapade 'ntardhāsyanti ||
children.translated_text: They will disappear all at once."

children.text: yāvadekapade 'ntarhitā ||
children.translated_text: Then they disappeared all at once.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāraṃ pratiprasrabhya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, withdrawing that formation of supernatural power, sat down on the prepared seat itself.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Having sat down, the Blessed One at that time spoke a verse:

children.text: tāvadavabhāsate kṛmiryāvannodayate divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: "A worm shines only so long as the sun has not risen;

children.text: virocana udgate tu vairavyārto bhavati na cāvabhāsate ||
children.translated_text: but when the radiant one has arisen, it is pained by rivalry and no longer shines.

children.text: tāvadavabhāsitamāsa tārkikairyāvannoditavāṃstathāgataḥ
children.translated_text: The disputants shone only so long as the Tathāgata had not arisen;

children.text: saṃbuddhāvabhāsite tu loke na tārkiko bhāsate na cāsya śrāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but when the world is illuminated by the perfectly awakened one, no disputant shines, nor does his disciple."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat vidarśitaṃ bhagavatā uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> said this to the Tīrthikas: "The Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacities.

children.text: yūyamapi vidarśayadhvam ||
children.translated_text: You too should display one."

children.text: evamukte tīrthyāstūṣṇīṃbhūtā yāvat prayāṇaparamāḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, the Tīrthikas became silent and stood there ready only to depart.

children.text: dvirapi prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat vidarśitaṃ bhagavatā uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryam ||
children.translated_text: A second time, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> said this to the Tīrthikas: "The Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power beyond ordinary human capacities.

children.text: yūyamapi vidarśayadhvam ||
children.translated_text: You too should display one."

children.text: evamukte tīrthyā anyonyaṃ vighaṭṭayanta evāhuḥ tvamuttiṣṭha tvamuttiṣṭheti ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, the Tīrthikas, nudging one another, said, "You get up, you get up."

children.text: na kaścidapyuttiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Not one of them got up.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena pāñciko mahāsenāpatistasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time <s>Pāñcika</s>, the great general, had assembled in that very gathering.

children.text: atha pāñcikasya yakṣasenāpateretadabhavat ciramapi te ime mohapuruṣā bhagavantaṃ viheṭhayiṣyanti bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ceti viditvā tumulaṃ vātavarṣaṃ saṃjanayya mahāntamutsṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pāñcika</s>, the yakṣa general, thought, "These deluded men will go on troubling the Blessed One and the community of monks for a long time." Knowing this, he produced and released a great tumultuous wind and rain.

children.text: tumulena vātavarṣeṇa tīrthyāṇāṃ maṇḍapā adarśanapathe kṣiptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the tumultuous wind and rain, the pavilions of the Tīrthikas were hurled out of sight.

children.text: tīrthyā hyaśanivarṣeṇa bādhyamānā diśo digbhyo vicalanti ||
children.translated_text: The Tīrthikas, afflicted by a rain of thunderbolts, scattered in all directions.

children.text: anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇyativarṣeṇa bādhyamānāni yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of beings, afflicted by the heavy rain, approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāni ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side.

children.text: bhagavatā tathā adhiṣṭhitam yathā tasyāṃ parṣadyekavāribindur na patitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One made such a determination that not a single drop of water fell in that assembly.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇānyanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇyudānamudānayanti aho buddhaḥ aho dharmaḥ aho saṃghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, the many hundreds of thousands of beings uttered an exclamation: "Ah, the Buddha! Ah, the Dharma! Ah, the Saṅgha!

children.text: aho dharmasya svākhyātatā ||
children.translated_text: Ah, how well the Dharma has been taught!"

children.text: pāñcikena yakṣasenāpatinā tīrthyā abhihitāḥ ete yūyaṃ mohapuruṣā bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchadhvaṃ dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The yakṣa-general <s>Pāñcika</s> said to the Tīrthikas: "You deluded men, go for refuge to the Blessed One, and to the Dharma, and to the community of monks."

children.text: te niṣpalāyamānāḥ kathayanti ete vayaṃ parvataṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmaḥ vṛkṣāṇāṃ kuḍyānāmārāmāṇāṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gacchāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they fled away, they said, "We go for refuge to a mountain; we go for refuge to trees, walls, and parks."

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time spoke a verse:

children.text: bahavaḥ śaraṇam yānti parvatāṃśca vanāni ca
children.translated_text: "Many people, stricken by fear, go for refuge to mountains and forests,

children.text: ārāmāṃścaityavṛkṣāṃśca manuṣyā bhayavarjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: to parks, shrines, and sacred trees.

children.text: na hyetaccharaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naitaccharaṇamuttamam
children.translated_text: But this refuge is not excellent; this refuge is not supreme.

children.text: naitaccharaṇamāgamya sarvaduḥkhāt pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: Having come to this refuge, one is not freed from all suffering.

children.text: yastu buddhaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: But whoever has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha,

children.text: āryasatyāni catvāri paśyati prajñayā yadā ||
children.translated_text: when he sees with wisdom the four noble truths:

children.text: duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasamutpannaṃ nirodhaṃ samatikramam
children.translated_text: suffering, the arising of suffering, cessation, and transcendence,

children.text: āryaṃ cāṣṭāṅgikaṃ mārgaṃ kṣemaṃ nirvāṇagāminām ||
children.translated_text: and the noble eightfold path, secure and leading to nirvāṇa,

children.text: etadvai śaraṇaṃ śreṣṭhametaccharaṇamuttamam
children.translated_text: this is indeed the excellent refuge; this is the supreme refuge.

children.text: etaccharaṇamāgamya sarvaduḥkhātpramucyate ||
children.translated_text: Having come to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering."

children.text: atha pūraṇasyaitadabhavat śramaṇo gautamo madīyāñ śrāvakānanvāvartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pūrṇa</s> thought, "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will win back my disciples."

children.text: iti viditvā niṣpalāyan kathayati aham yuṣmākaṃ śāsanasarvasvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, while fleeing, he said, "I shall tell you the whole essence of your teaching."

children.text: yāvad dṛṣṭigatān grāhayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he began to make them take up views.

children.text: yaduta antavāṃllokaḥ anantaḥ antavāṃścānantavāṃśca naivāntavānnānantavān sa jīvastaccharīramanyo jīvo 'nyaccharīramiti ||
children.translated_text: That is: "The world is finite; it is infinite; it is both finite and infinite; it is neither finite nor infinite. The soul is the same as the body; the soul is one thing and the body another."

children.text: te kalahajātā viharanti bhaṇḍanajātā vigṛhītā vivādamāpannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They lived having become quarrelsome, having become contentious, at odds, and fallen into dispute.

children.text: pūraṇo 'pi bhīto niṣpalāyitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūraṇa</s> too, frightened, began to flee.

children.text: sa niṣpalāyan paṇḍakena pratimārge dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was fleeing, he was seen on the road by a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch).

children.text: paṇḍako dṛṣṭvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the <s>paṇḍaka</s> spoke a verse:

children.text: kutastvamāgacchasi muktapāṇi rathakārameṣa iva nikṛttaśṛṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: "From where are you coming, open-handed one, like this cart-maker with his horn cut off?

children.text: dharmaṃ hyabhijñāya jinapraśastamāhiṇḍase kolikagardabho yathā ||
children.translated_text: Having understood the <s>dharma</s> praised by the Jina, you wander about like a weaver's donkey."

children.text: pūraṇaḥ prāha
children.translated_text: <s>Pūraṇa</s> said:

children.text: gamanāya me samayaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ kāyasya me balavīryam na kiṃcit
children.translated_text: "The time for my departure has arrived; there is no strength or vigor in my body.

children.text: spṛṣṭāśca bhāvāḥ sukhaduḥkhate me anāvṛtaṃ jñānamihārhatām ||
children.translated_text: States of pleasure and pain have been touched by me, and here the unobstructed knowledge of the <s>arhats</s> is mine.

children.text: dūrāpagato 'smi paratimirāpanudaśca tṛṣaṃ patati ||
children.translated_text: I have gone far away, and, dispeller of another's darkness, thirst falls away.

children.text: ācakṣva me dūṣika etamarthaṃ śītodakā kutra sā puṣkiriṇī ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, slanderer, this matter: where is that lotus pond with cool water?"

children.text: napuṃsakaḥ prāha
children.translated_text: The eunuch said:

children.text: eṣā khalu śītā puṣkiriṇī nalinī ca virājati toyadhārā
children.translated_text: "Here indeed is the cool lotus pond; the lotus-bed shines, with streams of water.

children.text: śramaṇādhama hīnāsatpuruṣa tvamimāṃ nanu paśyasi puṣkariṇīm ||
children.translated_text: Lowest of ascetics, base and unworthy man, do you not see this lotus pond?"

children.text: pūraṇaḥ prāha
children.translated_text: <s>Pūraṇa</s> said:

children.text: na tvaṃ naro nāpi ca nārikā tvaṃ śmaśrūṇi ca te nāsti na ca stanau tava
children.translated_text: "You are not a man, nor are you a woman; you have no beard, and you have no breasts.

children.text: bhinnasvaro 'si na ca cakravākaḥ evaṃ bhavān vātahato nirucyate ||
children.translated_text: You have a broken voice, and yet you are not a cakravāka bird; in this way, sir, you are called wind-struck."

children.text: atha pūraṇo nirgrantho vālukāghaṭaṃ kaṇṭhe baddhvā śītikāyāṃ puṣkiriṇyāṃ patitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pūraṇa</s> the <s>Nirgrantha</s>, having tied a pot of sand to his neck, fell into the cool lotus pond.

children.text: sa tatraiva kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There he died.

children.text: atha te nirgranthāḥ pūraṇaṃ mṛgayamāṇāḥ pratimārge gaṇikāṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛcchanti bhadre kaṃcit tvamadrākṣīrgacchantamiha pūraṇaṃ dharmaśāṭapraticchannaṃ kaṭacchavratabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>Nirgranthas</s>, searching for <s>Pūraṇa</s>, saw a courtesan on the road and asked her, "Lady, have you seen <s>Pūraṇa</s> going this way, covered with a rag of religion, eating the food of a ladle-vow?"

children.text: gaṇikā prāha
children.translated_text: The courtesan said:

children.text: āpāyiko nairayiko muktahastāvacārakaḥ
children.translated_text: "Bound for ruin, bound for hell, roaming with hands uncovered,

children.text: śvetābhyāṃ pāṇipādābhyāmeṣa dhvaṃsati pūraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Pūraṇa</s> is perishing, with his hands and feet turned white."

children.text: bhadre maivaṃ vocastvaṃ naitattava subhāṣitam
children.translated_text: "Lady, do not speak so; that is not well said by you.

children.text: dharmaśāṭapraticchanno dharmaṃ saṃcarate muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Covered with a rag of religion, the sage goes about practicing <s>dharma</s>."

children.text: gaṇikā prāha
children.translated_text: The courtesan said:

children.text: kathaṃ sa buddhimān bhavati puruṣo vyañjanānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: "How can a man endowed with marks be intelligent,

children.text: lokasya paśyato yo 'yaṃ grāme carati nagnakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when, while the world looks on, he wanders naked in the village?

children.text: yasyāyamīdṛśo dharmaḥ purastāllambate daśā
children.translated_text: For him whose <s>dharma</s> is such that a fringe hangs down in front,

children.text: tasya vai śravaṇau rājā kṣurapreṇāvakṛntatu ||
children.translated_text: let the king cut off both ears with the edge of a razor."

children.text: atha te nirgranthā yena śītikā puṣkiriṇī tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>Nirgranthas</s> approached the cool lotus pond.

children.text: adrākṣuste nirgranthāḥ pūraṇaṃ kāśyapaṃ puṣkiriṇyāṃ mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Nirgranthas</s> saw <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s> dead in the lotus pond.

children.text: kālagataṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ puṣkiriṇyā uddhṛtya ekānte chorayitvā prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that he had died, they drew him out of the lotus pond, threw him aside in a secluded place, and departed.

children.text: bhagavatā buddhanirmāṇo nirmito dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgato muṇḍaḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One created a Buddha apparition, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, shaven-headed and wearing a saṃghāṭī robe.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhā bhagavanto nirmitena sārdhaṃ niścayaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is the <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law) that Buddhas, Blessed Ones, settle matters together with what has been magically created.

children.text: yaṃ khalu śrāvako nirmitamabhinirmimīte yadi śrāvako bhāṣate nirmito 'pi bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: If a disciple creates an apparition, then when the disciple speaks, the apparition also speaks.

children.text: śrāvake tūṣṇībhūte nirmito 'pi tūṣṇībhavati ||
children.translated_text: When the disciple becomes silent, the apparition also becomes silent.

children.text: ekasya bhāṣamāṇasya sarve bhāṣanti nirmitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When one speaks, all the apparitions speak.

children.text: ekasya tūṣṇībhūtasya sarve tūṣṇībhavanti te ||
children.translated_text: When one becomes silent, all of them become silent.

children.text: bhagavān nirmitaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchati bhagavān vyākaroti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One asks the created apparition a question, and the Blessed One answers it.

children.text: eṣā hi dharmatā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksambuddhānām ||
children.translated_text: For this is the <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law) of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>arhats</s>, perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: bhagavatā tasya mahājanakāyasya tathā abhiprasannasya āśayaṃ cānuśayaṃ ca dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhakī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yathā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni kaiściduṣmagatānyadhigatāni mūrdhānaḥ kṣāntayo laukikā agradharmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, element, and nature of that great crowd of people who were so deeply inspired, gave such a teaching of the <s>dharma</s> that brings realization of the four noble truths, that many hundreds of thousands of beings took refuge and the training precepts; some attained warmths, summits, acceptances, and the highest worldly dharmas.

children.text: kaiścitsrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalamanāgāmiphalam ||
children.translated_text: Some realized the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, and the fruit of non-returning.

children.text: kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Some, having gone forth, realized <s>arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all defilements.

children.text: kaiścicchrāvakamahābodhau bījānyavaropitāni ||
children.translated_text: By some, seeds were planted for the great awakening of a disciple.

children.text: kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau bījānyavaropitāni ||
children.translated_text: By some, seeds were planted for the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>.

children.text: yadbhūyasā sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: For the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the Buddha, sloping toward the <s>dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>saṃgha</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstāṃ parṣadaṃ buddhanimnāṃ dharmapravaṇāṃ saṃghaprāgbhārāṃ vyavasthāpyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having established that assembly as inclined toward the Buddha, sloping toward the <s>dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>saṃgha</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: dhanyāste puruṣā loke ye buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: "Blessed are those people in the world who have gone to the Buddha for refuge.

children.text: nirvṛtiṃ te gamiṣyanti buddhakārakṛtau janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They will go to peace, those people who have done service for the Buddha.

children.text: ye 'lpānapi jine kārān kariṣyanti vināyake
children.translated_text: Those who will do even small services for the Jina, the Guide,

children.text: vicitraṃ svargamāgamya te lapsyante 'mṛtaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: having reached a wondrous heaven, will obtain the deathless state."

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 13
buddho bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s park.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena śiśumāragirau bodho nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī ||
children.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Śiśumāragiri</s>, there lived a householder named <s>Bodha</s>, rich, possessed of great wealth and great enjoyments, with an extensive and broad estate, endowed with wealth like that of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, and rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam ||
children.translated_text: A wife was brought for him from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati ||
children.translated_text: With her he played, took pleasure, and enjoyed himself.

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: As he was playing, taking pleasure, and enjoying himself, after some time his wife became pregnant.

children.text: sā upariprāsādatalagatā ayantritopacārā dhāryate kālartukaiścopakaraṇairanuvidhīyate vaidyaprajñaptaiścāhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitairāhāraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: She was kept on an upper terrace of the palace with unrestricted attendance; she was supplied with seasonally appropriate furnishings and with foods prescribed by physicians, foods that were not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, and not too astringent, foods free from excess bitterness, sourness, saltiness, sweetness, pungency, and astringency.

children.text: hārārdhahārabhūṣitagātrā apsareva nandanavanacāriṇī mañcānmañcaṃ pīṭhātpīṭhamavatarantī adharimāṃ bhūmim ||
children.translated_text: Her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an apsaras wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, she moved down from couch to couch and from seat to seat to the lower floor.

children.text: na cāsyāḥ kiṃcidamanojñaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadeva garbhasya paripākāya ||
children.translated_text: Nor did she hear any sound that was displeasing, all solely for the maturation of the child in her womb.

children.text: sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā ||
children.translated_text: After eight or nine months had passed, she gave birth.

children.text: dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā ||
children.translated_text: A daughter was born, beautiful, lovely to behold, pleasing, and endowed with every limb and minor part.

children.text: tasyāstrīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasān vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā varṇasaṃsthānaviśeṣānurūpaṃ nāmadheyaṃ vyapasthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: For her, after they had fully performed a birth festival for three sevens, twenty-one days, they established a name suited to her special beauty of color and form.

children.text: sā dhātryaṅkagatā unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiśca cottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Carried on the laps of nurses, she was brought up and made to grow with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, clarified butter, and other especially warmed articles of nurture.

children.text: āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam ||
children.translated_text: She grew quickly, like a lotus standing in a lake.

children.text: yadā mahatī saṃvṛttā tadā rūpiṇī yauvanānurūpayā ācāravihāraceṣṭayā devakanyeva tadgṛhamavabhāsamānā suhṛtsambandhibāndhavānām antarjanasya ca prītimutpādayati ||
children.translated_text: When she had become grown, beautiful, and with conduct, movements, and gestures suited to youth, she lit up that house like a daughter of the gods and produced delight among friends, relations, kinsmen, and the women of the household.

children.text: tasyāstādṛśīṃ vibhūtiṃ śrutvā nānādeśanivāsirājaputrā amātyaputrā gṛhapatiputrā dhaninaḥ śreṣṭhiputrāḥ sārthavāhaputrāśca bhāryārtham yācanakān preṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having heard of such splendor in her, princes, ministers' sons, householders' sons, wealthy men, merchants' sons, and caravan-leaders' sons living in various regions sent suitors to ask for her as a wife.

children.text: yathā yathā cāsau prārthyate tathā tathā bodho gṛhapatiḥ sutarāṃ prītimutpādayati ||
children.translated_text: The more she was sought in marriage, the more the householder <s>Bodha</s> felt still greater delight.

children.text: saṃlakṣayati mayā eṣā na kasyacidrūpeṇa deyā na śilpena nāpyādhipatyena kiṃtu yo mama kulaśīlena vā dhanena vā sadṛśo bhavati tasya mayā dātavyeti ||
children.translated_text: He considered: 'I must not give her to just anyone for beauty, nor for skill, nor even for authority; rather, whoever is equal to me in family and character, or in wealth, to him I should give her.'
