children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having consented by silence to the request of the brahmin householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: atha bhagavān vihāraṃ gatvā purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One went to the monastery and sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate gaccha ānanda bhikṣūṇāmevamārocaya śalākāṃ cāraya yo yuṣmākamutsahate aśvatīrthikaṃ nāgaṃ vinetum sa śalākāṃ gṛhṇātu iti ||
children.translated_text: Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce this to the monks: 'Pass around the token. Whoever among you is able to subdue the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s>, let him take the token.'"

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣusaṃghasyārocayitvā buddhapramukhe bhikṣusaṃghe śalākāṃ cārayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One; and, after announcing it to the community of monks, he began to pass around the token in the community of monks headed by the Buddha.

children.text: bhagavatā śalākā na gṛhītā ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One did not take the token.

children.text: sthavirā bhikṣavaḥ samanvāhartuṃ saṃvṛttāḥ kimarthaṃ bhagavatā śalākā na gṛhītā iti paśyantyāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya guṇodbhāvanāṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The elder monks began to reflect, "Why did the Blessed One not take the token?" Looking into the matter, they saw that he wished to bring forth the virtues of the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.

children.text: tairapi na gṛhītā ||
children.translated_text: They too did not take it.

children.text: āyuṣmān svāgataḥ samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavatā śalākā na gṛhītā sthavirasthaviraiśca bhikṣubhiriti paśyati mama guṇodbhāvanāṃ kartukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> began to reflect, "For what reason did the Blessed One not take the token, nor the monks senior among the elders?" He saw, "He wishes to bring forth my virtues."

children.text: tacchāsturmanorathaṃ pūrayāmi gṛhṇāmi śalākāmiti ||
children.translated_text: "Then I will fulfill the Teacher's wish; I will take the token."

children.text: tenārdhāsanaṃ muktvā gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya śalākā gṛhītā ||
children.translated_text: Leaving half his seat, he stretched out his arm, which was like an elephant's trunk, and took the token.

children.text: jānakāḥ pṛcchakā buddhā bhagavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Buddhas, Blessed Ones, know, yet they ask.

children.text: pṛcchati buddho bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandam katareṇānanda bhikṣuṇā śalākā gṛhīteti sa kathayati svāgatena bhadanteti ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, asked the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, "Which monk, <s>Ānanda</s>, took the token?" He said, "<s>Svāgata</s>, venerable sir."

children.text: bhagavānāha gaccha ānanda svāgataṃ bhikṣumevaṃ vada duṣṭanāgo 'sau kāyendriyaṃ te rakṣitavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and say this to the monk <s>Svāgata</s>: 'That nāga is wicked; you must guard your bodily faculty.'"

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One, and he went to where the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> was.

children.text: upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat āyuṣman svāgata bhagavānevamāha duṣṭanāgo 'sau kāyendriyaṃ te rakṣitavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, the Blessed One says this: 'That nāga is wicked; you must guard your bodily faculty.'"

children.text: sa kathayati āyuṣmannānanda akopyā śāsturājñā ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the Teacher's command is not to be shaken."

children.text: api tu yādṛśo 'śvatīrthiko nāgaḥ īdṛśānāṃ nāgānāmikṣuveṇunaḍavadyadi pūrṇo jambudvīpaḥ syāt tathāpi me te romāpi neñjayituṃ samarthāḥ syuḥ prāgevāśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ kāyendriyasyoparodhaṃ kariṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "Indeed, even if Jambudvipa were filled with such nagas as this <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga, like sugarcane, bamboo, and reeds, still they would not be capable of making even one hair of mine tremble, much less will the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga be able to obstruct the faculty of my body."

children.text: āyuṣmānānanda ārogyamityuktvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ananda</s>, having said, "May there be well-being," departed.

children.text: athāyuṣmān svāgatastasyā eva rātreratyayātpūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śuśumāragiriṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, after that same night had passed, dressed in the forenoon, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> for alms.

children.text: śuśumāragiriṃ piṇḍāya caritvā yenāśvatīrthikasya nāgasya bhavanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After walking for alms in <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, he approached the dwelling of the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga.

children.text: adrākṣīdaśvatīrthiko nāga āyuṣmantaṃ svāgataṃ dūrādeva ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga saw the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> from afar.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ saṃlakṣayati kimanena śramaṇakena mama mṛtipravṛttir yena me bhavanamāgacchatīti punaḥ saṃlakṣayati āganturayam āgacchatu tāvaditi ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, he reflected, "What death-proceeding of mine has been set in motion by this little ascetic, that he is coming to my dwelling?" Then he reflected again, "He is a guest. Let him come for now."

children.text: athāyuṣmān svāgatastasya hradaṃ gatvā pātracīvaramekāntamupasaṃkṣipya pādau prakṣālya hastau nirmādya pānīyaṃ parisrāvya jīrṇaparṇakāni samudānīya niṣadya bhaktakṛtyaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> went to his lake, put his bowl and robe aside in one place, washed his feet, cleaned his hands, strained drinking water, gathered old leaves, sat down, and began to perform the meal-duty.

children.text: aśvatīrthikena nāgenāsāvatithiriti kṛtvādhyupekṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga disregarded him, thinking, "He is a guest."

children.text: āyuṣmān svāgataḥ saṃlakṣayati nāsaṃkṣobhitā duṣṭanāgā damathamāgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> reflected, "Wicked nagas do not come to taming unless they have been agitated."

children.text: saṃkṣobhayāmyenamiti ||
children.translated_text: "I will agitate him."

children.text: tena pātraṃ prakṣālya tatpātrodakaṃ tasmin hrade prakṣiptam ||
children.translated_text: He washed his bowl and threw that bowl-water into the lake.

children.text: sa saṃkṣubdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The naga was agitated.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati ayaṃ mayā śramaṇa āgacchannadhyupekṣitaḥ bhuñjāno 'pyupekṣitaḥ anena mama bhavane ucchiṣṭodakaṃ choritam ||
children.translated_text: He reflected, "This ascetic was disregarded by me when he came; he was also disregarded while eating. Now he has poured leftover water into my dwelling."

children.text: nāmāvaśeṣamenaṃ karomīti tīvreṇa paryavasthānena paryavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I will leave him only a name," and he became possessed by a fierce hostile obsession.

children.text: uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya āyuṣmataḥ svāgatasyopari cakrakaṇapaparaśubhindipālādīni praharaṇāni kṣeptumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rising up into the sky above, he began to hurl weapons over the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: disc-blades, missiles, axes, javelins, and the like.

children.text: āyuṣmān svāgato maitrīsamāpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> had entered the attainment of loving-kindness.

children.text: tānyasya divyānyutpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandārakāṇi puṣpāṇi bhūtvā kāye nipatanti ||
children.translated_text: Those weapons became divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and mandaraka flowers, and fell upon his body.

children.text: aśvatīrthiko nāgo 'ṅgāravarṣamutsraṣṭumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga began to send down a rain of coals.

children.text: tadapi divyāni puṣpāṇi māndārakāṇi bhūtvā kāye nipatitumārabdham ||
children.translated_text: That too became divine mandaraka flowers and began to fall upon his body.

children.text: aśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ pāṃsu varṣitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga began to rain down dust.

children.text: tadapi divyānyagurucūrṇāni tamālapatracūrṇāni bhūtvā nipatitumārabdham ||
children.translated_text: That too became divine powders of agaru and powders of tamala leaves, and began to fall.

children.text: aśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ krodhaparyavasthānānubhāvāddhūmayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the force of his angry obsession, the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga began to emit smoke.

children.text: āyuṣmānapi svāgata ṛddhyanubhāvāddhūmayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> too, through the force of supernormal power, began to emit smoke.

children.text: aśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ krodhaparyavasthānānubhāvāt prajvalitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the force of his angry obsession, the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga burst into flame.

children.text: āyuṣmānapi svāgatastejodhātuṃ samāpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> too entered the fire-element attainment.

children.text: iti tatrāśvatīrthikasya nāgasya krodhasyānubhāvenāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya ṛddhyanubhāvena mahānavabhāsaḥ prādurbhūto yaṃ dṛṣṭvā śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ saṃbhrāntā itaścāmutaśca nirīkṣitumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus there, by the force of the anger of the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga and by the force of the supernormal power of the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, a great radiance appeared. Seeing it, the brahmans and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> became alarmed and began to look about here and there.

children.text: kathayanti eṣa bhavanto bhagavānaśvatīrthikaṃ nāgaṃ vinayati āgacchata paśyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Good people, this is the Blessed One taming the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga. Come, let us see."

children.text: anekāni prāṇaśatasahasrāṇi nirgatāni ||
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of living beings went out.

children.text: bhikṣavo 'pi tamudārāvabhāsaṃ tatrasthā eva nirīkṣitumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monks too, from where they stood, began to look at that lofty radiance.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāmabhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānām yaduta svāgato bhikṣuriti ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, foremost among my monk-disciples who repeatedly enter the fire-element attainment is this monk <s>Svāgata</s>."

children.text: yadāśvatīrthiko nāgo vigatamadadarpaḥ kṣīṇapraharaṇaśca saṃvṛttaḥ tadā niṣpalāyitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga had become free of intoxication and arrogance and had exhausted his weapons, then he began to flee.

children.text: āyuṣmatā svāgatena samantato 'gnir nirmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> created fire all around.

children.text: aśvatīrthako nāgo yām yāṃ diśaṃ gacchati tāṃ tāṃ diśamādīptāṃ pradīptāṃ samprajvalitāmekajvālībhūtāṃ paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Whichever direction the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga went, in each direction he saw it blazing, flaming, fully kindled, and become a single mass of flame.

children.text: sa itaścāmutaśca nairmāṇikenāgninā paryākulīkṛto 'trāṇaḥ sarvamaśāntaṃ paśyati nānyatrāyuṣmata eva svāgatasya samīpaṃ śāntaṃ śītībhūtam ||
children.translated_text: Confused here and there by the magically created fire, without protection, he saw everything unpeaceful; nowhere did he see anything peaceful and cooled except near the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> himself.

children.text: sa yenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He approached the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya āyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat alaṃ bhadanta svāgata ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "Enough, venerable <s>Svāgata</s>!

children.text: kiṃ māṃ viheṭhayasīti sa kathayati jarādharmā nāhaṃ tvāṃ viheṭhayāmi api tu tvameva māṃ viheṭhayasi ||
children.translated_text: Why are you harassing me?" He replied, "Old fellow, I am not harassing you; rather, you yourself are harassing me.

children.text: yadi mayā evaṃvidhā guṇagaṇā nādhigatā abhaviṣyan adyāhaṃ tvayā nāmāvaśeṣaḥ kṛto 'bhaviṣyamiti ||
children.translated_text: If qualities of such a kind had not been attained by me, today you would have left me only a name."

children.text: sa kathayati bhadanta svāgata ājñāpayatu kiṃ mayā karaṇīyam bhadramukha bhagavato 'ntikaṃ gatvā śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhāṇeti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, command me. What should I do?" "Good sir, go into the presence of the Blessed One and undertake going for refuge and the training precepts."

children.text: sa kathayati bhadanta svāgata śobhanam evaṃ karomīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, very well. I will do so."

children.text: athāyuṣmān svāgato 'śvatīrthanāgamādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, taking the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> naga with him, approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān svāgato bhagavantamidamavocat ayaṃ so 'śvatīrthiko nāga iti ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> said this to the Blessed One: "This is that nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s>."

children.text: tatra bhagavānaśvatīrthikaṃ nāgamāmantrayate tvaṃ tāvadbhadramukha pūrvakeṇa duścaritena pratyavarāyāṃ tiryagyonau upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s>: "Good sir, through former misconduct you have been reborn in a lower animal birth.

children.text: sa tvametarhi hataprahataniviṣṭaḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ paraprāṇoparodhena jīvikāṃ kalpayasi ||
children.translated_text: Now you are intent on killing and striking, taking the lives of others, and you make your living by obstructing the lives of others.

children.text: itaścyutasya te kā gatirbhaviṣyati kā upapattiḥ ko 'bhisamparāya iti ||
children.translated_text: When you pass away from here, what will your destiny be, what rebirth, what future state?"

children.text: sa kathayati bhagavan ājñāpaya kiṃ mayā karaṇīyamiti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Blessed One, command me. What should I do?"

children.text: bhagavānāha mamāntikāccharaṇaśikṣāpadāni gṛhāṇa śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmabhayamanuprayaccheti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Take refuge and the training precepts from me, and grant safety to the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>."

children.text: sa kathayati eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi śikṣāpadāni ca gṛhṇāmi adyāgreṇa ca śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmabhayamanuprayacchāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Here I go to the Blessed One for refuge, and I take the training precepts. From this day forward I grant safety to the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>."

children.text: atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ prabhūtamabhisāraṃ gṛhītvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, taking abundant gifts, approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇāḥ śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavantamidamavocan bhagavatā bhadanta aśvatīrthiko nāgo vinīto bhagavānāha na mayā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'śvatīrthako nāgo vinītaḥ api tu svāgatena bhikṣuṇā ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, has the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> been tamed by the Blessed One?" The Blessed One said, "Brahmins and householders, the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> was not tamed by me, but by the monk <s>Svāgata</s>."

children.text: katamena bhadanta ihanivāsinaiva bodhasya gṛhapateḥ putreṇa ||
children.translated_text: "By which one, venerable sir?" "By that very resident here, the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s>."

children.text: saṃpattikāmo loko vipattipratikūlaḥ ||
children.translated_text: People desire good fortune and are averse to misfortune.

children.text: tatraike kathayanti asmākamasau bhrātuḥ putro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: There some said, "He is our brother's son."

children.text: apare kathayanti asmākaṃ bhāgineya iti ||
children.translated_text: Others said, "He is our sister's son."

children.text: apare kathayanti asmākaṃ vayasyaputra iti ||
children.translated_text: Others said, "He is our friend's son."

children.text: atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapataya utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocan adhivāsayatvasmākaṃ bhagavān bhadantasvāgatamāgamya bhaktaṃ saptāhena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti ||
children.translated_text: Then the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> rose from their seats, arranged their upper garments over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to him: "May the Blessed One, venerable sir, out of regard for the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, consent to a meal for seven days together with the community of monks."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavāñ śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to the request of the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> by remaining silent.

children.text: atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, knowing from the Blessed One's silence that he had consented, bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and departed from his presence.

children.text: śuśumāragirau anyatamo brāhmaṇa ahituṇḍiko bodhasya gṛhapatervayasyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> there was a certain brahmin snake-charmer, a friend of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.

children.text: so 'śvatīrthikasya nāgasya bhayānniṣpalāyya śrāvastīṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Out of fear of the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s>, he had fled and gone to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: sa rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena hastimadhyasyopari viśvāsikaḥ sthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had been appointed by King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> to a trusted position over the elephant corps.

children.text: sa kenacideva karaṇīyena śuśumāragirimanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For some business he arrived at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>.

children.text: tena śrutam yathā svāgatena bhikṣuṇā bodhasya gṛhapateḥ putreṇāśvatīrthiko nāgo vinīta iti ||
children.translated_text: He heard that the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> had been tamed by the monk <s>Svāgata</s>, the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.

children.text: śrutvā ca punaryenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he approached the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramyāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>'s feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: sa brāhmaṇa āyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me āryasvāgataḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhakteneti ||
children.translated_text: That brahmin said this to the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "May noble <s>Svāgata</s> consent to a meal inside my house tomorrow."

children.text: āyuṣmān svāgataḥ kathayati brāhmaṇa māmāgamya śuśumāragirīyakairbrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhirbuddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho bhaktena saptāhenopanimantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> said, "Brahmin, on my account the brahmins and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> have invited the community of monks headed by the Buddha to a meal for seven days.

children.text: nāhamadhivāsayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I do not consent."

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati ārya yadi sāmprataṃ nādhivāsayasi yadā śrāvastīgato bhavasi tadā mama gṛhe tatprathamataḥ piṇḍapātaḥ paribhoktavya iti ||
children.translated_text: The brahmin said, "Noble one, if you do not consent at present, then when you have gone to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the first alms meal should be eaten in my house."

children.text: kathayati evamastu iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "So be it."

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The brahmin bowed at his feet and departed.

children.text: atha bhagavān yathābhiramyaṃ śuśumāragirau vihṛtya yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having stayed at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> as long as he wished, set out on tour toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Traveling on tour by stages, he arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: He stayed at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: aśrauṣīdanāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavān bhargeṣu janapadacārikām carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ ihaiva viharatyasmākamevārāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard: "The Blessed One, wandering on tour through the <s>Bharga</s> districts, has arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>; he is staying right here in our own park."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ śrāvastyā niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he went out from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇamanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One instructed the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, seated to one side, with a discourse on Dharma, caused him to undertake it, stirred him up, and gladdened him.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: Having, in many ways, instructed him with a discourse on Dharma, caused him to undertake it, stirred him up, and gladdened him, he became silent.

children.text: anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirutthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper garment over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One consent to take tomorrow's meal inside my house, together with the community of monks."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapatestūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to the invitation of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> by remaining silent.

children.text: athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, knowing that the Blessed One had consented by silence, rejoiced in and approved the Blessed One's words, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet, and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: aśrauṣīt sa brāhmaṇo bhagavān bhargeṣu janapadacārikāṃ carannihānuprāpta ihaiva viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāma iti ||
children.translated_text: That brahmin heard: "The Blessed One, wandering on tour through the <s>Bharga</s> districts, has arrived here and is staying right here in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s park."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaryenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he went to where the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> was.

children.text: upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat adhivāsayatu me āryaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhakteneti ||
children.translated_text: After approaching, he said this to the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "May the noble one consent to take tomorrow's meal inside my house."

children.text: adhivāsayatyāyuṣmān svāgatastasya brāhmaṇasya tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> consented to that brahmin's invitation by remaining silent.

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇa āyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that brahmin, knowing that the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> had consented by silence, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Then during that very night the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> prepared pure and excellent hard and soft food, rose at dawn, arranged seats, set out water jars, and informed the Blessed One of the time by messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. Let the Blessed One now consider the proper time."

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yenānāthapiṇḍadasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, went to the residence of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tenāpi brāhmaṇenāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya praṇīta āhāraḥ sajjīkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That brahmin too had prepared excellent food for the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.

children.text: āyuṣmānapi svāgataḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya yena tasya brāhmaṇasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> also dressed in the forenoon, took his bowl and robe, and went to that brahmin's residence.

children.text: upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After arriving, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān svāgatastena brāhmaṇena praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> was seated apart, that brahmin satisfied him with excellent food.

children.text: sa brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati āryeṇa svāgatena praṇīta āhāraḥ paribhuktaḥ no jarayiṣyati pānakamasmai prayacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: The brahmin considered, "The noble <s>Svāgata</s> has eaten rich food; it will not digest. I will give him a drink."

children.text: iti viditvā āyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat ārya praṇītaste āhāraḥ paribhuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having thought this, he said this to the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "Noble one, you have eaten rich food.

children.text: pānakaṃ piba ||
children.translated_text: Drink the beverage.

children.text: pānaṃ jarayiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: The drink will make it digest."

children.text: sa kathayati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Good.

children.text: evaṃ karomīti ||
children.translated_text: I will do so."

children.text: tena pānakaṃ sajjīkṛtya hastimadādaṅguliḥ prakṣiptā ||
children.translated_text: Having prepared the drink, the brahmin put into it a finger-measure of elephant-must liquor.

children.text: asamanvāhṛtyārhatāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate ||
children.translated_text: Without directing attention, knowledge and vision do not operate for arhats.

children.text: āyuṣmatā svāgatena tatpānakaṃ pītam ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Svāgata</s> drank that beverage.

children.text: tato dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ śrāvastīvīthīṃ kiliñjacchannām ||
children.translated_text: Then, after giving a discourse in acknowledgment of the offering, he departed along a reed-covered street of <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: sa tāmatikrānta ātapena spṛṣṭo madyakṣiptaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had passed along it, touched by the heat and overcome by the liquor, he fell down on the ground.

children.text: asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Buddhas, Blessed Ones, are not subject to forgetfulness.

children.text: bhagavatā suparṇikā kuṭir nirmitā maitaṃ kaścid dṛṣṭvā śāsane 'prasādaṃ pravedayiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One created a small shelter, thinking, "Let no one see him and thereby arouse lack of faith in the teaching."

children.text: anāthapiṇḍadaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena svahastena saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> knew that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, he satisfied and served them with pure and excellent hard and soft food with his own hands.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: After satisfying and serving them in many ways with his own hands, and knowing that the Blessed One had eaten, washed his hands, and put away his bowl, he took a lower seat and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the Dharma.

children.text: atha bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> with a discourse on Dharma, rose from his seat, and departed.

children.text: anupūrveṇa tatpradeśam anuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due order he arrived at that place.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma ayaṃ sa bhikṣavaḥ svāgato bhikṣuryenāśvatīrthiko nāgastāvaccaṇḍo vinītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One withdrew those magical formations and addressed the monks: "Monks, this is that monk <s>Svāgata</s> by whom the nāga <s>Aśvatīrthika</s>, so fierce, was tamed.

children.text: kimidānīmeṣa śakto durbhuktasyāpi viṣamapanetum no bhadanta iti ||
children.translated_text: Is he now able to remove the poison even from what has been badly consumed?" "No, venerable sir."

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ ime cānye cādīnavā madyapāne ||
children.translated_text: "Monks, these and other dangers attend the drinking of liquor.

children.text: tasmānna bhikṣuṇā madyaṃ pātavyaṃ dātavyaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore liquor is not to be drunk by a monk or given by him."

children.text: atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ svāgataṃ madyavaśāt suptamutthāpyedamavocat svāgata kimidam asamanvāhāro bhagavan asamanvāhāraḥ sugata ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One roused the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, who was asleep under the power of liquor, and said this: "<s>Svāgata</s>, what is this?" "Inattention, Blessed One; inattention, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: tato bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamādāya vihāraṃ gatvā purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One took the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, went to the monastery, and sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

children.text: niṣadya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma māṃ bho bhikṣavaḥ śāstāramuddiśya bhavadbhirmadyamapeyamadeyamantataḥ kuśāgreṇāpi ||
children.translated_text: Having sat down, he addressed the monks: "Monks, with me as your teacher, liquor is not to be drunk or given by you, even as much as with the tip of a blade of kuśa grass."

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kiṃ bhadantāyuṣmatā svāgatena karma kṛtaṃ yenāḍhye kule mahādhane mahābhoge jātaḥ kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena kroḍamallako jāto durāgata iti ca saṃjñā saṃvṛttā kiṃ karma kṛtam yena bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāṃ cāgratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭo bhagavānāha svāgatenaiva bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyabhāvīni svāgatena karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, who cuts off all doubts: "Venerable sir, what deed was done by the venerable <s>Svāgata</s> that he was born in a wealthy family, with great riches and great possessions? What deed was done that he was born a <s>Kroḍamallaka</s> and came to be known as <s>Durāgata</s>? What deed was done that, having gone forth in the Blessed One's teaching, he realized arhatship through the abandoning of all defilements, and was declared foremost among those who enter the fire element?" The Blessed One said, "Monks, the monk <s>Svāgata</s> himself performed and accumulated those deeds; they have acquired their provisions, their conditions have matured, they have appeared like a flood, and they are inevitable. <s>Svāgata</s> performed and accumulated the deeds; who else will experience them?"

children.text: na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātāvapi tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: "Monks, deeds that have been performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds that have been performed and accumulated, both good and bad, ripen only in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-fields."

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi
children.translated_text: "Deeds do not perish, even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: when they have obtained the proper combination and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karvaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī ||
children.translated_text: "In the past, monks, in a certain market-town there lived a householder who was wealthy, rich, possessed of great property, with extensive and broad possessions, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: so 'pareṇa samayena suhṛtsambandhibāndhavaparivṛto 'ntarjanaparivṛtaścodyānabhūmiṃ nirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At another time, surrounded by friends, relatives, and kinsmen, and surrounded also by the people of his household, he went out to the park grounds.

children.text: asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya ||
children.translated_text: When Buddhas do not arise, pratyekabuddhas arise in the world, compassionate toward the lowly and poor, fond of remote beds, seats, and food, and uniquely worthy of offerings in the world.

children.text: yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caraṃstaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now a certain pratyekabuddha, wandering on tour through the countryside, reached that market-town.

children.text: so 'dhvapariśramāddhātuvaiṣamyācca glānaḥ piṇḍārthī tadudyānaṃ praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fatigued from the road and ill because his bodily elements were out of balance, he entered that park in search of alms.

children.text: sa gṛhapatistaṃ dṛṣṭvā paryavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the householder saw him, he became hostile.

children.text: tena pauruṣeyāṇāmājñā dattā bhavantaḥ niṣkāsayatainaṃ pravrajitamiti ||
children.translated_text: He gave an order to his servants: 'Sirs, drive this renunciant out.'

children.text: teṣāṃ na kaścidutsahate niṣkāsayitum ||
children.translated_text: None of them dared to drive him out.

children.text: tena gṛhapatinā bhūyasā paryavasthitena sa mahātmā svayameva grīvāyāṃ gṛhītvā niṣkāsitaḥ uktaśca kroḍamallakānāṃ madhye prativaseti ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder, becoming still more hostile, himself seized that great-souled one by the neck and drove him out, saying, 'Go live among the <s>Kroḍamallakas</s>.'

children.text: sa durbalaprāṇo bhūmau nipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Weak in vitality, he fell to the ground.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati hato 'yaṃ tapasvī gṛhapatirupahataśca ||
children.translated_text: The householder thought, 'This ascetic has been struck down, and I too am ruined.

children.text: abhyuddhāro 'sya kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I must make amends to him.'

children.text: iti viditvā uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, the pratyekabuddha rose up into the sky above and began to perform miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and shining.

children.text: āśu pṛthagjanasyarddhirāvarjanakarī ||
children.translated_text: The miraculous power of noble ones quickly wins over an ordinary person.

children.text: sa mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati avatarāvatara mahādakṣiṇīya mama duścaritapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanuprayaccheti ||
children.translated_text: Like a tree cut at the root, he fell at his feet and said, 'Come down, come down, great recipient of offerings. Extend a helping hand to me, sunk in the mud of misconduct.'

children.text: sa tasyānugrahārthamavatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of showing him favor, he descended.

children.text: tena tasya pūjāsatkāraṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye 'pakāraḥ kṛtaḥ mā asya karmaṇo bhāgī syām ||
children.translated_text: The householder honored and revered him, and made an aspiration: 'Since I have done harm to such a true recipient of offerings, may I not become heir to that deed.

children.text: yattūpakāraḥ kṛtaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeyam evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: But since I have done a service, by this root of merit may I be born in a wealthy family, rich and possessing great property; may I obtain qualities such as these, and may I please a teacher more excellent than this one, not displease him.'

children.text: bhagavānāha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau gṛhapatireva asau svāgato bhikṣustena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? The one who was that householder at that time and on that occasion was none other than this monk <s>Svāgata</s>.

children.text: yadanena pratyekabuddhe kārāḥ kṛtāḥ tenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he showed honor to the pratyekabuddha, he was born in a wealthy family, rich and possessing great property.

children.text: yadapakāraḥ kṛtaḥ tena pañcajanmaśatāni kroḍamallako jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he did harm, he was born as a <s>Kroḍamallaka</s> for five hundred births.

children.text: yāvadetarhyapi caramabhaviko 'pi tatkroḍamallaka eva jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even now, although he is in his final existence, he was born as that very <s>Kroḍamallaka</s>.

children.text: yatpraṇidhānaṃ kṛtam tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Because he made that aspiration, after going forth in my teaching he realized arhatship through the abandoning of all defilements.

children.text: ahamanena pratyekabuddhakoṭiśatasahasrebhyaḥ prativiśiṣṭataraḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He has pleased me, a teacher more excellent than hundreds of thousands of crores of pratyekabuddhas, and has not displeased me.

children.text: bhūyo 'pi kāśyape bhagavati samyaksambuddhe pravrajito babhūva ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, under <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Blessed One, the perfectly awakened Buddha, he had gone forth.

children.text: yasya bhikṣorantike pravrajitaḥ sa bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenābhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monk in whose presence he went forth was repeatedly declared by the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, to be foremost among those who enter the fire element.

children.text: tatrānena yāvadāyurbrahmacaryaṃ cāritam na ca kaścidguṇagaṇo 'dhigataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There he practiced celibate religious life as long as he lived, but he did not attain any collection of qualities."

children.text: sa maraṇasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdho yanmayā bhagavati kāśyape samyaksambuddhe 'nuttare dakṣiṇīye yāvadāyurbrahmacaryaṃ caritam na ca kaścidguṇaguṇo 'dhigataḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenottaro māṇavo vyākṛto bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddha iti tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkuryām ||
children.translated_text: At the time of death he began to make an aspiration: "Although I practiced lifelong chastity under the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfect Buddha, the unsurpassed recipient of gifts, I did not attain even the slightest excellent quality. By this root of merit, may I go forth in the dispensation of that one, the Tathāgata, arhat, perfect Buddha named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, whom the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfect Buddha, predicted as the young man <s>Uttara</s>, saying, 'Young man, in a people whose lifespan is a hundred years you will be the Tathāgata, arhat, perfect Buddha named <s>Śākyamuni</s>'; and may I realize arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements."

children.text: yathā mām upādhyāyo bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenābhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ evaṃ māmapi sa bhagavāñ śākyamuniḥ śākyādhirājo 'bhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagraṃ nirdiśediti ||
children.translated_text: "Just as my preceptor was repeatedly declared by the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfect Buddha, to be foremost among those who enter the fire-element attainment, so may that Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, declare me too to be foremost among those who repeatedly enter the fire-element attainment."

children.text: tatpraṇidhānavaśādetarhi tathāgatenābhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the power of that aspiration, he has now been declared by the Tathāgata to be foremost among those who repeatedly enter the fire-element attainment.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ ekāntaśuklānāmekāntaśuklaḥ vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, for actions that are entirely black there is a result that is entirely black; for those that are entirely white, one that is entirely white; and for those that are mixed, one that is mixed.

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, having abandoned actions that are entirely black, and also those that are mixed, one should devote oneself only to actions that are entirely white.

children.text: ityevaṃ bho bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, monks, you should train yourselves.

children.text: ityavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Delighted, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 14

dharmatā khalu cyavanadharmaṇo devaputrasya pañca pūrvanimittāni prādurbhavanti akliṣṭāni vāsāṃsi kliśyanti amlānāni mālyāni mlāyanti daurgandhaṃ kāyena niṣkrāmati ubhābhyāṃ kakṣābhyāṃ svedaḥ prādurbhavati cyavanadharmā devaputraḥ sva āsane dhṛtiṃ na labhate ||
children.translated_text: It is the rule of things that five prior signs appear for a god's son who is subject to falling: unstained garments become stained, unwithered garlands wither, a foul smell comes forth from the body, sweat appears from both armpits, and the god's son who is subject to falling finds no firmness on his own seat.

children.text: athānyatamaścyavanadharmā devaputraḥ pṛthivyāmāvartate saṃparivartyaivaṃ cāha hā mandākini hā puṣkariṇi hā vāpi hā caitraratha hā pāruṣyaka hā nandanavana hā miśrakāvana hā pāriyātraka hā pāṇḍukambalaśilā hā devasabhā hā sudarśana iti karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevate sma ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain god's son who was subject to falling rolled on the ground, turning this way and that, and cried out, "Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>! Alas, the tank! Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas, <s>Pāruṣyaka</s>! Alas, <s>Nandanavana</s>! Alas, <s>Miśrakāvana</s>! Alas, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>! Alas, <s>Pāṇḍukambalaśilā</s>! Alas, the assembly of the gods! Alas, <s>Sudarśana</s>!" He lamented most pitifully.

children.text: adrākṣīcchakro devānāmindrastaṃ devaputramatyarthaṃ pṛthivyāmāvartantaṃ parivartantam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, saw that god's son rolling and turning about excessively on the ground.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā punaryena sa devaputrastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he approached that god's son.

children.text: upasaṃkramya taṃ devaputramidamavocat hā kasmāt tvaṃ mārṣa atyarthaṃ pṛthivyāmāvartase samparivartase karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevase hā mandākini hā puṣkiriṇi hā vāpi hā caitraratha hā pāruṣyaka hā nandanavana hā miśrakāvana hā pāriyātraka hā pāṇḍukambalaśilā hā devasabhā hā sudarśana iti karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevase evamukte devaputraḥ śakraṃ devānāmindramidamavocat eṣo 'haṃ kauśika divyaṃ sukhamanubhūya itaḥ saptame divase rājagṛhe nagare sūkaryāḥ kukṣau upapatsyāmi ||
children.translated_text: After approaching, he said this to the god's son: "Ah, friend, why are you rolling on the ground so excessively, turning about, and lamenting most pitifully, crying, 'Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>! Alas, the tank! Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas, <s>Pāruṣyaka</s>! Alas, <s>Nandanavana</s>! Alas, <s>Miśrakāvana</s>! Alas, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>! Alas, <s>Pāṇḍukambalaśilā</s>! Alas, the assembly of the gods! Alas, <s>Sudarśana</s>!'?" When this was said, the god's son said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, having experienced divine happiness, on the seventh day from now I shall be reborn in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the womb of a sow.

children.text: tatra mayā bahūni varṣāṇyuccāraprasrāvaḥ paribhoktavya iti ||
children.translated_text: There for many years I shall have to consume feces and urine."

children.text: atha śakro devānāmindraḥ kāruṇyatayā taṃ devaputramidamavocat ehi tvaṃ mārṣa buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha dvipadānāmagryam dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha virāgāṇāmagryam saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha gaṇānāmagryamiti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, out of compassion said this to the god's son: "Come, friend, go for refuge to the Buddha, the foremost of two-footed beings; go for refuge to the Dharma, the foremost of dispassionate states; go for refuge to the Saṃgha, the foremost of communities."

children.text: atha sa devaputrastiryagyonyupapattibhayabhīto maraṇabhayabhītaśca śakraṃ devānāmindramidamavocat eṣo 'haṃ kauśika buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgāṇāmagryam saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam ||
children.translated_text: Then that god's son, terrified of rebirth in an animal womb and terrified of death, said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, I go for refuge to the Buddha, the foremost of two-footed beings; I go for refuge to the Dharma, the foremost of dispassionate states; I go for refuge to the Saṃgha, the foremost of communities."

children.text: atha sa devaputrastriśaraṇaparigṛhīto bhūtvā cyutaḥ kālagatastuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that god's son, having been embraced by the three refuges, fell from there; and after dying he was reborn in the <s>Tuṣita</s> class of gods.

children.text: dharmatā khalu adhastāddevānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate nordhvam ||
children.translated_text: It is the rule of things that knowledge and vision among gods proceeds downward, not upward.

children.text: atha śakro devānāmindrastaṃ devaputramavalokayati kimasau devaputraḥ sūkarikāyāḥ kukṣau upapanno na veti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, looked for that god's son, thinking, "Was that god's son reborn in the womb of a sow, or not?"

children.text: yāvat paśyati nopapannastiryakpreteṣu ||
children.translated_text: As far as he looked, he saw that he had not been reborn among animals or pretas.

children.text: narakeṣūpapanna iti paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He looked to see whether he had been reborn in the hells.

children.text: nopapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had not been reborn there.

children.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupapanna iti paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He looked to see whether he had been reborn in the class of human beings.

children.text: nopapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had not been reborn there.

children.text: cāturmahārājakāyikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśāṃścāvalokayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to look among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: tatrāpi nādrākṣīt ||
children.translated_text: There too he did not see him.

children.text: atha śakro devānāmindraḥ kutūhalajāto yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, filled with curiosity, approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ śakro devānāmindro bhagavantamidamavocat ihāhaṃ bhadanta adrākṣamanyatamaṃ devaputraṃ cyavanadharmāṇaṃ pṛthivyāmāvartamānaṃ karuṇakaruṇaṃ ca paridevamānam hā mandākini hā puṣkiriṇi hā vāpi hā caitraratha hā pāruṣyaka hā nandanavana hā miśrakāvana hā pāriyātraka hā pāṇḍukambalaśilā hā devasabhā hā sudarśana iti ||
children.translated_text: Seated in seclusion, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Here, venerable sir, I saw a certain divine son, subject to death, rolling about on the earth and lamenting most pitifully: 'Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, <s>Puṣkiriṇī</s>! Alas, the pond! Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas, <s>Pāruṣyaka</s>! Alas, <s>Nandanavana</s>! Alas, <s>Miśrakāvana</s>! Alas, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>! Alas, the <s>Pāṇḍukambala</s> rock! Alas, the assembly hall of the gods! Alas, <s>Sudarśana</s>!'

children.text: tamenamevaṃ vadāmi kasmāt tvaṃ mārṣa atyarthaṃ śocasi paridevase krandasi urasi tāḍayasi saṃmohamāpadyasa iti sa evamāha eṣo 'haṃ kauśika divyaṃ sukhamapahāya itaḥ saptame divase rājagṛhe nagare sūkarikāyāḥ kukṣau upapatsyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I said this to him: 'Good sir, why are you grieving so excessively, lamenting, crying out, beating your breast, and falling into bewilderment?' He said this: 'I, <s>Kauśika</s>, having abandoned divine happiness, on the seventh day from now will be reborn in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the womb of a sow.'

children.text: tatra mayā bahūni varṣāṇi uccāraprasrāvaḥ paribhoktavyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: 'There for many years I will have to consume feces and urine.'

children.text: tamenamevaṃ vadāmi ehi tvaṃ mārṣa buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha dvipadānāmagryam dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha virāgāṇāmagryam saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha gaṇānāmagryamiti ||
children.translated_text: I said this to him: 'Come, good sir, go for refuge to the Buddha, foremost among two-footed beings; go for refuge to the Dharma, foremost among things free from passion; go for refuge to the Saṃgha, foremost among communities.'

children.text: sa evamāha eṣo 'haṃ kauśika buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgāṇāmagryam saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam ||
children.translated_text: He said this: 'I, <s>Kauśika</s>, go for refuge to the Buddha, foremost among two-footed beings; I go for refuge to the Dharma, foremost among things free from passion; I go for refuge to the Saṃgha, foremost among communities.'

children.text: ityuktvā sa devaputraḥ kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, that divine son died.

children.text: kutrāsau bhadanta devaputra upapanno bhagavānāha tuṣitā nāma kauśika devāḥ sarvakāmasamṛddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Where, venerable sir, has that divine son been reborn?" The Blessed One said, "<s>Kauśika</s>, there are gods named <s>Tuṣita</s>, endowed with every sensual pleasure.

children.text: tatrāsau modate devo gatveha śaraṇatrayam ||
children.translated_text: There that god rejoices, having gone here to the three refuges."

children.text: atha śakro devānāmindra āttamanāstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, delighted, at that time uttered these verses:

children.text: ye buddhaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim
children.translated_text: "Those who go to the Buddha for refuge do not go to a bad destiny;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies.

children.text: ye dharmaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim
children.translated_text: Those who go to the Dharma for refuge do not go to a bad destiny;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies.

children.text: ye saṃghaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim
children.translated_text: Those who go to the Saṃgha for refuge do not go to a bad destiny;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies."

children.text: atha bhagavāñ śakrasya devānāmindrasya bhāṣitamanusaṃvarṇayannevamāha evametat kauśika evametat ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, approving what <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had spoken, said this: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is.

children.text: ye buddhaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim
children.translated_text: Those who go to the Buddha for refuge do not go to a bad destiny;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies.

children.text: ye dharmaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim
children.translated_text: Those who go to the Dharma for refuge do not go to a bad destiny;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies.

children.text: ye saṃghaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim
children.translated_text: Those who go to the Saṃgha for refuge do not go to a bad destiny;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies."

children.text: atha śakro devānāmindro bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya prāñjalikṛtasampuṭo bhagavantaṃ namasyamānastatraivāntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, rejoiced in and approved the Blessed One's words, bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and, with his joined palms cupped, vanished right there while paying homage to the Blessed One.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo 'bhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: The monks, delighted, rejoiced in it.

children.text: Chapter 15
buddho bhagavāñśrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jīvatāṃ dhriyamāṇānām yāpayatāṃ keśanakhastūpā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed the nature of living, remaining, and continuing Buddhas, Blessed Ones, that there are stūpas for their hair and nails.

children.text: yadā buddhā bhagavantaḥ pratisaṃlīnā bhavanti tadā bhikṣavaḥ keśanakhastūpe pūjāṃ kṛtvā kecit piṇḍāya praviśanti kecid dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisukhānyanubhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, have withdrawn into seclusion, then the monks, after making worship at the hair-and-nail stūpa, some enter for alms, while others experience the happiness of meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments.

children.text: tena khalu samayena buddho bhagavān pratisaṃlīno 'bhūt athānyatamo bhikṣuḥ sāyāhnasamaye keśanakhastūpe sarvāṅgaiḥ praṇipatya tathāgatamākārataḥ samanusmaraṃścittamabhiprasādayati ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavāniti ||
children.translated_text: At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, had withdrawn into seclusion. Then a certain monk, in the evening, prostrated with all his limbs at the hair-and-nail stūpa and, recollecting the <s>Tathāgata</s> by his qualities, made his mind serene: 'Thus indeed that Blessed One is a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.'

children.text: atha bhagavān sāyāhne pratisaṃlayanādvyutthāya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the evening the Blessed One arose from seclusion and sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

children.text: adrākṣīdbhagavāṃstaṃ bhikṣuṃ keśanakhastūpe sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya cittamabhiprasādayantam ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One saw that monk prostrating with his whole body at the hair-and-nail stūpa and making his mind serene.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhikṣūnāmantrayate sma paśyata yūyaṃ bhikṣava etaṃ bhikṣuṃ keśanakhastūpe sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya cittamabhiprasādayantam evaṃ bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he addressed the monks: "Monks, do you see this monk prostrating with his whole body at the hair-and-nail stūpa and making his mind serene?" "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: anena bhikṣuṇā yāvatī bhūmirākrāntā adho 'śītiyojanasahasrāṇi yāvat kāñcanacakramityatrāntarā yāvatyo vālukāstāvantyanena bhikṣuṇā cakravartirājyasahasrāṇi paribhoktavyāni ||
children.translated_text: "As much ground as has been occupied by this monk, down below for eighty thousand yojanas as far as the golden disk, and as many grains of sand as there are in that space, so many thousands of reigns as a wheel-turning king will this monk enjoy."

children.text: atha teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāmetadabhavat puruṣamātrāyām yāvadgartāyāṃ na śakyate vālukā gaṇayitum kutaḥ punaraśītiyojanasahasrāṇi yāvat kāñcanacakramiti ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to those monks: "Even in a pit the size of a man, the grains of sand cannot be counted; how much less from eighty thousand yojanas down to the golden disk?"

children.text: kaḥ śakyate iyatkālaṃ saṃsāre saṃsaritumiti ||
children.translated_text: "Who could wander in saṃsāra for such a length of time?"

children.text: atha te bhikṣavo na bhūyaḥ keśanakhastūpe kārāṃ kartumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those monks no longer began to perform service at the stūpa of hair and nails.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ cetasā cittamājñāya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma anavarāgro bhikṣavaḥ saṃsāro 'vidyānivaraṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanānāṃ tṛṣṇārgalabaddhānāṃ dīrghamadhvānaṃ saṃdhāvatāṃ saṃsaratām ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought in the minds of those monks, addressed the monks: "Monks, saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning for beings covered by the obstruction of ignorance, bound by the fetter of craving, fastened by the bar of craving, who run on and wander through the long course of time.

children.text: pūrvā koṭir na prajñāyate duḥkhasya ||
children.translated_text: The former limit of suffering is not discerned.

children.text: āyuṣmānupālī buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papraccha yaduktaṃ bhagavatā asya bhikṣoriyatpuṇyaskandha iti kutra bhadanteyatpuṇyaskandhastanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gamiṣyati nāhamupālinn ito bahiḥ samanupaśyāmyeva kṣatiṃ copahatiṃ ca yathā sabrahmacārī sabrahmacāriṇo 'ntike ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, "Venerable sir, regarding what was said by the Blessed One, 'This monk has such a heap of merit,' where will this heap of merit go to thinness, destruction, and exhaustion?" "<s>Upāli</s>, I do not see any injury or harm outside this comparable to that caused by a fellow practitioner toward a fellow practitioner.

children.text: tatropālinn imāni mahānti kuśalamūlāni tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti ||
children.translated_text: There, <s>Upāli</s>, these great roots of wholesome action go to thinness, destruction, and exhaustion.

children.text: tasmāttarhi te upālinn evaṃ śikṣitavyam yaddagdhasthūṇāyā api cittaṃ na pradūṣayiṣyāmaḥ prāgeva savijñānake kāye ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, you should train in this way: 'We will not corrupt our minds even toward a burnt stump, much less toward a body endowed with consciousness.'"

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo 'bhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced.

children.text: Chapter 16
śrāvastyāṃ nidānam ||
children.translated_text: The occasion was at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā dvau śukaśāvakau pratilabdhau ||
children.translated_text: At that time two young parrots had been obtained by the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena niveśanaṃ nītvā ālāpitau poṣitau saṃvardhitau mānuṣālāpaṃ ca śikṣāpitau ||
children.translated_text: He brought them to his residence, made them speak, nourished them, raised them, and taught them human speech.

children.text: tayoścāyuṣmānānando 'bhīkṣṇamāgatya caturāryasatyasamprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ karoti yaduta idaṃ duḥkham ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipaditi ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> often came to them and gave a Dharma teaching leading to penetration of the four noble truths, namely: 'This is suffering; this is the arising of suffering; this is the cessation of suffering; this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

children.text: sthavirasthavirā api bhikṣavo 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanamupasaṃkrāmanti śāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapānandaraivataprabhṛtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Elder monks too, such as <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, and <s>Raivata</s>, visited the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s residence.

children.text: teṣāṃ kālānukālamupasaṃkrāmatāṃ tābhyāṃ śukaśāvakābhyāṃ nāmāni parijñātāni ||
children.translated_text: As they visited from time to time, their names became known to the two young parrots.

children.text: yāvadapareṇa samayenāyuṣmāñ śāriputro 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then at another time the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> came to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s residence.

children.text: adrāṣṭāṃ tau śukaśāvakau āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram ||
children.translated_text: The two young parrots saw the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā antarjanamāmantrayata eṣa bhadantaḥ sthaviraḥ śāriputra āgacchati āsanamasya prajñāpayateti ||
children.translated_text: On seeing him, they addressed the inner household: 'This venerable elder <s>Śāriputra</s> is coming; prepare a seat for him.'

children.text: evamāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ kāśyapaṃ raivatamāyuṣmantamānandaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayata eṣo 'smākamācāryānanda āgacchati āsanamasya prajñāpayateti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, when they saw the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Raivata</s>, and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, they would say, 'This is our teacher <s>Ānanda</s> coming; prepare a seat for him.'

children.text: yāvadapareṇa samayena bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then at another time the Blessed One came to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s residence.

children.text: adrāṣṭāṃ tau śukaśāvakau bhagavantaṃ dūrādevāgacchantaṃ prāsādikaṃ prasādanīyaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ parameṇa cittamatyupaśamena samanvāgataṃ suvarṇayūpamiva śriyā jvalantam ||
children.translated_text: The two young parrots saw the Blessed One coming from afar, handsome, inspiring faith, with peaceful faculties and peaceful mind, endowed with supreme tranquillity of mind, blazing with splendor like a golden sacrificial post.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punastvaritatvaritamantarjanamāmantrayata eṣa bhadanto bhagavānāgacchati āsanamasya prajñāpayateti hṛṣṭamadhurasvareṇa nikūjataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, they quickly and repeatedly addressed the inner household: 'This venerable Blessed One is coming; prepare a seat for him,' and they chirped in delighted, sweet voices.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstayoranugrahārthaṃ praviśya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, for the sake of showing favor to them, entered and sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavatā śukaśāvakau caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikayā dharmadeśanayā śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau ||
children.translated_text: After sitting down, the Blessed One established the two young parrots in the going for refuge and in the training precepts by means of a Dharma teaching leading to penetration of the four noble truths.

children.text: atha bhagavāñśukaśāvakau antarjanaṃ ca dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the two young parrots and the inner household with a Dharma talk, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: tau cāntarjanasya viharataḥ pramādavihāriṇau biḍālena prāṇinā gṛhītau ||
children.translated_text: While those two were dwelling carelessly as the inner household went about its affairs, they were seized by a cat.

children.text: vihvalavadanau chidyamāneṣu marmasu mucyamāneṣu saṃdhiṣu namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāyetyuktvā kālagatau cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣūpapannau ||
children.translated_text: With faces distraught, as their vital spots were being torn and their joints were loosening, they said, 'Homage to the Buddha; homage to the Dharma; homage to the Saṅgha,' and, when they died, they were reborn among the Cāturmahārājika gods.

children.text: atha bhagavānanyatamasmin pradeśe smitamakārṣīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One smiled in a certain place.

children.text: adrākṣīdāyuṣmānānando bhagavantaṃ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvantam ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw the Blessed One displaying a smile.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhagavantamidamavocat nāhetupratyayaṃ bhadanta tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, he said to the Blessed One, 'Venerable sir, tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not display a smile without a cause and condition.

children.text: ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāviṣkaraṇe evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, for the displaying of a smile?' 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.

children.text: nāhetupratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not display a smile without a cause and condition.

children.text: dṛṣṭau tvayā ānanda tau śukaśāvakau dṛṣṭau bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, those two young parrots?' 'I saw them, venerable sir.'

children.text: tau ānanda śukaśāvakau mama samanantaraprakrāntasya biḍālena prāṇinā jīvitād vyaparopitau ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ānanda</s>, immediately after I had departed, those two young parrots were deprived of life by a cat.

children.text: tau buddhadharmasaṃghāvalambanayā smṛtyā kālagatau cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣūpapannau ||
children.translated_text: When they died, through recollection supported by the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, they were reborn among the Cāturmahārājika gods.'

children.text: atha saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣan ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the morning, several monks dressed, took their bowls and robes, and entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.

children.text: aśrauṣuḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya pracaranto 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśane śukaśāvakau namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāyeti biḍālena prāṇinā vyaparopitau iti ||
children.translated_text: Many monks, while going about <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms, heard that in the house of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> two young parrots, saying, "Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṃgha," had been deprived of life by a cat.

children.text: śrutvā ca punaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyāḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntāḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamayya pādau prakṣālya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after hearing this, having again gone about <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms, having performed the duties connected with the meal, and having returned after the meal from the alms-round, they put away their bowl and robe, washed their feet, and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads to the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇāḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavo bhagavantamidamavocan iha vayaṃ bhadanta saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvavad yāvad anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśane dvau śukaśāvakau namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāyeti kurvāṇau biḍālena prāṇinā jīvitādvyaparopitau iti ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, the many monks said this to the Blessed One: "Here, venerable sir, we many monks, as before, up to: in the house of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, two young parrots, saying, 'Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṃgha,' were deprived of life by a cat.

children.text: tayorbhadanta kā gatiḥ kopapattiḥ ko 'bhisamparāyo bhagavānāha tau bhikṣavaḥ śukaśāvakau tasya śaraṇagamanasya vipākena ṣaṭtriṃśatkṛtvaścāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣūpapatsyete ṣaṭtriṃśatkṛtvastrāyastriṃśeṣu yāmeṣu tuṣiteṣu nirmāṇaratiṣu paranirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣūpapatsyete ||
children.translated_text: "What, venerable sir, is their destiny? What is their rebirth? What is their future course?" The Blessed One said, "Monks, through the ripening of that going for refuge, those two young parrots will be reborn thirty-six times among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> class; thirty-six times they will be reborn among the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, among the <s>Yāma</s> gods, among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, and among the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods.

children.text: tatastāvat ṣaṭsu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu sattvā vyapasaṃsṛtya paścime bhave paścime nikete paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe manuṣyapratilābhaṃ labdhvā pratyekāṃ bodhimabhisaṃbhotsyete dharmaśca sudharmaśca pratyekabuddhau bhaviṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when they have passed through beings among those six desire-realm gods, in their last existence, their last abode, their last acquisition of an individual body, they will obtain human birth and will realize solitary awakening. They will become the pratyekabuddhas <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Sudharma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ hi bhikṣavo mahāphalaṃ dharmaśravaṇaṃ mahānuśaṃsakam kaḥ punarvādo dharmadeśanā dharmābhisamayo vā ||
children.translated_text: "Thus, monks, hearing the Dharma has great fruit and great benefit; how much more so the teaching of the Dharma or the realization of the Dharma?

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yanno dharmaśravaṇābhiratā bhaviṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We shall be devoted to hearing the Dharma.'

children.text: ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Delighted in mind, those monks rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.

children.text: Chapter 17
evaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard.

children.text: ekasmin samaye bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām ||
children.translated_text: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, on the shore of <s>Markaṭahrada</s>, in the <s>Kūṭāgāraśālā</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms.

children.text: vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamayya yena cāpālacaityaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gone about <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms, having performed the duties connected with the meal, and having returned after the meal from the alms-round, he put away his bowl and robe and approached the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine.

children.text: upasaṃkramyānyatamaṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down at the root of a certain tree for the day's abiding.

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate ramaṇīyā ānanda vaiśālī vṛjibhūmiścāpālacaityaṃ saptāmrakam gautamanyagrodhaḥ śālavanaṃ dhurānikṣepanaṃ mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Pleasant, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Vaiśālī</s>; pleasant is the <s>Vṛji</s> land, the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, <s>Saptāmraka</s>, <s>Gautamanyagrodha</s>, <s>Śālavana</s>, <s>Dhurānikṣepana</s>, and the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Malla</s>s.

children.text: citro jambudvīpaḥ madhuraṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām ||
children.translated_text: "Variegated is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; sweet is the life of human beings.

children.text: yasya kasyacidānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ ākāṅkṣan sa kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and repeatedly practiced the four bases of supernormal power, if he wished, he might remain for a kalpa or for the remainder of a kalpa.

children.text: tathāgatasya ānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and repeatedly practiced the four bases of supernormal power.

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "If he wished, the <s>Tathāgata</s> might remain for a kalpa or for the remainder of a kalpa."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmānānandastūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was silent.

children.text: dvirapi trirapi bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate ramaṇīyā ānanda vaiśālī vṛjibhūmiścāpālaṃ caityaṃ saptāmrakaṃ bahupattrakaṃ gautamanyagrodhaḥ śālavanaṃ dhurānikṣepanaṃ mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam ||
children.translated_text: A second time and a third time the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Pleasant, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Vaiśālī</s>; pleasant is the <s>Vṛji</s> land, the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, <s>Saptāmraka</s>, <s>Bahupattraka</s>, <s>Gautamanyagrodha</s>, <s>Śālavana</s>, <s>Dhurānikṣepana</s>, and the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Malla</s>s.

children.text: citro jambudvīpaḥ madhuraṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām ||
children.translated_text: "Variegated is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; sweet is the life of human beings.

children.text: yasya kasyacidānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ ākāṅkṣan sa kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and repeatedly practiced the four bases of supernormal power, if he wished, he might remain for a kalpa or for the remainder of a kalpa.

children.text: tathāgatasya ānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and repeatedly practiced the four bases of supernormal power.

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "If he wished, the <s>Tathāgata</s> might remain for a kalpa or for the remainder of a kalpa."

children.text: dvirapi trirapi āyuṣmānānandastūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: A second time and a third time the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was silent.

children.text: atha bhagavata etadabhavat sphuṭo 'bhavadānando bhikṣurmāreṇa pāpīyasā yatredānīm yāvat trirapi audārike avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkriyamāṇe na śaknoti tannimittamājñātum yathāpi tataḥ sphuṭo māreṇa pāpīyasā ||
