children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One: "The monk <s>Ānanda</s> has evidently been clouded by <s>Māra Pāpīyān</s>, since now, even when a broad sign and indication has been made clear as many as three times, he is not able to understand that sign. Thus he has been clouded by <s>Māra Pāpīyān</s>."

children.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate gaccha tvamānanda anyataravṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya vihara mā ubhāvapi ākīrṇavihāriṇau bhaviṣyāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>; stay at the root of some other tree. Let us not both dwell in a crowded way."

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya anyatamavṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One, and he sat down at the root of another tree for the day's abiding.

children.text: sa māraḥ pāpīyān yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māra Pāpīyān</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocat parinirvātu bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One attain parinirvāṇa.

children.text: parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya ||
children.translated_text: "It is the time and occasion for the <s>Sugata</s>'s parinirvāṇa."

children.text: kasmāt tvaṃ pāpīyann evaṃ vadasi parinirvātu bhagavān parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya eko 'yaṃ bhadanta samayo bhagavānurubilvāyāṃ viharati nadyā nairañjanāyāstīre bodhimūle 'cirābhisaṃbuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Why, <s>Pāpīyan</s>, do you speak thus: 'Let the Blessed One enter parinirvāṇa; the time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s parinirvāṇa has come'? Venerable sir, there was this one occasion: the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Urubilvā</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the foot of the bodhi tree, shortly after his complete awakening.

children.text: so 'ham yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I approached the Blessed One there.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavantamevaṃ vadāmi parinirvātu bhagavān parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, I said this to the Blessed One: 'Let the Blessed One enter parinirvāṇa; the time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s parinirvāṇa has come.'

children.text: bhagavānevamāha na tāvat pāpīyan parinirvāsyāmi yāvanna me śrāvakāḥ paṇḍitā bhaviṣyanti vyaktā vinītā viśāradāḥ alamutpannotpannānāṃ parapravādināṃ sahadharmeṇa nigrahītāraḥ alaṃ svasya vādasya paryavadāpayitāro bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā upāsikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this: 'Not yet, <s>Pāpīyan</s>, will I enter parinirvāṇa, until my disciples, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, are wise, clear, disciplined, confident, able to restrain by the true Dharma any opposing teachers who arise, and able to bring their own doctrine to completion.

children.text: vaistārikaṃ ca te brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyanti bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃprakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: And they will practice the holy life in an extensive way, widespread and broadly established, until it has been rightly proclaimed among gods and humans.'

children.text: etarhi bhadanta bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ paṇḍitā vyaktā vinītā viśāradā alamutpannotpannānāṃ parapravādināṃ sahadharmeṇa nigrahītāraḥ svasya vādasya paryavadāpayitāro bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā upāsikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, venerable sir, the Blessed One's disciples, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, are wise, clear, disciplined, confident, able to restrain by the true Dharma any opposing teachers who arise, and able to bring their own doctrine to completion.

children.text: vaistārikaṃ ca te brahmacaryaṃ bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃprakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: And their holy life is extensive, widespread, broadly established, and rightly proclaimed among gods and humans.

children.text: tasmādahamevaṃ vadāmi parinirvātu bhagavān parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I say this: 'Let the Blessed One enter parinirvāṇa; the time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s parinirvāṇa has come.'"

children.text: alpotsukastvaṃ pāpīyan bhava ||
children.translated_text: "Be unconcerned, <s>Pāpīyan</s>.

children.text: na cirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasya trayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayānnirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Before long, at the end of three months from now, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will enter parinirvāṇa in the nirvāṇa-element without remainder."

children.text: atha mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhavat parinirvāsyate bata śramaṇo gautamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Māra Pāpīyān</s>: "Indeed, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is going to enter parinirvāṇa."

children.text: iti viditvā hṛṣṭastuṣṭaḥ pramudita udagraḥ prītisaumanasyajātastatraivāntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, delighted, pleased, glad, elated, and filled with joy and happiness, he vanished right there.

children.text: atha bhagavata etadabhavat kastathāgatasya saṃmukhaṃ vaineyaḥ supriyo gandharvarājā subhadraśca parivrājakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One: "Who is to be trained in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? <s>Supriya</s>, king of the gandharvas, and <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic.

children.text: tayostrayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayādindriyaparipāko bhaviṣyati sukhādhiṣṭhānaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: At the end of those three months their faculties will have matured, or there will be a basis for happiness.

children.text: śakyaṃ śrāvakavaineyastathāgatena vinayituṃ na tu tathāgatavaineyaḥ śrāvakeṇa ||
children.translated_text: One to be trained by a disciple can be disciplined by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, but one to be trained by the <s>Tathāgata</s> cannot be disciplined by a disciple."

children.text: atha bhagavata etadabhavat yannvahaṃ tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyeyaṃ yathā samāhite citte jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārānutsṛjeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One: "What if I entered such a samādhi (meditative concentration) that, with my mind concentrated, after sustaining the life-formations, I might relinquish the lifespan-formations?"

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārānutsraṣṭumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One entered such a samādhi (meditative concentration) that, with his mind concentrated, after sustaining the life-formations, he began to relinquish the lifespan-formations.

children.text: samanantarādhiṣṭhiteṣu jīvitasaṃskāreṣu mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūdulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the life-formations had been sustained, there was a great earthquake, meteors fell, and the quarters blazed.

children.text: antarikṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti ||
children.translated_text: Divine drums resounded in the sky.

children.text: samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu ṣaṇnimittāni prādurbhūtāni puṣpavṛkṣāḥ śīrṇāḥ ratnavṛkṣāḥ śīrṇāḥ ābharaṇavṛkṣāḥ śīrṇāḥ bhavanasahasrāṇi prakampitāni sumeruśṛṅgāni viśīrṇāni daivatāni vāditrabhāṇḍāni parāhatāni ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the lifespan-formations had been relinquished, six signs appeared among the gods of the desire realm: flower trees withered, jewel trees withered, ornament trees withered, thousands of mansions shook, the peaks of <s>Sumeru</s> shattered, and the deities' musical instruments were struck out of tune.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstasmāt samādhervyutthāya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One arose from that samādhi (meditative concentration) and at that time spoke this verse:

children.text: tulyamatulyaṃ ca saṃbhavaṃ bhavasaṃskāramapotsṛjanmuniḥ
children.translated_text: "Relinquishing both the comparable and the incomparable arising, the conditioned formations of existence, the sage,

children.text: adhyātmarataḥ samāhito hyabhinat kośamivāṇḍasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: delighting inwardly and concentrated, broke the sheath like one born from an egg."

children.text: samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣu ṣaṭ kāmāvacarā devāḥ kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā bhagavato 'ntikaṃ prakrāntā darśanāya vandanāya ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the lifespan-formations had been relinquished, the six classes of desire-realm gods made an agreement and set out to the Blessed One's presence, to see him and venerate him.

children.text: bhagavatā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yadanekairdevatāśatasahasraiḥ satyāni dṛṣṭāni dṛṣṭasatyāḥ svabhavanamanuprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One gave such a Dharma teaching that many hundreds of thousands of deities saw the truths; having seen the truths, they returned to their own dwellings.

children.text: samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣvanekāni parvatakandaragiriguhābhyo 'nekāni ṛṣiśatasahasrāṇyāgatāni ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the lifespan-formations had been relinquished, many hundreds of thousands of seers came from mountain caverns and mountain caves.

children.text: te bhagavatā eta bhikṣavaścarata brahmacaryam pravrajitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They were ordained by the Blessed One with the words, "Come, monks; practice the holy life."

children.text: tairyojayadbhirghaṭadbhiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: As they exerted themselves and applied themselves, through the abandonment of all defilements they realized arhatship.

children.text: samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣvanekā nāgayakṣagandharvakinnaramahoragā bhagavataḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntā bhagavato darśanāya ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the lifespan-formations had been relinquished, many nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and mahoragas approached the Blessed One, to see the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavatā teṣāmevaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā yadanekair nāgayakṣagandharvakinnarairmahoragaiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni yāvat svabhavanamanuprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One gave them such a Dharma teaching that many nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and mahoragas undertook the going for refuge and the training precepts, and then returned to their own dwellings.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ sāyāhṇe 'bhisaṃlayanādvyutthāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, in the evening, arose from seclusion and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet and stood to one side.

children.text: ekāntasthita āyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya aṣṭau ime ānanda aṣṭau pratyayā mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, for a great earthquake?" "There are, <s>Ānanda</s>, these eight causes and eight conditions for a great earthquake.

children.text: katame 'ṣṭau iyamānanda mahāpṛthivī apsu pratiṣṭhitā āpo vāyau pratiṣṭhitāḥ vāyurākāśe pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are the eight? This great earth, <s>Ānanda</s>, is established on water; the waters are established on wind; the wind is established in space.

children.text: bhavatyānanda samayo yadākāśe viṣamā vāyavo vānti āpaḥ kṣobhayanti āpaḥ kṣubdhāḥ pṛthivīṃ cālayanti ||
children.translated_text: There is a time, <s>Ānanda</s>, when irregular winds blow in space. They disturb the waters, and the disturbed waters shake the earth.

children.text: ayamānanda prathamo hetuḥ prathamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the first cause, the first condition, for a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda bhikṣurmaharddhiko bhavati mahānubhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, a monk may be of great supernormal power and great might.

children.text: sa ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ pṛthivīṃ cālayati ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes, he shakes the earth.

children.text: devatā maharddhikā bhavati mahānubhāvā ||
children.translated_text: A deity may be of great supernormal power and great might.

children.text: sāpi parīttāṃ pṛthivīsaṃjñāmadhitiṣṭhati apramāṇāṃ cāpsaṃjñām ||
children.translated_text: She establishes a limited perception of earth and an immeasurable perception of water.

children.text: sāpyākāṅkṣamāṇā pṛthivīṃ cālayati ||
children.translated_text: If she too wishes, she shakes the earth.

children.text: ayaṃ dvitīyo heturdvitīyaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This is the second cause, the second condition, for a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>:

children.text: yasmin samaye bodhisattvastuṣitād devanikāyāccyutvā mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: at the time when the bodhisattva, having fallen from the company of the gods in <s>Tuṣita</s>, descends into his mother's womb, then at that time there is a great earthquake, and this whole world is filled with a sublime radiance.

children.text: yā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatrāmū sūryācandramasau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those inter-world regions of the world, blind, dark, and enveloped in gloom, where those sun and moon, although of such great supernormal power and such great might, do not experience the radiance of one another's light, are also filled at that time with a sublime radiance.

children.text: tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ te tayānyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānante anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: The beings born there, seeing one another by that light, recognize: "Other beings, good sirs, have been born here too; other beings, good sirs, have been born here too."

children.text: ayamānanda tṛtīyo hetustṛtīyaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the third cause, the third condition, for a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣer niṣkrāmati atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the bodhisattva comes forth from his mother's womb, then at that time there is a great earthquake, and this whole world is filled with a sublime radiance.

children.text: yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃ mahānubhāvau ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those inter-world regions of the world too, blind, dark, and enveloped in gloom, where these sun and moon, although of such great might, do not experience the radiance of one another's light, are also filled at that time with a sublime radiance.

children.text: tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: The beings born there, seeing one another by that light, recognize: "Other beings, good sirs, have been born here too; other beings, good sirs, have been born here too."

children.text: ayamānanda caturtho hetuścaturthaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the fourth cause, the fourth condition, for a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo 'nuttaraṃ jñānamadhigacchati atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the bodhisattva attains unsurpassed knowledge, then at that time there is a great earthquake, and this whole world is filled with a sublime radiance.

children.text: yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those inter-world regions of the world too, blind, dark, and enveloped in gloom, where these sun and moon, although of such great supernormal power and such great might, do not experience the radiance of one another's light, are also filled at that time with a sublime radiance.

children.text: tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: The beings born there, seeing one another by that light, recognize: "Other beings, good sirs, have been born here too; other beings, good sirs, have been born here too."

children.text: ayamānanda pañcamo hetuḥ pañcamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the fifth cause, the fifth condition, for a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye tathāgatas triparivartadvādaśākāraṃ dharmacakraṃ parivartayati atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Tathāgata</s> sets in motion the wheel of Dharma with its three turnings and twelve aspects, then at that time there is an especially great earthquake, and this whole world is filled with a sublime radiance.

children.text: yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those inter-world regions of the world too, blind, dark, and enveloped in gloom, where these sun and moon, although of such great supernormal power and such great might, do not experience the radiance of one another's light, are also filled at that time with a sublime radiance.

children.text: tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: The beings born there, seeing one another by that light, recognize: "Other beings, good sirs, have been born here too; other beings, good sirs, have been born here too."

children.text: ayamānanda ṣaṣṭho hetuḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the sixth cause, the sixth condition, for a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye tathāgato jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārānutsṛjati atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati ulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ antarikṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having sustained the life-formations, relinquishes the lifespan-formations, then at that time there is an especially great earthquake, meteors fall, the quarters blaze, divine drums resound in the sky, and this whole world is filled with a sublime radiance.

children.text: yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Even those world-interstices of the world, blind, dark, wrapped in the darkness of gloom, where these sun and moon, though so great in miraculous power and so great in majesty, do not experience any illuminating radiance, at that time become pervaded by a sublime light.

children.text: tatra ye sattvā upapannās te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: There the beings who have been reborn, by that light, see one another and recognize: 'Other venerable beings too have been reborn here; other venerable beings too have been reborn here.'

children.text: ayamānanda saptamo hetuḥ saptamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the seventh cause, the seventh condition, of a great earthquake.

children.text: punaraparamānanda nacirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasya nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, before long the <s>Tathāgata</s> will enter parinirvāṇa in the nirvāṇa-element without remainder.

children.text: atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati ulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ antarikṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinandanti sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryacandramasau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Then at that time there is a great earthquake; meteors fall, the quarters blaze, divine drums resound in the sky, and this whole world becomes pervaded by a sublime light. Even those world-interstices of the world, blind, dark, wrapped in the darkness of gloom, where these sun and moon, though so great in miraculous power and so great in majesty, do not experience any illuminating radiance, at that time become pervaded by a sublime light.

children.text: tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: There the beings who have been reborn, by that light, see one another and recognize: 'Other venerable beings too have been reborn here; other venerable beings too have been reborn here.'

children.text: ayamānanda aṣṭamo heturaṣṭamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the eighth cause, the eighth condition, of a great earthquake.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat yathā khalvahaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi ihaiva bhagavatā jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārā utsṛṣṭā bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has said, here and now, after sustaining the life-formations, the Blessed One has relinquished the lifespan-formations.'

children.text: bhagavānāha evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.

children.text: etarhi ānanda tathāgatena jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārā utsṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Ānanda</s>, after sustaining the life-formations, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has relinquished the lifespan-formations.'

children.text: saṃmukhaṃ me bhadanta bhagavato 'ntikācchrutaṃ saṃmukhamudgṛhītam yasya kasyaciccatvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: 'Venerable sir, I heard it directly in the Blessed One's presence, and received it directly from him: for anyone by whom the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of miraculous power) have been practiced, developed, and cultivated, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, if he wished, could remain for a kalpa or for the remainder of a kalpa.

children.text: bhagavatā bhadanta catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Venerable sir, the Blessed One has practiced, developed, and cultivated the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of miraculous power).

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: If he wished, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could remain for a kalpa or for the remainder of a kalpa.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu bhagavān kalpam tiṣṭhatu sugataḥ kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed One remain for a kalpa; let the <s>Sugata</s> remain for the remainder of a kalpa.'

children.text: tavaivānanda aparādhastavaiva duṣkṛtam yastvaṃ tathāgatasya yāvat trirapyaudāre avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkṛte na śaknoṣi tannimittaṃ pratiśrāvayitum api tataḥ sphuṭo māreṇa pāpīyasā ||
children.translated_text: 'It is your own fault, <s>Ānanda</s>; it is your own wrongdoing, that when the <s>Tathāgata</s> had, as many as three times, made plain so lofty a sign of illumination, you were not able to respond to that sign. And afterward you were overwhelmed by <s>Māra Pāpīyān</s>.

children.text: kimanyasya ānanda bhāṣeta tathāgatastāṃ vācam yā syād dvidhā no bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: To whom else, <s>Ānanda</s>, would the <s>Tathāgata</s> speak a word that might be twofold?' 'No, venerable sir.'

children.text: sādhu sādhu ānanda asthānametadānanda anavakāśo yat tathāgatastāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣeta yā syāddvidhā ||
children.translated_text: 'Good, good, <s>Ānanda</s>. It is impossible, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no occasion, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> should speak a word that might be twofold.

children.text: gaccha tvamānanda yāvanto bhikṣavaścāpālaṃ caityamupaniśritya viharanti tān sarvānupasthānaśālāyāṃ saṃnipātaya ||
children.translated_text: Go, <s>Ānanda</s>. Gather in the attendance hall all the monks who are dwelling near the <s>Cāpāla</s> caitya.'

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta ||
children.translated_text: 'Yes, venerable sir.'

children.text: āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yāvanto bhikṣavaścāpālaṃ caityamupaniśritya viharanti tān sarvānupasthānaśālāyāṃ saṃnipātya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, gathered in the attendance hall all the monks who were dwelling near the <s>Cāpāla</s> caitya, and then approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet and stood to one side.

children.text: ekāntasthita āyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat yāvanto bhadanta bhikṣavaścāpālaṃ caityamupaniśritya viharanti sarve te upasthānaśālāyāṃ niṣaṇṇāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, all the monks who are dwelling near the <s>Cāpāla</s> caitya have assembled and are seated in the attendance hall. Now let the Blessed One consider the time for whatever he thinks fit.'

children.text: atha bhagavān yenopasthānaśālā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One approached the attendance hall.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down before the community of monks on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma anityā bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārā adhruvā anāśvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇo yāvadalameva bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārān saṃskaritumalam ||
children.translated_text: After sitting down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, all conditioned formations are impermanent, unstable, unreliable, subject to alteration; monks, it is enough to construct all conditioned formations, enough indeed.

children.text: viramantu tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, desist from them now.

children.text: etarhi vā me 'tyayādye te dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya saṃparāyahitāya saṃparāyasukhāya te bhikṣubhirudgṛhya paryavāpya tathā tathā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā grāhayitavyā yathaiva tatra brahmacaryaṃ cirasthitikaṃ syādbahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃprakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: Now, after my passing, those teachings that conduce to welfare in this present life, to happiness in this present life, to welfare in the next world, and to happiness in the next world must be learned, mastered, held in such and such a way, recited, and taught by the monks, so that the holy life may last long, become beneficial to many people and widespread, and be rightly proclaimed to gods and humans.'

children.text: etarhi bhikṣavo dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya saṃparāyahitāya saṃparāyasukhāya ye bhikṣubhirudgṛhya paryavāpya tathā tathā dhārayitavyā grāhayitavyā vācayitavyā yathaitadbrahmacaryaṃ cirasthitikaṃ syādbahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃprakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: Now, monks, there are dharmas (teachings) that lead to welfare in the present life, to happiness in the present life, to welfare in the next life, and to happiness in the next life. Having learned and mastered them, monks should preserve them, teach them, and recite them in such a way that this holy life may long endure, become widespread and extensive, and be rightly proclaimed among gods and humans.

children.text: yaduta catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ pañcendriyāṇi pañca balāni sapta bodhyaṅgāni āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is, the four establishments of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path.

children.text: ime te bhikṣavo dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya saṃparāyahitāya saṃparāyasukhāya bhikṣubhirudgṛhya paryavāpya tathā tathā dhārayitavyā grāhayitavyā vācayitavyā yathaitadbrahmacaryaṃ cirasthitikaṃ syādbahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃprakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: These, monks, are the dharmas (teachings) that lead to welfare in the present life, to happiness in the present life, to welfare in the next life, and to happiness in the next life. Having learned and mastered them, monks should preserve them, teach them, and recite them in such a way that this holy life may long endure, become widespread and extensive, and be rightly proclaimed among gods and humans.

children.text: āgamaya ānanda yena kuśigrāmakam ||
children.translated_text: Come, <s>Ānanda</s>; let us go to <s>Kuśigrāmaka</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavān vaiśālīvanamabhisaran dakṣiṇena sarvakāyena nāgāvalokitena vyavalokayati ||
children.translated_text: As the Blessed One was going from the grove of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, he looked back with a nāga-like glance, turning the whole right side of his body.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat nāhetvapratyayaṃ bhadanta tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhā dakṣiṇena nāgāvalokitamavalokayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not look back with a nāga-like glance without a cause and condition.

children.text: ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo nāgāvalokitasya evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, for this nāga-like glance?" "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhā dakṣiṇena sarvakāyena nāgāvalokitena vyavalokayanti ||
children.translated_text: Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not look back with a nāga-like glance, turning the whole right side of the body, without a cause and condition.

children.text: idamānanda tathāgatasyāpaścimaṃ vaiśālīdarśanam ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s final sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

children.text: na bhūya ānanda tathāgato vaiśālīmāgamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: No more, <s>Ānanda</s>, will the <s>Tathāgata</s> come to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

children.text: parinirvāṇāya gamiṣyati mallānāmupavartanam yamakaśālavanam ||
children.translated_text: He will go to the <s>Mallas</s>' <s>Upavartana</s>, to the twin sāla grove, for parinirvāṇa.

children.text: athānyataro bhikṣustasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain monk at that time spoke a verse:

children.text: idamapaścimakaṃ nātha vaiśālyāstava darśanam
children.translated_text: "Lord, this is your final sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>;

children.text: na bhūyaḥ sugato buddho vaiśālīmāgamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Sugata</s>, the Buddha, will not come again to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

children.text: nirvāṇāya gamiṣyati mallānāmupavartanam yamakaśālavanam ||
children.translated_text: He will go to the <s>Mallas</s>' <s>Upavartana</s>, to the twin sāla grove, for nirvāṇa."

children.text: yadā ha bhagavatā vāg bhāṣitā idamapaścimakaṃ vaiśālyā darśanam tadā anekābhirvaiśālīvananivāsinībhir devatairaśrupātaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had spoken the words, "This is the final sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>," many deities dwelling in the grove of <s>Vaiśālī</s> shed tears.

children.text: sthavirānandaḥ kathayati na bhagavannameghenaiva varṣāsu pravṛṣṭo bhagavānāha vaiśālīvananivāsinībhirdaivatairmama viyogādaśrupātaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The elder <s>Ānanda</s> said, "Venerable sir, surely rain has begun from a cloud in the rainy season." The Blessed One said, "The deities dwelling in the grove of <s>Vaiśālī</s> have shed tears because of separation from me."

children.text: tā api devatā vaiśālyāṃ śabdo niścārito bhagavān parinirvāṇāya gacchati na bhūyo bhagavān vaiśālīmāgamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Those deities too raised a cry in <s>Vaiśālī</s>: "The Blessed One is going to parinirvāṇa; the Blessed One will not come again to <s>Vaiśālī</s>."

children.text: devatānāṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā anekāni vaiśālikāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi bhagavatsakāśamupasaṃkrāntāni ||
children.translated_text: Hearing the deities' cry, many hundreds of thousands of living beings of <s>Vaiśālī</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavatā teṣāmāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā evaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā yathā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, knowing their dispositions, latent tendencies, elements, and natures, gave such a Dharma teaching that many hundreds of thousands of living beings undertook the going for refuge and the training precepts.

children.text: kaiścicchrotāpattiphalaṃ kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ kaiścidanāgāmiphalaṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: Some attained the fruit of stream-entry, some the fruit of once-returning, and some the fruit of non-returning.

children.text: kaiścit pravrajitvārhattvaṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: Some went forth and attained arhatship.

children.text: kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: Some generated the mind directed toward śrāvakabodhi (disciple awakening).

children.text: kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: Some generated the mind directed toward pratyekabodhi (solitary awakening).

children.text: kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: Some generated the mind directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni ||
children.translated_text: Some undertook the going for refuge and the training precepts.

children.text: yadbhūyasā sā parṣadbuddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: For the most part that assembly became inclined toward the Buddha, devoted to the Dharma, and turned toward the Saṅgha.

children.text: sthavirānandaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhagavantamidamavocat paśya bhadanta yāvat tvam ||
children.translated_text: The elder <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, said this to the Blessed One: "See, venerable sir, to what an extent you have acted.

children.text: bhagavatā parinirvāṇāya prasthitenānekāni devatāśatasahasrāṇi satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni ||
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had set out for parinirvāṇa, many hundreds of thousands of deities were established in the truths.

children.text: anekābhyaḥ parvatakandaragiriguhābhyo 'nekāni ṛṣiśatasahasrāṇyāgatāni ||
children.translated_text: From many mountain clefts, mountain hollows, and mountain caves, many hundreds of thousands of seers came.

children.text: bhagavatā ete bhikṣavaḥ pravrajitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These monks were ordained by the Blessed One.

children.text: tairyujyadbhirghaṭadbhirvyāyacchamānaiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: As they applied themselves, strove, and exerted themselves, they realized arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements.

children.text: anekairdevanāgayakṣagandharvakinnaramahoragaiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni ||
children.translated_text: Many gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and mahoragas undertook the going for refuge and the training precepts.

children.text: anekāni vaiśālakāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpitāni ||
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of living beings of <s>Vaiśālī</s> were established in the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: kecit sakṛdāgāmiphale kecidanāgāmiphale kecit pravrājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some were established in the fruit of once-returning, some in the fruit of non-returning, and some were ordained.

children.text: pravrajitvārhattvaṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: Having gone forth, they attained arhatship.

children.text: keciccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some were established in the going for refuge and the training precepts."

children.text: atrānanda kimāścaryaṃ mayā etarhi sarvajñena sarvākārajñenānuttarajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena astatṛṣṇena nirupādānena sarvāhaṃkāramamakārāsmimānābhiniveśānuśayaprahīṇena evaṃvidhaṃ vaineyakāryaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: "What is surprising here, <s>Ānanda</s>? Now that such a task of training those to be disciplined has been performed by me, who am omniscient, knowing all aspects, possessed of mastery over unsurpassed knowledge and what is to be known, free from craving, without grasping, and with all latent clinging to I-making, mine-making, and the conceit 'I am' abandoned?"

children.text: yanmayā atīte 'pyadhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsadharmeṇa yanmayā maraṇāntikayā vedanayā spṛṣṭena evaṃvidhā parikarmakathā kṛtā yadanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi gṛhāśramamapahāya ṛṣayaḥ pravrajitvā catvāro brahmavihārān bhāvayitvā kalpavṛndaṃ prahāya tadbahulavihāriṇo brahmalokasabhāgatāyām upapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Listen to how, in a past age too, when I was still with passion, with hatred, and with delusion, not yet freed, subject to birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress, and touched by pain at the point of death, I gave such a preparatory discourse that many hundreds of thousands of living beings, leaving the household life, went forth as seers, cultivated the four brahmavihāras, abandoned hosts of kalpas, and, dwelling much in those states, were reborn among those who share in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tacchṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Listen to that.

children.text: bhūtapūrvamānandopoṣadho nāma rājā babhūva ||
children.translated_text: In the past, <s>Ānanda</s>, there was a king named <s>Upoṣadha</s>.

children.text: upoṣadhasya rājño mūrdhni piṭṭako jāto mṛduḥ sumṛduḥ tadyathā tūlapicurvā karpāsapicurvā ||
children.translated_text: On the head of King <s>Upoṣadha</s> a swelling arose, soft, very soft, like a tuft of cotton or a tuft of kapok.

children.text: na kaṃcidābādhaṃ janayati ||
children.translated_text: It caused no affliction at all.

children.text: pakvaḥ sphuṭitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It ripened and burst open.

children.text: kumāro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: A prince was born, handsome, beautiful, pleasing, and endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man.

children.text: upoṣadhasya rājñaḥ ṣaṣṭistrīsahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Upoṣadha</s> had sixty thousand women.

children.text: sarvāsāṃ stanāḥ prasṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The breasts of all of them flowed with milk.

children.text: ekaikā kathayati māṃ dhaya māṃ dhaya ||
children.translated_text: Each one said, 'Suckle from me, suckle from me.'

children.text: mūrdhato jāto mūrdhāta iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Because he was born from the head, the name <s>Mūrdhāta</s> came about.

children.text: māṃ dhaya māṃ dhaya māndhāta iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Because they said, 'Suckle from me, suckle from me,' the name <s>Māndhātā</s> came about.

children.text: anye kathayanti kecinmādhāta iti saṃjānīte ||
children.translated_text: Others say that some know him as <s>Mādhāta</s>.

children.text: māndhātasya kumārasya kumārakrīḍāyāṃ krīḍataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: While the prince <s>Māndhātā</s> was playing at the games of boyhood, six wheels fell down.

children.text: yauvarājye pratiṣṭhitasya ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he was installed as heir apparent, six wheels fell down.

children.text: māndhātā janapadān gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māndhātā</s> went to the provinces.

children.text: janapadān gatasya pitā glānībhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While he was in the provinces, his father became ill.

children.text: sa mūlapatragaṇḍapuṣpabhaiṣajyairupasthīyamāno hīyata eva ||
children.translated_text: Though he was attended with medicines made from roots, leaves, knots, and flowers, he only declined.

children.text: tatastairamātyaiḥ saṃdeśo visarjitaḥ pitā te glānībhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those ministers sent a message: 'Your father has become ill.

children.text: āgacchatu ||
children.translated_text: Come.

children.text: devarājyaṃ pratīccha ||
children.translated_text: Receive the divine kingdom.'

children.text: tasyānāgacchataḥ pitā kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he did not come, his father passed away.

children.text: tairamātyaiḥ punaḥ saṃdeśo visarjitaḥ pitā te kāladharmaṇā saṃyuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those ministers again sent a message: 'Your father has met the law of time.

children.text: āgaccha devarājyaṃ pratīcchasva ||
children.translated_text: Come and receive the divine kingdom.'

children.text: tato 'sau saṃlakṣayati yadi mama pitā kālagataḥ kiṃ bhūyo 'haṃ gacchāmīti tato bhūyaḥ saṃdeśo 'bhyāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he reflected, 'If my father has passed away, why should I go back?' Then another message arrived.

children.text: āgaccha devarājyaṃ pratīccha ||
children.translated_text: 'Come and receive the divine kingdom.'

children.text: sa kathayati yadi mama dharmeṇa rājyaṃ prāpsyate ihaiva rājyābhiṣeka āgacchatu ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'If I am to obtain the kingdom by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), let the royal consecration come here itself.'

children.text: tataste amātyāḥ kathayanti ratnaśilayā deva prayojanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then those ministers said, 'Your Majesty, there is need of a jeweled slab.'

children.text: tasya ca divaukaso nāma yakṣaḥ purojavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had a yakṣa named <s>Divaukasa</s>, swift in advance.

children.text: tena ratnaśilā ānītā ||
children.translated_text: The jeweled slab was brought by him.

children.text: yadā ratnaśilā ānītā tataste amātyā bhūyaḥ kathayanti deva śrīparyaṅkenātra prayojanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When the jeweled slab had been brought, the ministers again said, 'Your Majesty, there is need here of a throne of splendor.'

children.text: tatastenaiva divaukasena śrīparyaṅka ānītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that same <s>Divaukasa</s> brought the throne of splendor.

children.text: tataste amātyā bhūyaḥ kathayanti devādhiṣṭhānamadhye 'bhiṣekaḥ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Then those ministers again said, 'The consecration is performed in the middle of the royal seat.'

children.text: sa kathayati yadi mama dharmeṇa rājyaṃ prāpsyate ihaivādhiṣṭhānamāgacchatu ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'If I am to obtain the kingdom by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), let the royal seat come here itself.'

children.text: tato 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ svayameva tatpradeśaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: Then the royal seat went of its own accord to that place.

children.text: svayamāgataṃ svayamāgataṃ sāketasāketamiti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Because it had come by itself, by itself, the name <s>Sāketa</s>, <s>Sāketa</s>, came about.

children.text: paścāt te 'mātyā bhaṭabalāgranaigamajanapadāścābhiṣekaṃ gṛhītvā āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards those ministers, soldiers, leading townsmen, and people of the provinces came, bringing the consecration.

children.text: te kathayanti abhiṣekaṃ deva pratīcchasva ||
children.translated_text: They said, 'Your Majesty, receive the consecration.'

children.text: sa kathayati mama manuṣyāḥ paṭṭaṃ bandhiṣyanti yadi dharmeṇa rājyaṃ prāpsyate amanuṣyāḥ paṭṭaṃ bandhantu ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'My human beings will bind on the diadem. If I am to obtain the kingdom by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), let nonhuman beings bind on the diadem.'

children.text: tato 'manuṣyaiḥ paṭṭo baddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the diadem was bound on by nonhuman beings.

children.text: tasya sapta ratnāni prādurbhūtāni tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnameva saptamam ||
children.translated_text: Seven jewels appeared for him: namely, the jewel of the wheel, the jewel of the elephant, the jewel of the horse, the jewel of the gem, the jewel of the steward, the jewel of the woman, and the jewel of the householder as the seventh.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ cāsya sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And he had a full thousand sons, brave, heroic, beautifully formed in their limbs, and crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: vaiśālīsāmantakena ramaṇīyaṃ vanakhaṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: Near <s>Vaiśālī</s> there was a delightful grove.

children.text: tatra pañca ṛṣiśatāni pañcābhijñāni dhyāyanti ||
children.translated_text: There five hundred seers possessing the five higher knowledges meditated.

children.text: tatra vanakhaṇḍe prabhūtāḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāśca prativasanti ||
children.translated_text: In that grove many birds and deer lived.

children.text: śabdakaṇṭakāni ca dhyānāni ||
children.translated_text: And sounds are thorns to meditations.

children.text: te ca pakṣiṇo 'vatīryamāṇā avatīryamāṇāḥ śabdaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Those birds, as they were alighting again and again, made noise.

children.text: durmukho nāma ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There was a seer named <s>Durmukha</s>.

children.text: sa kupitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became angry.

children.text: tenoktam bakānāṃ pakṣāṇi śīryantām ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'Let the wings of the cranes fall apart.'

children.text: yadā teṣām ṛṣikopena pakṣāṇi śīrṇāni tataste pādoddhārakeṇa prasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When their wings had fallen apart because of the seer's anger, they set out by lifting their feet.

children.text: sa ca rājā janapadānanusaṃsārya paśyati pādoddhārakeṇa gacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king, touring the provinces, saw them going by lifting their feet.

children.text: yataste 'mātyāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ kasmāt pādoddhārakeṇa gacchanti paścāt te 'mātyāḥ kathayanti deva śabdakaṇṭakāni dhyānānīti eteṣām ṛṣikopena pakṣāṇi śīrṇāni ||
children.translated_text: When those ministers were asked, 'Why are they going by lifting their feet?' the ministers then said, 'Your Majesty, sounds are thorns to meditations; their wings have fallen apart because of the anger of these seers.'

children.text: tato rājñā abhihitam evaṃvidhā api ṛṣayo bhavanti yeṣāṃ sattvānāmantike nāstyanukampā tato rājñā amātyāḥ saṃdiṣṭā gacchantu bhavantaḥ ṛṣīṇāmevaṃ vadantu tatra gacchata yatrāhaṃ na vasayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then the king said, 'Are there even such seers as these, in whose presence there is no compassion for living beings?' Then the king instructed the ministers, 'Go, gentlemen, and tell the seers this: Go where I shall not make you live.'

children.text: tatastairamātyair ṛṣayo 'bhihitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those ministers addressed the seers.

children.text: rājā samādiśati na mama rājye vastavyam ||
children.translated_text: 'The king commands: You must not dwell in my kingdom.'

children.text: gacchantu bhavanto yatrāhaṃ na vasayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: "Let the venerable sirs go where I do not make them dwell," he said.

children.text: tataste saṃlakṣayanti eṣo 'yaṃ caturdvīpeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they reflected, "This man is lord of the four continents.

children.text: gacchāmo vayaṃ sumeruparikhaṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: Let us go to the region around <s>Sumeru</s>."

children.text: te tatra gatvā avasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They went there and remained.

children.text: rājño mūrdhātasyāmātyāś cintakāstulakā upaparīkṣakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>'s ministers were planners, measurers, and inspectors.

children.text: cintayitvā tulayitvopaparīkṣya pṛthak pṛthaguktāḥ śilpasthānakarmasthānāni māpayitum ||
children.translated_text: After planning, measuring, and inspecting, they were individually instructed to lay out places for crafts and places for work.

children.text: cintakā ime tulakā upaparīkṣakā iti mantrajā mantrajā iti saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: These planners, measurers, and inspectors had the designation "council-born, council-born."

children.text: tairārabdhāni karṣaṇakarmāṇi kartum ||
children.translated_text: They began to carry out agricultural work.

children.text: yataḥ sa rājā paśyati janapadānanusaṃsāryākṛṣyān karmāntān kurvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, as he toured the provinces, saw them carrying out the work of cultivation.

children.text: yato rājñā abhihitaṃ kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti tatastairamātyai rājā abhihita ete deva manuṣyāḥ sasyādīni kṛṣanti tata oṣadhayo bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: When the king said, "What are these people doing?" those ministers said to the king, "Your Majesty, these people are cultivating grain and the like; from that, crops will come into being."

children.text: yataśca sa rājā kathayati mama rājye manuṣyāḥ kṛṣiṣyanti tatastenoktam saptāviṃśatibījajātīnāṃ devo varṣatu ||
children.translated_text: When the king said, "Will people farm in my kingdom?" he said, "Let rain fall as the twenty-seven kinds of seed."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājño mūrdhātasya saptāviṃśatibījajātirdevo vṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the mere arising of King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>'s thought, rain fell as the twenty-seven kinds of seed.

children.text: rājñā mūrdhātena janapadāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ kasyaitāni puṇyāni tairabhihitam devasya cāsmākaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> asked the people of the provinces, "Whose merits are these?" They said, "They are Your Majesty's and ours."

children.text: yataste manuṣyāḥ karpāsavāṭānārabdhā māpayitum bhūyo 'pi ca rājñā mūrdhātena janapadānanusaṃsārya tena pṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those people began to lay out cotton fields; and again King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>, after touring the provinces, asked them.

children.text: tato rājñā abhihitam kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti tairamātyairabhihitam deva manuṣyāḥ karpāsavāṭān māpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then the king said, "What are these people doing?" The ministers said, "Your Majesty, the people are laying out cotton fields."

children.text: paścāt rājñā abhihitam kasyārthe tairamātyairabhihitam deva vastrāṇāmarthe ||
children.translated_text: Afterward the king said, "For what purpose?" The ministers said, "Your Majesty, for the sake of garments."

children.text: tato rājñā tenoktam mama rājye manuṣyāḥ karpāsavāṭān māpayiṣyantīti karpāsameva devo varṣatu ||
children.translated_text: Then the king said, "Will people lay out cotton fields in my kingdom? Let rain fall as cotton itself."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājño mūrdhātasya karpāsāneva devo vṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the mere arising of King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>'s thought, rain fell as cotton itself.

children.text: sa ca rājā janapadān pṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: And that king asked the people of the provinces,

children.text: kasyaitāni puṇyāni te kathayanti devasya cāsmākaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "Whose merits are these?" They said, "They are Your Majesty's and ours."

children.text: paścāt tena janena tatkarpāsaṃ kartitumārabdham ||
children.translated_text: Afterward those people began to spin that cotton.

children.text: sa rājā kathayati kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti tairamātyairabhihitaṃ deva sūtreṇa prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "What are these people doing?" The ministers said, "Your Majesty, there is need of thread."

children.text: tato rājñā abhihitam mama rājye manuṣyāḥ kartiṣyanti sūtrameva devo varṣatu ||
children.translated_text: Then the king said, "Will people spin in my kingdom? Let rain fall as thread itself."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājño māndhātasya sūtrameva devo vṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the mere arising of King <s>Māndhāta</s>'s thought, rain fell as thread itself.

children.text: sa ca rājā kathayati kasyaitāni puṇyāni yataste kathayanti devasya cāsmākaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And that king said, "Whose merits are these?" Then they said, "They are Your Majesty's and ours."

children.text: yatastairanupūrveṇa vastrāṇyārabdhāni vāpayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then, in due order, they began to weave garments.

children.text: sa rājā kathayati kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti tairamātyairabhihitam deva vastrāṇi vāpayanti vastraiḥ prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "What are these people doing?" The ministers said, "Your Majesty, they are weaving garments; there is need of garments."

children.text: yato rājā saṃlakṣayati mama rājye manuṣyā vastrāṇi vāpayiṣyante vastrāṇyeva devo varṣatu ||
children.translated_text: Then the king reflected, "Will people weave garments in my kingdom? Let rain fall as garments themselves."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājño māndhātasya vastrāṇyeva devo vṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the mere arising of King <s>Māndhāta</s>'s thought, rain fell as garments themselves.

children.text: sa rājā kathayati kasyaitāni puṇyāni te kathayanti devasya cāsmākaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "Whose merits are these?" They said, "They are Your Majesty's and ours."

children.text: yataḥ sa rājā saṃlakṣayati manuṣyā mama puṇyānāṃ prabhāvaṃ na jānanti ||
children.translated_text: Then that king reflected, "People do not know the power of my merits."

children.text: atha rājño māndhātasyaitadabhavat ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Māndhāta</s>:

children.text: asti me jambudvīpa ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaśca ||
children.translated_text: "I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, prosperous, flourishing, secure, rich in food, and crowded with many people and human beings.

children.text: santi me sapta ratnāni tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam ||
children.translated_text: I have the seven jewels, namely: the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the gem-jewel, the householder-jewel, the woman-jewel, and, as the seventh, the counselor-jewel.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And I have a full thousand sons, valiant, heroic, beautiful in their noble limbs, and crushers of hostile armies.

children.text: aho bata me 'ntaḥpure saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ patet ekakārṣāpaṇo 'pi bahir na nipatet ||
children.translated_text: Ah, if only a rain of gold would fall in my inner palace for seven days, and not even a single <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> would fall outside."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājño māndhātasyāntaḥpure saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ vṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: At the mere arising of King <s>Māndhāta</s>'s thought, a rain of gold fell in his inner palace for seven days.

children.text: ekakārṣāpaṇo 'pi bahir na nipatito yathāpi tanmaharddhikasya sattvasya mahānubhāvasya kṛtapuṇyasya kṛtakuśalasya svakaṃ puṇyaphalaṃ pratyanubhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not even a single <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> fell outside, just as is the proper fruit of merit for such a being of great supernormal power, of great majesty, who had performed meritorious and wholesome acts and was experiencing the result of his own merit.

children.text: yataḥ sa rājā kathayati kasyaitāni puṇyāni te kathayanti devasya cāsmākaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Then that king said, "Whose merits are these?" They said, "They are Your Majesty's and ours."

children.text: yato sa rājā kathayati kṣuṇṇā bhavanto yadi yuṣmābhiḥ pūrvamevābhihitamabhaviṣyaddevasya puṇyānīti mayā sakalaṃ jambudvīpaṃ ratnairabhivṛṣṭamabhaviṣyat ||
children.translated_text: Then that king said, "You are at fault, sirs. If you had said earlier, 'They are Your Majesty's merits,' I would have rained jewels over all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: api tu yo yuṣmākaṃ ratnairarthī sa yāvadīpsitāni ratnāni gṛhṇātu ||
children.translated_text: But anyone among you who needs jewels may take as many jewels as he desires."

children.text: tasya tatra mūrdhātasya rājño mahārājyaṃ kārayataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: While that King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was exercising his great kingship there, six wheels disappeared.

children.text: rājño mūrdhātasya divaukaso yakṣaḥ purojavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> had a swift-moving yakṣa named <s>Purojava</s>, a dweller among the gods.

children.text: sa rājñā mūrdhātenokto 'sti kiṃcidanyadvīpe nājñāpitam yadvayamājñāpayema yataḥ paścāddivaukasenābhihito 'sti deva pūrvavideho nāma dvīpaḥ ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was told by King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>, "Is there any other island that has not been commanded, which we might command?" Then afterward he was told by <s>Divaukasa</s>, "Your Majesty, there is an island called <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men."

children.text: svayaṃ nu devo gatvā tamapyājñāpayet ||
children.translated_text: "Let Your Majesty go there himself and command that one too."

children.text: atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat asti me jambudvīpa ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaśca ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>: "I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: asti me sapta ratnāni tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam ||
children.translated_text: I have the seven jewels, namely the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the jewel-gem, the woman-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the adviser-jewel as the seventh.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And I have a full thousand sons, heroic, brave, handsome in their limbs, and crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: vṛṣṭaṃ me saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam ||
children.translated_text: For seven days a rain of gold has rained in my inner palace.

children.text: śrūyate atha khalu pūrvavideho nāma dvīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it is heard that there is an island called <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.

children.text: yannvahaṃ tamapi gatvā samanuśāseyam ||
children.translated_text: Suppose I were to go there too and govern it."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhāta uparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ saptaratnapurojavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhāta</s> rose up into the sky, together with eighteen crores at the head of his army, surrounded by his thousand sons, with the seven jewels going before him.

children.text: agamadrājā māndhātaḥ pūrvavidehadvīpam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhāta</s> went to the island of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.

children.text: pratyaṣṭhādrājā māndhātā pūrvavidehadvīpe ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhāta</s> took his stand on the island of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.

children.text: samanuviṣṭavān rājā mūrdhātaḥ pūrvavidehaṃ dvīpam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> brought the island of <s>Pūrvavideha</s> under his rule.

children.text: tasya tatra samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: While he was governing there, six wheels slipped away.

children.text: bhūyaḥ sa rājā divaukasam yakṣamāmantrayati asti divaukasa kiṃcidanyadvīpo nājñāpitam divaukasa āha asti deva aparagodānīyaṃ nāma dvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Again that king addressed the yakṣa <s>Divaukasa</s>: "<s>Divaukasa</s>, is there any other island that has not been commanded?" <s>Divaukasa</s> said, "Your Majesty, there is an island called <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men."

children.text: yannu devastamapi gatvā samanuśāset ||
children.translated_text: "Let Your Majesty go there too and govern it."

children.text: atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat asti me jambudvīpa ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaśca ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>: "I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: santi ca me sapta ratnāni ||
children.translated_text: And I have the seven jewels.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And I have a full thousand sons, heroic, brave, handsome in their limbs, and crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: vṛṣṭaṃ me saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam yathāpi tanmaharddhikasya sattvasya mahānubhāvasya kṛtakuśalasya svapuṇyaphalaṃ pratyanubhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For seven days a rain of gold has rained in my inner palace, just as is the fruit of his own merit being experienced by a being of great supernormal power, of great might, and of accumulated wholesome deeds.

children.text: śrūyate aparagodānīyaṃ nāma dvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It is heard that there is an island called <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: yannvahaṃ tamapi gatvā samanuśāseyam ||
children.translated_text: Suppose I were to go there too and govern it."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhātā uparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ saptaratnapurojavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhātā</s> rose up into the sky, together with eighteen crores at the head of his army, surrounded by his thousand sons, with the seven jewels going before him.

children.text: agamadrājā māndhātā aparagodānīyaṃ dvīpam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhātā</s> went to the island of <s>Aparagodānīya</s>.

children.text: anuśāsti rājā māndhātā aparagodānīyam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhātā</s> ruled <s>Aparagodānīya</s>.

children.text: tasya samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: While he was governing it, six wheels slipped away.

children.text: yataḥ sa rājā māndhātā divaukasam yakṣaṃ pṛcchati asti kaścidanyadvīpo nājñāpita āgato 'smi pūrvān ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Māndhātā</s> asked the yakṣa <s>Divaukasa</s>, "Is there any other island that has not been commanded? I have come from the eastern ones."

children.text: asti deva uttarakurur nāma dvīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Your Majesty, there is an island called <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: kiṃcāpi te manuṣyā amamā aparigrahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, those people are without possessiveness and without property.

children.text: yannu devo gatvā svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāset ||
children.translated_text: Let Your Majesty go there and govern your own leading force of soldiers."

children.text: atha rājño māndhātasyaitadabhavat asti me jambudvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Māndhāta</s>: "I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: santi me sapta ratnāni ||
children.translated_text: I have the seven jewels.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And I have a full thousand sons, heroic, brave, handsome in their limbs, and crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: vṛṣṭameva saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam ||
children.translated_text: For seven days indeed a rain of gold has rained in my inner palace.

children.text: śrūyate uttarakurur nāma dvīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is heard that there is an island called <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: kiṃcāpi te manuṣyā amamā aparigrahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, those people are without possessiveness and without property.

children.text: yannvahaṃ tatrāpi gatvā svaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāseyam ||
children.translated_text: Suppose I were to go there too and govern my own leading force of soldiers."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhātā sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ saptaratnapurojava uparivihāyasenābhyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhātā</s>, together with eighteen crores at the head of his army, surrounded by his thousand sons, with the seven jewels going before him, rose up into the sky.

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā māndhātaḥ sumerupārśvenānuyāyaṃś citropacitrān vṛkṣānāpīḍakajātān ||
children.translated_text: As King <s>Māndhāta</s> proceeded along the side of <s>Sumeru</s>, he saw trees of many different colors, grown as crests or garlands.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punardivaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate sma kimetaddivaukasa citropacitrān vṛkṣānāpīḍakajātān ||
children.translated_text: Having seen them, he addressed the yakṣa <s>Divaukasa</s> again: "<s>Divaukasa</s>, what are these trees of many different colors, grown as crests or garlands?"

children.text: ete devottarakauravāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ kalpadūṣyavṛkṣāḥ yata uttarakauravā manuṣyāḥ kalpadūṣyāṇi prāvṛṇvanti ||
children.translated_text: "Your Majesty, these are the wish-fulfilling garment trees of the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s>; from them the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s> clothe themselves in wish-fulfilling garments.

children.text: devo 'pyatraiva gatvā kalpadūṣyāni prāvarītu ||
children.translated_text: Let Your Majesty also go right there and put on wish-fulfilling garments."

children.text: śrutvā ca punā rājā māndhātā amātyānāmantrayate paśyatha yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaścitropacitrān vṛkṣānāpīḍakajātān evaṃ deva ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, King <s>Māndhātā</s> again addressed the ministers: "Headmen, do you see the trees of many different colors, grown as crests or garlands?" "Yes, Your Majesty."

children.text: ete grāmaṇya uttarakauravāṇāṃ mānuṣyāṇāṃ kalpadūṣyavṛkṣā yata uttarakauravā manuṣyāḥ kalpadūṣyāṇi prāvaranti ||
children.translated_text: "Headmen, these are the wish-fulfilling garment trees of the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s>; from them the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s> put on wish-fulfilling garments.

children.text: yūyamapyatra gatvā kalpadūṣyayugāni prāvaradhvam ||
children.translated_text: You too should go there and put on pairs of wish-fulfilling garments."

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā māndhātā sumerupārśvenānuyāyañ śvetaśvetaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar divaukasaṃ yakṣaṃ āmantrayate kimetaddivaukasa śvetaśvetaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam etaddeva uttarakauravakāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāmakṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśālim yata uttarakauravakā manuṣyā akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliṃ paribhuñjanti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhātā</s>, while proceeding along the side of <s>Sumeru</s>, saw a very white stretch of earth. Seeing it, he again addressed the divine <s>yakṣa</s>: "Divine one, what is this very white stretch of earth?" "Your Majesty, this is the rice with grains as its fruit, not ploughed or sown, of the people of the <s>Uttarakauravas</s>. From this the people of the <s>Uttarakauravas</s> eat rice with grains as its fruit, not ploughed or sown."

children.text: devo 'pyatra gatvā akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliṃ paribhuñjatu ||
children.translated_text: "Let Your Majesty also go there and eat the rice with grains as its fruit, not ploughed or sown."

children.text: agamadrājā māndhātā uttarakurudvīpam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhātā</s> went to the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: pratyaṣṭhādrājā māndhātā uttarakurau dvīpe ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhātā</s> established himself on the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: samanuśāsti rājā māndhātā uttarakurau dvīpe svakam bhaṭabalāgram ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Māndhātā</s> ruled his own foremost army on the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: atha rājā māndhātā divaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate asti kiṃcidanyadvīpam anājñāpitam iti nāsti deva ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Māndhātā</s> addressed the divine <s>yakṣa</s>: "Is there any other island that has not been brought under command?" "There is none, Your Majesty."

children.text: śrūyante devāstrāyastriṃśā dīrghāyuṣo varṇavantaḥ sukhabahulā ucceṣu vimāneṣu cirasthitikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods are heard to be long-lived, beautiful, full of happiness, and long abiding in lofty palaces.

children.text: yannu devo devāṃstrāyastriṃśān darśanāyopasaṃkramet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore Your Majesty should approach the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods in order to see them."

children.text: atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat asti me jambudvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>: "I possess <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, prosperous, flourishing, secure, well provisioned, and filled with many people and men.

children.text: asti me sapta ratnāni ||
children.translated_text: I possess the seven jewels.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām ||
children.translated_text: And I have a full thousand sons, brave, heroic, handsome in their fine limbs, and crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: vṛṣṭaṃ me saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam ||
children.translated_text: For seven days a rain of gold has rained in my inner palace.

children.text: samanuśiṣṭo me aparagodānīyo dvīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The island of <s>Aparagodānīya</s> has been brought under my rule.

children.text: samanuśiṣṭaṃ me uttarakurudvīpe svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgram ||
children.translated_text: My own foremost army has been brought under my rule on the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: śrūyante devāstrayastriṃśā dīrghāyuṣo varṇavantaḥ sukhabahulā ucceṣu vimāneṣu cirasthitikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods are heard to be long-lived, beautiful, full of happiness, and long abiding in lofty palaces.

children.text: yannvahaṃ devāṃstrayastriṃśān darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to approach the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods in order to see them?"

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhātā uparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ saptaratnapurojavaḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhātā</s> rose upward into the sky, together with eighteen koṭis of foremost troops, preceded by the seven jewels and surrounded by his thousand sons.

children.text: sumeruḥ parvatarājā saptakāñcanaparvataparivṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, is encircled by seven golden mountains.

children.text: atha rājā nimiṃdhare parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: Then the king established himself on the golden mountain <s>Nimiṃdhara</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: nimiṃdharāt parvatāt vinatake parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Nimiṃdhara</s> he established himself on the golden mountain <s>Vinataka</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: vinatakāt parvatādaśvakarṇagirau parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Vinataka</s> he established himself on the golden mountain <s>Aśvakarṇagiri</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: aśvakarṇagirerapi parvatāt sudarśane parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Aśvakarṇagiri</s> too he established himself on the mountain <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: sudarśanāt parvatāt khadirake parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Sudarśana</s> he established himself on the golden mountain <s>Khadiraka</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: khadirakāt parvatādīṣādhāre parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Khadiraka</s> he established himself on the golden mountain <s>Īṣādhāra</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: īṣādhārāt parvatādyugaṃdhare parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Īṣādhāra</s> he established himself on the golden mountain <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>.

children.text: tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was ruling his own foremost army there, six wheels fell away.

children.text: yugaṃdharāt parvatāduparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: From Mount <s>Yugaṃdhara</s> he rose upward into the sky.

children.text: tatra sumerupariṣaṇḍāyāṃ pañca ṛṣiśatāni dhyāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: There, on the slope of <s>Sumeru</s>, five hundred seers were meditating.

children.text: taiḥ sa rājā dṛṣṭa āgacchan ||
children.translated_text: They saw that king coming.

children.text: te kathayanti ayamasau bhavantaḥ kalirājā āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Sirs, this is that king of strife who is coming."

children.text: tatra durmukho nāma ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There was a seer named <s>Durmukha</s>.

children.text: tena gṛhyodakasyāñjaliḥ kṣiptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By him a handful of water, taken in his hands, was thrown.

children.text: viṣkambhitaṃ bhaṭabalāgram ||
children.translated_text: The foremost army was obstructed.

children.text: tasya cāgrataḥ pariṇāyakaratnamanuyāti ||
children.translated_text: And in front of it the jewel of the counselor proceeded along.

children.text: tena ṛṣayo 'bhihitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The seers were addressed by him:

children.text: gacchatha brāhmaṇyako 'yaṃ naitat sarvatra sidhyati
children.translated_text: "Go away; this man is favorable to Brahmins. This does not succeed everywhere.

children.text: mūrdhātā nṛpatirhyeṣo naite vaiśālikā bakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this is King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>; these are not the cranes of <s>Vaiśālī</s>."

children.text: atha rājā tasmiñ śāsane 'bhyāgataḥ kathayati kenaitadviṣkambhitaṃ bhaṭabalāgram tenoktam ṛṣibhirdeva taṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitam ||
children.translated_text: Then the king arrived at that command and said, "By whom has this foremost army been obstructed?" He replied, "Your Majesty, the foremost army has been obstructed by the seers."

children.text: paścād rājñā abhihitaṃ kimeṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ sarvaṃ priyamiti pariṇāyakaratnenoktaṃ jaṭā ṛṣīṇāṃ sarveṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward the king said, "What is most dear to all these seers?" The jewel of the counselor replied, "The matted locks of the seers are most dear to them all."

children.text: tato rājñā abhihitam ṛṣīṇāṃ jaṭāḥ śīryantām mama ca bhaṭabalāgraṃ vihāyasā gacchatu ||
children.translated_text: Then the king said, "Let the matted locks of the seers fall away, and let my foremost army go through the sky."

children.text: teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ jaṭāḥ śīrṇāḥ rājñaśca mūrdhātasya bhaṭabalāgraṃ vihāyasena prasthitam ||
children.translated_text: The matted locks of those seers fell away, and King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>'s foremost army set out through the sky.

children.text: sumeruḥ parvatarājā aśītiyojanasahasrāṇyadhastāt kāñcanamayyāṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhito 'śītiyojanasahasrāṇyudakādabhyudgata ūrdhvamadhaśca ṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasraṃ pārśvaṃ pārśvam aśītiyojanasahasrāṇi tadbhavati samantaparikṣepeṇa viṃśatyadhikāni trīṇi yojanaśatasahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, is established below for eighty thousand yojanas in a golden earth; it rises up from the water for eighty thousand yojanas. Above and below it measures sixty hundred-thousand yojanas, each side is eighty thousand yojanas, and in circumference it is three hundred twenty thousand yojanas.

children.text: abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaścatūratnamayaḥ ||
