children.translated_text: It is beautiful, lovely to behold, pleasing, and made of four kinds of jewels.

children.text: tasya mūrdhni devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma nagaram ||
children.translated_text: On its summit is the city of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, named <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ pañca rakṣāḥ sthāpitā udakaniśritā nāgāḥ karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ mālādhārā devāḥ sadāmattā devāḥ catvāraśca mahārājānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Five guards of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods have been established: the water-supported <s>nāgas</s>, the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> gods, the <s>Mālādhāra</s> gods, the <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods, and the four great kings.

children.text: tasya rājño mūrdhātasyodakaniśritair nāgairbalakāyo viṣkambhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The army of that king <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was checked by the water-supported <s>nāgas</s>.

children.text: rājā ca mūrdhātastatsthānamāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> arrived at that place.

children.text: tenoktaṃ kenaitadbhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitaṃ te kathayanti deva udakaniśritair nāgaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'By whom has this vanguard of troops been checked?' They answered, 'Your Majesty, by the water-supported <s>nāgas</s>.'

children.text: rājā kathayati tiryañco mama yudhyanti tena hyudakaniśritā eva me nāgāḥ purojavā bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: The king said, 'Do animals fight against me? Then let those very water-supported <s>nāgas</s> be my forerunners.'

children.text: tataste nāgā rājño mūrdhātasyāgrato 'nuyāyino jātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>nāgas</s> became followers running before King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ nāgānāmanusaṃyāyatāṃ karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ samprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As those <s>nāgas</s> were proceeding along, they came upon the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> gods.

children.text: yato nāgaistaiḥ karoṭapāṇibhirdevaiḥ sārdhaṃ miśrībhāvaṃ gatvā punastadbalāgraṃ stambhitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, when those <s>nāgas</s> had joined together with the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> gods, that vanguard of troops was again held back.

children.text: rājñā mūrdhātenoktaṃ kenaitadbhaṭabalāgraṃ stambhitaṃ te kathayanti deva ete karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said, 'By whom has this vanguard of troops been held back?' They answered, 'Your Majesty, these are the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> gods.'

children.text: etairbhaṭabalāgraṃ stambhitam ||
children.translated_text: 'The vanguard of troops has been held back by them.'

children.text: rājā mūrdhātaḥ kathayati ete 'pyeva me karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ purojavā bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said, 'Let these <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> gods too be my forerunners.'

children.text: yataste 'grataḥ pradhāvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they ran ahead in front.

children.text: paścāt teṣāṃ nāgaiḥ sārdhaṃ dhāvatāṃ mālādhārā devāḥ samprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, as they were running together with the <s>nāgas</s>, they came upon the <s>Mālādhāra</s> gods.

children.text: mālādhārairdevaiste pṛṣṭāḥ kiṃ bhavanto dhāvatas te kathayanti eṣa manuṣyarājā āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Mālādhāra</s> gods asked them, 'Why are you running, sirs?' They answered, 'This human king is coming.'

children.text: yatastaiḥ sambhūya nāgairdevaiśca punastadbalāgraṃ stambhitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after those gods had joined together with the <s>nāgas</s>, that vanguard of troops was again held back.

children.text: rājā ca māndhātastatsthānamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And King <s>Māndhāta</s> arrived at that place.

children.text: tenoktaṃ kimetadbhavantas te kathayanti deva mālādhārairdevaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'What is this, sirs?' They answered, 'Your Majesty, it is by the <s>Mālādhāra</s> gods.'

children.text: rājā kathayati mālādhārā devāḥ purojavā me bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: The king said, 'Let the <s>Mālādhāra</s> gods be my forerunners.'

children.text: yato mālādhārā devāstair nāgairdevaiśca sārdhaṃ mūrdhātasyāgrataḥ pradhāvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Mālādhāra</s> gods, together with those <s>nāgas</s> and gods, ran ahead in front of <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ dhāvatāṃ sadāmattakā devāḥ samprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they were running, they came upon the <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods.

children.text: sadāmattairdevaiḥ pṛṣṭāḥ kiṃ bhavanto dhāvatas tair nāgaiḥ karoṭapāṇyādibhiśca devairabhihitā eṣa manuṣyarājā āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods asked, 'Why are you running, sirs?' Those <s>nāgas</s> and the gods beginning with the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> replied, 'This human king is coming.'

children.text: yato bhūyaḥ sadāmattairdevaiḥ karoṭapāṇyādibhiśca devair nāgaiḥ sārdhaṃ miśrībhāvaṃ kṛtvā bhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitam ||
children.translated_text: Then once more the <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods, together with the gods beginning with the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s> and with the <s>nāgas</s>, joined together and checked the vanguard of troops.

children.text: rājā ca mūrdhātastatsthānamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> arrived at that place.

children.text: tenoktaṃ kimetadbhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitaṃ te kathayanty ete deva sadāmattā devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'Why has this vanguard of troops been checked?' They answered, 'Your Majesty, these are the <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods.'

children.text: rājñā abhihitaṃ sadāmattā eva me devāḥ purojavā bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: The king said, 'Let the <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods themselves be my forerunners.'

children.text: yataḥ sadāmattā devāstaiḥ sārdhaṃ devair nāgaiścāgrataḥ pradhāvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Sadāmatta</s> gods, together with those gods and <s>nāgas</s>, ran ahead in front.

children.text: teṣāṃ dhāvatāṃ cāturmahārājikā devāḥ samprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they were running, they came upon the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.

children.text: tairuktaṃ kimetadbhavanto dhāvato yato nāgādibhirdevairagrato 'nuyāyibhirabhihitā eṣa manuṣyarājā āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: They said, 'Why are you running, sirs?' Then the gods beginning with the <s>nāgas</s>, who were following ahead, replied, 'This human king is coming.'

children.text: catvāro mahārājānaḥ saṃlakṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: The four great kings considered the matter.

children.text: puṇyamaheśākhyo 'yaṃ sattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This being is of great power through merit.'

children.text: nāsya śakyaṃ viroddhumiti ||
children.translated_text: 'It is not possible to oppose him.'

children.text: tatastaiścaturbhirmahārājais trāyastriṃśānāmārocitam eṣa bhavanto manuṣyarājā mūrdhāta āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: Then those four great kings announced to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, 'Sirs, this human king <s>Mūrdhāta</s> is coming.'

children.text: trāyastriṃśā devāḥ saṃlakṣayanti puṇyavipākamaheśākhyo 'yaṃ sattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods considered, 'This being is of great power through the ripening of merit.'

children.text: nāsya viroddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: 'He must not be opposed.'

children.text: argheṇāsya pratyudgacchāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Let us go out to meet him with an <s>argha</s> (honor-offering).'

children.text: tataste trāyastriṃśā devā argheṇa pratyudgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods went out to meet him with an <s>argha</s> (honor-offering).

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā mūrdhātaḥ sumerumūrdhanyabhiruhannīlanīlāṃ vanarājiṃ medharājimivonnatām ||
children.translated_text: As King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was ascending the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, he saw a deep blue line of forest rising high like a mass of clouds.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punardivaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate kimetaddivaukasa nīlanīlā vanarājirmegharājirivonnatā eṣā deva devānāṃ pārijātako nāma kovidāro yatra devāstrāyastriṃśāścaturo vārṣikān māsān divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samanvaṅgībhūtāḥ krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti ||
children.translated_text: After seeing it, he addressed the yakṣa <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'What is this, <s>Divaukasa</s>, this deep blue line of forest rising high like a mass of clouds?' 'Your Majesty, this is the <s>Pārijātaka</s>, the <s>kovidāra</s> tree of the gods, where the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, furnished and endowed with the five divine strands of sensual pleasure, play, delight, and enjoy themselves during the four months of the rainy season.'

children.text: devo 'pyatra gatvā divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtaḥ krīḍatu ramatāṃ paricārayatu ||
children.translated_text: 'Let Your Majesty too go there and, furnished and endowed with the five divine strands of sensual pleasure, play, delight, and enjoy yourself.'

children.text: śrutvā ca punā rājā mūrdhāto 'mātyānāmantrayate paśyatha yūyaṃ nīlanīlāṃ vanarājiṃ megharājimivonnatām evaṃ deva ||
children.translated_text: After hearing this, King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> addressed his ministers: 'Do you see the deep blue line of forest rising high like a mass of clouds?' 'Yes, Your Majesty.'

children.text: eṣa devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ pārijātakaḥ kovidāro yatra devāstrāyastriṃśāścaturo vārṣikān māsān divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samanvaṅgībhūtāḥ krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>pārijātaka</s> <s>kovidāra</s> tree of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, where the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, furnished and endowed with the five divine objects of desire for the four months of the rains, play, delight, and enjoy themselves.

children.text: yūyamapi grāmaṇyo 'tra gatvā divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samanvaṅgībhūtāḥ krīḍata ramata paricārayata ||
children.translated_text: You too, headmen, should go there and, furnished and endowed with the five divine objects of desire, play, delight, and enjoy yourselves.

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā mūrdhātaḥ sumerumūrdhanyabhiruhañ śvetaśvetamabhrakūṭamivonnatam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, while ascending to the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, saw something lofty, very white like a mass of white cloud.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punardivaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate kimetaddivaukasa śvetaśvetamabhrakūṭamivonnatam eṣā deva devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudharmā nāma devasabhā yatra devāstrāyastriṃśāścatvāraśca mahārājānaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ saṃnipatitā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cārthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca cintayanti tulayanti upaparīkṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing it, he again addressed the divine <s>yakṣa</s>: "Divine one, what is this, lofty and very white like a mass of white cloud?" "Your Majesty, this is the divine assembly of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, named <s>Sudharmā</s>, where the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and the four great kings sit assembled and gathered together, considering, weighing, and examining the welfare and the <s>dharma</s> of gods and humans."

children.text: devo 'pyatra gamiṣyatu ||
children.translated_text: "Your Majesty should go there too."

children.text: śrutvā ca punaramātyānāmantrayate paśyatha yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ śvetaśvetamabhrakūṭamivonnatam evaṃ deva ||
children.translated_text: After hearing this, he again addressed his ministers: "Look, headmen, at that lofty thing, very white like a mass of white cloud." "Yes, Your Majesty."

children.text: eṣā trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudharmā nāma devasabhā yatra devāstrāyastriṃśāścatvāraśca mahārājānaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ saṃnipatitā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cārthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca cintayanti tulayanti upaparīkṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: "This is the divine assembly of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, named <s>Sudharmā</s>, where the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and the four great kings sit assembled and gathered together, considering, weighing, and examining the welfare and the <s>dharma</s> of gods and humans.

children.text: yūyamapi grāmaṇyo 'tra gamiṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: You too, headmen, should go there."

children.text: devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma nagaramardhatṛtīyāni yojanasahasrāṇyāyāmena ardhatṛtīyāni yojanasahasrāṇi vistareṇa samantataḥ parikṣepeṇa daśayojanasahasrāṇi saptabhiḥ kāñcanamayaiḥ prākāraiḥ parikṣiptam ||
children.translated_text: The city of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, named <s>Sudarśana</s>, is two and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length, two and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth, and ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> in circumference all around; it is enclosed by seven ramparts made of gold.

children.text: te prākārā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanānyucchrayeṇa ||
children.translated_text: Those ramparts are two and a half <s>yojanas</s> in height.

children.text: teṣu prākāreṣu caturvidhāḥ ṣoḍakā māpitāḥ suvarṇamayā rūpyamayā vaiḍūryamayāḥ sphaṭikamayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On those ramparts four kinds of upper structures were constructed: made of gold, made of silver, made of beryl, and made of crystal.

children.text: ūrdhvī ekā nibaddhā saṃkramaṇakā ||
children.translated_text: An elevated passageway was fastened above.

children.text: sudarśananagare 'bhyantare bhūmibhāgo 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaścitraḥ sucitra ekaikacitradhātuśatena mṛduḥ sumṛdus tadyathā tulapicurvā karpāsapicurvā ||
children.translated_text: Inside the city <s>Sudarśana</s>, the ground is lovely, beautiful to see, pleasing, variegated, finely variegated with hundreds of individual colored elements, and soft, very soft, like cotton down or kapok down.

children.text: prakṣipte pāde avanamatyutkṣipte pāde unnamati divyairmandāravaiḥ puṣpairjānumātreṇa oghena saṃstīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When a foot is set down it sinks, and when a foot is lifted it rises; it is strewn knee-deep with a flood of divine <s>mandārava</s> flowers.

children.text: vāyusaṃyogācca paurāṇānyavakīryante navāni puṣpāṇi samākīryante ||
children.translated_text: When the wind touches them, the old flowers are scattered away and new flowers are scattered over it.

children.text: sudarśane nagare ekonadvārasahasram ||
children.translated_text: In the city <s>Sudarśana</s> there are nine hundred and ninety-nine gates.

children.text: dvāre dvāre pañcaśatāni nīlavāsasām yakṣāṇāṃ sthāpitāni saṃnaddhāni santi citrakalāpāni yāvadeva devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmārakṣaṇārthamatyarthaṃ śobhanārtham ||
children.translated_text: At each gate five hundred blue-clad <s>yakṣas</s> are stationed, standing armed and splendidly arrayed, solely for the protection of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and for exceedingly beautiful adornment.

children.text: sudarśanasya nagarasya vīthyo 'rdhatṛtīyāni yojanasahasrāṇyāyāmena vistareṇa dvādaśa yojanānyabhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāḥ kanakavālukāstīrṇāś candanavāripariṣiktā hemajālāvanaddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The streets of the city <s>Sudarśana</s> are two and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and twelve <s>yojanas</s> in breadth; they are lovely, beautiful to see, pleasing, spread with golden sand, sprinkled with sandalwood water, and covered with golden netting.

children.text: sāmantakena vividhāḥ puṣkiriṇyo māpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All around, various lotus ponds were constructed.

children.text: tāḥ puṣkariṇyaścaturvidhair iṣṭakaiścitāḥ suvarṇamayai rūpyamayaiḥ sphaṭikamayairvaiḍūryamayaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those lotus ponds are lined with four kinds of bricks: made of gold, made of silver, made of crystal, and made of beryl.

children.text: vedikāyāḥ sphaṭikamayā sūcī ālambanamadhiṣṭhānam ||
children.translated_text: The posts, rails, and foundations of the railing are made of crystal.

children.text: sphaṭikamayyā vaiḍūryamayī sūcī ālambanamadhiṣṭhānam ||
children.translated_text: For the crystal work, the posts, rails, and foundations are made of beryl.

children.text: tāḥ puṣkiriṇyaḥ pūrṇāḥ śītalena vāriṇā kṣaudrakalpenāmbunā utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannā vividhairjalajaiḥ śakunakairvalgusvarairmanojñasvaraiḥ kāmarūpibhir nikūjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those lotus ponds are full of cool water, water like honey; they are covered with blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water lilies, and white lotuses, and they resound with the calls of various water birds, sweet-voiced, pleasing-voiced, and able to assume whatever form they desire.

children.text: sāmantake vividhāḥ puṣpavṛkṣāḥ phalavṛkṣāḥ sujātāḥ susaṃsthitā āpīḍakajātāḥ tadyathā dakṣeṇa mālākāreṇa vā mālākārāntevāsinā vā mālā vā agrasthitāvataṃsakāni vā suracitāni ||
children.translated_text: In the surrounding area, various flower trees and fruit trees are well grown, well arranged, and clustered like garlands, just as garlands or foremost head-wreaths might be well arranged by a skillful garland-maker or a garland-maker's apprentice.

children.text: vividhaiḥ sthalajaiḥ śakunakair valgusvarairmanojñasvaraiḥ kāmarūpibhirabhinikūjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They resound with the calls of various land birds, sweet-voiced, pleasing-voiced, and able to assume whatever form they desire.

children.text: sudarśane nagare caturvidhāḥ kalpadūṣyavṛkṣā nīlāḥ pītā lohitā avadātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the city <s>Sudarśana</s> there are four kinds of <s>kalpadūṣya</s> trees, wish-fulfilling cloth trees: blue, yellow, red, and white.

children.text: kalpadūṣyavṛkṣaiścaturvidhāni tuṇḍicelāni ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>kalpadūṣya</s> trees come four kinds of <s>tuṇḍicela</s> cloths.

children.text: taistuṇḍicelaiścaturvidhāni kalpadūṣyāni nīlāni pītāni lohitānyavadātāni ||
children.translated_text: From those <s>tuṇḍicela</s> cloths come four kinds of <s>kalpadūṣya</s> garments: blue, yellow, red, and white.

children.text: yādṛśamākāṅkṣati devo vā devakanyā vā sahacittotpādāddhaste prādurbhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, it appears in the hand at the very arising of the thought.

children.text: caturvidhā ābharaṇavṛkṣā hastopagāḥ pādopagā guhyāḥ prakāśitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are four kinds of ornament trees: for the hands, for the feet, hidden, and displayed.

children.text: yādṛśamākāṅkṣati devo vā devakanyā vā sahacittotpādāddhaste prādurbhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, it appears in the hand at the very arising of the thought.

children.text: caturvidhā vādyabhāṇḍavṛkṣā veṇuvallarisughoṣakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are four kinds of musical-instrument trees: <s>veṇu</s>, <s>vallarī</s>, and <s>sughoṣaka</s> instruments.

children.text: yādṛśamākāṅkṣati devo vā devakanyā vā sahacittotpādāddhaste prādurbhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, it appears in the hand at the very arising of the thought.

children.text: caturvidhāpi ca sudhā nīlā pītā lohitā avadātā ||
children.translated_text: And there are four kinds of <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia): blue, yellow, red, and white.

children.text: yādṛśamākāṅkṣati devo vā devakanyā vā sahacittotpādāddhaste prādurbhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, it appears in the hand at the very arising of the thought.

children.text: madhumādhavaḥ kādambarī pāripānam ||
children.translated_text: There were honey-wine and spring wine, kādambarī liquor, and drinking.

children.text: gṛhāḥ kūṭāgārā harmyāḥ prāsādāḥ svāsanakā avalokanakā saṃkramaṇakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There were houses, upper chambers, mansions, palaces, comfortable seats, lookouts, and passageways.

children.text: nārīgaṇavirājitam apsaraḥsahasrasaṃghaniṣevitaṃ tūryanādābhināditam upetamannapānam ||
children.translated_text: It was adorned with groups of women, attended by hosts of thousands of apsarases, resounding with the sound of music, and supplied with food and drink.

children.text: yatra trāyastriṃśāḥ krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti svakaṃ puṇyaphalaṃ pratyanubhavanti ||
children.translated_text: There the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods play, delight themselves, are attended upon, and experience the fruit of their own merit.

children.text: devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudharmā devasabhā trīṇi yojanaśatānyāyāmena trīṇi yojanaśatāni vistareṇa samantaparikṣepeṇa navayojanaśatāni abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sphaṭikamayī ardhapañcamāni yojanāni tasmānnagarīto 'bhyudgatā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sudharmā</s>, the divine assembly hall of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, was three hundred yojanas in length, three hundred yojanas in breadth, and nine hundred yojanas in circumference; beautiful, lovely to behold, gracious, made of crystal, it rose four and a half yojanas above that city.

children.text: tatra devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmāsanāni prajñaptāni yatra pṛthak dvātriṃśatīnāmupendrāṇāmāsanāni trayastriṃśatimaṃ śakrasya devānāmindrasya ||
children.translated_text: There seats were prepared for the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods: separate seats for the thirty-two <s>upendra</s>s, and the thirty-third for <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: teṣāmeva devānāṃ sarvānte mūrdhātasya rājña āsanaṃ prajñaptam ||
children.translated_text: At the very end of those gods' seats, a seat was prepared for King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>.

children.text: paścāddevāstrāyastriṃśā mūrdhātasya rājño 'rghaṃ gṛhya pratyudgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, taking an argha guest-offering for King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, went out to meet him.

children.text: tatra ye puṇyamaheśākhyāḥ sattvā anupūrveṇa praviṣṭā avaśiṣṭā bahiḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There those beings of great merit and power entered in order, while the rest remained outside.

children.text: yataḥ sa rājā mūrdhātaḥ saṃlakṣayati yānyetānyāsanāni prajñaptakāni etebhyo yadantimamāsanam etanmama bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> considered, "Of these seats that have been prepared, the last seat among them will be mine."

children.text: atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat aho bata me śakro devānāmindro 'rdhāsanenopanimantrayate ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>: "Ah, if only <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, would invite me to share half his seat."

children.text: sahacittotpādādeva śakro devānāmindro rājño māndhāturardhāsanamadāt ||
children.translated_text: At the very arising of that thought, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, gave half his seat to King <s>Māndhātā</s>.

children.text: praviṣṭo rājā mūrdhātaḥ śakrasya devānāmindrasyārdhāsane ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> entered upon the half-seat of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: na khalu rājño mūrdhātasya śakrasya devānāmindrasyaikāsane niṣaṇṇayoḥ kaścidviśeṣo vā abhiprāyo vā nānākaraṇaṃ vā yaduta ārohapariṇāhau varṇapuṣkalatā svaraguptyā svaragupteḥ nānyatra śakrasya devānāmindrasyānimiṣatena ||
children.translated_text: When King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, were seated on one seat, there was no distinction, difference of appearance, or dissimilarity at all between them, whether in height and breadth, fullness of complexion, or restraint of voice and bearing, except for the unblinking nature of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: rājño mūrdhātasya deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu tiṣṭhataḥ ṣaṭtriṃśāścakrāścyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: While King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> was staying among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, thirty-six wheels fell away.

children.text: tatra ca teṣāṃ devānāṃ devāsurasaṃgrāmaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then among those gods there was a battle between the gods and the <s>asura</s>s.

children.text: tatra yadyasurāḥ parājayante paścādasurapuryāṃ dvārāṇi badhnanti ||
children.translated_text: There, if the <s>asura</s>s are defeated, afterward they close the gates in the city of the <s>asura</s>s.

children.text: devānāmapi pañca rakṣāḥ parājayante ||
children.translated_text: The five defenses of the gods also were defeated.

children.text: te 'pi devapuryāṃ dvārāṇi badhnanti ||
children.translated_text: They too closed the gates in the city of the gods.

children.text: teṣāmevaṃ devāsurāṇāṃ parasparataḥ saṃbhrama utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way mutual alarm arose among those gods and <s>asura</s>s.

children.text: yato rājñā mūrdhātena trāyastriṃśānāmuktaṃ kimetadbhavanto 'tīva saṃbhramajātā devais trāyastriṃśairuktam etairasurairasmākaṃ pañca rakṣā bhagnāḥ yato 'smābhirdvārāṇi baddhāni ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> said to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, "What is this, sirs, that you have become so very alarmed?" The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods said, "These <s>asura</s>s have broken our five defenses; therefore we have closed the gates."

children.text: yato mūrdhātena rājñā uktam ātmapuruṣāḥ ānayantu bhavanto dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> said, "My own men, let Your Honors bring the bow."

children.text: yatastasya dhanurānītam ||
children.translated_text: Then his bow was brought.

children.text: tena paścāddhanurgṛhya guṇaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, taking the bow, he made the sound of the bowstring.

children.text: tasya ca dhanuṣo guṇaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the sound of that bowstring was made.

children.text: asuraiḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was heard by the <s>asura</s>s.

children.text: taṃ śrutvā asurāḥ kathayanti kasyaiṣa guṇaśabdas taiḥ śrutaṃ rājño mūrdhātasyaiṣa guṇaśabdaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing it, the <s>asura</s>s said, "Whose bowstring sound is this?" They were told, "This is the bowstring sound of King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>."

children.text: te taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā vismayamāpannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that sound, they were filled with astonishment.

children.text: paścādrājā mūrdhāto nirgatastasmādeva nagarāt teṣāṃ devānāmasurair bhagnakānāṃ svaṃ ca kāyaṃ saṃnahya ||
children.translated_text: Afterward King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> went forth from that very city, armoring his own body on behalf of those gods who had been broken by the <s>asura</s>s.

children.text: dharmatā ca punareṣāṃ devāsurāṇām yudhyatāṃ rathā vaihāyasena tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: And this is the dharmatā, the fixed rule, of gods and <s>asura</s>s when they fight: their chariots stand in the air.

children.text: teṣāmanyonyaṃ na kasyacidadhiko vā hīno vā ||
children.translated_text: Among them, no one's chariot is higher or lower than another's.

children.text: rājño mūrdhātasya sarveṣāmapyasurāṇāṃ vaihāyasamabhyudgamyoparisthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>'s chariot rose into the air above all the <s>asura</s>s and stood over them.

children.text: paścāt te 'surāḥ kathayanti ka eṣo 'smākamuparivihāyasamabhyudgato yatastaiḥ śrutaṃ manuṣyarājā eṣa mūrdhāto nāma ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>asura</s>s said, "Who is this who has risen into the air above us?" Then they were told, "This is a human king named <s>Mūrdhātā</s>."

children.text: paścāt te saṃlakṣayanti puṇyavipākamaheśākhyo 'yaṃ sattvo yasyāsmākamuparivaihāyasaṃ ratho gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Afterward they considered, "This being is great in the ripening of merit, since his chariot moves in the air above us."

children.text: jitā bhagnāḥ parājitāḥ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛtā āsurīṃ purīṃ praviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They were conquered, broken, defeated, turned back, and entered the city of the <s>asura</s>s.

children.text: paścādrājā mūrdhātaḥ kathayati kasya jayo yato 'mātyāḥ kathayanti devasya jayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> said, "Whose is the victory?" Then his ministers said, "The victory is Your Majesty's."

children.text: sa rājā saṃlakṣayati ahameva devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sakāśādabhyadhikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king considered, "I alone am superior even to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods."

children.text: tasya rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavati etadasti me jambudvīpaḥ asti me sapta ratnāni asti me sahasraṃ putrāṇām vṛṣṭaṃ me 'ntaḥpure saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ samanuśiṣṭaṃ me pūrvavidehaṃ samanuśiṣṭaṃ me 'paragodānīyaṃ dvīpaṃ samanuśiṣṭaṃ me uttarakuruṣu svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgram adhiṣṭhitaṃ me 'sti devāṃstrāyastriṃśān praviṣṭo 'smi sudharmāṃ devasabhām dattaṃ me śakreṇa devendreṇārdhāsanam ||
children.translated_text: This occurred to King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>: "I possess <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; I possess the seven jewels; I possess a thousand sons; for seven days a rain of gold has rained in my inner palace; <s>Pūrvavideha</s> has been brought under my rule; the island of <s>Aparagodānīya</s> has been brought under my rule; my own foremost army has been established among the <s>Uttarakuru</s>s; I have entered among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods; I have entered the divine assembly hall <s>Sudharmā</s>; half a seat has been given to me by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: aho batāhaṃ śakraṃ devānāmindramasmāt sthānāccyāvayitvā svayameva devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayeyam ||
children.translated_text: Ah, if only I could make <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, fall from this place and myself exercise royal sovereignty, lordship, and dominion over both gods and human beings."

children.text: sahacittotpādādrājā mūrdhātastasmāt ṛddhitaḥ paribhraṣṭo jambudvīpeṣu pratyaṣṭhāt ||
children.translated_text: At the arising of that very thought, King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, fallen from his supernatural power, landed in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: kharamābādhaṃ spṛṣṭavān pragāḍhāṃ devānāṃ maraṇāntikīm ||
children.translated_text: He was struck by a harsh illness, a severe death-ending condition of the gods.

children.text: atha rājño mūrdhātasyāmātyagaṇamahāmātyā rājyakartāro mantrasahajīvino yena rājā mūrdhātastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the ministers, great ministers, administrators of the kingdom, and companions in counsel of King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> approached King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ mūrdhātamidamavocan bhaviṣyanti khalu devasyātyayāt paścimā janapadāḥ paripṛṣṭavanto rājñā mūrdhātena maraṇasamaye kiṃ vyākṛtaṃ saced vo grāmaṇyo mamātyayāt kaścidupasaṃkramyaivaṃ pṛcchet kiṃ bhavanto rājñā mūrdhātena maraṇasamaye vyākṛtam teṣāmidaṃ syādvacanīyaṃ rājā bhavanto mūrdhāto ratnaiḥ samanvāgato 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they said this to King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>: "Indeed, after Your Majesty's passing, later peoples will ask, 'What was declared by King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> at the time of death?' If, headmen, after my passing someone should approach you and ask, 'Sirs, what was declared by King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> at the time of death?' this should be said to them: 'Sirs, King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> was endowed with jewels.

children.text: catasṛbhiśca mānuṣikābhir ṛddhibhiścaturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayitvā devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after exercising sovereignty, lordship, and dominion over the kingdoms on the four continents by means of the four human supernatural powers, he ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: atṛpta eva pañcānāṃ kāmaguṇānāṃ kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Still unsatisfied with the five strands of sensual pleasure, he died.

children.text: na kārṣāpaṇavarṣeṇa tṛptiḥ kāmeṣu vidyate
children.translated_text: Even by a rain of kārṣāpaṇas there is no satisfaction among sensual pleasures.

children.text: alpāsvādān bahuduḥkhān kāmān vijñāya piṇḍataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having understood sensual pleasures in sum as slight in taste and great in suffering,

children.text: api divyeṣu kāmeṣu ratiṃ naivādhigacchati
children.translated_text: one does not obtain delight even in divine sensual pleasures.

children.text: tṛṣṇākṣaye rato bhavati samyaksambuddhaśrāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A disciple of the perfectly awakened one delights in the destruction of craving.

children.text: parvato 'pi suvarṇasya samo himavatā bhavet
children.translated_text: Even if there were a mountain of gold equal to <s>Himavat</s>,

children.text: nālamekasya tadvittamiti vidvān samācaret ||
children.translated_text: that wealth would not be enough for one person; knowing this, one should act accordingly.

children.text: yaḥ prekṣati duḥkhamitonidānaṃ kāmeṣu jātu sa kathaṃ ramate
children.translated_text: Whoever sees suffering as arising from this source in sensual pleasures, how could he ever delight in them?

children.text: loke hi śalyamupādhiṃ viditvā tasyaiva dhīro vinayāya śikṣet ||
children.translated_text: For, having known acquisition to be the barb in the world, the wise man should train for its very removal.'"

children.text: yadā ca punastena janakāyena śrutaṃ rājā mūrdhāto glāno maraṇāvasthita iti tataste 'mātyā janapadāścānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi rājānaṃ mūrdhātamupasaṃkramya darśanāya ||
children.translated_text: And when that body of people heard, "King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> is ill and near death," then those ministers and peoples, and many hundreds of thousands of living beings, approached King <s>Mūrdhātā</s> in order to see him.

children.text: yatastena rājñā tasya janasya tāvadevaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā kāmeṣvādīnavakathā gṛhāśramapadasyādīnavo bhāṣitas tathā kāmo jugupsito yathā anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi ṛṣīṇāmantike pravrajya gṛhāśramapadānyapahāya vanaṃ saṃśritā ṛṣibhiḥ pravrajitvā catvāri brahmavihārān bhāvayitvā kāmeṣu kāmacchandaṃ prahāya tadbahulavihāriṇo brahmalokasabhāgatāyām upapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that king gave such a teaching of the Dharma to those people: a discourse on the danger in sensual pleasures was given, and the danger of the station of household life was explained; sensual pleasure was condemned in such a way that many hundreds of thousands of living beings, having gone forth in the presence of seers, abandoned the stations of household life and resorted to the forest. Having gone forth among the seers, cultivated the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings), abandoned sensual desire toward sensual pleasures, and dwelt much in that practice, they were reborn in a state corresponding to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: yāvacca jambudvīpe yāvacca pūrvavidehe dvīpe yāvaccāparagodānīye dvīpe yāvaccottarakuruṣu yāvacca saptasu kāñcanamayeṣu parvateṣu yāvacca devāṃstrāyastriṃśān adhirūḍhaḥ atrāntare caturdaśottaraṃ śakraśataṃ cyutam ||
children.translated_text: And for as long as he ascended in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, on the island of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, on the island of <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, among the <s>Uttarakurus</s>, on the seven golden mountains, and among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, during that interval one hundred and fourteen <s>Śakras</s> passed away.

children.text: śakrasya bhikṣavo devānāmindrasyāyuṣaḥ pramāṇam yanmanuṣyāṇāṃ varṣamekaṃ devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmekarātriṃdivasam ||
children.translated_text: Monks, the measure of the lifespan of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, is this: one human year is one night and day for the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: rātriṃdivasena triṃśadrātrakena māsena dvādaśamāsena saṃvatsareṇa divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmāyuṣaḥ pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: With thirty nights in a month, twelve months in a year, a thousand divine years is the measure of the lifespan of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: tadbhavati mānuṣikayā gaṇanayā tisro varṣalakṣāḥ ṣaṣṭiśca varṣasahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: By human reckoning that becomes three hundred thousand and sixty thousand years.

children.text: yasminnānanda samaye rājā mūrdhāto devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍha evaṃvidhaṃ cittamutpāditam aho bata me śakro devānāmindro 'rdhāsanenopanimantrayate kāśyapo bhikṣustena kālena tena samayena śakro devānāmindro babhūva ||
children.translated_text: At the time, <s>Ānanda</s>, when King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, having ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, produced such a thought as, 'Ah, if only <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, would invite me to half his seat,' the monk <s>Kāśyapa</s>, at that time and on that occasion, was <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: yasmin khalvānanda samaye rājño mūrdhātasyaivaṃvidhaṃ cittamutpannam yannvahaṃ śakraṃ devānāmindramasmāt sthānāccyāvayitvā svayameva devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayeyaṃ kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddhastena kālena tena samayena śakro devānāmindro babhūva ||
children.translated_text: But at the time, <s>Ānanda</s>, when this thought arose in King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, 'What if I were to remove <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, from this position and myself exercise sovereignty, lordship, and dominion over gods and men?' <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, at that time and on that occasion, was <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: maheśākhye sattve cittaṃ pradūṣitam tasmādṛddheḥ paribhraṣṭo jambudvīpe pratyaṣṭhāt kharamābādhaṃ spṛṣṭavān pragāḍhāṃ vedanāṃ maraṇāntikīm ||
children.translated_text: His mind was corrupted toward a being of great power; therefore, fallen from his supernatural power, he landed in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and was struck by a harsh illness, a severe feeling ending in death.

children.text: yo 'sau rājā mūrdhāto 'hamevānanda tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: That King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, was none other than I myself at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: tatra tāvanmayā ānanda sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohena aparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsadharmeṇa maraṇakālasamaye tāvadevaṃvidhā parikathā kṛtā yadanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi gṛhāśramamapahāya ṛṣibhyaḥ pravrajitvā kāmeṣu kāmacchandaṃ vyapahāya tadbahulavihāriṇo brahmalokamupapāditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, <s>Ānanda</s>, while I was still with passion, with hatred, with delusion, not liberated, subject to birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and distress, at the time of death I gave such a discourse that many hundreds of thousands of living beings abandoned household life, went forth among seers, cast off sensual desire toward sensual pleasures, dwelt much in that practice, and were caused to be reborn in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ sarvajñenānuttarajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena nirvāṇāya samprasthitena tāvadevaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā yadanekāni devatāśatasahasrāṇi satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni ||
children.translated_text: Now, as the all-knowing one who has attained mastery over the objects known by unsurpassed knowledge and has set out toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, I have given such a teaching of the Dharma that many hundreds of thousands of deities have been established in the truths.

children.text: anekāni ṛṣiśatasahasrāṇi eta bhikṣava iti pravrajitāni ||
children.translated_text: And many hundreds of thousands of seers have been ordained with the words, 'Come, monks.'

children.text: tairyujyadbhirghaṭadbhirvyāyacchadbhiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: By those who yoked themselves, applied themselves, and exerted themselves, arhatship was attained through the abandonment of all defilements.

children.text: anekadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu vyavasthāpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Many gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas were established in taking refuge and in the precepts.

children.text: anekāni vaiśālikāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi yeṣāṃ kecitsrotāpattiphale vyavasthāpitāḥ kecit sakṛdāgāmiphale kecidanāgāmiphale kaiścit pravrajitvārhattvaṃ prāptaṃ kaiścit śrāvakabodhau kaiścit pratyekabodhau kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpāditāni kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni ||
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of living beings in <s>Vaiśālī</s> were affected: some were established in the fruit of stream-entry, some in the fruit of once-returning, some in the fruit of non-returning; some, after going forth, attained arhatship; some generated the thought directed toward disciple-awakening, some toward solitary-buddha-awakening, and some toward unsurpassed perfect awakening; and some undertook taking refuge and the precepts.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti kāni bhadanta karmāṇi kṛtāni rājñā mūrdhātena yeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākena sahacittotpādādeva saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣaṃ vṛṣṭaṃ bhagavānāha ||
children.translated_text: The monks, being filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts: "Venerable sir, what deeds were done by King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, as the ripening of which, from the mere arising of a thought, a rain of gold rained for seven days in his inner palace?" The Blessed One said:

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani sarvābhibhūr nāma tathāgato 'rhaṃl loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: "Monks, in the past, in a former time, there arose in the world a Tathāgata named <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, an arhat, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a guide of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: tena khalu samayena anyataraḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'cirapratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time a certain merchant's son had only recently been established in marriage.

children.text: tatra viṣaye dharmatā yā aciroḍhā dārikā bhartari pravahaṇakena pratipradīyate sā catūratnamayaiḥ puṣpairavakīrya baddhakā svāmine pradīyate ||
children.translated_text: In that region the custom was this: a girl who had recently been married was sent to her husband in a carriage; after being strewn with flowers made of four kinds of jewels and adorned, she was given to her lord.

children.text: sā ca bhartāramādāya svagṛhaṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: And she took her husband and went to her own home.

children.text: sa ca śreṣṭhidārakaś catūratnamayāni puṣpāṇi pratigṛhya yānamadhiruhya śvaśuragṛham anuprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That merchant's son received the flowers made of four kinds of jewels, mounted the vehicle, and set out toward his father-in-law's house.

children.text: tasya gacchato 'bhimukhaṃ sarvābhibhūḥ samyaksambuddho janapadeṣu caryāṃ carannanupūrveṇābhyāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was going, the perfectly awakened <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, who was traveling on his rounds through the countryside, gradually came toward him.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā dvātriṃśallakṣaṇālaṃkṛtamasecanakadarśanamatīva prasāda utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, adorned with the thirty-two marks and delightful to behold, he felt an exceedingly strong faith.

children.text: yato 'sau prasādīkṛtacetā yānādavatīrya taṃ bhagavantaṃ taiścatūratnamayaiḥ puṣpairavakirati ||
children.translated_text: Then, with his mind filled with faith, he descended from the vehicle and scattered those flowers made of four kinds of jewels over the Blessed One.

children.text: tāni sarvābhibhuvā samyaksambuddhenādhiṣṭhitāni tathā yathā śakaṭacakramātrāṇyabhinirvṛttāni ||
children.translated_text: Those flowers were empowered by the perfectly awakened <s>Sarvābhibhū</s> in such a way that they became as large as cartwheels.

children.text: tāni vitānaṃ baddhvā gacchato 'nugacchanti tiṣṭhatastiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Having formed a canopy, they followed him as he walked and stood still when he stood still.

children.text: sa prasādajāto gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Filled with faith, he spoke a verse:

children.text: anena dānena mahadgatena buddho bhaveyaṃ sugataḥ svayambhūḥ
children.translated_text: "By this great gift may I become a Buddha, a Sugata, self-born,

children.text: tīrṇaśca tārayeyaṃ mahājanaughān atāritā ye pūrvakairjinendraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having crossed over, may I carry across the great floods of people who were not carried across by the former lordly victors.

children.text: sarvābhibhūrme bhagavān maharṣiravakīrṇaḥ puṣpaiḥ sumanoramaiśca
children.translated_text: The Blessed One <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, the great seer, has been strewn by me with beautiful and very pleasing flowers,

children.text: praṇidhiśca me tatra kṛtā udārā ākāṅkṣatā vā idamagrabodhim ||
children.translated_text: and there I made a noble aspiration, longing for this supreme awakening.

children.text: tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākato me prāptā hi me bodhiḥ śivā anuttarā
children.translated_text: From the ripening of that very karma, awakening, auspicious and unsurpassed, has indeed been attained by me,

children.text: vṛṣṭaṃ ca saptāhahiraṇyavarṣaṃ mūrdhātasya rājño mahābalasya ||
children.translated_text: and a rain of gold rained for seven days for mighty King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>.

children.text: tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākato me nagaramapi sauvarṇakāñcanaṃ babhūva mahāsudarśanasya ramaṇīyā kuśāvatī nāma purī babhūva ||
children.translated_text: From the ripening of that very karma, the city also became golden, made of gold; the delightful city of <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, named <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, came into being."

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti kīdṛśaṃ bhadanta rājñā mūrdhātena karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena caturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritaṃ devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍho bhagavānāha ||
children.translated_text: The monks, being filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts: "Venerable sir, what kind of deed was done by King <s>Mūrdhātā</s>, as the ripening of which lordship and royal sovereignty over the four continents was exercised by him and he ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods?" The Blessed One said:

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vipaśyī nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho loke utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Monks, in the past, in a former time, there arose in the world a Tathāgata named <s>Vipaśyī</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: atha sa vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddho janapadeṣu caryāṃ caramāṇo 'nupūrveṇa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the perfectly awakened <s>Vipaśyī</s>, traveling on his rounds through the countryside, gradually reached the capital city <s>Bandhumatī</s>.

children.text: atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bandhumatīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the forenoon, the perfectly awakened <s>Vipaśyī</s> dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Bandhumatī</s> for alms.

children.text: tatrānyataraścotkariko nāma vaṇik ||
children.translated_text: There was a certain merchant named <s>Otkarika</s>.

children.text: bhagavantaṃ vipaśyinamasecanakadarśanarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā adhikaḥ prasāda utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the Blessed One <s>Vipaśyī</s>, whose form was delightful to behold, an exceptional faith arose in him.

children.text: prasādajātena tasya mudgānāṃ muṣṭiṃ gṛhītvā pātre prakṣiptā ||
children.translated_text: With faith arisen, he took a handful of mung beans and cast it into his bowl.

children.text: tato mudgāścatvāraḥ pātre patitā ekaḥ kaṇṭakamāhatya bhūmau patitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then four mung beans fell into the bowl; one struck the rim and fell to the ground.

children.text: avaśiṣṭaṃ naivaṃ samprāptaṃ pātram asamprāptā eva bhūmau patitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rest did not reach the bowl; before reaching it, they fell to the ground.

children.text: tato vaṇik prasādajātaḥ praṇidhiṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Then the merchant, filled with faith, made an aspiration:

children.text: anena dānena mahadgatena buddho bhaveyaṃ sugataḥ svayambhūḥ
children.translated_text: "By this great gift may I become a Buddha, a Sugata, self-born,

children.text: tīrṇaśca tārayeyaṃ mahājanaughān na tāritā ye pūrvakairjinendraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having crossed over, may I carry across the great floods of people who were not carried across by the former lordly victors."

children.text: bhagavānāha yo 'sāvotkariko vaṇik ahameva tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "The merchant <s>Otkarika</s> at that time and on that occasion was I myself.

children.text: yanmayā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya prasādajātena mudgānāṃ muṣṭiḥ pātre prakṣiptā tasmāccatvāro mudgāḥ pātre patitā avaśiṣṭā bhūmau patitās tasya karmaṇo vipākena caturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritam ||
children.translated_text: Since, when faith had arisen in me, I cast a handful of mung beans into the bowl of the perfectly awakened <s>Vipaśyī</s>, and four mung beans from it fell into the bowl while the rest fell to the ground, as the ripening of that karma lordship and royal sovereignty over the four continents was exercised by me."

children.text: yaścāsau mudgaḥ pātrakaṇṭakamāhatya bhūmau patitas tasya karmaṇo vipākena trāyastriṃśān devānadhirūḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that mung bean, after striking the sharp rim of the bowl, fell on the ground; through the ripening of that action he ascended among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: sacedbhikṣavaḥ sa mudgaḥ pātre patito 'bhaviṣyanna bhūmau sthānametadvidyate yaddeveṣu ca manuṣyeṣu ca rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritamabhaviṣyat ||
children.translated_text: If, monks, that mung bean had fallen into the bowl and not onto the ground, this possibility would have existed: he would have exercised royal power, lordship, and sovereignty among gods and humans.

children.text: yo 'sāvotkariko vaṇik tena kālena tena samayena sa eṣa rājā mūrdhātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The merchant who was the grain-dealer at that time, on that occasion, is this very King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.

children.text: yo mūrdhāto rājā ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: And the king <s>Mūrdhāta</s> at that time, on that occasion, was I myself.

children.text: yasmādevaṃ buddhe bhagavati mahākāruṇike kārāḥ kṛtā atyarthaṃ mahāphalā bhavanti mahānuśaṃsā mahādyutayo mahāvaistārikā iti tasmādbhavadbhiḥ kiṃ karaṇīyaṃ buddhe dharme saṃghe kārāḥ karaṇīyāḥ samyakpraṇidhānāni ca karaṇīyānīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since acts of service performed toward the Buddha, the Blessed One, the greatly compassionate one, have exceedingly great fruit, great benefit, great splendor, and great extension, what should you do? Acts of service should be performed toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and right aspirations should be made.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.

children.text: Chapter 18
evaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard.

children.text: ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīya anupūrveṇa grāmanigamapallīpattanarājadhānīṣu cañcūryamāṇāni mahāsamudrataṭamanuprāptāni ||
children.translated_text: At that time about five hundred merchants, having gathered their merchandise and wandering in succession through villages, market towns, hamlets, ports, and royal capitals, reached the shore of the great ocean.

children.text: tair nipuṇataḥ sāmudram yānapātraṃ pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: They carefully prepared a sea-going vessel.

children.text: yato vaṇijastaṃ mahāsamudraṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbhinnamanaso na prasahante samavataritum ||
children.translated_text: When the merchants saw that great ocean, their minds were unsettled and they did not dare to go down into it.

children.text: paścāttairvaṇigbhiḥ karṇadhāra ukta udghoṣaya naḥ puruṣa mahāsamudrasya bhūtaṃ varṇam ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards those merchants said to the helmsman, "Sir, proclaim to us the true description of the great ocean."

children.text: yato karṇadhāra udghoṣayituṃ pravṛttaḥ śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ santyasmin mahāsamudre evaṃvidhāni ratnāni tadyathā maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilā pravālo rajataṃ jātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the helmsman began to proclaim: "Let the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> hear, sirs. In this great ocean there are such jewels as these: gems, pearls, beryl, conch-shell stone, coral, silver, gold, <s>aśmagarbha</s>, <s>musāragalva</s>, <s>lohitikā</s>, and right-turning conches.

children.text: ya icchati evaṃrūpai ratnairātmānaṃ samyaksukhena prīṇayituṃ mātāpitarau putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ mitrāmātyajñātisālohitam kālena ca kālaṃ dakṣiṇīyebhyaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayitumūrdhvagāminīṃ saubhāgyakarīṃ sukhavipākāmāyatyāṃ svargasaṃvartanīm so 'smin mahāsamudre avataratu dhanahetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to satisfy himself with perfect happiness through such jewels, to satisfy his mother and father, sons and wife, female and male servants, workers and hired men, friends, ministers, relatives, and blood relations, and from time to time to establish among worthy <s>śramaṇas</s> and brahmins a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (religious gift) that goes upward, produces good fortune, has pleasant ripening, and in the future leads to heaven, let him enter this great ocean for the sake of wealth."

children.text: evamukte ca punaḥ sarva eva sattvāḥ saṃpattikāmā vipattipratikūlāstaṃ śrutvā tasmin mahāsamudre vyavasitāḥ samavataritum ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, all beings desire prosperity and are averse to misfortune; hearing it, they resolved to go down into that great ocean.

children.text: yatastadvahanam atiprabhūtairmanuṣyairatibhāreṇa ca ākrāntatvāt tatraivāvasīdati ||
children.translated_text: Then that ship, because it was loaded with too many people and excessive weight, began to sink right there.

children.text: tataḥ karṇadhāreṇoktam asahyaṃ vahanam ||
children.translated_text: Then the helmsman said, "The ship cannot bear this."

children.text: yato vaṇijaḥ kathayanti kasyedānīṃ vakṣyāmo vahanāt pratyavatarasveti ||
children.translated_text: Then the merchants said, "To whom shall we now say, 'Get down from the ship'?"

children.text: tairvaṇigbhiḥ karṇadhārasyoktaṃ mahāsamudrasya bhūtaṃ varṇamudghoṣayata ||
children.translated_text: Those merchants said to the helmsman, "Proclaim the true description of the great ocean."

children.text: tataḥ sa udghoṣayituṃ pravṛttaḥ śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ santyasmin mahāsamudre imāni evaṃrūpāṇi mahānti mahābhayāni tadyathā timibhayaṃ timiṃgilabhayamūrmibhayaṃ kūrmabhayaṃ sthale utsīdanabhayaṃ jale saṃsīdanabhayamantarjalagatānāṃ parvatānāmāghaṭṭanabhayaṃ kālikāvātabhayam ||
children.translated_text: Then he began to proclaim: "Let the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> hear, sirs. In this great ocean there are great terrors of the following kinds: danger from <s>timi</s> fish, danger from <s>timiṃgila</s> monsters, danger from waves, danger from turtles, danger of running aground on dry land, danger of sinking in the water, danger of striking mountains beneath the water, and danger from black storms.

children.text: caurā api āgacchanti nīlavāsaso dhanahāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Pirates also come, dressed in blue, robbers of wealth.

children.text: yena cātmano jīvitaparityāgo vyavasthito mātāpitarau putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ mitrāmātyajñātisālohitaṃ citraṃ ca jambudvīpaṃ parityaktum sa mahāsamudramavataratu ||
children.translated_text: Whoever is resolved to give up his own life, and to abandon mother and father, sons and wife, female and male servants, workers and hired men, friends, ministers, relatives, blood relations, and beautiful <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, let him enter the great ocean."

children.text: alpāḥ śūrā bahavaḥ kātarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Few are brave; many are timid.

children.text: taṃ śrutvā tathodghuṣya tu tasmādyānapātrādavatīrṇā bahavaḥ kecidavaśiṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing it proclaimed in that way, many descended from that vessel, while some remained.

children.text: tatastairvaṇigbhirvahanasyaikaṃ varatraṃ chinnam ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants cut one cable of the ship.

children.text: paścād dvau trayo yāvadanupūrveṇa sarve varatrāśchinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards they cut two, then three, until in succession all the cables had been cut.

children.text: tāsu chinnāsu tadvahanaṃ mahākarṇadhārasaṃpreritaṃ gagane mahāvātasaṃprerito megha iva balavadvāyusaṃpreritaṃ kṣiprameva samprasthitam ||
children.translated_text: When those had been cut, the ship, urged on by the great helmsman, like a cloud in the sky driven by a great wind, propelled by a strong wind, quickly set out.

children.text: yāvadratnadvīpamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At last it reached <s>Ratnadvīpa</s>.

children.text: sa taṃ pradeśamanuprāptānāṃ karṇadhāraḥ kathayati santyasmin ratnadvīpe kācamaṇayo ratnasadṛśās te bhavadbhirupaparīkṣyopaparīkṣya gṛhītavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they had reached that place, the helmsman said to them, "On this <s>Ratnadvīpa</s> there are glass stones that resemble jewels; you must take them only after examining them again and again.

children.text: mā vaḥ paścājjambudvīpagatānāṃ tāpyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Let there be no regret for you afterwards when you have gone back to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: tatraiva ca kroñcakumārikā nāma striyo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And there, too, are women named <s>Kroñcakumārikās</s>.

children.text: tāḥ puruṣaṃ labdhvā tathopalāṃstāḍayanti yathā atraivānayena vyasanamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained a man, they strike him with stones in such a way that he falls into calamity right there through that very act.

children.text: atraiva ca madanīyāni phalāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And there, too, are intoxicating fruits.

children.text: tāni yo bhakṣayati sa sapta rātriṃdivasān suptastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats them remains asleep for seven days and nights."

children.text: asminneva ca ratnadvīpe saptāhāt pareṇa amanuṣyā na sahante tāvadvidhān viparītān vāyūnutpādayanti yairvahanamapahriyate yathāpi tadakṛtakāryāṇām ||
children.translated_text: And on this very Jewel Island, after seven days, nonhuman beings do not tolerate them; they produce contrary winds of such a kind that the ship is carried away, just as happens to those whose business has not been accomplished.

children.text: tāni bhavadbhirlabdhāni na bhakṣayitavyāni ||
children.translated_text: Those things obtained by you must not be eaten.

children.text: tacchrutvā vaṇijo 'vahitamanaso 'pramādenāvasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the merchants, with attentive minds, remained heedful.

children.text: prāpya ca taṃ ratnadvīpaṃ prayatnamāsthāya ratnānveṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā anupūrveṇopaparīkṣya ratnānāṃ tadvahanaṃ pūritaṃ tadyathā yavānāṃ vā yavasasyānāṃ vā mudgānāṃ vā māṣāṇāṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: And having reached that Jewel Island, they made an effort, searched for jewels, examined them successively, and filled that ship with jewels, just as one might fill it with barley, barley-grain, green gram, or black gram.

children.text: vahanaṃ pūrayitvā te 'nukūlaṃ jambudvīpābhimukhena vāyunā samprasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having filled the ship, they set out with a favorable wind facing toward <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: mahāsamudre ca tribhiḥ skandhaiḥ prāṇinaḥ saṃniśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the great ocean living beings are distributed in three masses.

children.text: prathame yojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ dvistriyojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the first, their bodies are a hundred yojanas, two hundred yojanas, or three hundred yojanas in size.

children.text: dvitīye skandhe 'ṣṭayojanaśatikā ātmabhāvā navadaśayāvaccaturdaśayojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the second mass, their bodies are eight hundred yojanas, and from nine hundred up to fourteen hundred yojanas in size.

children.text: tṛtīye skandhe pañcadaśayojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ ṣoḍaśayojanaśatikā yāvadekaviṃśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the third mass, their bodies are fifteen hundred yojanas, sixteen hundred yojanas, and up to twenty-one hundred yojanas in size.

children.text: tatra ca mahāsamudre tā matsyajātayaḥ parasparānyonyabhakṣaṇaparāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And there in the great ocean those species of fish are intent on devouring one another.

children.text: ye prathamāyāṃ bhūmau avasthitāḥ te dvitīyabhūmisthairbhakṣyante ||
children.translated_text: Those that are situated in the first level are eaten by those situated in the second level.

children.text: ye dvitīyabhūmisthāḥ te tṛtīyabhūmisthairbhakṣyante ||
children.translated_text: Those situated in the second level are eaten by those situated in the third level.

children.text: tatra timiṃgilo nāma matsyas tṛtīyādudakaskandhādabhyudgamya uparimandakaskandhamādāya carati ||
children.translated_text: There a fish named <s>timiṃgila</s>, rising up from the third mass of water, takes in the upper, shallow mass and moves about.

children.text: sa yasyāṃ velāyāṃ mukhamāvṛṇoti tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahāsamudrāt pānīyaṃ mahatā vegenākṣiptaṃ mukhadvāram yato dhāvati ||
children.translated_text: At the moment when it opens its mouth, at that moment water from the great ocean, drawn in with great force, rushes toward the doorway of its mouth.

children.text: tenaivodakaskandhenākṣiptā matsyakacchapavallabhakaśuśumāramakarādyā matsyajātayo mukhadvāreṇodare patanti ||
children.translated_text: Carried along by that very mass of water, fish, turtles, vallabhakas, śuśumāras, makaras, and other species of fish fall through the mouth-door into its belly.

children.text: tasyaivaṃ carata ātmabhāvācchira evaṃ lakṣyate dūrata eva tadyathā parvato nabhaḥpramāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As it moves about in this way, only the head of its body is seen from far away, like a mountain as high as the sky.

children.text: akṣīṇi cāsya dūrata eva saṃlakṣyante nabhasīvādityau ||
children.translated_text: And its eyes are seen from afar like suns in the sky.

children.text: yatastairvaṇigbhirdūrata evopadhāritam ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants observed it from far away.

children.text: tanmahārṇavarūpamupadhārya cintayituṃ pravṛttāḥ kimetadbhavanta ādityadvayasyodayanaṃ teṣāmevaṃ cintayatāṃ tadvahanaṃ tasya mukhadvāram yato vegenopahartumārabdham ||
children.translated_text: Observing that form on the great ocean, they began to think, 'Sirs, what is this? Is it the rising of two suns?' While they were thinking in this way, their ship began to be swept rapidly toward the doorway of its mouth.

children.text: teṣāṃ vahanaṃ vegenāpahriyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā ādityadvayotpādanaṃ ca saṃlakṣya saṃvega utpannaḥ kiṃ bhavanto yat tacchrūyate saptādityāḥ kalpasaṃvartanyāṃ samudāgamiṣyantīti tadevedānīṃ proditāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing their ship being carried away with force, and noticing the appearance of two suns, alarm arose in them: 'Sirs, could this be what is heard, that seven suns will arise at the destruction of the aeon? Have those very suns now risen?'

children.text: yataḥ karṇadhāreṇa teṣāṃ vimarśajātānāmuktaṃ yat tadbhavantaḥ śrūyate timitimiṃgila iti timitimiṃgilabhayamidam ||
children.translated_text: Then, as they were thrown into uncertainty, the helmsman said to them, 'Sirs, what is spoken of as the timi and the <s>timiṃgila</s>: this is the danger of the <s>timiṃgila</s>.'

children.text: tat paśyantu bhavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Let Your Honors look.'

children.text: pānīyādabhyudgataparvatavadālokyate etattasya śiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'That head of its is seen rising from the water like a mountain.'

children.text: paśyatha caiṣā tasya parā dantamālā ||
children.translated_text: 'And look: that is its far row of teeth.'

children.text: paśyatha etau dūrata eva sūryavadavalokyete etau akṣitārakau ||
children.translated_text: 'Look: those two pupils of its eyes are seen from far away like the sun.'

children.text: punarasau karṇadhāro vaṇijāṃ kathayati śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ nāsmākamidānīṃ jīvitopāyaḥ kaścidyena vayamasmādbhayāt mucyema ||
children.translated_text: Again that helmsman said to the merchants, 'Let Your Honors hear: now there is no means of life for us by which we might be freed from this danger.'

children.text: sarveṣāmevāsmākaṃ maraṇaṃ pratyupasthitam ||
children.translated_text: 'Death has come near for every one of us.'

children.text: tadidānīṃ bhavadbhiḥ kiṃ karaṇīyaṃ yasya vo yasmin deve bhaktiḥ sa tamāyācatu ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore what is to be done by Your Honors now is this: whatever deity any of you has devotion toward, let him entreat that deity.'

children.text: yadi tenāpi tāvadāyācanena kāciddevatā asmākamasmānmahābhayādvimokṣaṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Perhaps by even that entreaty some deity may bring about our release from this great danger.'

children.text: na cānyo 'sti kaścidupāyo jīvitasya ||
children.translated_text: 'There is no other means for life.'

children.text: yatastairvaṇigbhirmaraṇabhayabhītaiḥ śivavaruṇakuberamahendropendrādayo devā jīvitaparitrāṇārtham āyācitumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants, terrified by fear of death, began to entreat gods such as <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, and <s>Upendra</s> for the protection of their lives.

children.text: naiva ca teṣāmāyācatāṃ tasmānmaraṇabhayāt jīvitaparitrāṇaviśeṣaḥ kaścit ||
children.translated_text: But although they entreated them, there was no special protection of life for them from that fear of death.

children.text: tathaiva tadvahanaṃ salilavegāt kṣiptaṃ timiṃgilamukhadvāram yato 'pahriyate ||
children.translated_text: Just the same, that ship, hurled by the force of the water, was being carried toward the mouth-door of the <s>timiṃgila</s>.

children.text: tatra copāsako 'bhirūḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And there a lay follower had boarded the ship.

children.text: tenoktaṃ bhavantaḥ nāsmākamasmānmaraṇabhayānmokṣaḥ kaścit ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'Sirs, there is no release for us from this fear of death.'

children.text: sarvairevāsmābhirmartavyam ||
children.translated_text: 'All of us must certainly die.'

children.text: kiṃtu sarva evaikaraveṇa namo buddhāyeti vadāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'But let all of us, with one voice, say: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!'

children.text: sati maraṇe buddhāvalambanayā smṛtyā kālaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'If death comes, we shall die with mindfulness supported by the <s>Buddha</s>.'

children.text: sugatigamanaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: 'There will be going to a happy destiny.'

children.text: yatastairvaṇigbhirekaraveṇa namo buddhāyeti praṇāmaḥ kṛtaḥ sarvaireva ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants all together, with one voice, made the salutation, 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!'

children.text: bhagavatā ca jetavanasthena sa vādaḥ śruto divyena śrotreṇa viśuddhena atikrāntamānuṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One, dwelling in <s>Jetavana</s>, heard that sound with his divine ear, purified and surpassing the human.

children.text: śrutvā ca punarbhagavatā sa nādastathā adhiṣṭhito yathā tena timiṃgilena śrutam ||
children.translated_text: And having heard it, the Blessed One then determined that sound in such a way that the <s>timiṃgila</s> heard it.

children.text: tasya taṃ namo buddhāyeti rāvaṃ śrutvā manaso 'marṣa utpanno viklavībhūtaśca buddho bata loka utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it heard that cry, 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>,' displeasure arose in its mind and it became disturbed: 'Surely a <s>Buddha</s> has arisen in the world.'

children.text: na mama pratirūpaṃ syāt yadahaṃ buddhasya bhagavato nāmodghoṣaṃ śrutvā āhāramāhareyam ||
children.translated_text: 'It would not be fitting for me, after hearing the proclamation of the name of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, to take food.'

children.text: sa cintayituṃ pravṛtto yadyahamidānīṃ sahasaiva mukhadvāraṃ pidhāsyāmi salilavegapratyāhatasya vahanasya vināśo bhaviṣyati eteṣāṃ cānekānāṃ jīvitavināśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to think, "If I now suddenly close the opening of my mouth, the ship, struck back by the force of the water, will be destroyed, and the lives of these many people too will be lost.

children.text: yannvahaṃ mṛdunopakrameṇa svairaṃ svairaṃ mukhadvāraṃ saṃpidadhyām ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to close the opening of my mouth gently and gradually, little by little?"

children.text: tatastena timiṃgilenātmīyaṃ mukhadvāraṃ mṛdunopakrameṇa svairaṃ svairaṃ pihitam ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>timiṃgila</s> gently and gradually closed the opening of its own mouth, little by little.

children.text: paścāt tadvahanaṃ tasmānmahāgrāhamukhādvinirmuktam anuguṇaṃ vāyumāsādya tīramanuprāptam ||
children.translated_text: After that, the ship was freed from the mouth of that great sea-monster, obtained a favorable wind, and reached the shore.

children.text: atha te vaṇijastīramāsādya tadbhāṇḍaṃ śakaṭoṣṭragogardabhādibhiḥ pūrayitvā anupūrveṇa grāmanigamapallīpattanādiṣu cañcūryamāṇāḥ śrāvastīmanuprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants, having reached the shore, loaded their goods onto carts, camels, oxen, donkeys, and the like, and, traveling in sequence through villages, market towns, hamlets, ports, and so on, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: te tatra gatvā saṃlakṣayanti dharmataiṣā yasya nāmnā vahanaṃ saṃsiddhayānapātramāgacchati tasyaiva tāni ratnāni gamyāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When they had gone there, they reflected, "This is the fixed order of things: when a ship comes back as a successful vessel through someone's name, those jewels are destined for that very one.

children.text: yannu vayametāni ratnāni buddhasya bhagavato dadyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What if we were to give these jewels to the Buddha, the Blessed One?"

children.text: te tāni ratnāni saṃgṛhya bhagavataḥ sakāśamupagatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gathering those jewels, they approached the Blessed One.

children.text: anupūrveṇa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavataḥ kathayanti bhagavan asmākaṃ samudre yānapātreṇāvatīrṇānāṃ timiṃgilagrāheṇa tasmin yānapātre 'pahriyamāṇe jīvitavināśe pratyupasthite bhagavataḥ smaraṇaparāyaṇānāṃ nāmagrahaṇaṃ tasmāt mahāgrāhamukhādvinirmuktaṃ tato vayaṃ bhagavan saṃsiddhayānapātrāḥ kṣemasvastinā ihāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having in due order bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet, they said to the Blessed One, "Blessed One, when we had embarked on a vessel upon the ocean, and when that vessel was being carried off by a <s>timiṃgila</s> sea-monster and the destruction of our lives was imminent, because we were devoted to remembering the Blessed One, the taking of your name released us from that great sea-monster's mouth. Then, Blessed One, with our vessel successful, we came here safe and sound.

children.text: dharmatā caiṣā yasya nāmnā vahanaṃ saṃsiddhayānapātrā āgacchanti tasya tadgamyaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And this is the fixed order of things: when ships come back as successful vessels through someone's name, that property belongs to him.

children.text: tadvayaṃ bhagavato nāmagrahaṇena maraṇabhayāduttīrṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the taking of the Blessed One's name, we have crossed beyond the fear of death.

children.text: tadasmākametāni ratnāni bhagavān gṛhṇātu ||
children.translated_text: So let the Blessed One accept these jewels of ours."

children.text: bhagavānāha yena mayendrāya balabodhyaṅgaratnānyadhigatāni kiṃ tathāgatasya bhūyaḥ prākṛtaratnaiḥ karaṇīyaṃ yadi cecchata asmacchāsane vatsāḥ pravrajitum āgacchatha ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Since the jewels consisting of the powers and the factors of awakening have been attained by me, what need has the <s>Tathāgata</s> of further ordinary jewels? But if you wish to go forth in my teaching, children, come."

children.text: yataste saṃlakṣayanti vaṇijo yadasmākaṃ kiṃcit jīvitam tatsarvaṃ buddhasya bhagavatastejasā ||
children.translated_text: Then those merchants reflected, "Whatever life is ours, all of it exists by the power of the Buddha, the Blessed One.

children.text: yadvayametāni ratnāni tyaktvā bhagavato 'ntike pravrajema iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let us give up these jewels and go forth in the presence of the Blessed One."

children.text: paścāt te tāni ratnāni mātāpitṛbhyaḥ putradāradāsīdāsakarmakaramitrāmātyajñātisālohitebhyo yathānyāyataḥ saṃvibhajya pravrajitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward they distributed those jewels, as was proper, among their mothers and fathers, sons and wives, female and male slaves, workers, friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood-relatives, and went forth.

children.text: pravrajya tairyujyadbhirghaṭadbhir vyāyacchadbhiryāvadarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: After going forth, by yoking themselves, applying themselves, and exerting themselves, they realized arhatship.

children.text: yato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti kīdṛśāni karmāṇi bhagavan ebhirvaṇigbhiḥ kṛtānyupacitāni yeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākena bhagavānārāgito na virāgito bhagavānāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts, "Blessed One, what deeds were done and accumulated by these merchants, by the ripening of which the Blessed One was pleased and not displeased?" The Blessed One said:

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddho loka utpanno 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: "Monks, in the past, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a perfectly awakened Buddha, arose in the world.

children.text: tasya ca śāsane eta eva ca pravrajitā abhūvan ||
children.translated_text: In his teaching these very men had gone forth.

children.text: tatra pravrajya ca na kaścit tadrūpo guṇagaṇo 'dhigato nānyatra sabrahmacāriṇāmuddiṣṭamadhītaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: After going forth there, no such collection of qualities was attained by them, apart from what had been recited, studied, and repeated with their fellow celibates.

children.text: maraṇakālasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavanto yadasmābhiḥ kāśyapaṃ samyaksambuddhamāsādyoddiṣṭamadhītaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ ca na kaścit guṇagaṇo 'dhigato 'sti asya karmaṇo vipākena vayam yo 'sau anāgate 'dhvani kāśyapena samyaksambuddhena śākyamunirnāma samyaksambuddho vyākṛtaḥ taṃ vayamārāgayemo na virāgayemaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the time of death they made an aspiration: 'Having met <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, we recited, studied, and repeated his teaching, but no collection of qualities has been attained by us. As the ripening of this karma, may we please and not displease that one who, in a future time, has been predicted by <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, as the perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Śākyamuni</s>.'

children.text: bhagavānāha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāni tāni pañcabhikṣuśatānyatīte 'dhvanyāsan kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane pravrajitāni etāvantyetāni pañcabhikṣuśatāni ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? Those five hundred monks who in the past had gone forth in the teaching of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, are these same five hundred merchants.

children.text: tadā caiṣāmindriyāṇi paripācitāni etarhi arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: At that time their faculties were brought to maturity, and now they have realized arhatship.

children.text: yaścāsau mahāsamudre timistimiṃgilo nāma matsyo buddhaśabdaṃ śrutvā anāhāratāyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ sa svabhāvenaiva tīkṣṇāgnitayā kṣudduḥkhasyāsahatvāccyutaḥ kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that fish in the great ocean named <s>timistimiṃgila</s>, having heard the word 'Buddha,' remained without food; and because by nature its digestive fire was sharp and it could not bear the pain of hunger, it fell away and died.

children.text: tena śrāvastyāṃ ṣaṭkarmanirate brāhmaṇakule pratisaṃdhirgṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that karma it took rebirth in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in a brahmin family devoted to the six rites.

children.text: tasya taccharīraṃ kalevaraṃ mahāsamudre utplutam ||
children.translated_text: Its body, its corpse, floated up in the great ocean.

children.text: nāgaiśca tasya svabhavanasamīpasthasya gandhamasahadbhiranyato vikṣiptam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nāgas</s>, unable to bear the smell of it as it lay near their own dwelling, cast it elsewhere.

children.text: yatra ca vikṣiptaṃ tatrāpi samīpe nāgasyaiva bhavanam ||
children.translated_text: And wherever it was cast, there too, nearby, was the dwelling of a <s>nāga</s>.

children.text: tenāpi gandhamasahatā anyataḥ kṣiptam ||
children.translated_text: That one also, unable to bear the smell, threw it elsewhere.

children.text: evaṃ kṣiptena pāramparyeṇa tat kalevaraṃ mahāsamudrataṭaṃ samudānītam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by being thrown on in succession, that corpse was brought to the shore of the great ocean.

children.text: yato 'nantaraṃ samudravelayotsārya sthale prakṣiptam ||
children.translated_text: Immediately afterward, it was driven up by the ocean tide and cast onto dry land.

children.text: taccānekaiḥ kākagṛdhraśvaśṛgālaśvāpadādyaiḥ pakṣibhistatsamucchritaiśca kṛmibhirbhakṣyamāṇamasthikaraṅkajīrṇamāṃsaṃ śvetaṃ śvetaṃ vyavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: And that body, being eaten by many crows, vultures, dogs, jackals, beasts of prey and the like, by birds, and by worms that had swarmed over it, remained as a frame of bones with decayed flesh, whitish all over.

children.text: asyāṃ ca śrāvastyāṃ tasya brāhmaṇasya yadā patnī antarvartinī saṃvṛttā tadeva tasyā garbhotpādādatīva kṣudduḥkhena pīḍyamānayā gṛhasvāmyabhihita āryaputra kṣudduḥkhenātīva bādhye ||
children.translated_text: And in this <s>Śrāvastī</s>, when that brahmin's wife became pregnant, from the very arising of the embryo she was afflicted by extreme suffering from hunger, and she said to the master of the house, "Noble son, I am terribly oppressed by the pain of hunger."

children.text: tasyā evaṃ vadantyā gṛhasvāminoktaṃ bhadre yadasmadgṛhe 'nnapānaṃ tatsarvamabhyavaharasva ||
children.translated_text: When she spoke in this way, the master of the house said, "Good lady, whatever food and drink there is in our house, eat all of it."

children.text: tayā abhyavahartumārabdham ||
children.translated_text: She began to eat it.

children.text: sā ca tadannapānaṃ sarvamabhyavahṛtya naiva tṛptimupayāti ||
children.translated_text: But after eating all that food and drink, she still did not become satisfied.

children.text: punarapi gṛhasvāminaṃ vijñāpayati āryaputra naiva tṛptimupagacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: Again she informed the master of the house, "Noble son, I still do not become satisfied."

children.text: yatastena tiraḥprātiveśyasuhṛtsvajanādibhyo 'ntikādannapānamanviṣya tasyā anupradattam ||
children.translated_text: Then he searched out food and drink from neighbors, friends, kinsmen, and others, and gave it to her.

children.text: sā tamapyavahṛtya naiva tṛptiṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: She ate that too, but still did not reach satisfaction.
