children.text: bhūyo gṛhasvāminaḥ kathayaty āryaputra naiva tṛptimupagacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: Again she said to the master of the house, "Noble son, I still do not become satisfied."

children.text: yato 'sau brāhmaṇaḥ saṃvignamanāḥ khedamāpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that brahmin became alarmed in mind and fell into distress.

children.text: kimetadbhavantaḥ syād asyāḥ sattvamudare utpannam yasyotpādānnaiva tṛptimupayāti yataḥ sa brāhmaṇo naimittakānāṃ darśayitvā saṃśayanirṇayanārthaṃ vaidyādīn bhūtatantravidaśca paśyantu bhavanta iyaṃ brāhmaṇī kiṃ mahatā rogeṇābhibhūtā syādatha bhūtagrahāviṣṭā syādanyadvā syādrūpaṃ maraṇaliṅgamanenopakrameṇa pratyupasthitā syāt ||
children.translated_text: "What can this be, sirs? Has a being arisen in her womb, through whose arising she does not become satisfied?" Therefore that brahmin, after showing her to prognosticators in order to settle his doubt, said to physicians and those skilled in spirit lore, "Let the gentlemen examine whether this brahmin woman is overcome by a grave disease, or is possessed by a spirit, or whether some other condition, a sign of death, has appeared through this affliction."

children.text: taiḥ śrutvā tathāvidha upakramaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they heard this, they undertook such an examination.

children.text: tasyā brāhmaṇyāste indriyāṇāmanyathātvamupalakṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: They examined that brahmin woman's faculties for any alteration.

children.text: yadā asyā indriyāṇāmanyathātvaṃ nopalakṣayanti tadā tairvaidyanaimittakabhūtatantravidbhiścikitsakaiḥ sā brāhmaṇī paryanuyuktā kasmāt kālādārabhya tavaivaṃvidhā dīptāgnitā samutpannā tayābhihitaṃ garbhalambhasamakālameva sa evaṃvidha upakramaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they perceived no alteration in her faculties, the physicians, prognosticators, healers, and those skilled in spirit lore questioned that brahmin woman: "Beginning from what time did this kind of blazing digestive fire arise in you?" She replied, "From the very time of conception this kind of condition began."

children.text: yato naimittakavaidyacikitsakairabhihitaṃ nāsyāḥ kaścidanyastadrūpo rogo nāpi bhūtagrahāveśo bādhākara utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the prognosticators, physicians, and healers said, "No other disease of that kind has arisen in her, nor any afflicting possession by a spirit.

children.text: asyaivaiṣā garbhasyānubhāvenaivaṃvidhā dīptāgnitā ||
children.translated_text: This kind of blazing digestive fire is due simply to the power of this fetus."

children.text: yato 'sau brāhmaṇa upalabdhavṛttāntaḥ svasthībhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that brahmin, having learned the matter, became reassured.

children.text: sāpi brāhmaṇī naiva kadācidannapānasya tṛptā ||
children.translated_text: But that brahmin woman was never satisfied with food and drink at any time.

children.text: anupūrveṇa samakālameva putro jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due course, at the proper time, a son was born.

children.text: tasya dārakasya jātamātrasya sā brāhmaṇī vinītakṣudduḥkhā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: As soon as that boy was born, the brahmin woman became free from the suffering of hunger.

children.text: sa dārako jātamātra eva atyarthaṃ bubhukṣayopapīḍyate ||
children.translated_text: But the boy, immediately upon birth, was tormented by intense hunger.

children.text: tasya bubhukṣayā pīḍyamānasya mātā stanaṃ dātuṃ pravṛttā ||
children.translated_text: While he was being afflicted by hunger, his mother began to give him the breast.

children.text: sa ca dārakaḥ stanaṃ pītvāpi sarvaṃ naiva tṛptimupayāti ||
children.translated_text: Even after drinking all the milk from the breast, that boy still did not become satisfied.

children.text: paścāt tena brāhmaṇena tayā ca brāhmaṇyā tiraskṛtaprātiveśyasvajanayuvatyaścābhyarthya stanaṃ tasya dārakasya dāpayituṃ pravṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, that brahmin and the brahmin woman entreated women from neighboring households, female relatives, and young women, and had them begin giving the breast to that boy.

children.text: sa ca dārakaḥ sarvāsāmapi stanaṃ pītvā naiva tṛptimabhyupagacchate ||
children.translated_text: But that boy, even after drinking from the breasts of all of them, still did not attain satisfaction.

children.text: paścāt tena brāhmaṇena tasyārthe chagalikā krītā ||
children.translated_text: Afterward that brahmin bought a she-goat for his sake.

children.text: sa dārakastasyā api chagalikāyāḥ kṣīraṃ pītvā janikāyāśca stanaṃ naiva tṛpyate ||
children.translated_text: Yet the boy was not satisfied even after drinking the milk of that she-goat and his mother's breast.

children.text: tatra kālena kālaṃ bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyaśca piṇḍapātaṃ praviśya parikathāṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: There, from time to time, monks and nuns entered for alms and engaged in conversation.

children.text: sa dārakastāṃ parikathāṃ śrutvā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ na roditi avahitaśrotrastūṣṇībhūtvā tāṃ dharmaśravaṇakathāṃ śṛṇoti ||
children.translated_text: When the boy heard that conversation, at that moment he did not cry; with attentive ears, he became silent and listened to that talk on hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: pratyavasṛteṣu bhikṣubhikṣuṇīṣu ca punaḥ pipāsāduḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedayamāno rodituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when the monks and nuns had withdrawn, he again experienced the suffering of thirst and began to cry.

children.text: taiḥ saṃlakṣitam dharme vatsāya ruciriti ||
children.translated_text: They observed, "The dear child has a taste for the <s>Dharma</s>."

children.text: tasya dharmarucīti nāma pratiṣṭhāpitam ||
children.translated_text: They established his name as <s>Dharmaruci</s>, "Delighting in the Dharma."

children.text: sa ca dārako 'nupūrveṇa māsārdhamāsādīnām atyayādbhuñjāno naiva kadācidannapānasya tṛpyati ||
children.translated_text: And that boy, in due course, as months and half-months passed, went on eating but was never at any time satisfied with food and drink.

children.text: yadā ca viśiṣṭe vayasi sthitaḥ tadā tasya mātāpitṛbhyāṃ bhaikṣabhājanaṃ dattam ||
children.translated_text: When he had reached a more advanced age, his mother and father gave him a begging bowl.

children.text: gaccha vatsa idaṃ te bhaikṣabhājanam ||
children.translated_text: "Go, child; this is your begging bowl.

children.text: gṛhītvā śrāvastyāṃ bhikṣāṃ paryaṭitvā āhārakṛtyaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: Take it, wander for alms in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and do what is needed for food."

children.text: yataḥ sa dārako bhaikṣabhājanaṃ gṛhītvā śrāvastyāṃ bhaikṣaṃ paryaṭati ||
children.translated_text: Then that boy took the begging bowl and wandered for alms in <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: paryaṭanneva ca bhuktvā bhuktvā atṛpyamāna eva gṛhamāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: As he wandered, eating and eating, still unsatisfied, he returned home.

children.text: yato 'sau saṃlakṣayati kiṃ mayā karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena na kadācit vitṛpyamāna āhāramārāgayāmi sa viṣaṇṇacetāścintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ kiṃ tāvadagnipraveśaṃ karomi uta jalapraveśam atha taṭaprapātaṃ karomi sa evaṃ cintayā sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he reflected, "What karma have I done, through the ripening of which I consume food without ever being satisfied?" With dejected mind he began to think, "Shall I enter fire, or shall I enter water, or shall I throw myself from a cliff?" He remained in this thought.

children.text: upāsakenopalakṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was noticed by an <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee).

children.text: tasya tenoktaṃ kiṃ cintāpara evaṃ tiṣṭhasi gaccha tvam mahāntaṃ buddhaśāsanaṃ maharddhikaṃ mahānubhāvam ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Why do you stand here so absorbed in thought? Go into the great, powerful, mighty dispensation of the Buddha.

children.text: tatra pravraja ||
children.translated_text: Go forth there.

children.text: tatra ca tvaṃ pravrajitaḥ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃcayaṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: And when you have gone forth there, you will make an accumulation of wholesome dharmas.

children.text: akuśalāśca te dharmā ye 'sminnapi janmani saṃcitā bhaviṣyanti te tanvībhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: And the unwholesome dharmas of yours that will have been accumulated even in this birth will become slight.

children.text: yadi tāvadguṇagaṇānadhigamiṣyasi paryantīkṛtaste saṃsāro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: If indeed you attain a multitude of virtues, your <s>saṃsāra</s> will have been brought to an end."

children.text: atha sa mahātmā upāsakena codito jetavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that great-souled man, urged on by the lay devotee, went to <s>Jetavana</s>.

children.text: jetavanaṃ gatvā tatra bhikṣūn pāṭhasvādhyāyamanasikārodyuktān dṛṣṭvā atīva prasādajātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to <s>Jetavana</s>, he saw the monks there engaged in recitation, study, and attention, and an exceedingly strong faith arose in him.

children.text: bhikṣumupasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadaty arya pravrajitumicchāmi ||
children.translated_text: He approached a monk and said, "Noble one, I wish to go forth."

children.text: yato bhikṣubhirukto mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñāto 'si sa kathayati nāhaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the monks asked, "Have you been permitted by your mother and father?" he said, "I have not been permitted by my mother and father."

children.text: tairukto gaccha vatsa mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñāṃ mārgasva ||
children.translated_text: They said to him, "Go, child, and seek permission from your mother and father."

children.text: yataḥ sa mātāpitṛbhyāṃ sakāśādanujñāṃ mārgituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he set about seeking permission from his mother and father.

children.text: sa mātāpitṛbhyāmabhihito gaccha vatsa yathābhipretaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: He was told by his mother and father, "Go, child; do as you wish."

children.text: sa labdhānujño bhikṣusakāśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained permission, he went to the monk.

children.text: paścādbhikṣuṇā pravrājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that he was caused to go forth by the monk.

children.text: tatra ca bhikṣūṇāṃ kadācit piṇḍapāto bhavati kadācit nimantraṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Among those monks, sometimes there was <s>piṇḍapāta</s> (alms-food), and sometimes there was an invitation to a meal.

children.text: sa ca yasmin divase piṇḍapāto bhavati tatropādhyāyenocyate vatsa kiṃ tṛpto 'si uta na sa upādhyāyasya kathayati nāsti tṛptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: On a day when there was <s>piṇḍapāta</s>, his preceptor would say to him, "Child, are you satisfied or not?" He would say to his preceptor, "There is no satisfaction."

children.text: yata upādhyāyenāsya saṃlakṣitas taruṇavayasā pravrajito dīptāgnitayā na tṛptimupayāti ||
children.translated_text: Then his preceptor observed of him, "He has gone forth while young, and because his digestive fire is blazing, he does not become satisfied."

children.text: sa ātmīyādapi piṇḍapātāt tasya saṃvibhāgaṃ prārabdhaḥ kartum ||
children.translated_text: He began to share even from his own <s>piṇḍapāta</s> with him.

children.text: punaśca pṛcchati vatsa kimidānīṃ tṛpto 'si atha sa tamupādhyāyaṃ vadati na tṛpto 'smi ||
children.translated_text: Again he asked, "Child, are you satisfied now?" Then he said to that preceptor, "I am not satisfied."

children.text: yata upādhyāyastaṃ śrutvā sapremān bhikṣūnanyāṃśca sārdhavihāriṇaḥ prārabdho vaktum ||
children.translated_text: When the preceptor heard that, out of affection he began to speak to the monks and to the other fellow residents.

children.text: yataḥ samānopādhyāyaiḥ samānācāryairanyaiśca sapremakairbhikṣubhirupasaṃhāra ārabdhaḥ kartum ||
children.translated_text: Then those who had the same preceptor, those who had the same teacher, and other affectionate monks began to bring him extra portions.

children.text: teṣāmantikāllabhamāno naiva tṛptimupayāti ||
children.translated_text: Even while receiving food from them, he still did not become satisfied.

children.text: yadā ca nimantraṇaṃ bhavati tadāpi te tathaiva tasyopasaṃhāraṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: And when there was an invitation to a meal, they likewise brought him extra portions there too.

children.text: dānapatirapi viditvā yadyadadhikaṃ tattadasmai dattvāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: The donor, too, having learned of this, would give him whatever was extra and then depart.

children.text: atha pānakaṃ bhavati tadapi tathaiva yadadhikaṃ bhavati tattasyānupradīyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, when there was a drink, whatever was extra of that also was given over to him in the same way.

children.text: tasya ca yataḥ pravrajitasya na kadācidannapānena kukṣiḥ pūrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the time he had gone forth, his belly was never once filled with food and drink.

children.text: tena khalu samayena anyatamena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgha upanimantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time a certain householder had invited the community of monks headed by the Buddha.

children.text: bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamantargṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya ||
children.translated_text: In the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered the house together with the community of monks.

children.text: dharmarucirvihāre upadhivāriko vyavasthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmaruci</s> was appointed in the monastery as the <s>upadhivārika</s> (monastery attendant).

children.text: tatra ca śrāvastyāmanyatamo gṛhapatiḥ prativasati ||
children.translated_text: Now a certain householder was living there in <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: tena caivamupalabdhaṃ yo 'saṃviditameva buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayati sa sahasaiva bhogairabhyudgacchati ||
children.translated_text: He had learned this: "Whoever feeds the community of monks headed by the Buddha without prior arrangement immediately rises in wealth."

children.text: yatastena pañcamātrāṇāṃ bhikṣuśatānāmāhāraḥ samudānītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he prepared food for about five hundred monks.

children.text: sa tasyāhārasya śakaṭaṃ pūrayitvā praṇītapraṇītasya śucinaḥ sārdhaṃ sarvarūpairmitrasvajanasahāyo buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmīti vihāraṃ nirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having filled a cart with that food, very excellent and pure, and accompanied by friends, kinsmen, and helpers of every kind, he set out for the monastery, saying, "I will feed the community of monks headed by the Buddha."

children.text: sa paśyati tasmiñ jetavane bhikṣava eva na santi ||
children.translated_text: He saw that there were no monks at all in that <s>Jetavana</s>.

children.text: tena tatrānvāhiṇḍatā upadhivāriko dharmarucirdṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he wandered about there, he saw <s>Dharmaruci</s>, the <s>upadhivārika</s>.

children.text: tasya tena gṛhapatinoktam ārya kva gatā bhikṣavaḥ sa kathayaty antargṛhe upanimantritāḥ praviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: That householder said to him, "Noble one, where have the monks gone?" He said, "They have entered the house, having been invited there."

children.text: sa gṛhapatistacchrutvā durmanā vyavasthitaḥ kaṣṭam evamasmākaṃ viphalaḥ pariśramo jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the householder stood downcast: "Alas, our effort has become fruitless."

children.text: saṃcintya ca tasya dharmaruceḥ kathayaty ārya bhakṣa tvamapi tāvat ||
children.translated_text: After reflecting, he said to <s>Dharmaruci</s>, "Noble one, you at least should eat."

children.text: sa kathayati yadi te mahātman parityaktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Great-souled one, if it has been relinquished by you."

children.text: tatastena gṛhapatinā saṃlakṣayitvā yenāhāreṇaikasya bhikṣoḥ paryāptaṃ bhavati tāvadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ gṛhītvā taṃ dharmaruciṃ pariveṣayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder considered the matter, took from the cart as much food and drink as would be enough for one monk, and began to serve <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

children.text: tena dharmarucinā bhoktumārabdhaṃ tanniravaśiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmaruci</s> began to eat, and all of that was finished without remainder.

children.text: naiva tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Still he was not satisfied.

children.text: gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati nāyaṃ tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder observed, "He is not satisfied."

children.text: tenocyata ārya punarbhokṣyase sa kathayati mahātman yadi te parityaktam ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Noble one, will you eat again?" He said, "Great-souled one, if it has been relinquished by you."

children.text: tatastena gṛhapatinā bhūyastasmāt śakaṭādyena bhikṣudvayasyāhāreṇa paryāptaṃ syāt tāvadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ gṛhītvā bhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder again took from that cart as much food and drink as would be enough for two monks and began to feed him.

children.text: yato dharmarucistadapi bhuktvā naiva tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But after <s>Dharmaruci</s> had eaten that too, he was still not satisfied.

children.text: gṛhapatinā bhūyaḥ saṃlakṣitaṃ nāyaṃ tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder again observed, "He is not satisfied."

children.text: tenoktam ārya punarbhokṣyase sa kathayati mahātman yadi te parityaktam ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Noble one, will you eat again?" He said, "Great-souled one, if it has been relinquished by you."

children.text: yatastasmācchakaṭādannapānaṃ gṛhītvā trayāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ paryāptaṃ syāditi punarbhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, taking food and drink from that cart, enough for three monks, he again began to feed him.

children.text: sa dharmarucistadapi bhuktvā naiva tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Dharmaruci</s>, even after eating that too, was still not satisfied.

children.text: pṛṣṭa ārya punarbhokṣyase sa kathayati yadi te parityaktam ||
children.translated_text: Asked, "Noble one, will you eat again?" he said, "If you have given it up."

children.text: yataḥ sa gṛhapatistasmādannapānaṃ gṛhītvā yena caturṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ paryāptaṃ syāditi punarbhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that householder, taking from it enough food and drink for four monks, again began to feed him.

children.text: sa dharmarucistadapi bhuktvā naiva tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Dharmaruci</s>, even after eating that too, was still not satisfied.

children.text: pṛṣṭa ārya punarbhokṣyase bhūyaḥ sa kathayati yadi te parityaktam ||
children.translated_text: Asked, "Noble one, will you eat still more?" he said, "If you have given it up."

children.text: yataḥ punastasmācchakaṭādyena pañcabhikṣūṇāmannapānaistṛptiḥ syāt tāvadgṛhītvā punarbhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again, from that cart, he took as much food and drink as would satisfy five monks and began again to feed him.

children.text: tadapi cābhyavahṛtam ||
children.translated_text: That too was consumed.

children.text: naiva tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Still he was not satisfied.

children.text: vistareṇa yāvaddaśānāṃ bhikṣūṇāmannapānena paryāptaṃ syāt tāvad bhuktvā naiva tṛpyate ||
children.translated_text: In detail, up to the point that he had eaten as much food and drink as would be enough for ten monks, he still was not satisfied.

children.text: yatastena saṃlakṣitaṃ nāyaṃ manuṣyo manuṣyavikāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the man perceived, "This is not a human being; it is a transformation of a nonhuman being."

children.text: yataḥ śrūyate pañcabhir nīlavāsaso yakṣaśatairjetavanamaśūnyamiti teṣāṃ bhaviṣyatyeva anyatamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For it is heard that <s>Jetavana</s> is not empty of five hundred yakṣas wearing blue garments; he must be one of them.

children.text: iti saṃcintya garbharūpāṇi gṛhe 'nupraveśayituṃ pravṛtto gacchatha yūyaṃ śīghraṃ gṛhameva ahamevaiko yadi jīvāmi mriye veti ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, he began to send the pregnant women and the rest into the house, saying, "Go quickly, all of you, straight home. I alone will see whether I live or die."

children.text: sa gṛhajanaṃ visarjya maraṇabhayabhītastasmāt śakaṭādannapānaṃ gṛhītvā pariveṣayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having dismissed the people of his household, and terrified by fear of death, he took food and drink from that cart and began to serve it.

children.text: sa ca svairaṃ bhuñjati ||
children.translated_text: And he ate at leisure.

children.text: gṛhapatinā uktam ārya tvaritatvaritaṃ pratīcchasva ||
children.translated_text: The householder said, "Noble one, receive it quickly, quickly."

children.text: yatastena dharmarucinā kṣipraṃ pratigṛhītvā bhoktumārabdham ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaruci</s>, having received it quickly, began to eat.

children.text: sa gṛhapatistvaritatvaritaṃ pariveṣayitvā niravaśeṣatastadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ dattvā dakṣiṇādeśanāmapi bhayagṛhīto 'śrutvā tvaritatvaritaṃ vandāmyāryeti pṛṣṭhamanavalokayamāno nagaraṃ prasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder, serving it very quickly, gave the entire cart of food and drink without remainder and, seized by fear, without even hearing the thanksgiving discourse, said hurriedly, "I bow, noble one," and set out for the city without looking back.

children.text: tasmānnagarāt piṇḍapātanirhārako bhikṣus tasyaiva piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: A monk who carried away alms from that city took that very alms-food to him.

children.text: tena tadapi bhuktam ||
children.translated_text: He ate that too.

children.text: tasya dharmarucer na kadācidyato jātasya kukṣiḥ pūrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the time <s>Dharmaruci</s> had been born, his belly had never once been filled.

children.text: taddivasaṃ cāsya tenāhāreṇa tṛptirjātā ||
children.translated_text: But on that day, through that food, satisfaction arose in him.

children.text: tasya ca gṛhapater nagaraṃ praviśato 'bhimukhaṃ bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtaḥ samprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As that householder was entering the city, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the community of monks, came toward him.

children.text: sa gṛhapatirbhagavataḥ kathayati bhagavan ahaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamuddiśya pañcānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāṃ tṛptitaḥ śakaṭamannapānasya pūrayitvā jetavanaṃ gato buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: The householder said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, "Bhagavān, I filled a cart with food and drink sufficient to satisfy five hundred monks, intending it for the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, and went to <s>Jetavana</s>, thinking, 'I shall feed the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.'

children.text: na ca me tatra bhikṣavo labdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But I did not find the monks there.

children.text: eko me bhikṣurdṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I saw one monk.

children.text: tena samākhyātaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamantargṛham upanimantraṇaṃ praviṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: He told me that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> had entered an invitation inside a house.

children.text: tasya mamaivaṃ cittamutpannam eṣo 'pi tāvadeko bhuṅktāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in me: 'Let this one at least eat.'

children.text: yatastasya mamānupūrveṇa sarvaṃ tadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ dattam ||
children.translated_text: So, little by little, I gave him that whole cart of food and drink.

children.text: tena sarvaṃ nipuṇato 'bhyavahṛtam ||
children.translated_text: He consumed it all completely.

children.text: kiṃ bhagavan manuṣyo 'thavāmanuṣyo bhagavatābhihitaṃ gṛhapate bhikṣuḥ sa dharmarucir nāmnā ||
children.translated_text: Bhagavān, is he a human being or a nonhuman being?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said, "Householder, he is a monk named <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

children.text: prāmodyamutpādaya adya sa tvadīyenānnapānena tṛpto 'rhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Give rise to joy. Today, satisfied by your food and drink, he will realize arhatship."

children.text: atha bhagavāñ jetavanamabhyāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> came to <s>Jetavana</s>.

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati ko 'sau dānapatirbhaviṣyati yo 'sau dharmaruceretāvatā āhāreṇa pratidivasam yogodvahanaṃ kariṣyati yato 'sya bhagavatā abhihitaṃ dṛṣṭastvayā dharmaruce mahāsamudraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> considered, "Who will be the donor who, every day, will undertake the burden of providing <s>Dharmaruci</s> with such a quantity of food?" Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to him, "Have you seen the great ocean, <s>Dharmaruci</s>?"

children.text: sa kathayati no bhagavan ||
children.translated_text: He said, "No, Bhagavān."

children.text: yato bhagavānāha gṛhāṇa madīyaṃ cīvarakarṇikam paścāt te 'haṃ mahāsamudraṃ darśayāmi ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said, "Take hold of the corner of my robe; afterwards I shall show you the great ocean."

children.text: yato dharmarucinā bhagavataścīvarakarṇiko 'valambitaḥ paścādbhagavān vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājaḥ sahacittotpādāt ṛddhyā dharmaruciṃ gṛhītvā samudrataṭamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> grasped the corner of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s robe, and afterwards the <s>Bhagavān</s>, like a king of geese with wings spread, at the arising of that thought, took <s>Dharmaruci</s> by miraculous power and reached the ocean shore.

children.text: yasmiṃścāsya sthāne timitimiṃgilabhūtasyāsthiśakalā tiṣṭhati tatra nītvā sthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He brought him to the place where the fragment of bone from when he had been a <s>timiṃgila</s> was standing, and set him down there.

children.text: uktaṃ cāsya gaccha vatsa manasikāraṃ cintaya ||
children.translated_text: And he said to him, "Go, child, and apply your mind in contemplation."

children.text: yato 'sau dharmarucistāṃ samīkṣitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> began to examine it.

children.text: kimetat kāṣṭhaṃ syādathāsthiśakalā atha phalakinī syāt ||
children.translated_text: "What is this? Could it be wood, or a piece of bone, or perhaps a plank?"

children.text: sa tasmād vyaktimalabhamānaḥ paryantamanveṣituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since he could not determine it, he began to search for its end.

children.text: vyaktiṃ copalabdham ||
children.translated_text: And he did gain some ascertainment.

children.text: sa itaścāmutaśca tasyā anupārśvena tāṃ paryeṣamāṇaḥ śramamupagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Searching for it on this side and that, along its flanks, he became weary.

children.text: na cāsya paryantamāsādayati ||
children.translated_text: But he did not reach its end.

children.text: tasyaitadabhavan nāhamasya vyaktiṃ jñāsyāmi kimetaditi na ca paryantamāsādayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "I shall not understand the nature of this, what it is, nor shall I reach its end.

children.text: gacchāmi asminnarthe bhagavantameva pṛcchāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall go and ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself about this matter."

children.text: yato 'sau bhagavato 'ntikaṃ gatvā bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati kiṃ tadbhagavan nāhaṃ tasya vyaktimupalabhāmi ||
children.translated_text: Then he went to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence and asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>, "What was that, Bhagavān? I cannot discern its nature."

children.text: yato 'sya bhagavānāha vatsa asthiśakalaiṣā ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to him, "Child, this is a fragment of bone."

children.text: sa kathayati bhagavan evaṃvidho 'sau sattvo yasyedṛśī asthiśakalā bhagavatoktaṃ tṛpyasva dharmaruce bhavebhyaḥ tṛpyasva bhavopakaraṇebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Blessed One, was that being of such a kind that a bone fragment like this belonged to him?" The Blessed One said, "Be satisfied, <s>Dharmaruci</s>, with states of existence; be satisfied with the supports of existence.

children.text: tavaiṣā asthiśakalā ||
children.translated_text: This bone fragment is yours.

children.text: dharmarucistaṃ śrutvā bhagavadvaco vyākulitacetāḥ kathayati mamaiṣedṛśī asthiśakalā tasyoktam eṣā dharmaruce tavāsthiśakalā ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Dharmaruci</s> heard that word of the Blessed One, his mind was disturbed, and he said, "Is such a bone fragment mine?" He was told, "This, <s>Dharmaruci</s>, is your bone fragment."

children.text: tathāvidhamupaśrutya atīva saṃvignaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing such a thing, he became extremely shaken.

children.text: yato 'sya bhagavatā avavādo datto dharmaruce idaṃ cedaṃ manasi kuru ||
children.translated_text: Then an instruction was given to him by the Blessed One: "<s>Dharmaruci</s>, bring this and that to mind."

children.text: ityuktvā bhagavān vitatapakṣa iva rājahaṃsa ṛddhyā jetavanamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, the Blessed One, like a royal swan with wings outspread, arrived at <s>Jetavana</s> by supernatural power.

children.text: atha dharmarucinā cintayatā manasikāramanutiṣṭhatā uṣmagatānyutpāditāni mūrdhānaḥ kṣāntayo laukikā agradharmā darśanamārgo bhāvanāmārgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Dharmaruci</s> reflected and practiced attentive contemplation, the stages of heat, summits, acceptances, the supreme worldly dharmas, the path of seeing, and the path of cultivation arose in him.

children.text: srotāpattiphalaṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: He attained the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: sakṛdāgāmiphalam anāgāmiphalamarhattvaṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: He attained the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship.

children.text: arhan saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto 'nunayapratighaprahīṇo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukho vāsīcandanakalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became an arhat, free from passion for the three realms, regarding a clod and gold alike, with a mind equal toward the sky and the palm of his hand, having abandoned attachment and aversion, having split the eggshell by knowledge, having attained knowledge, superknowledges, and analytic insights, turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor, and comparable to sandalwood before an axe.

children.text: sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became worthy of worship, honor, and reverence by the gods together with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: samanvāhartumātmanaḥ pūrvajātiṃ pravṛttaḥ kuto hyahaṃ cyutaḥ kutropapanna iti ||
children.translated_text: He began to contemplate his own former births, thinking, "From where have I fallen, and where have I been reborn?"

children.text: yataḥ paśyati anekāni jātiśatāni narakatiryakpretacyutaścopapannaśca ||
children.translated_text: Then he saw many hundreds of births, dying and being reborn among hell-beings, animals, and ghosts.

children.text: tasyaitadabhavad yadahaṃ bhagavatā na samanvāhṛto 'bhaviṣyam anāgatāsvapi jātiṣu upasṛto 'bhaviṣyam ||
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "If I had not been attended to by the Blessed One, I would have entered into future births as well."

children.text: yataḥ saṃlakṣayaty anāgatāpyātmano jātisaṃtatir nirantaramanuparataprabandhena narakapretopapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For he perceived that his own future succession of births too would have continued without break or interruption, with rebirth in hells and among ghosts.

children.text: sa evaṃ saṃlakṣya duṣkarakārako bata me bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: Having perceived this, he thought, "Indeed, the Blessed One has done a difficult deed for me."

children.text: yadi ca bhagavatā mamaivaikasyārthe 'nuttarā samyaksambodhiradhigatā syāt tanmahaddhi upakṛtaṃ syāt prāgevānekeṣāṃ sattvasahasrāṇāmapāyagatigamanamapanayati ||
children.translated_text: "And if the Blessed One had attained unsurpassed perfect awakening for my sake alone, that would have been a great benefit; how much more so, since he removes the passage of many thousands of beings into bad destinies."

children.text: tato 'sau dharmarucirṛddhyā jetavanamanuprāpto bhagavantaṃ darśanāya ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> arrived at <s>Jetavana</s> by supernatural power in order to see the Blessed One.

children.text: tena khalu samayena bhagavānanekaśatāyā bhikṣuparṣadaḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: At that time the Blessed One was seated before an assembly of many hundreds of monks.

children.text: dharmaṃ deśayati ||
children.translated_text: He was teaching the Dharma.

children.text: athāsau dharmaruciryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte nyaṣīdat ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed his head to the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇo bhagavatā abhihitaś cirasya dharmaruce dharmarucirāha cirasya bhagavan ||
children.translated_text: When he had sat down to one side, the Blessed One said to him, "After a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>." <s>Dharmaruci</s> said, "After a long time, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha sucirasya dharmaruce dharmarucirāha sucirasya bhagavan ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "After a very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>." <s>Dharmaruci</s> said, "After a very long time, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha suciracirasya dharmaruce dharmarucirāha suciracirasya bhagavan ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "After a very, very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>." <s>Dharmaruci</s> said, "After a very, very long time, Blessed One."

children.text: yato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti bhagavan dharmarucirihaiva śrāvastyāṃ jāto 'sminneva jetavane pravrajito na kutaścidāgato na kutracidgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the monks became doubtful and asked the Blessed Buddha, the cutter-off of all doubts, "Blessed One, <s>Dharmaruci</s> was born right here in <s>Śrāvastī</s> and went forth right here in this <s>Jetavana</s>; he has not come from anywhere, nor has he gone anywhere.

children.text: ihaiva tiṣṭhan bhagavatā dharmarucirevamucyate cirasya dharmaruce sucirasya dharmaruce suciracirasya dharmaruce ||
children.translated_text: While he remains right here, the Blessed One addresses <s>Dharmaruci</s> in this way: 'After a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; after a very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; after a very, very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>.'

children.text: kiṃ saṃdhāya bhagavān kathayaty evamukte bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma na bhikṣavaḥ pratyutpannaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi ||
children.translated_text: With reference to what does the Blessed One say this?" When this had been said, the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, I do not say this with reference to the present.

children.text: atītaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I say it with reference to the past.

children.text: atītaṃ saṃdhāya mayaivamuktam ||
children.translated_text: It was with reference to the past that I spoke in this way.

children.text: icchatha bhikṣavo 'sya dharmaruceḥ pūrvikāṃ karmaplotimārabhya dhārmikathāṃ śrotum etasya bhagavan kāla etasya sugata samayo yadbhagavān dharmarucimārabhya bhikṣūṇāṃ dhārmikathāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Do you wish, monks, to hear a Dharma discourse concerning <s>Dharmaruci</s>, beginning with the woven course of his former karma?" "Blessed One, this is the time; Sugata, this is the occasion for the Blessed One to give the monks a Dharma discourse concerning <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

children.text: bhagavataḥ śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will retain it."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani prathame 'saṃkhyeye kṣemaṃkaro nāma tathāgato loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: "Monks, in former times, in the past, in the first incalculable aeon, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One.

children.text: sa ca kṣemāvatīṃ rājadhānīmupaniśritya viharati ||
children.translated_text: He dwelt in dependence on the capital city <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca kṣemāvatyāṃ kṣemo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ||
children.translated_text: In that <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>, a king named <s>Kṣema</s> ruled the kingdom.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca kṣemāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmanyatamo vaṇikśreṣṭhī prativasati ||
children.translated_text: And in that capital city <s>Kṣemāvatī</s> there lived a certain merchant guild-master.

children.text: tenāsau kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ traimāsān sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena sarvopakaraṇairupasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That fully awakened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, together with the community of monks, was served by him with all requisites for sixty rainy-season periods of three months.

children.text: yato 'sau śreṣṭhī saṃlakṣayati gacchāmi mahāsamudram ||
children.translated_text: Then that guild-master reflected, "I shall go to the great ocean.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīya tasmācca ratnānyānīya saṃghe pañcavārṣikaṃ kariṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Having gathered merchandise, I shall bring jewels from there and hold a five-year festival for the saṅgha."

children.text: evaṃ saṃcintya bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīya grāmanigamapallīpattanarājadhānīṣvanupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇaḥ samudramanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having reflected in this way, he collected his merchandise and, wandering successively through villages, market towns, hamlets, ports, and royal capitals, reached the ocean.

children.text: ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā sāmudreṇa yānapātreṇa mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After making a proclamation by bell, he set out upon the great ocean in a seagoing vessel.

children.text: asya tasmin mahāsamudre 'vatīrṇasya kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had entered that great ocean, <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, having completed the whole work of a Buddha, passed completely into the nirvāṇa-element without remainder.

children.text: tasya parinirvṛtasya vaśino bhikṣavaḥ parinirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After he had passed into parinirvāṇa, his disciplined monks also passed into parinirvāṇa.

children.text: saptāhaparinirvṛtasya śāsanamantarhitam ||
children.translated_text: Seven days after his parinirvāṇa, the dispensation disappeared.

children.text: sa ca śreṣṭhī saṃsiddhayānapātreṇa devatāmānuṣyaparigṛhītena tasmānmahāsamudrāt tīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that merchant, in a vessel that had accomplished its voyage and was protected by gods and humans, crossed over from that great ocean.

children.text: uttīrya ca taṃ bhāṇḍaṃ śakaṭairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhaiśca cotkṣipya anupūrveṇa samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After crossing over, he loaded that merchandise onto carts, camels, oxen, and donkeys, and gradually set out.

children.text: sa ca panthānaṃ gacchan prātipathikān pṛcchati kiṃ bhavanto jānīdhvaṃ kṣemāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ pravṛttis tairuktam jānīmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he went along the road, he asked travelers coming the other way, "Sirs, do you know any news concerning the royal capital <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>?" They said, "We know."

children.text: sa kathayaty asti kaścit kṣemāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ kṣemaṃkaro nāma samyaksambuddhas te kathayanti parinirvṛtaḥ sa bhagavān kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Is there in the royal capital <s>Kṣemāvatī</s> a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>?" They said, "That Blessed One, the perfectly awakened Buddha <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, has passed into parinirvāṇa."

children.text: sa ca tacchrutvā paraṃ khedamupagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he heard that, he was overcome by extreme grief.

children.text: saṃmūrchitaśca bhūmau patitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He fainted and fell to the ground.

children.text: tasmācca jalābhiṣekeṇa pratyāgataprāṇo jīvita utthāya bhūyaḥ pṛcchati kiṃ bhavanto jānīdhvaṃ śrāvakā api tāvattasya bhagavatastiṣṭhanti tairuktas te 'pi vaśino bhikṣavaḥ parinirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when his life had returned through sprinkling with water, he rose and asked again, "Sirs, do you know whether even his disciples still remain?" They said, "Those disciplined monks too have passed into parinirvāṇa."

children.text: saptāhaparinirvṛtasya ca buddhasya bhagavataḥ kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya kṣemeṇa rājñā caityamalpeśākhyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam ||
children.translated_text: And seven days after the Blessed Buddha <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, had passed into parinirvāṇa, King <s>Kṣema</s> established a caitya of small renown.

children.text: tena ca gatvā śreṣṭhinā janapadāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that merchant went and questioned the people of the country.

children.text: asti bhavantastasya bhagavato buddhasya kiṃcit stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam ||
children.translated_text: "Sirs, has any stūpa of that Blessed Buddha been established?"

children.text: tairuktam asti kṣemeṇa rājñā alpeśākhyaṃ caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam ||
children.translated_text: They said, "There is one: King <s>Kṣema</s> has established a caitya of small renown."

children.text: tasya etadabhavad etaṃ mayā suvarṇaṃ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksambuddham uddiśyānītam ||
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "I brought this gold for the sake of <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: sa ca parinirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he has passed into parinirvāṇa.

children.text: yannvahametenaiva suvarṇena tasyaiva bhagavataścaityaṃ maheśākhyataraṃ kārayeyam ||
children.translated_text: What if, with this very gold, I were to have a much more eminent caitya made for that very Blessed One?"

children.text: evaṃ vicintya kṣemaṃ rājānaṃ vijñāpayati mahārāja idaṃ mayā suvarṇaṃ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksambuddhamuddiśyānītam ||
children.translated_text: Having reflected in this way, he petitioned King <s>Kṣema</s>: "Great king, I brought this gold for the sake of <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: sa ca bhagavān parinirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that Blessed One has passed into parinirvāṇa.

children.text: idānīṃ mahārāja yadi tvamanujānīyād ahametenaiva suvarṇenaitat tasya bhagavataścaityaṃ maheśākhyataraṃ kārayeyam ||
children.translated_text: Now, great king, if you permit it, I would have this caitya of that Blessed One made much more eminent with this very gold."

children.text: sa rājñābhihito yathābhipretaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: The king said to him, "Do as you intend."

children.text: tato brāhmaṇā nagaraṃ prati nivāsinaḥ sambhūya sarve tasya mahāśreṣṭhinaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayanti bho mahāśreṣṭhin yadā kṣemaṃkaro buddho loke 'nutpanna āsīt tadā vayaṃ lokasya dakṣiṇīyā āsan ||
children.translated_text: Then the brahmins living in the city gathered together, all went to that great merchant, and said, "Good sir, great merchant, when the Buddha <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> had not arisen in the world, we were worthy recipients of the world's offerings.

children.text: yadā tūtpannaḥ tadā dakṣiṇīyo jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when he arose, he became the worthy recipient of offerings.

children.text: idānīṃ tu tasya parinirvṛtasya vayameva dakṣiṇīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, since he has passed into parinirvāṇa, we alone are the worthy recipients of offerings.

children.text: etat suvarṇamasmākaṃ gamyam ||
children.translated_text: This gold should come to us."

children.text: sa teṣāṃ kathayati nāham yuṣmākametat suvarṇaṃ dāsyāmi ||
children.translated_text: He said to them, "I will not give you this gold."

children.text: te kathayanti yadyasmākaṃ na dāsyasi na vayaṃ tava kāmakāraṃ dāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They said, "If you will not give it to us, we will not allow you to do as you wish."

children.text: te brāhmaṇā bahavaḥ śreṣṭhī cālpaparivāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those brahmins were numerous, while the merchant had only a small retinue.

children.text: teṣāṃ tathā vyutpadyatāṃ na lebhe taccaityam yathepsitaṃ tena suvarṇena kārayitum ||
children.translated_text: Because they acted in that way, he was not able to have that caitya made with the gold as he wished.

children.text: atha sa śreṣṭhī rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati mahārāja taccaityaṃ na labhe brāhmaṇānāṃ sakāśādyathābhipretaṃ kārayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then the merchant went to the king and said, "Great king, because of the brahmins I am not able to have that caitya made as I wish."

children.text: yato 'sya rājñā svapuruṣo dattaḥ sahasrayodhī ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the king assigned him one of his own men, a warrior over a thousand soldiers.

children.text: evaṃ ca rājñā svapuruṣa ājñapto yadyasya mahāśreṣṭhinaḥ stūpamabhisaṃskurvataḥ kaścidapanayaṃ karoti sa tvayā mahatā daṇḍena śāsayitavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the king commanded his man as follows: "If anyone causes harm while this great merchant is restoring the stūpa, he is to be punished by you with a heavy penalty."

children.text: evaṃ deveti sahasrayodhī puruṣo rājñaḥ pratiśrutya nirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, lord," said the warrior over a thousand soldiers; having accepted the king's order, he departed.

children.text: nirgamya ca tān brāhmaṇānevaṃ vadati śṛṇvantu bhavanto 'haṃ rājñāsya mahāśreṣṭhinaḥ svapuruṣo datto yadyasya stūpamabhisaṃskurvataḥ kaścidvighātaṃ kuryāt sa tvayā mahatā daṇḍena śāsayitavya iti ||
children.translated_text: After departing, he said this to those brahmins: "Listen, sirs. I have been assigned by the king as this great merchant's own man, with the order: If anyone should make an obstruction while he is restoring the stūpa, he is to be punished by you with a heavy penalty.

children.text: yadi yūyamatra kiṃcid vighnaṃ kariṣyatha ahaṃ vo mahatā daṇḍenānuśāsayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: If you make any obstruction here, I will discipline you with a heavy penalty."

children.text: te brāhmaṇāḥ sahasrayodhinaḥ puruṣasyaivaṃ śrutvā bhītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When those brahmins heard this from the warrior over a thousand soldiers, they became afraid.

children.text: yatastena mahāśreṣṭhinā saṃcintya yathaitat suvarṇaṃ tatraiva garbhasaṃsthaṃ syāt tathā kartavyamiti tasya stūpasya sarvaireva caturbhiḥ pārśvaiḥ pratikaṇṭhukayā catvāri sopānāni ārabdhāni kārayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then that great merchant reflected, "It must be arranged so that this gold is enclosed there in the interior." Accordingly, on all four sides of that stūpa, four flights of steps with enclosing projections began to be constructed.

children.text: yāvadanupūrveṇa prathamā meḍhī tato 'nupūrveṇa dvitīyā tatastṛtīyā meḍhī yāvadanupūrveṇāṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: Gradually the first terrace was made, then in due order the second, then the third terrace, and finally, step by step, the dome.

children.text: tathāvidhaṃ ca stūpasyāṇḍaṃ kṛtam yatra sā yūpayaṣṭirabhyantare pratipāditā ||
children.translated_text: And a dome of the <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary mound) was made in such a form that the sacrificial post-shaft was set inside it.

children.text: paścāt tasyātinavāṇḍasyopari harmikā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, a harmikā was made on top of that very new dome.

children.text: anupūrveṇa yaṣṭyāropaṇaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Gradually the setting up of the shaft was carried out.

children.text: varṣasthāle mahāmaṇiratnāni tānyāropitāni ||
children.translated_text: Those great jewel-gems were mounted on the rain-plate.

children.text: tatra ca kriyamāṇe sahasrayodhinaḥ puruṣasyaivamutpannaṃ nātra kaścididānīṃ prahariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: While that was being done, it occurred to the man <s>Sahasrayodhī</s>, "Now no one here will strike."

children.text: viśvastamanāḥ kenacitkāryeṇa janapadeṣu gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With his mind at ease, he went to the provinces on some business.

children.text: tena ca mahāśreṣṭhinā tasya stūpasya caturbhiḥ pārśvaiścatvāro dvārakoṣṭhakā māpitāḥ caturbhiḥ pārśvaiścatvāri mahācaityāni kāritāni tadyathā jātirabhisambodhirdharmacakrapravartanaṃ parinirvāṇam ||
children.translated_text: And that great merchant had four gateway chambers built on the four sides of that <s>stūpa</s>, and on the four sides he had four great shrines made, namely: birth, perfect awakening, the turning of the wheel of dharma, and final nirvāṇa.

children.text: tacca stūpāṅgaṇaṃ ratnaśilābhiścitam ||
children.translated_text: The courtyard of that <s>stūpa</s> was paved with jeweled stones.

children.text: catvāraścopāṅgāścaturdiśaṃ māpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And four subsidiary structures were built in the four directions.

children.text: puṣkariṇyaścaturdiśamanupārśvena māpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lotus ponds were also built along the sides in the four directions.

children.text: tatra ca vividhāni jalajāni mālyāni ropitāni tadyathā utpalaṃ padmaṃ kumudaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ sugandhikaṃ mṛdugandhikam ||
children.translated_text: There various water-born garland flowers were planted, namely blue lotus, lotus, white water-lily, white lotus, sugandhika, and mṛdugandhika.

children.text: vividhāni ca puṣkariṇītīreṣu sthalajāni mālyāni ropitāni tadyathā atimuktakaṃ campakapāṭalāvārṣikāmallikāsumanāyūthikā dhātuṣkārī ||
children.translated_text: And on the banks of the lotus ponds various land-born garland flowers were planted, namely atimuktaka, campaka, pāṭalā, vārṣikā, mallikā, sumanā, yūthikā, and dhātuṣkārī.

children.text: sarvartukālikāḥ puṣpaphalāḥ stūpapūjārtham ||
children.translated_text: There were flowers and fruits for every season, for the purpose of worshiping the <s>stūpa</s>.

children.text: sthāvarāvṛttiprajñaptāḥ stūpadāsā dattāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fixed revenues were assigned, and servants for the <s>stūpa</s> were given.

children.text: śaṅkhapaṭahavādyāni tūryāṇi dattāni ||
children.translated_text: Conches, drums, musical instruments, and trumpets were given.

children.text: ye tasmiṃścaitye gandhairdhūpairmālyaiśca cūrṇaiḥ kārāḥ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Those who performed acts of worship at that shrine did so with perfumes, incense, garlands, and powders.

children.text: tasmāccādhiṣṭhānādviṣayāccāgamya janapadā gandhairmālyairdhūpaiścūrṇaistasmiṃścaitye kāraṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: And people from that settlement, district, and the provinces came with perfumes, garlands, incense, and powders, and performed worship at that shrine.

children.text: yadi ca dakṣiṇo vāyurvāti dakṣiṇena vāyunā sarvapuṣpajātīnāṃ gandhena taccaityamaṅgaṇaṃ cāsya sphuṭaṃ bhavatyanubhāvitam ||
children.translated_text: If a southern wind blew, then by that southern wind the courtyard of the shrine was filled and suffused with the fragrance of every kind of flower.

children.text: evaṃ paścimena vāyunā anupūrveṇāpi ca vāyunā ||
children.translated_text: So too it was with a western wind, and in sequence with every other wind as well.

children.text: vāyatā vāyatā taccaityāṅgaṇaṃ ca tena vividhena gandhamālyena sphuṭaṃ bhavatyanubhāvitam ||
children.translated_text: As each wind blew, the courtyard of that shrine became filled and suffused with that varied fragrance of flowers and garlands.

children.text: tasmiṃśca stūpe sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭhite sahasrayodhī abhyāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that <s>stūpa</s> had been completely finished in every respect, <s>Sahasrayodhī</s> returned.

children.text: sa taṃ stūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭhitaṃ kathayaty asmiṃścaitye kārāṃ kṛtvā kimavāpyate yato 'sau śreṣṭhī buddhodāharaṇaṃ pravṛttaḥ kartum evaṃ tribhirasaṃkhyeyairvīryeṇa vyāyamatānuttarā bodhiravāpyate ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that <s>stūpa</s> completely finished in every respect, he said, "What is obtained by performing worship at this shrine?" Then the merchant began to present the example of a Buddha: "In this way, by exerting energy for three asaṃkhyeyas, unsurpassed awakening is obtained."

children.text: sa taṃ śrutvā viṣādamāpanno hīnotsāhatayā kathayati nāhaṃ śakṣyāmi anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ samudānayitum ||
children.translated_text: When he heard that, he became despondent and, with diminished resolve, said, "I will not be able to bring forth unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: tato 'sau śreṣṭhī pratyekabuddhodāharaṇaṃ pravṛttaḥ kartum evaṃ sahasrayodhī tasyāpi varṇodāharaṇaṃ śrutvā viṣaṇṇacetāḥ kathayaty etāmapyahaṃ pratyekabodhiṃ na śaktaḥ samudānayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then that merchant began to present the example of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha). Hearing the description of that too, <s>Sahasrayodhī</s>, dejected in mind, said, "I am not able to bring forth even this solitary awakening."

children.text: tataḥ sa mahāśreṣṭhī śrāvakavarṇodāharaṇaṃ kṛtvā kathayaty asminnapi tāvat praṇidhatsva cittam ||
children.translated_text: Then that great merchant, having presented the description of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), said, "At least set your mind upon this."

children.text: yataḥ sahasrayodhyāha tvayā punarmahāśreṣṭhin katamasyāṃ bodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tena mahāśreṣṭhinoktam anuttarasyāṃ bodhau cittamutpāditam ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sahasrayodhī</s> said, "But you, great merchant, toward which awakening have you made your vow?" The great merchant said, "I have produced the mind directed toward unsurpassed awakening."

children.text: sahasrayodhyāha yadi tvayā anuttarasyāṃ bodhau cittamutpāditam ahaṃ tavaiva śrāvakaḥ syām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sahasrayodhī</s> said, "If you have produced the mind directed toward unsurpassed awakening, then I shall be your own disciple."

children.text: tvayāhaṃ samanvāhartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You must keep me in mind.

children.text: yato 'sya śreṣṭhī āha bahukilbiṣakārī bata bhavān ||
children.translated_text: At this the merchant said to him, "You, sir, are indeed a maker of much wrongdoing."

children.text: kiṃtu loke yadā tvaṃ buddhotpādaśabdaṃ śrutvā smṛtiṃ pratilabhethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, when in the world you hear the sound of the arising of a Buddha, may you regain mindfulness.

children.text: sa ca śreṣṭhī taṃ caityaṃ kṛtvā nirīkṣya pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: And that merchant, having built and inspected that shrine, fell at its feet and made an aspiration.

children.text: anena dānena mahadgatena buddho bhaveyaṃ sugataḥ svayambhūḥ
children.translated_text: By this great gift may I become a Buddha, a <s>Sugata</s> (well-gone one), self-arisen;

children.text: tīrṇo 'haṃ tārayeyaṃ janaughān atāritā ye paurvakairjinendraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: having crossed over myself, may I carry across the floods of people whom the former lords of conquerors have not carried across.

children.text: bhagavānāha yo 'sau atīte 'dhvani śreṣṭhī abhūt ahameva sa tasmin samaye bodhisattvacaryāṃ vartāmi ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "The merchant who existed in the past was none other than I; at that time I was engaged in the bodhisattva conduct."

children.text: yo 'sau sahasrayodhī eṣa eva dharmarucistena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: The one who was <s>Sahasrayodhī</s> at that time and on that occasion is this very <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

children.text: idaṃ mama prathame 'saṃkhyeye etasya dharmarucerdarśanam ||
children.translated_text: This was my first encounter with this <s>Dharmaruci</s> in the first asaṃkhyeya.

children.text: tatsaṃdhāya kathayāmi cirasya dharmaruce ||
children.translated_text: With reference to that I say, "It has been a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>."

children.text: yato dharmarucir ājñāyāha cirasya bhagavan ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaruci</s>, understanding, said, "It has indeed been a long time, Blessed One."

children.text: dvitīye dīpaṃkaro nāma samyaksambuddho loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasamyaksambuddhaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: In the second, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One.

children.text: atha dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddho janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran dīpāvatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, while wandering on tour through the provinces, arrived at the capital <s>Dīpāvatī</s>.

children.text: dīpāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ dīpo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In the capital <s>Dīpāvatī</s>, a king named <s>Dīpa</s> ruled; it was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people.

children.text: tatra dīpena rājñā dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There King <s>Dīpa</s> invited <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, to enter the city with full ceremonial preparation.

children.text: tasya ca dīpasya rājño vāsavo nāma sāmantarājo 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: And that King <s>Dīpa</s> had a feudatory king named <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: tena tasya dūto 'nupreṣita āgaccha iha mayā dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He sent a messenger to him, saying, "Come here; <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has been invited by me to enter the city with full ceremonial preparation.

children.text: tasya pūjāṃ kariṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: We shall perform worship for him."

children.text: tadā ca vāsavena rājñā dvādaśavarṣāṇi yajñamiṣṭvā yajñāvasāne rājñā pañca mahāpradānāni vyavasthāpitāni tadyathā sauvarṇakaṃ daṇḍakamaṇḍalu sauvarṇā sapātrī catūratnamayī śayyā pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni kanyā ca sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā ||
children.translated_text: At that time King <s>Vāsava</s>, after performing a sacrifice for twelve years, arranged five great gifts at the end of the sacrifice, namely: a golden staff and water-pot, a golden bowl with its vessel, a bed made of the four jewels, five hundred kārṣāpaṇas, and a maiden adorned with every ornament.

children.text: tena khalu samayena anyeṣu janapadeṣu dvau māṇavakau prativasataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that same time two young brahmins were living in other districts.

children.text: tābhyāṃ copādhyāyasakāśād vedādhyayanaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: They had studied the Vedas under their preceptor.

children.text: dharmatā ācāryasyācāryadhanam upādhyāyasyopādhyāyadhanaṃ pradeyamiti jñātvā cintayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that, by rule, a teacher's fee should be given to the ācārya and a preceptor's fee to the upādhyāya, they began to think.

children.text: tābhyāṃ ca śrutaṃ vāsavena rājñā pañca mahāpradānāni yajñāvasāne samudānītāni yo brāhmaṇaḥ svādhyāyasampanno bhaviṣyati sa lapsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: And they heard that King <s>Vāsava</s> had assembled five great gifts at the end of the sacrifice, and that whatever brahmin was accomplished in recitation would receive them.

children.text: tayoretadabhavad gacchāvastatra taṃ pradānaṃ pratigṛhṇīvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They thought, "Let us go there and receive that gift."

children.text: ko 'smākaṃ tatra bahuśrutatamo vā svādhyāyatamo bhaviṣyatīti saṃcintya yena vāsavasya rājño mahānagaraṃ tena samprasthitau ||
children.translated_text: Reflecting, "Which of us there will be the more learned or the more accomplished in recitation?" they set out for the great city of King <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: tasya ca rājño devatayā ārocitam ||
children.translated_text: And the king was informed by a deity.

children.text: yau etau dvau māṇavakau āgacchataḥ sumatiśca matiśca anayordvayoḥ sumateretatpradānaṃ dada ||
children.translated_text: "These two young brahmins who are coming are <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Mati</s>; of these two, give this gift to <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: yadevaṃ mahārāja tvayā dvādaśa varṣāṇi yajña iṣṭaḥ asmāt puṇyaphalānmahattamapadasya sumatermāṇavakasya mahāpradānaṃ dāsyasi ||
children.translated_text: Since, great king, you have performed a sacrifice for twelve years, from the fruit of this merit you will give the great gift to the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s>, who has the highest station."

children.text: sa rājā saṃlakṣayati nūnametau mahātmānau yeṣāmarthāya devatā apyārocayanti ||
children.translated_text: The king considered, "Surely these are great-souled men, for even deities make announcements on their behalf."

children.text: yato 'sau rājā paśyati māṇavakau dūrata evāgacchantau prāsādikāvabhirūpau tau ca gatvā tatra yajñe brāhmaṇapaṅktiṣu prajñapteṣu āsaneṣvagrāsanam abhiruhyāvasthitau ||
children.translated_text: Then the king saw the two young brahmins coming from afar, gracious and handsome; and they went there to the sacrifice and took their place on the foremost seats prepared among the rows of brahmins.

children.text: yato rājā vāsavastau sumatiṃ māṇavaṃ pṛcchati bhavān sumatis tenoktam aham ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s> asked the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s>, "Are you <s>Sumati</s>?" He replied, "I am."

children.text: yato rājā vāsavaḥ sumatiṃ māṇavamagrāsane bhojayitvā pañca pradānāni prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, after feeding the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> on the foremost seat, gave him the five gifts.

children.text: sumatirmāṇavaścatvāri mahāpradānāni gṛhṇāti daṇḍakamaṇḍaluprabhṛtīni ekaṃ kanyāpradānaṃ na pratigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> accepted the four great gifts, beginning with the staff and water-pot, but he did not accept the gift of the maiden.

children.text: sa kathayaty ahaṃ brahmacārī ||
children.translated_text: He said, "I am a celibate student."

children.text: yataḥ sā kanyā sumatiṃ māṇavaṃ prāsādikamabhirūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā lubdhā snehotpannā taṃ sumatiṃ māṇavamevamāha pratigṛhṇa māṃ brāhmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: Then the maiden, seeing that the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> was gracious and handsome, became attracted and felt affection arise; she said to that young brahmin <s>Sumati</s>, "Accept me, brahmin."

children.text: sa kathayati na śakyaṃ pratigṛhītum ||
children.translated_text: He said, "I cannot accept you."

children.text: yataḥ sā kanyā rājñā pradānabuddhyā parityaktā na punargṛhītā sumatināpi māṇavenāpratigṛhyamāṇā rājño dīpasya dīpāvatīṃ nagarīṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: Then, since the maiden had been given up by the king with the intention of a gift and was not taken back, and since she was not accepted by the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> either, she went to King <s>Dīpa</s>'s city <s>Dīpāvatī</s>.

children.text: sā tatra gatvā tadātmīyamalaṃkāraṃ śarīrādavatārya mālākārāyānuprayacchaty asyālaṃkārasya mūlyaṃ me pratidivasaṃ devasyārthe nīlotpalāni dadasva ||
children.translated_text: Having gone there, she removed her own ornaments from her body and handed them over to a garland-maker, saying, "For the value of these ornaments, give me blue lotuses every day for the sake of the deity."

children.text: sā tenopakrameṇa tad alaṃkārikaṃ suvarṇaṃ dattvā devaśuśrūṣikā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: By that means, having given the gold from those ornaments, she became an attendant serving the deity.

children.text: sa ca māṇavakaḥ sumatistāni catvāri mahāpradānāni gṛhya upādhyāyasakāśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s>, taking those four great gifts, went to his preceptor.

children.text: gatvā copādhyāyāya tāni catvāri mahāpradānānyanuprayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Having gone, he handed over those four great gifts to the preceptor.

children.text: tebhyaścopādhyāyastrīṇi pratigṛhṇāti kārṣāpaṇānāṃ tu pañca śatāni tasyaiva sumaterdadāti ||
children.translated_text: From them the preceptor accepted three, but gave the five hundred kārṣāpaṇas back to that same <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: sa ca sumatistasyāmeva rātrau daśa svapnānadrākṣīt mahāsamudraṃ pibāmi vaihāyasena gacchāmi imau candrādityau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau pāṇinā āmārṣṭi parimārṣṭi rājño rathe yojayāmi ṛṣīn śvetān hastinaḥ haṃsān siṃhān mahāśailaṃ parvatāniti ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>Sumati</s> saw ten dreams that very night: "I drink the great ocean; I travel through the air; I rub and stroke with my hand these moon and sun, so great in power and majesty; I yoke the king's chariot; I see white seers, elephants, haṃsas, lions, a great mountain, and mountains."

children.text: sa tān dṛṣṭvā pratibuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After seeing them, he awoke.

children.text: pratibuddhasyaitadabhavat ka eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ mama vyākaraṇaṃ kariṣyati tatra pañcābhijña ṛṣir nātidūre prativasati ||
children.translated_text: When he had awakened, it occurred to him, "Who will interpret these dreams of mine? There is a seer with the five superknowledges living not far from here."

children.text: atha sumatirmāṇavaḥ saṃśayanirṇayanārtham ṛṣeḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> went to the seer in order to resolve his uncertainty.

children.text: sumatistasya ṛṣeḥ pratisaṃmodanaṃ kṛtvā svapnānākhyāyāha kuruṣva me eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ nirṇayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumati</s> exchanged greetings with that seer, related the dreams, and said, "Make a determination for me about these dreams."

children.text: sa ṛṣirāha nāhameṣāṃ svapnānāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ kariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: The seer said, "I shall not interpret these dreams.

children.text: gaccha dīpāvatīṃ rājadhānīm ||
children.translated_text: Go to the capital city <s>Dīpāvatī</s>.

children.text: tatra dīpena rājñā dīpaṃkaro nāma samyaksambuddhaḥ sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There King <s>Dīpa</s> has invited <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, a perfectly awakened Buddha, to enter the city with full ceremonial preparation.

children.text: sa eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will interpret these dreams."

children.text: atha vāsavo rājā tasya dīpasya rājñaḥ pratiśrutya aśītyamātyasahasraparivṛto dīpāvatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, having given his promise to that King <s>Dīpa</s>, arrived at the capital city <s>Dīpāvatī</s> surrounded by eighty thousand ministers.

children.text: tena ca dīpena rājñā saptamāddivasāddīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśaṃ kariṣyāmīti sarvaviṣayādhiṣṭhānācca sarvapuṣpāṇāṃ saṃgrahaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And by that king <s>Dīpa</s>, it was begun: "On the seventh day I shall make the city-entry of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, with elaborate preparations." From every district and settlement he began to collect all flowers.

children.text: tatra ca yasmin divase rājñā dīpena tasya dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśa ārabdhaḥ kartum tasminneva divase sumatirapi tatraivāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And there, on the very day when king <s>Dīpa</s> began to arrange that ceremonious city-entry of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the fully awakened Buddha, <s>Sumati</s> too arrived there.

children.text: tatra rājñā sarvapuṣpāṇāṃ saṃgrahaḥ kāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the king had caused all the flowers to be gathered.

children.text: sā ca devopasthāyikā dārikā mālākārasakāśaṃ gatā prayaccha me nīlotpalāni devārcanaṃ kariṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: And that girl who served the deity went to the florist and said, "Give me blue lotuses; I shall perform worship of the deity."

children.text: mālākāra āha adya rājñā sarvapuṣpāṇi gṛhītāni dīpaṃkaranagarapraveśasyārthe ||
children.translated_text: The florist said, "Today all the flowers have been taken by the king for the sake of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>'s entry into the city."

children.text: sā kathayati gacchata punarapi tatra puṣkiriṇyām yadi matpuṇyair nīlotpalapadmam anuddhṛtamāsādyeta ||
children.translated_text: She said, "Go again to that lotus pond, in case, through my merits, an unplucked blue-lotus blossom may be found."

children.text: tatra puṣkiriṇyāṃ sumateḥ puṇyānubhāvāt sapta nīlapadmāni prādurbhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: There in the lotus pond, through the power of <s>Sumati</s>'s merit, seven blue lotuses appeared.

children.text: yataḥ sa mālākāro gataḥ sa tāni paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Then the florist went there and saw them.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca dārikayā mālākārasyoktam uddharaitāni padmāni ||
children.translated_text: Having seen them, the girl said to the florist, "Pull out these lotuses."

children.text: mālākāraḥ kathayati nāhamuddhariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: The florist said, "I will not pull them out.

children.text: rājakulānmamopālambho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: I shall receive blame from the royal household."

children.text: yataḥ sā kathayati na ||
children.translated_text: Then she said, "No.

children.text: tvayā sarvapuṣpāṇyuddhṛtya rājñaḥ pūrvaṃ dattānyeva ||
children.translated_text: You have already pulled out all the flowers and given them earlier to the king."

children.text: mālākāra āha dattāni ||
children.translated_text: The florist said, "They have been given."

children.text: yataḥ sā dārikā kathayati madīyaiḥ puṇyairetāni prādurbhūtāni prayacchoddhṛtāni mama ||
children.translated_text: Then that girl said, "These have appeared through my own merit; pull them out and give them to me."

children.text: mālākāraḥ kathayati kathametāni praveśakāni bhaviṣyantyasaṃviditaṃ rājakulasya dārikāhoddharatu bhavān ||
children.translated_text: The florist said, "How will these be brought inside without the royal household knowing?" The girl said, "Let your honor pull them out.

children.text: ahamudakakumbhe prakṣiptaṃ praveśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall put them in a water jar and bring them in."

children.text: tena mālākāreṇaivaṃ śrutvā tasyā dārikāyāstānyuddhṛtya anupradattāni ||
children.translated_text: When that florist had heard this, he pulled them out and handed them over to that girl.

children.text: sā tāni gṛhītvā udakakumbhe prakṣipya tatkumbhamudakasya pūrayitvā adhiṣṭhānaṃ gatā prasthitā ||
children.translated_text: She took them, put them in a water jar, filled that jar with water, and set out for the city.

children.text: sa ca sumatistatsthānamanusaṃprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Sumati</s> reached that place.

children.text: tasyaitadabhavat kathamahaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantam dṛṣṭvā na pūjayāmi sa mālākāragṛhāṇyanvāhiṇḍati sarvapuṣpānveṣaṇaparaḥ na ca kiṃcidekapuṣpamāsādayati ||
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "How, after seeing the Buddha, the Blessed One, could I fail to worship him?" Intent on searching for all flowers, he went about through the florists' houses, but he did not find even a single flower.

children.text: paścād bāhyenādhiṣṭhānānnirgamya ārāmeṇārāmaṃ puṣpāṇi paryeṣamāṇaḥ paryaṭati na caikapuṣpamāsādayati ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, having gone out from the city on the outside, he wandered from park to park searching for flowers, but he did not find a single flower.

children.text: atha paryaṭamānastadudyānaṃ samprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, as he wandered, he reached that garden.

children.text: sā ca dārikā tasmādudyānāt tasya sumater māṇavasyābhimukhamāgatā ||
children.translated_text: And that girl came out from that garden toward the brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: yataḥ puṇyānubhāvena tāni nīlapadmāni tasmādudakakumbhādabhyudgatāni ||
children.translated_text: Then, through the power of merit, those blue lotuses rose up out of that water jar.

children.text: yatastāni sumatirdṛṣṭvā tasyā dārikāyāḥ kathayati prayaccha mamaitāni padmāni ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Sumati</s> saw them, he said to that girl, "Give me these lotuses.

children.text: matsakāśādeṣāṃ niṣkrayaṃ pañcakārṣāpaṇaśataṃ gṛhāṇa ||
children.translated_text: Take from me five hundred kārṣāpaṇas as their price."

children.text: sā dārikā tasya sumateḥ kathayati tadā necchasi māṃ pratigṛhītum ||
children.translated_text: The girl said to that <s>Sumati</s>, "At that time you did not wish to receive me.

children.text: idānīṃ māṃ padmāni yācase ||
children.translated_text: Now you ask me for the lotuses.

children.text: nāhaṃ dāsyāmi ||
children.translated_text: I will not give them."

children.text: evamuktvā taṃ sumatiṃ māṇavamuvāca kimebhiḥ kariṣyasi sumatirāha buddhaṃ bhagavantamarcayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: After speaking thus, she said to the brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s>, "What will you do with these?" <s>Sumati</s> said, "I shall worship the Buddha, the Blessed One."

children.text: paścāddārikā kathayati kiṃ mama kārṣāpaṇaiḥ kṛtyam evamahaṃ buddhāya dāsye yadi tvameṣāṃ padmānāṃ pradānaphalena mamāpi jātyāṃ jātyāṃ patnīmicchasi asya dānasya pradānakāle yadyevaṃ praṇidhānaṃ karoṣi jātyāṃ jātyāṃ mama bhāryā syāditi ||
children.translated_text: Then the girl said, "What use have I for kārṣāpaṇas? I myself shall give them to the Buddha, if, through the fruit of giving these lotuses, you too desire me as your wife in birth after birth, and if, at the time of giving this gift, you make this aspiration: 'In birth after birth may she be my wife.'"

children.text: sumatirāha vayaṃ dānābhiratāḥ svagarbharūpaparityāgaṃ svamāṃsaparityāgaṃ ca kurmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumati</s> said, "We delight in giving; we give up our own fetus-formed body and even our own flesh.

children.text: tataḥ sā dārikā sumateḥ kathayati tvamevaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kuru paścād yenābhyarthīyase tasya māmanuprayacchethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that girl said to <s>Sumati</s>, "Make this very aspiration, and afterward, to whomever you are asked for me, you may give me away."

children.text: evamukte tayā dārikayā tasya sumateḥ pañca padmānyanupradattāni ātmanā dve gṛhīte ||
children.translated_text: When the girl had said this, five lotuses were handed over to <s>Sumati</s>, and she kept two herself.

children.text: gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: And she spoke a verse:

children.text: praṇidhim yatra kuryāstvaṃ buddhamāsādya nāyakam
children.translated_text: Wherever you make your aspiration after meeting the Buddha, the Leader,

children.text: tatra te 'haṃ bhavet patnī nityaṃ sahadharmacāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: there may I be your wife, always a companion in the Dharma."

children.text: tena rājñā tatra sarvamapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ kāritam ucchritadhvajapatākātoraṇam āmuktapaṭṭadāmaṃ gandhodakacūrṇapariṣiktam ||
children.translated_text: There that king had everything cleared of stones, gravel, and potsherds, with raised standards, banners, and gateways, festooned with cloth garlands, and sprinkled with perfumed water and powder.

children.text: nagaradvārādārabhya yāvacca vihāro yāvacca nagarametadantaram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ kāritamucchritadhvajapatākatoraṇam āmuktapaṭṭadāma gandhodakacūrṇapariṣiktam ||
children.translated_text: Beginning from the city gate as far as the monastery, and through all the space up to the city, he had it cleared of stones, gravel, and potsherds, with raised standards, banners, and gateways, festooned with cloth garlands, and sprinkled with perfumed water and powder.

children.text: sa ca rājā śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ gṛhītvā dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya pratyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that king, taking a parasol with a hundred ribs, went out to meet <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the fully awakened Buddha.

children.text: evamevāmātyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ministers did likewise.

children.text: evameva vāsavo rājā amātyaiḥ saha pratyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise king <s>Vāsava</s>, together with his ministers, went out to meet him.

children.text: dīpo rājā bhagavato buddhasya pādayor nipatya vijñāpayati bhagavan adhiṣṭhānaṃ praviśa ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Dīpa</s> fell at the feet of the Blessed Buddha and requested, "Blessed One, enter the city."

children.text: yataḥ sa bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto 'dhiṣṭhānapraveśābhimukhaḥ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that Blessed One, with the community of monks before him, set out facing toward entry into the city.

children.text: sa ca rājā dīpaḥ śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya dhārayati ||
children.translated_text: And that king <s>Dīpa</s> held a parasol with a hundred ribs over <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: tathaivāmātyā vāsavo rājā amātyasahāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way the ministers did so; and King <s>Vāsava</s> too, attended by his ministers.

children.text: bhagavatā ṛddhyā tathādhiṣṭhitaṃ yathā ekaikaḥ saṃlakṣayaty ahaṃ bhagavataśchatraṃ dhārayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: By the Blessed One's miraculous power it was so determined that each one perceived, "I am holding the parasol over the Blessed One."

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstathāvidhayā śobhayā janamadhyamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, with such splendor, reached the midst of the people.

children.text: tatra bhagavatā sābhisaṃskāra indrakīle pādo vyavasthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One deliberately set his foot upon the threshold-post.

children.text: yadaiva bhagavatā indrakīle pādo vyavasthāpitas tadaiva samanantarakālaṃ pṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitā calitā pracalitā saṃpracalitā vedhitā pravedhitā saṃpravedhitā ||
children.translated_text: As soon as the Blessed One set his foot upon the threshold-post, at that very next instant the earth shook in six ways: it shook, moved, moved violently, quivered, quivered strongly, and quivered all around.
