children.text: dharmatā ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatām yadendrakīle sābhisaṃskāreṇa pādau vyavasthāpayanti citrāṇyāścaryāṇyadbhutadharmāḥ prādurbhavanty unmattāḥ svacittaṃ pratilabhante 'ndhāścakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante badhirāḥ śrotraśravaṇasamarthā bhavanti mūkāḥ pravyāharaṇasamarthā bhavanti paṅgavo gamanasamarthā bhavanti mūḍhā garbhiṇīnāṃ strīṇāṃ garbhā anulomībhavanti haḍinigaḍabaddhānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ bandhanāni śithilībhavanti janmajanmavairānubaddhāstadanantaraṃ maitracittatāṃ pratilabhante vatsā dāmāni chittvā mātṛbhiḥ saṃgacchanti hastinaḥ krośanti aśvā hreṣante ṛṣabhā garjanti śukasārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakā madhuraṃ nikūjanti aneritāni vāditrabhāṇḍāni madhuraśabdān niścārayanti peḍākṛtā alaṃkārā madhuraśabdānniścārayanty unnatāḥ pṛthivīpradeśā avanamanty avanatāśconnamanti apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālāstiṣṭhanty antarikṣāddevatā divyānyutpalāni kṣipanti padmāni kumudāni puṇḍarīkānyagurucūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni tamālapatrāṇi divyāni mandārakāṇi puṣpāṇi kṣipanti pūrvo digbhāga unnamati paścimo 'vanamati paścima unnamati pūrvo 'vanamati dakṣiṇa unnamatyuttaro 'vanamaty uttara unnamati dakṣiṇo 'vanamati madhya unnamatyanto 'vanamati anta unnamati madhyo 'vanamati ||
children.translated_text: And it is the nature of the blessed Buddhas that, when they deliberately set their feet upon a threshold-post, various marvelous and wonderful events appear: the mad regain their own minds, the blind regain their eyes, the deaf become able to hear sounds, the mute become able to speak, the lame become able to walk, and the mispositioned fetuses of pregnant women turn to their proper course; the fetters of beings bound with chains and shackles become loosened; those bound by enmity from birth to birth immediately obtain minds of friendliness; calves break their tethers and come together with their mothers; elephants trumpet, horses neigh, bulls bellow, and parrots, mynas, cuckoos, and jīvaṃjīvaka birds sing sweetly; musical instruments, though not played, emit sweet sounds; ornaments arranged in boxes emit sweet sounds; raised places on the earth sink down and sunken places rise up; places free from stones, gravel, and potsherds remain so; from the sky deities scatter divine blue lotuses, lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, aloe-powder, sandal-powder, tagara-powder, tamala leaves, and divine mandārava flowers; the eastern quarter rises and the western sinks, the western rises and the eastern sinks, the southern rises and the northern sinks, the northern rises and the southern sinks, the middle rises and the end sinks, and the end rises and the middle sinks.

children.text: tatra ca dīpāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi puṣpairdhūpairgandhaiśca kārāṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: And there in the capital city <s>Dīpāvatī</s>, many hundreds of thousands of living beings performed acts of worship with flowers, incense, and perfumes.

children.text: te 'pi ca sumatiśca dārikā ca yena dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhastenānugacchanti padmāni gṛhya ||
children.translated_text: And they, together with <s>Sumati</s> and the girl, followed after <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, holding lotuses.

children.text: te ca tatra mahājanakāyena pūjārthaṃ saṃparivṛtasya bhagavata upaśleṣaṃ na labhante ||
children.translated_text: But there, because the Blessed One was surrounded by a great mass of people for worship, they could not get near him.

children.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati bahutaraṃ sumatirmāṇavo 'smānmahājanakāyāt puṇyaprasavaṃ kariṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One perceived, "The brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s> will produce more merit for us than this great mass of people."

children.text: matvā mahatīṃ tumulāṃ vātavṛṣṭim abhinirmiṇoti ||
children.translated_text: Having thought this, he created a great and violent storm of wind and rain.

children.text: yatastena janakāyenāvakāśo dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, space was given by that crowd of people.

children.text: labdhāvakāśaśca sumatirmāṇavo bhagavantamasecanakadarśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā atīva prasādajātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s> had obtained room, he saw the Blessed One, whose sight was never enough, and became exceedingly filled with faith.

children.text: prasādajātena ca tāni pañca padmāni bhagavataḥ kṣiptāni ||
children.translated_text: Filled with faith, he threw those five lotuses toward the Blessed One.

children.text: tāni ca bhagavatā dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena tathā adhiṣṭhitāni yathā śakaṭīcakramātrāṇi vitānaṃ baddhvā vyavasthitāni ||
children.translated_text: And those lotuses were so empowered by the Blessed One <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, that they remained arranged as a canopy, each the size of a cart wheel.

children.text: gacchato 'nugacchanti tiṣṭhato 'nutiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: When he went, they followed along; when he stood, they stood along with him.

children.text: tathā dṛṣṭvā tayā dārikayā prasādajātayā dvau padmau bhagavataḥ kṣiptau ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that, the girl too, filled with faith, threw two lotuses toward the Blessed One.

children.text: tau cāpi bhagavatā tathādhiṣṭhitau yathā śakaṭīcakramātrau karṇasamīpe vitānaṃ baddhvā vyavasthitau ||
children.translated_text: And those two also were so empowered by the Blessed One that, each the size of a cart wheel, they remained arranged as a canopy near his ears.

children.text: tatra ca pradeśe tumulena vātavarṣeṇa kardamo jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in that place, because of the violent wind and rain, mud had formed.

children.text: paścāt sumatirmāṇavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakardamaṃ pṛthivīpradeśamupagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward the brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s> approached the Buddha, the Blessed One, at that muddy place on the ground.

children.text: tasmin sakardame pṛthivīpradeśe jaṭāṃ saṃtīrya bhagavato purato gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: In that muddy place on the ground, he spread out his matted hair and spoke a verse before the Blessed One:

children.text: yadi buddho bhaviṣyāmi bodhāya buddhabodhana
children.translated_text: "If I am to become a Buddha, O awakener to awakening and to the Buddha's awakening,

children.text: ākramiṣyasi me padbhyāṃ jaṭāṃ janmajarāntakām ||
children.translated_text: you will step with your feet upon my matted hair, which is to end birth and old age."

children.text: tatastena dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena tasya sumatermāṇavasya jaṭāsu pādau vyavasthāpitau ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, placed both feet upon the matted hair of that brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: tasya ca sumateḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubuddha eva matirmāṇavastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: And behind that <s>Sumati</s> stood the brahmin youth <s>Mati</s>, one who had only just awakened to understanding.

children.text: tena kupitenābhihitaṃ bhagavato dīpaṃkarasya paśya tāvadbhoḥ anena dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhenāsya sumatermāṇavasya tiraścām yathā padbhyāṃ jaṭā avaṣṭabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Angry, he said to the Blessed One <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, "Just look, sir: this <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has pressed down the matted hair of this brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s> with his feet as if he were an animal."

children.text: paścāt dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena sumatirmāṇavo vyākṛto bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ nṛbhavādvimukto mukto vibhurlokahitāya śāstā
children.translated_text: Afterward the brahmin youth <s>Sumati</s> was given a prediction by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha: "You will become, freed from human existence, liberated, sovereign, a teacher for the welfare of the world,

children.text: śākyātmajaḥ śākyamunīti nāmnā trilokasāro jagataḥ pradīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the essence of the three worlds, the lamp of the world."

children.text: yadā ca sa sumatirmāṇavo dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena vyākṛtas tatsamakālameva vaihāyasaṃ saptatālānabhyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> had been predicted by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, at that very moment he rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees.

children.text: tāścāsya jaṭāḥ śīrṇā anyāḥ praviśiṣṭatarā jaṭāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: His matted locks fell away, and other, more excellent matted locks appeared.

children.text: sa vaihāyasastho mahatā janakāyena dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Standing in the air, he was seen by a great multitude of people.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ yadā anenānuttarajñānamadhigataṃ tadāsya vayaṃ śrāvakā bhavema ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, they made the aspiration: "When he has attained unsurpassed knowledge, may we be his <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples)."

children.text: sāpi ca dārikā praṇidhānaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: And that girl too made an aspiration.

children.text: praṇidhānam yatra kuryāstvaṃ buddhamāsādya nāyakam
children.translated_text: "Wherever you should make your aspiration and attain the Buddha, the leader,

children.text: tatra te 'haṃ bhavetpatnī nityaṃ sahadharmacāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: there may I be your wife, always a companion in the Dharma."

children.text: yadā bhavasi saṃbuddho loke jyeṣṭhavināyakaḥ
children.translated_text: "When you become a fully awakened Buddha, the foremost leader in the world,

children.text: śrāvikā te bhaviṣyāmi tasmin kāla upasthite ||
children.translated_text: I shall become your female disciple when that time has arrived."

children.text: khagasthaṃ māṇavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
children.translated_text: Seeing the young brahmin in the sky, many hundreds and thousands

children.text: śrāvakatvaṃ prārthayante sarve tatra hyanāgate ||
children.translated_text: all there sought discipleship for the future.

children.text: yadā bhavasi saṃbuddho loke jyeṣṭhavināyakaḥ
children.translated_text: "When you become a fully awakened Buddha, the foremost leader in the world,

children.text: śrāvakāste bhaviṣyāmastasmin kāle hyupasthite ||
children.translated_text: we shall be your disciples when that time has arrived."

children.text: yadā ca sumatirmāṇavo dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena vyākṛtas tadāsya dīpena rājñā jaṭā gṛhītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> had been predicted by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, his matted locks were taken by king <s>Dīpa</s>.

children.text: vāsavo rājā kathayati mamaitā jaṭā anuprayaccha ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Vāsava</s> said, "Give those matted locks to me."

children.text: tatastasya dīpena rājñā anupradattāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then king <s>Dīpa</s> handed them over to him.

children.text: tena gṛhītvā gaṇitā aśītirvālasahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Having taken them, he counted them: there were eighty thousand hairs.

children.text: tasya rājño 'mātyāḥ kathayanti deva asmākamekaikaṃ vālamanuprayaccha ||
children.translated_text: The ministers of that king said, "Your Majesty, give each of us one hair.

children.text: vayameṣāṃ caityāni kariṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We will make <s>caityas</s> (shrines) for them."

children.text: tena rājñā teṣāṃ bhṛtyānāmekaiko vālo dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That king gave one hair to each of those servants.

children.text: tairamātyaiḥ svake vijite gatvā caityāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni ||
children.translated_text: Those ministers went to their own domains and established <s>caityas</s>.

children.text: yadā sumatirmāṇavo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksambuddhau vyākṛtaḥ tadā dīpena rājñā vāsavena ca rājñā tairanekaiśca naigamajānapadaiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārito 'nāgataguṇāvekṣatayā ||
children.translated_text: When the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s> had been predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening, king <s>Dīpa</s>, king <s>Vāsava</s>, and many townsmen and country people invited him with every requisite, looking ahead to his future qualities.

children.text: tataḥ sa matirmāṇava ucyate 'hamanuttarasyāṃ samyaksambodhau vyākṛtas tvayā kutra cittamutpāditaṃ sa kathayati kṣato 'haṃ sumate māṇava ||
children.translated_text: Then the young brahmin <s>Mati</s> was addressed: "I have been predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Toward what have you produced your mind?" He said, "I am wounded, young brahmin <s>Sumati</s>."

children.text: sa kathayati kathaṃ kṛtvā kṣato 'si tataḥ sa kathayati yadā tava dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena padbhyāṃ jaṭā avaṣṭabdhās tadā kupitena vāṅ niścāritā dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena śrotriyasya jaṭā tiraścām yathā padbhyāmavaṣṭabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "How have you been wounded?" Then he said, "When your matted locks were pressed down by the feet of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, I became angry and uttered these words: 'How can the matted locks of a learned brahmin be pressed down by the feet of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha?'"

children.text: yatastasya sumatiḥ kathayaty āgacchasva buddhasya bhagavato 'ntike pravrajāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, <s>Sumati</s> said to him, "Come; let us go forth in the presence of the Buddha, the Blessed One."

children.text: tatastau sumatirmatiśca dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya pravacane pravrajitau ||
children.translated_text: Then both <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Mati</s> went forth in the teaching of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: sumatinā ca pravrajya trīṇi piṭakānyadhītāni dharmeṇa parṣat saṃgṛhītā ||
children.translated_text: After going forth, <s>Sumati</s> studied the three <s>piṭakas</s> (collections), and the assembly was gathered by means of the Dharma.

children.text: sa ca sumatirmāṇavaścyutaḥ kālagatastuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the young brahmin <s>Sumati</s>, when he passed away and died, was reborn among the gods in <s>Tuṣita</s>.

children.text: matirmāṇavaścyutaḥ kālagato narakeṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The young brahmin <s>Mati</s>, when he passed away and died, was reborn in the hells.

children.text: bhagavānāha yo 'sau vāsavo rājābhūt tena kālena tena samayena sa rājā bimbisāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "The one who was king <s>Vāsava</s> at that time and on that occasion is king <s>Bimbisāra</s> now.

children.text: yāni tānyaśītiramātyasahasrāṇi tena kālena tena samayena tānyetarhyaśītirdevatāsahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Those eighty thousand ministers at that time and on that occasion are now the eighty thousand deities.

children.text: yo 'sau dīpāvatīyako janakāyaḥ yāsau dārikā eṣaiva sā yaśodharā ||
children.translated_text: The people of <s>Dīpāvatī</s> who were there, and the girl who was there, she is this very <s>Yaśodharā</s>.

children.text: yo 'sau sumatir ahameva tasmin samaye bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ vartāmi ||
children.translated_text: The one who was <s>Sumati</s> was myself; at that time I was engaged in <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct.

children.text: yo 'sau matiḥ eṣa eva sa dharmaruciḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one who was <s>Mati</s> is this very <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

children.text: etaddvitīye 'saṃkhyeye asya ca dharmarucermama ca darśanam yadahaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi cirasya dharmaruce sucirasya dharmaruce ||
children.translated_text: This was the second meeting, in the second <s>asaṃkhyeya</s> (incalculable aeon), between this <s>Dharmaruci</s> and me, with reference to which I say, 'It has been long, <s>Dharmaruci</s>, very long, <s>Dharmaruci</s>.'

children.text: tasmādapyarvāk tṛtīye 'saṃkhyeye krakucchando nāma samyaksambuddho loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: Still later than that, in the third <s>asaṃkhyeya</s>, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāmanyataro mahāśreṣṭhī prativasati ||
children.translated_text: In that capital city there lived a certain great merchant guild-master.

children.text: tena ca sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam ||
children.translated_text: He brought home a wife from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa ca kalatrasahāyaḥ krīḍati ramate paricārayati ||
children.translated_text: Together with his wife he played, took pleasure, and enjoyed himself.

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he was playing, taking pleasure, and enjoying himself, a son was born to him.

children.text: sa ca gṛhapatiḥ śrāddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That householder was faithful.

children.text: tasya cārhan bhikṣuḥ kulāvavādako 'sti ||
children.translated_text: And an arhat monk was the instructor of his family.

children.text: sa ca gṛhapatistāṃ patnīmevamāha jāto 'smākam ṛṇadharo dhanaharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That householder said this to his wife: "A bearer of debt, a taker of wealth, has been born to us.

children.text: gacchāmyahamidānīṃ bhadre vaṇigdharmāṇāṃ deśāntaraṃ bhāṇḍamādāya ||
children.translated_text: Now, good lady, I am going to another country, following the merchants' way, taking merchandise with me."

children.text: sa ca vaṇiglokenāvṛto dūrataraṃ gato bhāṇḍamādāya ||
children.translated_text: Surrounded by a company of merchants, he went very far away, taking merchandise with him.

children.text: yato 'sya na bhūyaściramapyāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: After that he did not return for a very long time.

children.text: sa ca dārakaḥ kālāntareṇa mahān saṃvṛtto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the course of time that boy grew up, handsome, good-looking, and pleasing.

children.text: tato 'sau mātaraṃ pṛcchaty amba kimasmākaṃ kulārthāgataṃ karma sā kathayati vatsa pitā tava āpaṇaṃ vāhayannāsīt ||
children.translated_text: Then he asked his mother, "Mother, what occupation has come down in our family as its livelihood?" She said, "Child, your father used to conduct a shop."

children.text: tataḥ sa dāraka āpaṇamārabdho vāhayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then the boy began to conduct a shop.

children.text: sā ca mātā asya kleśairbādhyamānā cintayituṃ pravṛttā ka upāyaḥ syāt yadahaṃ kleśān vinodayeyaṃ na ca me kaścijjānīyāt tayā saṃcintyaivamadhyavasitam evameva putrakāmahetostathā paricarāmi yathā anenaiva me sārdhaṃ rogavinodakaṃ bhavati naiva svajanasya śaṅkā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And that mother of his, tormented by afflictive passions, began to think, "What means might there be by which I could dispel these passions, and no one would know of me?" Having thought this over, she resolved, "For the sake of having a son I attend on him in such a way that, with this very one, my sickness may be relieved, and there will be no suspicion among my own people."

children.text: tatastayā vṛddhayuvatī āhūya bhojayitvā dvis triḥ paścānnavena paṭenācchāditā ||
children.translated_text: Then she summoned an old woman, fed her two or three times, and afterward covered her with a new cloth.

children.text: tasyāḥ sā vṛddhā kathayati kena kāryeṇaiva mamānupradānādinā upakrameṇānupravṛttiṃ karoṣi sā tasyā vṛddhāyā viśvastā bhūtvā evamāha amba śṛṇu vijñāpyam ||
children.translated_text: The old woman said to her, "For what purpose are you entering upon this course of winning me over by such gifts and attentions?" Having become confident in that old woman, she said to her, "Mother, listen to what I have to say."

children.text: kleśairatīva bādhye priyatāṃ mamotpādya manuṣyānveṣaṇaṃ kuru yo 'bhyantara eva syānna ca śaṅkanīyo janasya ||
children.translated_text: "I am extremely tormented by passions. Produce affection for me and seek out a man, one who would be within the household and yet would not arouse people's suspicion."

children.text: vṛddhā kathayati neha gṛhe tathāvidho manuṣyaḥ saṃvidyate nāpi praṇayavān kaścit praviśati yo janasyāśaṅkanīyo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The old woman said, "In this house there is no such man, nor does any intimate person come in who would be unsuspected by people."

children.text: katamaḥ sa manuṣyo bhaviṣyati yasyāhaṃ vakṣyāmi tataḥ sā vaṇikpatnī tasyā vṛddhāyāḥ kathayati yadyanyo manuṣya evaṃvidhopakramayukto nāsty eṣa eva me putro bhavati naiṣa lokasya śaṅkanīyo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "What man will there be to whom I may speak?" Then the merchant's wife said to that old woman, "If there is no other man suited to such an undertaking, then this very son of mine will do. He will not be suspected by the world."

children.text: tasyāstayā vṛddhayā abhihitaṃ kathaṃ nu putreṇa sārdhaṃ ratikrīḍāṃ gamiṣyasi yuktaṃ syādanyena manuṣyeṇa sārdhaṃ ratikrīḍāmanubhavitum ||
children.translated_text: That old woman said to her, "How indeed will you go to sexual play with your son? It would be proper to experience sexual play with another man."

children.text: tataḥ sā vaṇikpatnī kathayati yadyanyo 'bhyantaro manuṣyo na saṃvidyate bhavatu eṣa eva me putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the merchant's wife said, "If there is no other man within the household, let this very son of mine be the one."

children.text: tayā vṛddhayā abhihitaṃ yathepsitaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: The old woman said to her, "Do as you wish."

children.text: tataḥ sā vṛddhayuvatī tasya vaṇijaḥ putrasyaivāgamya pṛcchati vatsa taruṇo 'si rūpavāṃśca ||
children.translated_text: Then that old woman went to the merchant's son himself and asked, "Child, you are young and handsome."

children.text: kiṃ pratiṣṭhito 'syārthena tena tasyā abhihitaṃ kimetat tataḥ sā vṛddhā kathayati bhavānevamabhirūpaśca yuvā ca asmin vayasi taruṇayuvatyā sārdhaṃ śobhethāḥ krīḍan raman paricārayan kimeva kāmabhogaparihīnastiṣṭhasi vaṇigdārakastaṃ śrutvā lajjāvyapatrāpyasaṃlīnacetāstasyā vṛddhāyāstadvacanaṃ nādhivāsayati ||
children.translated_text: "On what purpose are you intent?" He said to her, "What is this?" Then the old woman said, "You are so good-looking and young; at this age you would be well suited to sport, enjoy yourself, and be attended by a young woman. Why do you remain deprived of sensual pleasures, young merchant?" Hearing this, the merchant's son, his mind drawn in by shame and modesty, did not accept those words of the old woman.

children.text: tataḥ sā vṛddhā evaṃ dvirapi trirapi tasya dārakasya kathayati taruṇayuvatistavārthe kleśairbādhyate ||
children.translated_text: Then the old woman spoke in this way to the boy a second and a third time: "A young woman is tormented by passion on your account."

children.text: sa vaṇigdārako dvirapi trirapyucyamānastasyā vṛddhāyāḥ kathayaty amba kiṃ tasyāstaruṇayuvatyāḥ sannimitte kiṃcidabhihitaṃ tataḥ sā vṛddhā kathayaty uktaṃ tasyā mayā tannimittam ||
children.translated_text: When he had been told two and three times, the merchant's son said to that old woman, "Mother, has anything been said with reference to that young woman?" Then the old woman said, "I have spoken to her about that matter."

children.text: tayā mama nimitte na pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: "She did not make a promise with regard to me."

children.text: sā ca dārikā hrīvyapatrāpyagṛhītā na kiṃcidvakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "But that girl, seized by shame and modesty, will not say anything."

children.text: na ca śarīramāvṛtaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Nor will she cover her body."

children.text: na tvayā tasyā vānveṣaṇe yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "You must not make any effort to inquire about her."

children.text: tatastena vaṇigdārakeṇa tasyā vṛddhāyā abhihitaṃ kutrāsmākaṃ saṃgataṃ bhaviṣyati tayā abhihitaṃ madīye gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: Then the merchant's son said to that old woman, "Where will our meeting take place?" She said, "In my house."

children.text: tenoktaṃ kutrāvakāśe tava gṛhaṃ tato 'sya tayā vṛddhayā gṛhaṃ vyapadiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Where is your house situated?" Then the old woman pointed out her house to him.

children.text: sā ca vṛddhā tasyā vaṇikpatnyāḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati icchāpitaḥ sa vo 'yaṃ dārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that old woman went to the merchant's wife and said, "This boy has been made willing for you."

children.text: sā kathayati kutrāvakāśe saṃgataṃ bhaviṣyati madīye gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: She said, "Where will the meeting take place?" "In my house."

children.text: sa ca dārakaḥ kāryāṇi kṛtvā gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the boy, after doing his duties, went away.

children.text: anupūrveṇa bhuktvā tasyā mātuḥ kathayati gacchāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: In due course, after he had eaten, he said to his mother, "I am going."

children.text: vayasyagṛhe svapsye ||
children.translated_text: "I shall sleep in a friend's house."

children.text: tato 'sya mātrāpyanujñātaṃ gaccha ||
children.translated_text: Then he was given permission by his mother as well: "Go."

children.text: sa dārako labdhānujñastasyā vṛddhāyā gṛhaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained permission, the boy went to that old woman's house.

children.text: tasya dārakasya tasmin gṛhe gatasya ratikrīḍākālamāgamayamānasya tiṣṭhato niśi kālamapratyabhijñātam ||
children.translated_text: When the boy had gone into that house and was standing there waiting for the time of sexual play, he did not notice the time during the night.

children.text: rūpe kāle sā mātā asya vaṇigdārakasya tasminneva gṛhe ratikrīḍāmanubhavanārthaṃ tatraiva gatā ||
children.translated_text: At the proper time that mother of the merchant's son went to that same house in order to experience sexual play there.

children.text: gatvā ca tasmin gṛhe vikālam avyaktiṃ vibhāvyamāne rūpākṛtau nirgūḍhenopacārakrameṇa ratikrīḍāṃ putreṇa sārdhamanubhavituṃ pravṛttā pāpakenāsaddharmeṇa ||
children.translated_text: Having gone into that house, when it was late and his form and appearance could not be made out, she secretly began, by a contrived manner of approach, to experience sexual play with her son through evil, unrighteous conduct.

children.text: sā ca parikṣīṇāyāṃ rātrau anubhūtaratikrīḍā satamo'ndhakāre kālāyāmeva rajanyām avibhāvyamānarūpākṛtau svagṛhaṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: And when the night had waned, after experiencing sexual play, while it was still the time of darkness, in the black night when form and appearance could not be discerned, she went to her own house.

children.text: sa cāpi vaṇigdārako ratikrīḍāmanubhūya prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ bhāṇḍāvāriṃ gatvā kuṭumbakāryāṇi karoti ||
children.translated_text: The merchant's son too, after experiencing sexual play, when the night had dawned, went to the shop and did the household business.

children.text: evaṃ dvirapi trirapi ||
children.translated_text: So it happened a second and a third time.

children.text: tatra vṛddhāyā gṛhe ratikrīḍāmanubhavaṃśca cirakālamevaṃ vartamānena ratikrīḍākrameṇa tasya dārakasya sā mātā cintayituṃ pravṛttā kiyatkālam anyadgṛham ahamevam avibhāvyamānarūpā ratikrīḍāmanubhaviṣyāmi yannvahamasyaitat ratikrīḍākramaṃ tathāvidhaṃ krameṇa saṃvedayeyaṃ yathā ihaiva gṛhe ratikrīḍā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: There, in the old woman's house, as he was experiencing sexual play, and as this manner of sexual play continued in this way for a long time, that boy's mother began to think: "For how long shall I experience sexual play in another's house like this, while my form is not recognized? What if I were gradually to make him know this manner of sexual play in such a way that the sexual play would take place right here in the house?"

children.text: iti saṃcintya tatraiva vṛddhāgṛhe gatvā ratikrīḍāṃ putreṇa sārdhamanubhūya rajanyāḥ kṣaye satamo'ndhakārakāle tasya dārakasyoparimaṃ prāvaraṇaṃ nivasyātmanīyāṃ ca śirottarapaṭṭikāṃ tyaktvā svagṛhaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: Having thought this, she went there to the old woman's house, experienced sexual play together with her son, and, at the end of the night, in the time of dense darkness, put on that boy's upper covering, left behind her own head-cloth, and went to her own house.

children.text: sa ca dārakaḥ prabhātakāle tāṃ paṭṭikāṃ śirasi mañcasyāvatiṣṭhantīṃ saṃpaśyati ||
children.translated_text: And in the morning the boy saw that head-cloth lying at the head of the bed.

children.text: ātmīyāmevopariprāvaraṇapotrīm alabhamānastatraiva tāṃ paṭṭikāṃ saṃlakṣya tyaktvā bhāṇḍāvārīṃ gatvā yugalamanyaṃ prāvṛtya svagṛhaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not finding his own upper covering, and noticing that head-cloth there, he left it, went to the storeroom, put on another set of garments, and went to his own house.

children.text: tatra ca gataḥ saṃpaśyati tamevātmīyaṃ prāvaraṇaṃ tasyā mātuḥ śirasi prāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: When he had gone there, he saw that very upper covering of his own worn on his mother's head.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ mātaraṃ pṛcchaty amba kuto 'yaṃ śirasi prāvaraṇo 'bhyāgato yatastayā abhihitam adyāpyahaṃ tavāmbā evaṃ cirakālaṃ tava mayā sārdhaṃ kāmān paribhuñjato 'dyāpyahaṃ tava saivāmbā yataḥ sa vaṇigdārakastathāvidhaṃ mātṛvacanamupaśrutya saṃmūḍho vihvalacetā bhūmau nipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing it, he asked his mother, "Mother, where has this covering on your head come from?" She replied, "Even now am I still your mother? After you have enjoyed pleasures with me for such a long time, even now am I that same mother of yours?" When that merchant's son heard such words from his mother, he became bewildered, his mind overwhelmed, and fell to the ground.

children.text: tatastayā sa mātrā ghaṭajalapariṣekeṇāvasiktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that mother sprinkled him with water from a pitcher.

children.text: sa jalapariṣekāvasikto dārakaścireṇa kālena pratyāgataprāṇastayā mātrā samāśvāsyate kimevaṃ khedamupāgatastvam asmadīyaṃ vacanamupaśrutya dhīramanā bhavasva ||
children.translated_text: The boy, sprinkled with water, after a long time regained consciousness, and his mother reassured him: "Why have you fallen into such distress after hearing my words? Be firm-minded.

children.text: na te viṣādaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You should not be despondent."

children.text: sa dārakastasyāḥ kathayati kathamahaṃ khedaṃ na kariṣyāmi saṃmohaṃ vā yena mayā evaṃvidhaṃ pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ tataḥ sa tayābhihito na te manaḥśūkam asminnarthe utpādayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: The boy said to her, "How shall I not be distressed or bewildered, since I have done such an evil deed?" Then she said to him, "You should not give rise to mental anguish in this matter.

children.text: panthāsamo mātṛgrāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Women are like a road.

children.text: yenaivaṃ hi yathā pitā gacchati putro 'pi tenaiva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: For just as the father goes by that road, the son too goes by that same road.

children.text: na cāsau panthā putrasyānugacchato doṣakārako bhavaty evameva mātṛgrāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that road does not become a cause of fault for the son who follows it. Women are just the same.

children.text: tīrthasamo 'pi ca mātṛgrāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And women are also like a ford.

children.text: yatraiva hi tīrthe pitā snāti putro 'pi tasmin snāti na ca tīrthaṃ putrasya snāyato doṣakārakaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For at whatever ford the father bathes, the son too bathes there, and the ford does not become a cause of fault for the son who bathes.

children.text: evameva mātṛgrāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Women are just the same.

children.text: api ca pratyanteṣu janapadeṣu dharmataivaiṣā yasyāmeva pitā asaddharmeṇābhigacchati tāmeva putro 'pyadhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the frontier countries this is simply the established custom: the very woman whom the father approaches through <s>asaddharma</s> (illicit conduct), the son also approaches.

children.text: evamasau vaṇigdārako mātrā bahuvidhairanunayavacanairvinītaśokastayā mātrā tasmin pātake 'saddharme punaḥ punaratīva saṃjātarāgaḥ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way that merchant's son, freed from grief by his mother's many kinds of conciliatory words, again and again became exceedingly attached to that sin, that <s>asaddharma</s> (illicit conduct), and engaged in it with his mother.

children.text: tena ca śreṣṭhinā gṛhe lekhyo 'nupreṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a letter was sent to the house by that merchant.

children.text: bhadre dhīrorjitamahotsāhā bhavasva ||
children.translated_text: "Good lady, be firm, strong, and greatly energetic.

children.text: ahamapi lekhānupadamevāgamiṣye ||
children.translated_text: I too shall come immediately after the letter."

children.text: sā vaṇikpatnī tathāvidhaṃ lekhārthaṃ śrutvā vaimanasyajātā cintayituṃ pravṛttā mahāntaṃ kālaṃ mama tasyāgamanamudīkṣamāṇāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the merchant's wife heard the meaning of such a letter, she became dejected and began to think: "For a long time I waited for his coming.

children.text: tadā nāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he did not come.

children.text: idānīṃ mayā evaṃvidhenopakrameṇa putraṃ ca paricaritvā sa cāgamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Now, after I have attended to my son by such a device, he too will come.

children.text: ka upāyaḥ syāt yadahaṃ tamihāsamprāptameva jīvitāt vyaparopayeyam iti saṃcintya taṃ putramāhūya kathayati pitrā te lekhyo 'nupreṣita āgamiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: What means could there be by which I might deprive him of life before he even arrives here?" Having thought this, she called that son and said, "Your father has sent a letter saying that he will come.

children.text: jānase 'smābhiridānīṃ kiṃ karaṇīyamiti gacchasva pitaramasamprāptameva ghātaya ||
children.translated_text: You know what must now be done by us. Go, and kill your father before he even arrives."

children.text: sa kathayati kathamahaṃ pitaraṃ ghātayiṣye yadā asau na prasahate pitṛvadhaṃ kartum tadā tayā mātrā bhūyo 'nuvṛttivacanairabhihitas tasyānuvṛttivacanairucyamānasya kāmeṣu saṃraktasyādhyavasāyo jātaḥ pitṛvadhaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: He said, "How shall I kill my father?" When he could not bring himself to commit the killing of his father, then, being addressed by his mother with further coaxing words, and being attached to pleasures, he formed the resolve for patricide.

children.text: kāmān khalu pratisevato na hi kiṃcit pāpakaṃ karmākaraṇīyamiti vadāmi ||
children.translated_text: For one who is surely devoted to pleasures, I say, there is no evil deed that is not to be done.

children.text: tatastenoktaṃ kenopāyena ghātayāmi tayā abhihitam ahamevopāyaṃ saṃvidhāsye ||
children.translated_text: Then he said, "By what means shall I kill him?" She replied, "I myself shall arrange the means."

children.text: ityuktvā viṣamādāya samitāyāṃ miśrayitvā maṇḍilakān paktvā anye 'pi ca nirviṣāḥ paktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, she took poison, mixed it into the meal, and cooked cakes; she also cooked other cakes without poison.

children.text: yatastaṃ dārakamāhūya kathayati gacchasva ||
children.translated_text: Then she called the boy and said, "Go.

children.text: amī saviṣā maṇḍilakā nirviṣāśca ||
children.translated_text: These cakes are poisonous, and these are without poison.

children.text: gṛhya pitṛsakāśaṃ gatvā ca tasya viśvastasyaikatra bhuñjata etān saviṣān maṇḍilakān prayacchasva ātmanā ca nirviṣān bhakṣaya ||
children.translated_text: Take them, go to your father's presence, and when he trusts you and eats together with you in one place, give him these poisonous cakes, while you yourself eat the ones without poison."

children.text: tataḥ sa dārakastena lekhavāhikamanuṣyeṇa sārdhaṃ tān maṇḍilakān gṛhya gataḥ pitṛsakāśam ||
children.translated_text: Then the boy took those cakes and went together with the man who carried the letter to his father's presence.

children.text: āgamya pitā asya atīva taṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā abhirūpaprāsādikaṃ maheśākhyaṃ prāmodyaṃ prāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he arrived, his father, seeing that son to be very handsome, pleasing, and eminent, was filled with joy.

children.text: sahyāsahyaṃ pṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ vaṇijāmākhyāty ayaṃ bhavanto 'smākaṃ putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: After asking those various merchants whether it was bearable or unbearable, he told them, "Gentlemen, this is our son."

children.text: yadā tena dārakeṇa saṃlakṣitaṃ sarvatra ahamanena pitrā pratisaṃvedita iti tatastaṃ pitaramāha tāta ambayā maṇḍilakāḥ praheṇakamanupreṣitam ||
children.translated_text: When that boy perceived, "Everywhere I have been made known by this father," he said to his father, "Father, mother has sent maṇḍilakas as a present.

children.text: tattātaḥ paribhuñjatu ||
children.translated_text: So let father eat them."

children.text: paścāttena pitrā sārdhamekaphalāyāṃ bhuñjatā tasya pituḥ saviṣā maṇḍilakā dattāḥ ātmanā nirviṣāḥ prabhakṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, while eating together with his father from one dish, he gave his father the poisoned maṇḍilakas, while he himself ate the unpoisoned ones.

children.text: yato 'sya pitā tān saviṣān maṇḍilakān bhakṣayitvā mṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then his father ate those poisoned maṇḍilakas and died.

children.text: tasya ca pituḥ kāladharmaṇā yuktasya ca dārako na kenacit pāpakaṃ karma kurvāṇo 'bhiśaṅkito vā pratisaṃvedito vā ||
children.translated_text: And when his father had met the law of death, the boy was neither suspected nor denounced by anyone as having committed an evil deed.

children.text: paścāttairiṣṭasnigdhasuhṛdbhirvaṇigbhiḥ śocayitvā yattattu kiṃcittasya vaṇijo bhāṇḍamāsīddhiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ vā tattasya dārakasya dattam ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, those merchants, dear, affectionate friends, mourned for him; and whatever goods that merchant had, whether silver or gold, they gave to that boy.

children.text: sa dārakastaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ gṛhya svagṛhamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The boy took that paternal merchandise, silver, and gold, and arrived at his own house.

children.text: tasya ca gatasya svagṛhaṃ sā mātā pracchannāsaddharmeṇa taṃ putraṃ paricaramāṇā ratiṃ nādhigacchaty anabhiratarūpā ca taṃ putraṃ vadati kiyatkālaṃ vayamevaṃ pracchannena krameṇa ratikrīḍāmanubhaviṣyāmo yannu vayamasmāddeśādanyadeśāntaraṃ gatvā prakāśakrameṇa niḥśaṅkā bhūtvā jāyāpatīti vikhyātadharmāṇaḥ sukhaṃ prativasema ||
children.translated_text: When he had gone to his own house, that mother, serving her son in secret illicit conduct, did not attain satisfaction; and, appearing dissatisfied, she said to her son, "How long shall we experience the sport of love in this hidden way? Rather, let us go from this region to another country and live happily without fear, openly known under the accepted status of wife and husband."

children.text: tatastau gṛhaṃ tyaktvā mitrasvajanasambandhivargānapahāya purāṇadāsīdāsakarmakarāṃstyaktvā yāvadarthajātaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ ca gṛhya anyaviṣayāntaraṃ gatau ||
children.translated_text: Then the two abandoned the house, left behind their friends, kinsmen, and circle of relations, abandoned the old female and male slaves and servants, took as much wealth and gold and silver as they needed, and went to another region.

children.text: tatra gatvā janapadeṣu vikhyāpayamānau jāyāṃpatikamiti ratikrīḍāmanubhavamānau vyavasthitau ||
children.translated_text: Having gone there, they made it known among the people, "We are wife and husband," and remained enjoying the sport of love.

children.text: yāvadarhan bhikṣuḥ kenacit kālāntareṇa janapadacārikāṃ caraṃs tamadhiṣṭhānamanuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Eventually, after some time, an <s>arhat</s> monk, wandering on a tour through the countryside, arrived at that town.

children.text: tena tatra piṇḍapātamanvāhiṇḍatā vīthyāṃ niṣadyāyaṃ vaṇigdharmaṇā saṃvyavahāramāṇaḥ sa dārako dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While he was going about there for alms, he saw that boy sitting in the street and conducting business according to the practice of a merchant.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā cārogyayitvā cābhibhāṣyokto mātuste kuśalam sa ca dārakastamarhantaṃ tathā abhivadamānamupaśrutya saṃbhinnacetāḥ svena duścaritena karmaṇā śaṅkitamanāścintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, greeted him, and addressed him, he said, "Is your mother well?" And when the boy heard the <s>arhat</s> addressing him in that way, his mind was troubled, and, anxious because of his own misconduct, he began to think.

children.text: sa vicintya mātṛsakāśaṃ gatvā saṃvedayati yatirabhyāgato yo 'sau asmadgṛhamupasaṃkrāmaty eṣa sa ihādhiṣṭhāne pratisaṃvedayiṣyati eṣā asya dārakasya māteti ||
children.translated_text: After thinking, he went to his mother and reported, "An ascetic has arrived, the one who approaches our house. Here in this town he will make it known: 'This is that boy's mother.'

children.text: vayaṃ ceha jāyāṃpatikamiti khyātau ||
children.translated_text: But here we are known as wife and husband.

children.text: kathameṣa śakyaṃ ghātayituṃ tatastayoḥ saṃcintya taṃ gṛhamenamupanimantrayitvā bhuñjānaṃ ghātayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How can this man be killed?" Then, after the two had considered, they thought, "Let us invite him into the house and kill him while he is eating."

children.text: tatastayorevaṃ saṃcintya so 'rhan bhikṣurantargṛhamupanimantrayitvā bhojayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After the two had considered in this way, they invited that <s>arhat</s> monk into the house and began to feed him.

children.text: sa dārako gūḍhaśastro bhūtvā arhantaṃ bhojayituṃ mātrā saha nirjanaṃ gṛhaṃ kṛtvā sa cārhadbhikṣurbhuktvā tasmādgṛhādviśrabdhacārakrameṇa pratinirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The boy, having concealed a weapon, prepared to feed the <s>arhat</s> together with his mother after making the house empty of people; and that <s>arhat</s> monk, having eaten, went out from that house with the confident gait of one moving freely.

children.text: tatastena dārakeṇainaṃ antargṛhaviśrabdhacārakramam avekṣya nirgacchantaṃ parāpṛṣṭhībhūtvā śarīre 'sya śastraṃ nipātya jīvitād vyaparopayati ||
children.translated_text: Then that boy watched him going out through the interior of the house with that confident gait, came behind him, struck his body with the weapon, and deprived him of life.

children.text: kāmāśca lavaṇodakasadṛśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And sensual pleasures are like salt water.

children.text: yathā yathā sevyanti tathā tathā tṛṣṇāvṛddhimupayānti ||
children.translated_text: The more they are enjoyed, the more they lead to the increase of thirst.

children.text: tasya dārakasya sā mātā taṃ putramasaddharmeṇānuvartamānā tasminnevādhiṣṭhāne śreṣṭhiputreṇa sārdhaṃ pracchannakāmā asaddharmeṣu saktacittā jātā ||
children.translated_text: That boy's mother, while following her son in illicit conduct, in that very town became secretly desirous of the son of a guild-master and attached in mind to illicit acts with him.

children.text: tasya dārakasya tathāvidha upakramaḥ pratisaṃviditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Such an undertaking of the boy's mother became known to him.

children.text: tatastena tasya māturuktam amba nivartasvedṛśāddoṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Then he said to his mother, "Mother, turn back from such a fault."

children.text: sā ca tasmiñ śreṣṭhiputre saṃraktacittā dvirapi trirapyucyamānā na nirvartate ||
children.translated_text: But she, her mind impassioned for that guild-master's son, did not desist, though told a second and a third time.

children.text: tatastena niṣkoṣamasiṃ kṛtvā sā mātā jīvitādvyaparopitā ||
children.translated_text: Then he drew a sword from its sheath and deprived that mother of life.

children.text: yadā tasya trīṇyānantaryāṇi paripūrṇāni tadā devatābhirjanapadeṣvārocitaṃ pāpa eṣa pitṛghātako 'rhadghātako mātṛghātakaśca ||
children.translated_text: When his three ānantarya crimes were complete, the deities announced among the people, "This wicked man is a patricide, a killer of an <s>arhat</s>, and a matricide.

children.text: trīṇyanenānantaryāṇi narakakarmasaṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni ||
children.translated_text: He has done and accumulated three ānantarya deeds, karmic acts that lead to hell."

children.text: tatastenādhiṣṭhānajanena tacchrutvā tadadhiṣṭhānānnirvāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the people of that town heard this, he was banished from that town.

children.text: sa yadā nirvāsitastasmādadhiṣṭhānāt tadā cintayituṃ pravṛtto 'sti cāsya buddhaśāsane kaścidevānunaya evaṃ manasi kṛtaṃ gacchāmi idānīṃ pravrajāmīti ||
children.translated_text: When he had been banished from that town, he began to think, "He still has some favorable inclination toward the Buddha's dispensation." Having formed this thought in his mind, he said, "I shall now go forth."

children.text: sa ca vihāraṃ gatvā bhikṣusakāśamupasaṃkramya evaṃ kathayaty ārya pravrajeyam ||
children.translated_text: He went to a monastery, approached the monks, and said, "Noble sir, I wish to go forth."

children.text: tatastena bhikṣuṇā uktaṃ mā tāvat pitṛghātako 'si tena bhikṣurabhihito 'sti mayā ghātitaḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: Then that monk said to him, "First, are you not a patricide?" The monk was told by him, "My father was killed by me."

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ pṛṣṭo mā tāvanmātṛghātako 'si tenoktam ārya ghātitā mayā mātā ||
children.translated_text: Then, when he was asked again, "Surely you are not a matricide?" he said, "Venerable sir, my mother was killed by me."

children.text: sa bhūyaḥ pṛṣṭo mā tāvadarhadvadhaste kṛtas tataḥ sa kathayaty arhannapi ghātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was asked once more, "Surely you have not committed the killing of an arhat?" Then he says, "An arhat too was killed."

children.text: tatastena bhikṣuṇābhihita ekaikena eṣāṃ karmaṇāmācaraṇānna pravrajyārho bhavasi prāgeva samastānām ||
children.translated_text: Then that monk said, "By the commission of even one of these acts you are not fit for ordination, much less by all of them together.

children.text: gaccha vatsa nāhaṃ pravrājayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Go, child. I will not ordain you."

children.text: tataḥ sa puruṣo 'nyasya bhikṣoḥ sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayaty ārya pravrajeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then that man approached another monk and said, "Venerable sir, I would go forth."

children.text: tatastenāpi bhikṣuṇā anupūrveṇa pṛṣṭvā pratyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after questioning him in order, that monk too rejected him.

children.text: tataḥ paścādanyasya bhikṣoḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that he went to the presence of another monk.

children.text: tamapi tathaiva pravrajyāmāyācate ||
children.translated_text: He begged him too for ordination in just the same way.

children.text: tenāpi tathā anupūrvakrameṇa pṛṣṭvā pratyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That monk too, after questioning him in the same sequential manner, rejected him.

children.text: sa yadā dvirapi trirapi pravrajyāmāyācamāno 'pi bhikṣubhir na pravrājitas tadā amarṣajātaścintayituṃ pravṛtto yā api sarvasādhāraṇā pravrajyā tāmahamapyāyācanna labhāmi ||
children.translated_text: When, though begging for ordination a second and even a third time, he was not ordained by the monks, he became indignant and began to think, "Even that ordination which is common to all, though I beg for it, I do not obtain."

children.text: tatastena tasmin vihāre śayitānāṃ bhikṣūṇāmagnirdattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he set fire to the monks who were sleeping in that monastery.

children.text: tasmin vihāre 'gniṃ dattvā anyatra vihāraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After setting fire to that monastery, he went to another monastery.

children.text: tatrāpi gatvā bhikṣūṇāmupasaṃkramya pravrajyāmāyācate ||
children.translated_text: Having gone there too, he approached the monks and begged for ordination.

children.text: tairapi tathaivānupūrveṇa pṛṣṭvā pratyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They too, after questioning him in just the same way and in order, rejected him.

children.text: tatrāpi tena tathaiva pratihatacetasā agnirdattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too, with his mind struck down in the same way, he set a fire.

children.text: tatrāpi vihāre bahavo bhikṣavaḥ śaikṣāśaikṣāśca dagdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that monastery too many monks, both trainees and adepts, were burned.

children.text: evaṃ tasyānekān vihārān dahataḥ sarvatra śabdo visṛta evaṃvidhaścaivaṃvidhaśca pāpakarmakārī puruṣo bhikṣubhyaḥ pravrajyāmalabhan vihārān bhikṣūṃśca dahatīti ||
children.translated_text: As he was burning many monasteries in this way, word spread everywhere: "A man of such and such a kind, a doer of evil deeds, failing to obtain ordination from the monks, is burning monasteries and monks."

children.text: sa ca puruṣo 'nyavihāraṃ prasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that man set out for another monastery.

children.text: tatra ca vihāre bodhisattvajātīyo bhikṣuḥ prativasati tṛpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that monastery there lived a monk born as a bodhisattva, <s>Tripiṭa</s>.

children.text: tena śrutaṃ sa evaṃ duṣkarakarmakārī puruṣa ihāgacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: He heard, "That very man, a doer of such difficult evil deeds, is coming here."

children.text: yataḥ sa bhikṣustasya puruṣasyāsamprāptasyaiva tasmin vihāre pratyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that monk went out to meet the man before he had even reached that monastery.

children.text: sa taṃ puruṣaṃ sametya kathayati bhadramukha kimetad yato 'sya puruṣeṇoktam ārya pravrajyāṃ na labhāmi ||
children.translated_text: Meeting that man, he said, "Good sir, what is this?" Then the man said, "Venerable sir, I do not obtain ordination."

children.text: tatastena bhikṣuṇoktam āgaccha vatsa ahaṃ te pravrājayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then that monk said, "Come, child. I will ordain you."

children.text: paścāt tena bhikṣuṇā tasya puruṣasya śiro muṇḍāpayitvā kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi dattāni ||
children.translated_text: Afterward that monk had the man's head shaved and gave him ocher robes.

children.text: paścāt sa puruṣaḥ kathayaty ārya śikṣāpadāni me 'nuprayaccha ||
children.translated_text: Then the man said, "Venerable sir, please give me the training precepts."

children.text: tatastena bhikṣuṇā uktaḥ kiṃ te śikṣāpadaiḥ prayojanam evaṃ sarvakālaṃ vadasva namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Then that monk said, "What need have you of training precepts? At all times say this: 'Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṅgha.'"

children.text: paścāt sa bhikṣustasya puruṣasya dharmadeśanāmārabdhaḥ kartum tvamevaṃvidhaścaivaṃvidhaśca pāpakarmakārī sattvo yadi kadācidbuddhaśabdaṃ śṛṇoṣi smṛtiṃ pratilabhethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward that monk began to give him a teaching of the Dharma: "You are a being who has done evil deeds of such and such a kind. If at any time you hear the word 'Buddha,' may you regain mindfulness."

children.text: athāsau tripiṭo bhikṣuścyutaḥ kālagato deveṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that monk <s>Tripiṭa</s> passed away, died, and was reborn among the gods.

children.text: sa cāpi puruṣaścyutaḥ kālagato narakeṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that man too passed away, died, and was reborn in the hells.

children.text: yato bhagavānāha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau atīte 'dhvani bhikṣus tripiṭa āsa ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? The monk <s>Tripiṭa</s> who lived in the past was I myself at that time and on that occasion.

children.text: yo 'sau pāpakarmakārī sattvo mātāpitrarhadghātakaḥ eṣa eva dharmaruciḥ ||
children.translated_text: That being who did evil deeds, the killer of his mother, father, and an arhat, is this very <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

children.text: idaṃ mama tṛtīye 'saṃkhyeye 'sya dharmarucerdarśanam ||
children.translated_text: This was my third seeing of this <s>Dharmaruci</s> in the third incalculable aeon.

children.text: tadahaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi cirasya dharmaruce sucirasya dharmaruce suciracirasya dharmaruce ||
children.translated_text: It is with reference to that that I say, 'After a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; after a very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; after an exceedingly long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>.'

children.text: yāvacca mayā bhikṣavastribhirasaṃkhyeyaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhiranyaiśca duṣkaraśatasahasrairanuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ samudānītā tāvadanena dharmarucinā yadbhūyasā narakatiryakṣu kṣapitam ||
children.translated_text: And while, monks, over three incalculable aeons, through the six perfections and through hundreds of thousands of other difficult deeds, I brought forth unsurpassed complete awakening, for that long this <s>Dharmaruci</s> spent his time mostly in hells and among animals."

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this. Glad at heart, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

children.text: Chapter 19
buddho bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the Bamboo Grove, at the squirrels' feeding place.

children.text: rājagṛhe nagare subhadro nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> there lived a householder named <s>Subhadra</s>, rich, with great wealth and great possessions.

children.text: so 'tyarthaṃ nirgrantheṣvabhiprasannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was exceedingly devoted to the <s>Nirgranthas</s>.

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam ||
children.translated_text: He brought a wife from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati ||
children.translated_text: Together with her he sported, delighted himself, and enjoyed pleasure.

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: As he sported, delighted himself, and enjoyed pleasure, after some time his wife became pregnant.

children.text: bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: In the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms.

children.text: rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caran yena subhadrasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Walking for alms in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, he approached the householder <s>Subhadra</s>'s residence.

children.text: adrākṣīt subhadro gṛhapatirbhagavantaṃ dūrādeva ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Subhadra</s> saw the Blessed One from afar.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ patnīmādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And, seeing him, he took his wife and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocad bhagavan iyaṃ me patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this wife of mine has become pregnant."

children.text: kiṃ janayiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "What will she give birth to?"

children.text: bhagavānāha gṛhapate putraṃ janayiṣyati kulamuddyotayiṣyati divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Householder, she will give birth to a son; he will illuminate the family, experience divine and human splendor, go forth under my teaching, and, through the abandonment of all defilements, directly realize arhatship."

children.text: tena bhagavataḥ śucinaḥ praṇītasya khādanīyabhojanīyasya pātrapūro dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he gave the Blessed One a bowlful of pure and excellent hard and soft food.

children.text: bhagavānārogya ityuktvā piṇḍapātamādāya prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, saying, "May there be health," took the alms-food and departed.

children.text: tasya nātidūre bhūrikastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Not far from him stood <s>Bhūrika</s>.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati yadapyasmākamekaṃ bhaikṣākulam tadapi śramaṇo gautamo 'nvāvartayati ||
children.translated_text: He reflected, "Even the one alms-family that belongs to us, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is taking over too.

children.text: gacchāmi paśyāmi kiṃ śramaṇena gautamena vyākṛtamiti ||
children.translated_text: I shall go and see what has been predicted by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: sa tatra gatvā kathayati gṛhapate śramaṇo gautama āgata āsīt āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He went there and said, "Householder, did the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come here?" "He came."

children.text: kiṃ tena vyākṛtam ārya mayā tasya patnī darśitā kiṃ janayiṣyati sa kathayati putraṃ janayiṣyati kulamuddyotayiṣyati divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "What did he predict?" "Ārya, I showed him my wife. 'What will she give birth to?' He said, 'She will give birth to a son; he will illuminate the family, experience divine and human splendor, go forth under my teaching, and, through the abandonment of all defilements, directly realize arhatship.'"

children.text: sa bhūriko gaṇitre kṛtāvī śvetavarṇāṃ gṛhītvā gaṇayitumārabdhaḥ paśyati yathā bhagavatā vyākṛtaṃ tatsarvaṃ tathaiva ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Bhūrika</s>, being skilled in calculation, took a white calculating mark and began to calculate; he saw that everything was just as the Blessed One had predicted.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati yadi anusaṃvarṇayiṣyāmyahaṃ gṛhapatirbhūyasyā mātrayā śramaṇasya gautamasyābhipraśaṃsyati ||
children.translated_text: He reflected, "If I confirm it, the householder will praise the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> all the more.

children.text: tadatra kiṃcid saṃvarṇayitavyaṃ kiṃcit vivarṇayitavyamiti viditvā hastau saṃparivartayati mukhaṃ ca vibhaṇḍayati ||
children.translated_text: So here something must be praised and something must be disparaged." Having understood this, he turned his hands about and distorted his face.

children.text: subhadro gṛhapatiḥ kathayati ārya kiṃ hastau saṃparivartayasi mukhaṃ ca vibhaṇḍayasīti sa kathayati gṛhapate atra kiṃcit satyaṃ kiṃcinmṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Subhadra</s> said, "Ārya, why do you turn your hands about and distort your face?" He said, "Householder, in this there is something true and something false."

children.text: ārya kiṃ satyaṃ kiṃ vā mṛṣā gṛhapate yadanenoktaṃ putraṃ janayiṣyatīti idaṃ satyaṃ kathayati ||
children.translated_text: "Ārya, what is true and what is false?" "Householder, when he said, 'She will give birth to a son,' this he spoke truly.

children.text: kulamuddyotayiṣyatītīdamapi satyam ||
children.translated_text: 'He will illuminate the family': this too is true.

children.text: agrajyotiriti saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: His name will be <s>Agrajyotis</s>.

children.text: mandabhāgyaḥ sa sattvo jātamātra evāgninā kulaṃ dhakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: That being is unfortunate: as soon as he is born, he will burn the family with fire.

children.text: yat kathayati divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatīti idaṃ mṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: When he says, 'He will experience divine and human splendor,' this is false.

children.text: gehapate asti kaścit tvayā dṛṣṭo manuṣyabhūto divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhavan yatkathayati mama śāsane pravrajiṣyatīti idaṃ satyam ||
children.translated_text: Householder, have you seen anyone born as a human experiencing divine and human splendor? When he says, 'He will go forth under my teaching,' this is true.

children.text: yadā asya na bhaktaṃ na vastram tadā niścayena śramaṇasya gautamasyāntike pravrajiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When he has neither food nor clothing, then he will certainly go forth in the presence of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti idaṃ mṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: 'He will directly realize arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements': this is false.

children.text: śramaṇasyaiva tāvadgautamasya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ nāsti prāgevāsya bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Even the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> himself has no arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements; how much less will this one have it?"

children.text: subhadro viṣādamāpannaḥ kathayati ārya atra mayā kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti bhūrikaḥ kathayati gṛhapate vayaṃ pravrajitāḥ śamānuśikṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> became despondent and said, "Ārya, how should I act in this matter?" <s>Bhūrika</s> said, "Householder, we are renunciants, training in calm.

children.text: tvameva jānīṣe ||
children.translated_text: You yourself know."

children.text: ityuktvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, he departed.

children.text: subhadraḥ saṃlakṣayati sarvathā parityājyo 'sau iti viditvā sa bhaiṣajyaṃ dātumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> reflected, "By all means that one must be gotten rid of." Having resolved this, he began to give medicine.

children.text: caramabhaviko 'sau sattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But that being was in his final existence.

children.text: tadasya bhaiṣajyārthāya syāditi ||
children.translated_text: "Let this be for him as medicine," he thought.

children.text: sa tasyā vāmakukṣiṃ marditumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He began to press her left side.

children.text: sa garbho dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The embryo went to the right side.

children.text: subhadro dakṣiṇakukṣiṃ marditumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> began to press the right side.

children.text: sa vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It went to the left side.

children.text: asthānametadanavakāśo yaccaramabhavikaḥ sattvo 'ntarāducchidya kālaṃ kariṣyati aprāpte āśravakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: It is impossible, there is no occasion, that a being in his final existence should be cut off in the meantime and die before attaining the destruction of the outflows.

children.text: sā gṛhapatipatnī kukṣiṇā mṛdyamānena vikroṣṭumārabdhā ||
children.translated_text: That householder's wife, while her belly was being pressed, began to cry out.

children.text: prātiveśyaiḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: The neighbors heard it.

children.text: te tvaritatvaritaṃ gatāḥ pṛcchanti bhavantaḥ kimiyaṃ gṛhapatipatnī virauti subhadraḥ kathayati kukṣimatyeṣā ||
children.translated_text: They went in great haste and asked, "Sirs, why is this householder's wife crying out?" <s>Subhadra</s> said, "She is pregnant.

children.text: nūnamasyāḥ prasavakāla iti ||
children.translated_text: Surely it is her time for giving birth."

children.text: te prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They departed.

children.text: subhadraḥ saṃlakṣayati na śakyamasyā atropasaṃkramaṃ kartum ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> reflected, "It is not possible to approach her here.

children.text: araṇyaṃ nayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: I shall take her to the forest."

children.text: sā tenāraṇyaṃ nītvā tathopakrāntā yathā kālagatā ||
children.translated_text: He took her to the forest and attacked her in such a way that she died.

children.text: sa tāṃ pracchannaṃ gṛhamānīya suhṛtsambandhibāndhavānāṃ prātiveśakānāṃ ca kathayati bhavantaḥ patnī me kālagateti ||
children.translated_text: Then he secretly brought her home and said to his friends, relations, kinsmen, and neighbors, "Sirs, my wife has died."

children.text: te vikroṣṭumārabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They began to cry out in lamentation.

children.text: sā tairvikrośadbhir nīlapītalohitāvadātairvastraiḥ śibikāmalaṃkṛtya śītavanaṃ śmaśānamabhinirhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: While they were lamenting, they adorned a bier with blue, yellow, red, and white cloths and carried her out to the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground.

children.text: nirgranthaiḥ śrutaṃ te hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditāśchatrapatākā ucchrayitvā rājagṛhasya nagarasya rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭake upāhiṇḍamānā ārocayanti śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nirgranthas</s> heard of it, and they, delighted, pleased, and joyful, raised parasols and banners and, wandering through the roads, streets, squares, and crossroads of the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, announced, "Listen, sirs!

children.text: śramaṇena gautamena subhadrasya gṛhapateḥ patnī vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati kulamuddyotayiṣyati divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> predicted of the wife of the householder <s>Subhadra</s>: 'She will give birth to a son; he will illuminate the family, experience divine and human splendor, go forth under my teaching, and directly realize arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements.'"

children.text: sā ca kālagatā śītavanaśmaśānamabhinirhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: And she died and was carried out to the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground.

children.text: yasya tāvadvṛkṣamūlameva nāsti kutastasya śākhāpatraphalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti atrāntare nāsti kiṃcidbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāmajñātamadṛṣṭamaviditamavijñātam ||
children.translated_text: For one who does not even have the root of a tree, how will there be branches, leaves, and fruit? Meanwhile, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unlearned, or unrecognized by the blessed Buddhas.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānām ṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ caturvaiśāradyaviśāradānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānām asaṃhatavihāriṇāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trirdivasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kamahamapāyāduddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyaṃ kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam ||
children.translated_text: For it is the nature of the blessed Buddhas, who are greatly compassionate, who act for the benefit of the world, who have a single protection, who dwell in calm and insight, who are skilled in the three bases of taming, who have crossed the four floods, whose feet are well planted on the bases of miraculous power, who have long familiarity with the four means of gathering, who are confident in the four fearlessnesses, who have abandoned the five factors, who have passed beyond the five destinies, who are endowed with the six qualities, who have fulfilled the six perfections, who dwell unimpeded, who are rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, who teach the eightfold path, who are skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abidings, who are mighty with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and who surpass the lords of hundreds of hundreds, to survey the world three times by night and three times by day with the Buddha-eye, and for knowledge and vision to arise: Who is declining? Who is increasing? Who has come into difficulty? Who has come into danger? Who has come into distress? Who has come into difficulty, danger, and distress? Who inclines toward the lower realms? Who slopes toward the lower realms? Who is bent toward the lower realms? Whom shall I lift up from the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation? Whose unplanted roots of good shall I plant? Whose planted roots of good shall I mature? Whose matured roots of good shall I liberate?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apyevātikramedvelāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of makaras, might indeed overstep its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velāmatikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha would not overstep the proper time for the dear beings to be trained.

children.text: atha bhagavānanyatarasmin pradeśe smitamakārṣīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One smiled in a certain place.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: It is the nature of the blessed Buddhas that, at the time when they reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white flames issue from their mouth; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastādgacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhavamutpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakaṃ gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ||
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhava</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells among them, they fall cooled.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that, the particular torments of those beings are allayed.

children.text: teṣāmevaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ āhosvidanyatropapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: They think, 'Have we, good sirs, died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati ||
children.translated_text: To generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃ bhavati na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ nāpyanyatropapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the emanation, they think, 'Surely we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn somewhere else.

children.text: api tvayamapūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvādasmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti ||
children.translated_text: Rather, this is a being never seen before; through his power our particular torments have been allayed.'

children.text: te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya tannarakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Having gained serene faith toward that emanation, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become fit vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭādgacchanti tāścāturmahārājakāyikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitānnirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānatapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhān devān gatvā duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmetyudghoṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: Those that go upward go to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> class, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, and they proclaim: 'Suffering is empty and without self.'

children.text: gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: And they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: Begin, go forth, apply yourselves in the teaching of the Buddha;

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: shake off the army of death like an elephant a reed hut.

children.text: yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever lives heedfully in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, will make an end of suffering.

children.text: atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti ||
children.translated_text: Then those flames, after wandering through the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, follow the Blessed One from behind, from behind.

children.text: bhagavata āsye 'ntarhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They disappeared into the Blessed One's mouth.

children.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with joined palms, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: A mass, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises.

children.text: gāthāśca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: The Buddhas, whose becoming has passed away, who have abandoned wretchedness and pride, are the supreme cause in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Jinas, conquerors of enemies, do not show without cause a smile white like a conch and lotus-fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīrabuddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇajinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood the occasion with firm wisdom, O ascetic lord of Jinas, for the listeners who long to know,

children.text: dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O steadfast bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with steadfast, excellent, and auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
children.translated_text: The steadfast, perfectly awakened ones, firm as the king of mountains and the salt-water ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti nāthāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people long to hear that thing for whose sake the Lords show a smile.

children.text: bhagavānāha evametadānanda evametat ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetupratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Not without a cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>arhats</s>, perfectly awakened Buddhas, reveal a smile.

children.text: gaccha ānanda bhikṣūṇāmārocaya tathāgato bhikṣavaḥ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the monks: "Monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> wishes to go on a cemetery round."

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantum sa cīvarakāṇi gṛhṇātu ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you is able to go on the cemetery round together with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take his robe-cloths.

children.text: evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati tathāgata āyuṣmantaḥ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, venerable sir," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One, and he announced to the monks, "Venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> wishes to go on a cemetery round.

children.text: yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantum sa cīvarakāṇi gṛhṇātu ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you is able to go on the cemetery round together with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take his robe-cloths."

children.text: evamāyuṣmanniti te bhikṣavaḥ sarve saṃśrutya bhagavatsakāśamupagatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, venerable sir," all those monks agreed, and they approached the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gajarāja iva kalabhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭrigaṇaparivṛto haṃsarāja iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto deśika ivādhvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva paurajanaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaścakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaścandra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛto vemacitrīvāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛto brahmeva brahmakāyikaparivṛtaḥ stimita iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntairindriyair asaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛto 'śītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātro vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtamūrtiḥ sūryasahasrātirekaprabho jaṅgama iva ratnaparvataḥ samantato bhadrako daśabhirbalaiścaturbhirvaiśāradyaistribhirāveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānairmahākaruṇayā ca samanvāgata ājñātakauṇḍinyāśvajidbāṣpamahānāmabhadrikaśāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapayaśaḥpūrṇaprabhṛtimahāśrāvakaiḥ parivṛto 'nyena ca mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena anekaiśca prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ śītavanaṃ mahāśmaśānaṃ samprasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, tamed and surrounded by a tamed retinue, peaceful and surrounded by a peaceful retinue, liberated and surrounded by a liberated retinue, confident and surrounded by a confident retinue, disciplined and surrounded by a disciplined retinue, an <s>arhat</s> surrounded by <s>arhats</s>, free from passion and surrounded by those free from passion, inspiring and surrounded by an inspiring retinue, like a bull surrounded by a herd of cattle, like a royal elephant surrounded by a group of young elephants, like a lion surrounded by fanged beasts, like a royal goose surrounded by a flock of geese, like <s>Suparṇin</s> surrounded by birds, like a Brahmin surrounded by pupils, like a good physician surrounded by the sick, like a hero surrounded by warriors, like a guide surrounded by travelers, like a caravan leader surrounded by merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by townspeople, like a king surrounded by ministers, like a
