children.text: athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirbhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder, knowing from the Blessed One's silence that he had accepted, bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, rose from his seat, and departed.

children.text: aśrauṣīdbandhumān rājā vipaśyī samyaksambuddho dvāṣaṣṭibhikṣusahasraparivāro janapadacārikāṃ caran bandhumatīmanuprāpto bandhumatyāṃ viharati bandhumatīye dāve iti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Bandhumān</s> heard, "<s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, attended by a retinue of sixty-two thousand monks, has come to <s>Bandhumatī</s> while wandering on a tour through the countryside, and is staying at <s>Bandhumatī</s>, in the <s>Bandhumatī</s> grove."

children.text: śrutvā ca punarasyaitadabhavad bahuśo mayā bhagavānantargṛhe upanimantrya bhojitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After hearing this, the thought occurred to him: "Many times I have invited the Blessed One into my house and fed him.

children.text: na tu kadācit traimāsīṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But never have I provided for him for three months with all the requisites.

children.text: yannvahaṃ vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayeyam ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to provide for <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, with all the requisites?"

children.text: iti viditvā yena vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having understood this, he went to where <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, was.

children.text: upasaṃkramya vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gone there, he bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ bandhumantaṃ rājānaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: As King <s>Bandhumān</s> was seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed him, moved him to undertake, stirred him, and gladdened him with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: After instructing him, moving him to undertake, stirring him, and gladdening him in many ways with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>, he became silent.

children.text: atha bandhumān rājā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocad adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃstraimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bandhumān</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with joined palms toward <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and said this to him: "May the Blessed One accept from me for three months robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines and requisites for the sick, together with the community of monks."

children.text: upanimantrito 'smi mahārāja tvatprathamato 'naṅgaṇena gṛhapatinā ||
children.translated_text: "Great king, I have already been invited before you by <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder."

children.text: adhivāsayatu bhagavān ahaṃ tathā kariṣye yathā anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirājñāsyati ||
children.translated_text: "Let the Blessed One accept. I shall act in such a way that <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder will consent."

children.text: sacet te mahārāja anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiranujānīte evaṃ te 'hamadhivāsayāmi ||
children.translated_text: "Great king, if <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder permits you, then I accept from you."

children.text: atha bandhumān rājā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrānto yena svaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bandhumān</s> bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, rose from his seat, departed, and went to his own residence.

children.text: bandhumān rājā anaṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ dūtena prakrośyedamavocad yatkhalu gṛhapate jānīyād ahaṃ tvatprathamato vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhojayāmi tataḥ paścāt tavāpi na duṣkaraṃ bhaviṣyati vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhojayitumiti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Bandhumān</s> had <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder summoned by a messenger and said this: "Householder, you should know this: I shall feed <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, before you; afterward it will not be difficult for you also to feed <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha."

children.text: sa kathayati deva mayā vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastvatprathamata upanimantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Your Majesty, <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, was invited by me before you.

children.text: ahameva bhojayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I myself shall feed him."

children.text: rājā kathayati gṛhapate yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi tvaṃ mama viṣayanivāsī ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "Householder, even if that is so, still you live in my domain."

children.text: nārhāmyahaṃ tvatprathamato bhojayitum deva yadyapyahaṃ tava viṣayanivāsī tathāpi yena pūrvanimantritaḥ sa eva bhojayati ||
children.translated_text: "Your Majesty, it is not fitting that I should feed him only after you. Although I live in your domain, still the one by whom he was first invited is the very one who feeds him.

children.text: nātra devasya nirbandho yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your Majesty's insistence is not proper in this matter."

children.text: na te gṛhapate kāmakāraṃ dadāmi ||
children.translated_text: "Householder, I do not give you freedom to do as you wish.

children.text: api tu yo bhaktottarikayā jeṣyati so 'vaśiṣṭaṃ kālaṃ bhojayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Rather, whoever wins by the superiority of the meal will feed him for the remaining time."

children.text: tathā bhavatu ityanaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
children.translated_text: "So be it," <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder agreed.

children.text: tathā anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāyodakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, that very night <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> the householder gathered pure and excellent foods to be eaten and meals to be consumed, rose very early, set out the water-jars, and announced the time to the Blessed One by messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. Let the Blessed One now consider the time appropriate."

children.text: atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto yenānaṅgaṇasya gṛhapaterbhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, dressed in the forenoon, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks, went to the meal-offering of the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared in front of the community of monks.

children.text: athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, satisfied and fully served them with his own hand with pure, excellent foods to be chewed and eaten.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: After satisfying and fully serving them in many ways with pure, excellent foods to be chewed and eaten, and knowing that the Blessed One had eaten, had washed his hands, and had put away his bowl, he took a lower seat and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddho 'naṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, instructed, enjoined, encouraged, and gladdened the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After instructing, encouraging, and gladdening him in many ways with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>, he departed.

children.text: evaṃ bandhumatā rājñā bhojitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this same way he was fed by King <s>Bandhumān</s>.

children.text: eṣa eva grantho vistareṇa kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This same passage is to be supplied in detail.

children.text: na kvacidbhaktottarikayā parājayati ||
children.translated_text: He was nowhere defeated in the contest over meal-offerings.

children.text: tato bandhumān rājā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bandhumān</s>, placing his cheek in his hand, remained absorbed in thought.

children.text: amātyāḥ kathayanti deva kasmāt tvaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparastiṣṭhasīti sa kathayati bhavantaḥ kathamahaṃ na cintāparastiṣṭhāmi yo 'haṃ mama viṣayanivāsinaṃ kuṭumbinaṃ na śaknomi bhaktottarikayā parājayitum te kathayanti deva tasya gṛhapateḥ kāṣṭhaṃ nāsti ||
children.translated_text: The ministers said, "Your Majesty, why do you stand with your cheek in your hand, absorbed in thought?" He said, "Gentlemen, how could I not stand absorbed in thought, when I cannot defeat a householder dwelling in my own realm in a contest over meal-offerings?" They said, "Your Majesty, that householder has no firewood.

children.text: kāṣṭhavikrayo vidhāryatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Let the sale of firewood be prohibited."

children.text: rājñā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam ||
children.translated_text: The king had a proclamation made by bell.

children.text: bhavanto na kenacit madviṣayanivāsinā kāṣṭhaṃ vikretavyam ||
children.translated_text: "Gentlemen, no one dwelling in my realm is to sell firewood.

children.text: yo vikrīṇīte tena madviṣaye na vastavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever sells it is not to live in my realm."

children.text: anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirgandhakāṣṭhairbhaktaṃ sādhayitumārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> began to prepare the meal with fragrant wood.

children.text: sugandhatailena ca vastrāṇi tīmayitvā khādyakānyullāḍayitum ||
children.translated_text: And, after moistening cloths with fragrant oil, he began to prepare delicacies.

children.text: surabhiṇā gandhena sarvā bandhumatī nagarī sphuṭā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: The whole city of <s>Bandhumatī</s> became filled with a fragrant scent.

children.text: bandhumān rājā pṛcchati bhavantaḥ kuta eṣa manojñagandha iti tairvistareṇa samākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Bandhumān</s> asked, "Gentlemen, from where does this delightful scent come?" They explained it to him in detail.

children.text: sa kathayati ahamapyevaṃ karomi ||
children.translated_text: He said, "I too will do this.

children.text: kiṃ mama vibhavo nāstīti amātyāḥ kathayanti deva kasyārthe evaṃ kriyate ayaṃ gṛhapatiraputro nacirāt kālaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Do I lack wealth?" The ministers said, "Your Majesty, for what purpose is this being done? This householder has no son, and before long he will die.

children.text: devasyaiva sarvaṃ santaḥsvāpateyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: All the property stored inside will belong to Your Majesty alone.

children.text: kāṣṭhavikrayo 'nujñāsyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the sale of firewood be permitted."

children.text: tena kāṣṭhavikrayo 'nujñātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sale of firewood was permitted by him.

children.text: anaṅgaṇena gṛhapatinā śrutaṃ rājñā kāṣṭhavikrayo 'nujñāta iti ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> heard that the sale of firewood had been permitted by the king.

children.text: tena cittaṃ pradūṣya kharā vāṅ niścāritā tāvanme bhaktakāṣṭhamasti yenāham enaṃ sahāmātyaṃ citāmāropya dhmāpayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: With his mind defiled, he uttered harsh words: "I have enough firewood for the meal that I could set this man, together with his ministers, upon a funeral pyre and burn them."

children.text: rājā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king, placing his cheek in his hand, remained absorbed in thought.

children.text: amātyāḥ kathayanti deva kimarthaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparastiṣṭhasīti tena vistareṇa samākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: The ministers said, "Your Majesty, why do you stand with your cheek in your hand, absorbed in thought?" He explained the matter to them in detail.

children.text: te kathayanti deva alaṃ viṣādena ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Your Majesty, enough of despondency.

children.text: vayaṃ tathā kariṣyāmo yathā devaścānaṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ parājayatīti ||
children.translated_text: We shall act in such a way that Your Majesty defeats the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>."

children.text: tairaparasmin divase bandhumatī rājadhānī apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhalyā vyavasthāpitā candanavāripariṣiktā surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddhā āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpā ucchritadhvajapatākā nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇā nandanavanodyānasadṛśā ||
children.translated_text: On the next day they arranged the capital <s>Bandhumatī</s> with stones, gravel, and potsherds removed, sprinkled with sandal-water, furnished with vessels of fragrant incense, adorned with hanging cloth garlands and festoons, with standards and banners raised, strewn with many kinds of flowers, and resembling the pleasure grove <s>Nandana</s>.

children.text: tatpratispardhaśobhāvibhūṣito maṇḍavāṭaḥ kāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A pavilion was made, adorned with beauty that rivaled that splendor.

children.text: tasmin nānāratnavibhūṣitāsanavasanasampannaśobhāsanaprajñaptiḥ kāritā ||
children.translated_text: In it they had a beautiful arrangement of seats made, furnished with seats and coverings adorned with many jewels.

children.text: mṛduviśadasurabhigandhasampanno vividhabhaktavyañjanasahito divyasudhāmanojñasaṃkāśas trailokyaguroranurūpa āhāra upasamanvāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Food was brought there, endowed with soft, clear, fragrant scents, accompanied by various dishes and condiments, resembling delightful divine nectar, and suitable for the teacher of the three worlds.

children.text: tato bandhumān rājā dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bandhumān</s>, seeing it, was filled with the highest amazement.

children.text: tato vismayāvarjitacittasaṃtatirvipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya dūtena kālamārocayati samaye bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, his stream of thought overcome by amazement, he announced the time to <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, by a messenger: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. Let the Blessed One now consider the time."

children.text: atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena bandhumato rājño bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, dressed in the forenoon, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks with the community of monks before him, went to the meal-offering of King <s>Bandhumān</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared in front of the community of monks.

children.text: bandhumato rājño maṅgalyābhiṣeko hastināgo vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya śataśalākaṃ chatramupari mūrdhno dhārayati avaśiṣṭā hastināgā bhikṣūṇām ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Bandhumān</s>'s auspiciously consecrated elephant held a parasol with a hundred ribs above the head of <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha; the remaining elephants held them for the monks.

children.text: bandhumato rājño 'gramahiṣī vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sauvarṇena maṇivālavyajanena vījayati avaśiṣṭā antaḥpurikā avaśiṣṭānāṃ bhikṣūṇām ||
children.translated_text: The chief queen of King <s>Bandhumat</s> fanned <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, with a golden jeweled yak-tail fan, and the remaining women of the inner apartments fanned the remaining monks.

children.text: anaṅgaṇena gṛhapatinā avacarakaḥ puruṣaḥ preṣito gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa paśya kīdṛśenāhāreṇa bandhumān rājā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayatīti ||
children.translated_text: The householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> sent an attendant man: "Go, good man, and see with what sort of food King <s>Bandhumat</s> is feeding the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks) headed by the Buddha."

children.text: sa gatastāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāvarjitamanāstatraivāvasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He went, saw that splendor, and, his mind overcome with amazement, remained right there.

children.text: evaṃ dvitīyaḥ tṛtīyaḥ preṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way a second and a third were sent.

children.text: so 'pi tatraiva gatvā avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too went there and remained right there.

children.text: tato 'naṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ svayameva gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> himself went.

children.text: so 'pi tāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ viṣādamāpannaḥ saṃlakṣayati śakyamanyat saṃpādayitum ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that splendor, he too fell into deep despondency and thought, "It is possible to provide something else;

children.text: kiṃtu hastināmantaḥpurasya ca kuto mama vibhava iti viditvā niveśanaṃ gato dauvārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate bhoḥ puruṣa yadi kaścidyācanaka āgacchati sa yat prārthayate taddātavyaṃ no tu praveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but where could I have the means for elephants and for the women's quarters?" Knowing this, he went to his house and addressed the doorkeeper: "Good man, if any beggar comes, whatever he asks for must be given, but entry must not be given."

children.text: ityuktvā śokāgāraṃ praviśya avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, he entered the chamber of sorrow and remained there.

children.text: śakrasya devendrasyādhastāt jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: A knowledge and vision directed downward arose in <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: sa saṃlakṣayati ye kecilloke dakṣiṇīyā vipaśyī samyaksambuddhasteṣāmagro dānapatīnāmapyanaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He thought, "Of all those in the world who are worthy of offerings, <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, is the foremost; and among donors, the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> is foremost.

children.text: sāhāyyamasya kalpayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Assistance must be arranged for him."

children.text: iti viditvā kauśiko brāhmaṇaveṣamabhinirmāya yenānaṅgaṇasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, <s>Kauśika</s> fashioned the appearance of a brahmin and approached the house of the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya dauvārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa anaṅgaṇasya gṛhapateḥ kathaya kauśikagotro brāhmaṇo dvāre tiṣṭhati bhavantaṃ draṣṭukāma iti ||
children.translated_text: After approaching, he addressed the doorkeeper: "Go, good man, and tell the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>: 'A brahmin of the <s>Kauśika</s> lineage is standing at the door and wishes to see you.'"

children.text: sa kathayati brāhmaṇa gṛhapatinā ahaṃ sthāpito yaḥ kaścid yācanaka āgacchati sa yat prārthayate taddātavyaṃ na tu praveśa iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Brahmin, I have been stationed by the householder with the order: 'If any beggar comes, whatever he asks for must be given, but entry must not be given.'

children.text: yena te prayojanaṃ tadgṛhītvā gaccha ||
children.translated_text: Take what you need and go."

children.text: kiṃ te gṛhapatinā dṛṣṭeneti sa kathayati bhoḥ puruṣa na mama kenacit prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: "What need have you of seeing the householder?" He said, "Good man, I have no need of anything.

children.text: ahaṃ gṛhapatimeva draṣṭukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish only to see the householder."

children.text: gaccheti ||
children.translated_text: "Go," he said.

children.text: tenānaṅgaṇasya gṛhapatergatvā niveditam ārya kauśikasagotro brāhmaṇo dvāre tiṣṭhati āryaṃ draṣṭukāma iti ||
children.translated_text: He went to the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> and reported, "Noble sir, a brahmin of the <s>Kauśika</s> lineage is standing at the door and wishes to see you, noble sir."

children.text: sa kathayati gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa yena tasya prayojanaṃ tat prayaccha kiṃ tenātra praviṣṭeneti sa kathayati ārya ukto mayā evaṃ kathayati nāhaṃ kiṃcit prārthayāmi api tu gṛhapatimeva draṣṭukāma iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Go, good man, and give him what he needs. What is the use of his entering here?" The man said, "Noble sir, I spoke to him, and he says this: 'I do not ask for anything; rather, I wish only to see the householder.'"

children.text: sa kathayati bhoḥ puruṣa yadyevam praveśaya ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Good man, if that is so, let him enter."

children.text: sa tena praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was brought in by him.

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati kasmāt tvaṃ gṛhapate kare kapolaṃ cintāparastiṣṭhasīti sa gṛhapatirgāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: The brahmin said, "Householder, why do you stand there with your cheek in your hand, absorbed in thought?" Then the householder spoke a verse:

children.text: na tasya kathayecchokaṃ yaḥ śokānna pramocayet
children.translated_text: One should not tell one's sorrow to one who would not free one from sorrow;

children.text: tasmai tu kathayecchokaṃ yaḥ śokātsaṃpramocayet ||
children.translated_text: but one should tell one's sorrow to one who would completely free one from sorrow.

children.text: śakraḥ kathayati gṛhapate kastava śokaḥ kathaya ahaṃ te śokātpramocayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said, "Householder, what is your sorrow? Tell me; I will free you from your sorrow."

children.text: tena vistareṇa samākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: He explained it in full.

children.text: atha śakro devendraḥ kauśikabrāhmaṇarūpamantardhāpya svarūpeṇa sthitvā kathayati gṛhapate viśvakarmā te devaputraḥ sāhāyyaṃ kalpayiṣyatītyuktvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, made the form of the <s>Kauśika</s> brahmin disappear, stood in his own form, and said, "Householder, the godling <s>Viśvakarman</s> will arrange assistance for you." Having said this, he departed.

children.text: atha śakro devendro devāṃstrāyastriṃśān gatvā viśvakarmāṇaṃ devaputramāmantrayate gaccha viśvakarman anaṅgaṇasya gṛhapateḥ sāhāyyaṃ kalpaya ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, went to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and addressed the godling <s>Viśvakarman</s>: "Go, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, arrange assistance for the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>."

children.text: paraṃ bhadraṃ tava kauśiketi viśvakarmaṇā devaputreṇa śakrasya devendrasya pratiśrutya āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "Very well, <s>Kauśika</s>; may there be supreme good for you," the godling <s>Viśvakarman</s> assented to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and came.

children.text: prativiśiṣṭatarā nagaraśobhā nirmitā divyo maṇḍalavāṭo divyāsanaprajñaptirdivya āhāraḥ samanvāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A city-splendor surpassing the other was created: a divine circular enclosure, a divine arrangement of seats, and divine food were brought together.

children.text: airāvaṇo nāgarājo vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya śataśalākaṃ chatramupari mūrdhno dhārayati avaśiṣṭā nāgā avaśiṣṭānāṃ bhikṣūṇām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, king of nāgas, held a parasol with a hundred ribs above the head of <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and the remaining nāgas held them above the remaining monks.

children.text: śacī devakanyā vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sauvarṇena maṇivālavyajanena vījayati avaśiṣṭā apsaraso bhikṣūn ||
children.translated_text: The divine maiden <s>Śacī</s> fanned <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, with a golden jeweled yak-tail fan, and the remaining apsarases fanned the monks.

children.text: bandhumatā rājñā avacarakaḥ puruṣaḥ preṣito gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa kīdṛśenāhāreṇānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatir buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ tarpayatīti sa puruṣastatra gatastāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā tatraiva avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Bandhumat</s> sent an attendant man: "Go, good man, and see with what sort of food the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> is satisfying the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the Buddha." That man went there, saw that splendor, and remained right there.

children.text: tenāmātyaḥ preṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A minister was sent by him.

children.text: so 'pi tatraivāvasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too remained right there.

children.text: kumāraḥ preṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The prince was sent.

children.text: so 'pi tatraivāvasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too remained right there.

children.text: tato bandhumān rājā svayameva taddvāraṃ gatvā avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bandhumat</s> himself went to that door and stood there.

children.text: vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ kathayati gṛhapate bandhumān rājā dṛṣṭasatyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, said, "Householder, King <s>Bandhumat</s> has seen the truth.

children.text: tasyāntike tvayā kharavākkarma niścāritam ||
children.translated_text: In his presence you uttered a harsh act of speech.

children.text: sa eva dvāre tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: He himself is standing at the door.

children.text: gaccha kṣamayeti ||
children.translated_text: Go and ask his forgiveness."

children.text: tenāsau nirgatya kṣamita uktaśca mahārāja praviśa svahastena pariveṣaṇaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: Then, having gone out, he asked his pardon and said, "Great king, enter and serve the meal with your own hand."

children.text: sa praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He entered.

children.text: paśyati divyāṃ vibhūtim ||
children.translated_text: He saw a divine splendor.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ kathayati gṛhapate tvamevaiko 'rhasi dine dine buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayituṃ na vayam iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing it, he was overcome with great amazement and said, "Householder, you alone are able to feed the community of monks headed by the Buddha day after day; we are not."

children.text: athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirvipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhamanayā vibhūtyā traimāsyaṃ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdho yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kārā kṛtā anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeyaṃ divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaveyam evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām evaṃvidhameva śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, having satisfied <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, for three months with this splendor and with excellent food, fell at his feet and began to make an aspiration: "By this root of merit from the service I have performed for such a true recipient of offerings, may I be born in a family that is rich, possessing great wealth and great enjoyments; may I experience divine and human prosperity; may I obtain qualities such as these; may I please just such a teacher and not displease him."

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau anaṅgaṇo nāma gṛhapatir eṣa evāsau jyotiṣkaḥ kulaputrastena kālena tena samayena ||
children.translated_text: "What do you think, monks? The householder named <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> at that time and on that occasion was this very <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, the son of good family.

children.text: yadanena bandhumato rājño dṛṣṭasatyasyāntike kharā vāṅniścāritā tasya karmaṇo vipākena pañcaśatāni samātṛkaścitāyāmāropya dhmāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he uttered harsh speech in the presence of King <s>Bandhumat</s>, who had seen the truths, as the ripening of that karma he was placed on a pyre and burned five hundred times together with his mother.

children.text: yāvadetarhi api citāmāropya dhmāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even now, too, he was placed on a pyre and burned.

children.text: yadvipaśyini tathāgate kārāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he performed service for the Tathāgata <s>Vipaśyin</s> and made an aspiration, as the ripening of that karma he was born in a family that was rich, possessing great wealth and great enjoyments.

children.text: divyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā ||
children.translated_text: Divine and human prosperity appeared for him.

children.text: mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Having gone forth in my teaching, through the abandonment of all defilements he realized arhatship.

children.text: ahamanena vipaśyinā samyaksambuddhena sārdhaṃ samajavaḥ samabalaḥ samadhuraḥ samasāmānyaprāptaḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I, as a teacher equal in vigor, equal in strength, equal in bearing, and attaining the same common rank as <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, was pleased by him, not displeased.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipāka ekāntaśuklānāmekāntaśuklo vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, for actions that are wholly black the ripening is wholly black; for actions that are wholly white it is wholly white; for mixed actions it is mixed.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, abandoning actions that are wholly black, and mixed actions too, attention should be directed only to actions that are wholly white.

children.text: ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, you should train yourselves."

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 20
evaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard.

children.text: ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s park, together with a great community of monks, with twelve and a half hundred monks.

children.text: satkṛto bhagavān gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito bhikṣubhirbhikṣuṇībhirupāsakairupāsikābhī rājabhī rājamātrair nānātīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakair devair nāgairyakṣairasurairgaruḍairgandharvaiḥ kinnarairmahoragaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One was honored, highly regarded, respected, and worshiped by monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, ascetics, brahmins, itinerants, and wanderers of various other sects, and by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.

children.text: lābhī bhagavān prabhūtānāṃ praṇītānāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ divyānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One obtained abundant and excellent requisites: robes, almsfood, beds and seats, and medicines and supplies for illness, both divine and human.

children.text: taiśca bhagavān anupaliptaḥ padmamiva vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One was unstained by them, like a lotus by water.

children.text: bhagavataścāyamevaṃrūpo digvidikṣu udārakalyāṇakīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgata ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: And this noble, auspicious sound and verse of fame concerning the Blessed One had arisen through the quarters and intermediate quarters: "Thus, he is the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One."

children.text: sa imaṃ sadevakaṃ lokaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ saśramaṇabrāhmaṇīṃ prajāṃ sadevamānuṣīṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayamabhijñāya sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya pravedayate ||
children.translated_text: Having directly known, realized, and entered this world with its gods, with <s>Māra</s>, with <s>Brahmā</s>, this population with its ascetics and brahmins and with its gods and humans, he proclaims it in this very life.

children.text: sa dharmaṃ deśayati ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye paryavasāne kalyāṇam ||
children.translated_text: He teaches the Dharma, good at the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end.

children.text: svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati ||
children.translated_text: He reveals the brahmacarya, good in meaning and good in expression, entire, complete, pure, and perfectly clear.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma sacedbhikṣavaḥ sattvā jānīyurdānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākaṃ yathāhaṃ jānāmi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam apīdānīm yo 'sau apaścimaḥ kavaḍaś carama ālopas tato 'pyadattvā asaṃvibhajya na paribhuñjīran sacellabheran dakṣiṇīyaṃ pratigrāhakam ||
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, if beings knew the fruit of giving and the resultant fruit of sharing gifts as I know the fruit of giving and the resultant fruit of sharing gifts, then even this last morsel, the final mouthful, they would not consume without giving from it and without sharing it, if they could obtain a worthy recipient to receive it.

children.text: na caiṣāmutpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: Nor would arisen stinginess take hold of their mind and remain there.

children.text: yasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ sattvā na jānante dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākaṃ yathāhaṃ jānāmi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākaṃ tasmāddhetor adattvā asaṃvibhajya paribhujyante āgṛhītena cetasā ||
children.translated_text: But since, monks, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the resultant fruit of sharing gifts as I know the fruit of giving and the resultant fruit of sharing gifts, for that reason they consume without giving and without sharing, with a grasping mind.

children.text: utpannaṃ caiṣāṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: And arisen stinginess takes hold of their mind and remains there.

children.text: tatkasya hetor bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani rājābhūt kanakavarṇo nāma abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paramayā suvarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? Monks, in the past, in a former time, there was a king named <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, and endowed with the highest abundance of gold.

children.text: rājā bhikṣavaḥ kanakavarṇa āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Monks, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> was wealthy, very rich, and possessed of great enjoyments.

children.text: prabhūtasattvasvāpateyaḥ prabhūtavittopakaraṇaḥ prabhūtadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpaḥ prabhūtahastyaśvagaveḍakaḥ paripūrṇakośakoṣṭhāgāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had abundant animate and inanimate property, abundant wealth and equipment, and abundant riches: grain, gold, bullion, jewels, pearls, beryl, conch, stone, coral, silver, and refined gold; he had many elephants, horses, cattle, and sheep, and his treasuries and granaries were full.

children.text: rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya khalu bhikṣavaḥ kanakāvatī nāma rājadhānī babhūva pūrveṇa paścimena ca dvādaśa yojanānyāyāmena dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca sapta yojanāni ca vistāreṇa ||
children.translated_text: Now, monks, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> had a capital city named <s>Kanakāvatī</s>, twelve yojanas in length from east to west and seven yojanas in breadth from south to north.

children.text: ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca ramaṇīyā ca ||
children.translated_text: It was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, crowded with many people, and delightful.

children.text: rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāśītir nagarasahasrāṇyabhūvan ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> had eighty thousand cities.

children.text: aṣṭādaśa kulakoṭī ṛddhāni sphītāni kṣemāṇi subhikṣāṇyākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: There were eighteen crores of families, prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people.

children.text: saptapañcāśadgrāmakoṭya ṛddhāḥ sphītāḥ kṣemāḥ subhikṣā ramaṇīyā mahājanākīrṇamanuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There were fifty-seven crores of villages, prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, delightful, and filled with multitudes of people.

children.text: ṣaṣṭiḥ karvaṭasahasrāṇyabhūvann ṛddhāni sphītāni kṣemāṇi subhikṣāṇyākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: There were sixty thousand market towns, prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people.

children.text: rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāṣṭādaśāmātyasahasrāṇy abhūvan ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> had eighteen thousand ministers.

children.text: viṃśatistrīsahasrāṇyantaḥpuramabhūt ||
children.translated_text: His inner apartments consisted of twenty thousand women.

children.text: rājā bhikṣavaḥ kanakavarṇo dhārmiko babhūva ||
children.translated_text: Monks, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> was righteous.

children.text: dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati ||
children.translated_text: He caused the kingdom to be governed according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: athāpareṇa samayena rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya ekākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasya evaṃ cetasi cetaḥparivitarkamudapādi yannvahaṃ sarvavaṇijo 'śulkānagulmān muñceyam ||
children.translated_text: Then at another time, while King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> was alone, withdrawn in a private place, this reflection arose in his mind: "What if I were to release all merchants from tolls and guard-post dues?

children.text: sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyān akārānagulmān muñceyamiti ||
children.translated_text: What if I were to release all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> from taxes and guard-post dues?"

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇo gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyān āmantrayate adyāgreṇa vo grāmaṇyaḥ sarvavaṇijo 'śulkān muñcāmi sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyān akārānaśulkān muñcāmi ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the accountants, chief officers, ministers, doorkeepers, and councilors: "Headmen, from this day forward I release all merchants from tolls; I release all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> from taxes and tolls."

children.text: tasyānenopāyena bahūni varṣāṇi rājyaṃ kārayato 'pareṇa samayena nakṣatraṃ viṣamībhūtaṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na varṣati ||
children.translated_text: As he governed the kingdom in this way for many years, at another time the heavenly bodies became adverse, and for twelve years the rain-god did not rain.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇā lakṣaṇajñā naimittikā bhūmyantarikṣamantrakuśalā nakṣatraśukragrahacariteṣu tat saṃlakṣayitvā yena rājā kanakavarṇaḥ tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then brahmins who knew the marks, omen-readers skilled in spells concerning the earth and sky and in the courses of the lunar mansions, Venus, and the planets, perceived this and went to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamidamavocan yatkhalu devo jānīyān nakṣatraṃ viṣamībhūtam dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na varṣiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they said this to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: "Your Majesty should know that the heavenly bodies have become adverse; for twelve years the rain-god will not rain."

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇa idamevaṃrūpaṃ nirghoṣaṃ śrutvā aśrūṇi pravartayati aho bata me jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ aho bata me jambudvīpa ṛddhaḥ sphītaḥ kṣemaḥ subhikṣo ramaṇīyo bahujanākīrṇamanuṣyo nacirādeva śūnyo bhaviṣyati rahitamanuṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> heard this report of such a kind, tears began to flow. "Alas for my people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! Alas for my <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, delightful, and crowded with many people! Before long it will become empty, devoid of people."

children.text: atha rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya muhūrtaṃ śocitvā etadabhavat ya ime āḍhyā mahādhanā mahābhogās te śakṣyanti yāpayitum ||
children.translated_text: Then, after King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> had grieved for a moment, this occurred to him: "Those who are wealthy, very rich, and possessed of great enjoyments will be able to keep themselves going.

children.text: ya ime daridrā alpadhanā alpānnapānabhogāḥ te katham yāpayiṣyanti tasyaitadabhavad yannvahaṃ jambudvīpādannādyaṃ saṃhareyaṃ sarvajāmbudvīpān sattvān gaṇayeyam ||
children.translated_text: But how will those who are poor, with little wealth and few enjoyments of food and drink, keep themselves going?" This occurred to him: "What if I were to gather the food and provisions from <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and count all the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?

children.text: atha gaṇayitvā māpayeyaṃ māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvekaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ kārayeyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after counting them, I would measure it out; after measuring it out, I would have one granary made in every village, city, town, market town, and capital.

children.text: ekaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ kārayitvā sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ samaṃ bhaktaṃ pratyarpayeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Having had one granary made, I would allot equal food to all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."

children.text: atha kanakavarṇo rājā gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyān āmantrayate gacchata yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ saṃhṛtya gaṇayata gaṇayitvā māpayata māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvekaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ sthāpayata ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the accountants, chief officers, ministers, doorkeepers, and councilors: "Go, headmen. After gathering the food and provisions from all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, count them; after counting them, measure them; after measuring them, establish one granary in every village, city, town, market town, and capital."

children.text: paraṃ deveti gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya pratiśrutya sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ gaṇayanti gaṇayitvā māpayanti māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvekasmin koṣṭhāgāre sthāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: "Very well, Your Majesty," said the accountants, chief officers, ministers, doorkeepers, and councilors. Having assented to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, they counted the food and provisions from all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; after counting them, they measured them; after measuring them, they stored them in a granary in every village, city, town, market town, and capital.

children.text: ekasmin koṣṭhāgāre sthāpayitvā yena rājā kanakavarṇaḥ tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After storing them in a granary, they went to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamidamavocad yat khalu deva jānīyāḥ sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣv annādyaṃ saṃhṛtam saṃhṛtya gaṇitam gaṇayitvā māpitam māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamarājadhānīṣvekasmin koṣṭhāgāre sthāpitaṃ yasyedānīṃ devaḥ kālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they said this to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: "Your Majesty should know that the food and provisions have been gathered from every village, city, town, market town, and capital; after being gathered, they have been counted; after being counted, they have been measured; after being measured, they have been stored in a granary in every village, city, town, and capital. Now let Your Majesty consider the time for whatever is appropriate."

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ saṃkhyāgaṇakalipikapauruṣeyānāmantrayitvā etadavocad gacchata yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyān gaṇayata gaṇayitvā grāmaṇyaḥ sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ samaṃ bhaktaṃ prayacchata ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> summoned the counting-officers, calculators, scribes, and agents and said this: "Go, headmen. Count all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; after counting them, headmen, give equal food to all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."

children.text: paraṃ deveti saṃkhyāgaṇakalipikapauruṣeyā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya pratiśrutya sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyān gaṇayanti saṃgaṇya rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamādau kṛtvā sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ samaṃ bhaktaṃ prajñapayanti ||
children.translated_text: "Very well, your Majesty," they replied. The enumerators, accountants, scribes, and officers promised King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, counted all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and, after counting them, beginning with King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, assigned an equal ration of food to all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: te yāpayantyekādaśavarṣāṇi dvādaśavarṣaṃ na yāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: They made it last for eleven years, but they did not make it last through the twelfth year.

children.text: nirgato dvādaśasya varṣasyaiko māso yāvadbahavaḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikā jighatsitāḥ pipāsitāḥ kālaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: When one month of the twelfth year had passed, many women, men, boys, and girls, hungry and thirsty, died.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ parikṣīṇamanyatra rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaikā mānikā bhaktasyāvaśiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: At that time food and provisions had been exhausted throughout all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, except that one <s>mānikā</s> measure of cooked rice remained to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena anyatamaścatvāriṃśatkalpasamprasthito bodhisattva imāṃ sahālokadhātumanuprāpto babhūva ||
children.translated_text: At that time a certain bodhisattva, who had set out for forty <s>kalpas</s>, arrived in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system.

children.text: adrākṣīd bodhisattvo 'nyatarasmin vanaṣaṇḍe putraṃ mātrā sārdhaṃ vipratipadyamānam ||
children.translated_text: The bodhisattva saw, in a certain forest thicket, a son falling into conflict with his mother.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat kliśyanti bateme sattvāḥ saṃkliśyanti bateme sattvā yatra hi nāma asyāmeva nava māsān kukṣau uṣitvā asyā eva stanau pītvā atraiva kālaṃ kariṣyati iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, he thought, "Alas, these beings are afflicted; alas, these beings are defiled, when, having lived for nine months in this very woman's womb and having drunk from these very breasts, he will die right here."

children.text: alaṃ me īdṛśaiḥ sattvair adhārmikair adharmarāgaraktair mithyādṛṣṭakair viṣamalobhābhibhūtair amātṛjñair aśrāmaṇyair abrāhmaṇyair akule jyeṣṭhāpacāyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Enough for me of such unrighteous beings, attached to unrighteous passion, holding wrong views, overcome by perverse greed, not knowing their mothers, devoid of the conduct of śramaṇas, devoid of the conduct of brahmins, and failing to honor the elders in their families.

children.text: ka utsahata īdṛśānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya bodhisattvacaryāṃ carituṃ yannvahaṃ svake kārye pratipadyeyam ||
children.translated_text: Who could be eager to practice the bodhisattva's conduct for the sake of such beings? What if I were to attend to my own business?"

children.text: atha bodhisattvo yenānyataradvṛkṣamūlaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva approached the foot of a certain tree.

children.text: upasaṃkramya tasmin vṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down at the foot of that tree.

children.text: paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya pañcasūpādānaskandheṣūdayavyayānudarśī viharati yadutedaṃ rūpam ayaṃ rūpasamudayaḥ ayaṃ rūpasyāstaṃgamaḥ iyaṃ vedanā iyaṃ saṃjñā ime saṃskārāḥ idaṃ vijñānam ayaṃ vijñānasamudayaḥ ayaṃ vijñānasyāstaṃgama iti ||
children.translated_text: Folding his legs crosswise, holding his body straight, and establishing mindfulness before him, he remained contemplating arising and passing away in the five aggregates subject to clinging: "This is form; this is the arising of form; this is the disappearance of form. This is feeling; this is perception; these are formations. This is consciousness; this is the arising of consciousness; this is the disappearance of consciousness."

children.text: sa evaṃ pañcasūpādānaskandheṣūdayavyayānudarśī viharannacirādeva yatkiṃcit samudayadharmakaṃ tat sarvaṃ nirodhadharmakamiti viditvā tatraiva pratyekāṃ bodhimadhigatavān ||
children.translated_text: As he remained thus contemplating arising and passing away in the five aggregates subject to clinging, before long he understood, "Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of cessation," and right there he attained the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavān pratyekabuddho yathāprāptānavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, surveying what he had attained, at that moment spoke a verse:

children.text: saṃsevamānasya bhavanti snehāḥ snehānvayaṃ sambhavatīha duḥkham
children.translated_text: For one who keeps company, affections arise; from affection suffering arises here.

children.text: ādīnavaṃ snehagataṃ viditvā ekaścaret khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the danger that lies in affection, one should wander alone, like the horn of a rhinoceros.

children.text: atha tasya bhagavataḥ pratyekabuddhasyaitadabhavad bahūnāṃ me sattvānāmarthāya duṣkarāṇi cīrṇāni na ca kasyacit sattvasya hitaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then that Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, thought, "For the sake of many beings I have performed difficult deeds, but I have not accomplished the welfare of any being.

children.text: kamadyāham anukampeyaṃ kasyāhamadya piṇḍapātamāhṛtya paribhuñjīya atha bhagavān pratyekabuddho divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣeṇa sarvāvantamimaṃ jambudvīpaṃ samantādanuvilokayannadrākṣīt sa bhagavān pratyekabuddhaḥ sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ parikṣīṇam anyatra rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaikā mānikā bhaktasyāvaśiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: On whom shall I have compassion today? From whose alms-offering shall I bring food and eat?" Then the Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, with his divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, surveyed all this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> on every side. The Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, saw that food and provisions had been exhausted throughout all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, except that one <s>mānikā</s> measure of cooked rice remained to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.

children.text: tasyaitadabhavad yannvahaṃ rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamanukampeyam ||
children.translated_text: He thought, "What if I were to have compassion on King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>?"

children.text: yannvahaṃ rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya niveśanāt piṇḍapātamapahṛtya paribhuñjīya ||
children.translated_text: "What if I were to take alms from the dwelling of King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> and eat?"

children.text: atha bhagavān pratyekabuddhastat eva ṛddhyā vihāyasamabhyudgamya dṛśyatā kāyena śakuniriva ṛddhyā yena kanakāvatī rājadhānī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, from that very place rose up into the sky by miraculous power and, with his body visible, like a bird, went by miraculous power toward <s>Kanakāvatī</s>, the royal capital.

children.text: tena khalu samayena rājā kanakavarṇa upariprāsādatalagato 'bhūt pañcamātrairamātyasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> was on the upper terrace of the palace, surrounded by five thousand ministers.

children.text: adrākṣīdanyatamo mahāmātrastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyekabuddhaṃ dūrata evāgacchantam ||
children.translated_text: One chief officer saw that Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, coming from afar.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarmahāmātrānāmantrayate paśyata paśyata grāmaṇyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, he addressed the chief officers: "Look, look, gentlemen!

children.text: dūrata eva lohitapakṣaḥ śakunta ihāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: A red-winged bird is coming here from afar."

children.text: dvitīyo mahāmātra evamāha naiṣa grāmaṇyo lohitapakṣaḥ śakuntaḥ rākṣasa eva ojohāra ihāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: A second chief officer said, "This is no red-winged bird, gentlemen. It is a rākṣasa, an essence-snatcher, coming here.

children.text: eṣo 'smākaṃ bhakṣayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: It will devour us."

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇa ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ mukhaṃ saṃparimārjya mahāmātrānāmantrayate naiṣa grāmaṇyo lohitapakṣaḥ śakuntaḥ na ca rākṣasa ojohāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> wiped his face with both hands and addressed the chief officers: "This is no red-winged bird, gentlemen, nor is it a rākṣasa, an essence-snatcher.

children.text: ṛṣireṣo 'smākamanukampayehāgacchati ||
children.translated_text: This is a seer coming here out of compassion for us."

children.text: atha sa bhagavān pratyekabuddho rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya prāsāde pratyaṣṭhāt ||
children.translated_text: Then that Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, alighted on King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>'s palace.

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyekabuddhamutthāyāsanāt pratyudgamya pādau śirasā vanditvā prajñapta evāsane niṣīdayati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> rose from his seat, went out to meet that Blessed One, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, bowed to his feet with his head, and seated him on the prepared seat.

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyekabuddhamidamavocat kimartham ṛṣe ihābhyāgamanaṃ bhojanārthaṃ mahārāja ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> said this to that Blessed One, the pratyekabuddha: "For what purpose, seer, have you come here?" "For food, great king."

children.text: evamukte rājā kanakavarṇaḥ prārodīt ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> began to weep.

children.text: aśrūṇi pravartayannevamāha aho me dāridryam aho dāridryaṃ yatra hi nāma jambudvīpaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayitvā ekasyāpi ṛṣerasamarthaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ pratipādayitum ||
children.translated_text: Shedding tears, he said this: "Ah, my poverty! Ah, poverty, when, after exercising lordship and sovereignty over <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, I am unable to provide alms-food even for a single seer."

children.text: atha yā kanakāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmadhyuṣitā devatā sā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya purastādgāthāṃ bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: Then the deity who dwelt in the capital city <s>Kanakāvatī</s> spoke a verse in the presence of King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>:

children.text: kiṃ duḥkhaṃ dāridryaṃ kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ tadeva dāridryam ||
children.translated_text: What is suffering? Poverty. What is still more painful? That very poverty.

children.text: maraṇasamaṃ dāridryam ||
children.translated_text: Poverty is equal to death.

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ koṣṭhāgārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate asti bhoḥ puruṣa mama niveśane kiṃcidbhaktaṃ yadahamasya ṛṣeḥ pradāsyāmi sa evamāha yat khalu deva jānīyāḥ sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ parikṣīṇam anyatra devasyaikā mānikā bhaktasyāvaśiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the man in charge of the storehouse: "Good man, is there any food in my residence that I may give to this seer?" He said this: "Your Majesty should know that food and provisions from all <s>Jambudvīpa</s> have been exhausted, except for one mānikā measure of cooked rice left for Your Majesty."

children.text: atha rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaitadabhavat sacet paribhuñje jīviṣye ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: "If I eat it, I will live.

children.text: atha na paribhokṣye mariṣye ||
children.translated_text: But if I do not eat it, I will die."

children.text: tasyaitadabhavad yadi paribhokṣye yadi vā na paribhokṣye avaśyaṃ mayā kālaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This occurred to him: "Whether I eat it or do not eat it, I must inevitably meet my time."

children.text: alaṃ me jīvitena ||
children.translated_text: "Enough of life for me.

children.text: kathaṃ nāmehedṛśa ṛṣiḥ śīlavān kalyāṇadharmā mama niveśane 'dya yathādhautena pātreṇa nirgamiṣyati atha rājā kanakavarṇo gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyān saṃnipātyaivamavocad anumodata yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ ayaṃ rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāpaścima odanātisargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could such a seer as this, virtuous and of good qualities, depart today from my residence with his bowl as clean as when it was washed?" Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> assembled the accountants, high officials, ministers, doorkeepers, and council members and said this: "Approve this, headmen: this is King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>'s final gift of boiled rice.

children.text: anena kuśalamūlena sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ dāridryasamucchedaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: By this root of merit, may the poverty of all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be cut off."

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇastasya maharṣestat pātraṃ gṛhītvā ekāṃ mānikāṃ bhaktasya pātre prakṣipya ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ pātraṃ gṛhītvā jānubhyāṃ nipatya tasya bhagavataḥ pratyekabuddhasya dakṣiṇe pāṇau pātraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> took the bowl of that great seer, placed the one mānikā measure of cooked rice in the bowl, grasped the bowl with both hands, fell on his knees, and placed the bowl in the right hand of that Blessed One, the pratyekabuddha.

children.text: dharmatā punarbhagavatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ kāyikī dharmadeśanā na vācikī ||
children.translated_text: It is the nature of blessed pratyekabuddhas that their teaching of dharma is bodily, not verbal.

children.text: atha bhagavān pratyekabuddho rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāntikāt piṇḍapātramādāya tat eva ṛddhyā uparivihāyasā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the pratyekabuddha, took the alms-bowl from King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> and departed by that very miraculous power, upward through the air.

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā tāvadanimiṣaṃ prekṣamāṇo 'sthāt yāvaccakṣuṣpathādatikrānta iti ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, with hands joined, stood gazing without blinking until he had passed beyond the range of sight.

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇo gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyān āmantrayate gacchata grāmaṇyaḥ svakasvakāni niveśanāni ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the accountants, high officials, ministers, doorkeepers, and council members: "Go, headmen, each to his own residence.

children.text: mā ihaiva prāsāde jighatsāpipāsābhyāṃ sarva eva kālaṃ kariṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: Do not all die right here in the palace from hunger and thirst."

children.text: ta evamāhur yadā devasya śrīsaubhāgyasampadāsīt tadā vayaṃ devena sārdhaṃ krīḍatā ramatā kathaṃ punarvayamidānīṃ devaṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye parityakṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: They said this: "When Your Majesty possessed the abundance of royal fortune and prosperity, we played and rejoiced together with Your Majesty. How then could we now abandon Your Majesty at the last time, at the final moment?"

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ prārodīt ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> began to weep.

children.text: aśrūṇi pravartayati ||
children.translated_text: Tears flowed from him.

children.text: aśrūṇi saṃparimārjya gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyān idamavocad gacchata grāmaṇyo yathāsvakasvakāni niveśanāni ||
children.translated_text: Wiping away his tears, he said this to the accountants, high officials, ministers, doorkeepers, and council members: "Go, headmen, each to his own residence.

children.text: mā ihaiva prāsāde jighatsāpipāsābhyāṃ sarva eva kālaṃ kariṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: Do not all die right here in the palace from hunger and thirst."

children.text: evamuktā gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyāḥ prarudanto 'śrūṇi pravartayanto 'śrūṇi saṃparimārjya yena rājā kanakavarṇastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they had been addressed in this way, the accountants, high officials, ministers, doorkeepers, and council members, weeping, shedding tears, and wiping away their tears, approached King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya pādau śirasā vanditvā añjaliṃ kṛtvā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaitadūcuḥ kṣantavyaṃ te yadasmābhiḥ kiṃcidaparāddham ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>'s feet, joined their hands, and said this to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: "You must forgive whatever offense has been committed by us.

children.text: adyāsmākaṃ devasyāpaścimaṃ darśanam ||
children.translated_text: Today is our last sight of Your Majesty."

children.text: tadyathā tena bhagavatā pratyekabuddhena sa piṇḍapātraḥ paribhuktaḥ atha tasminneva kṣaṇe samantāccatasṛṣu dikṣu catvāryabhrapaṭalāni vyutthitāni śītalāśca vāyavo vātumārabdhāḥ ye jambudvīpādaśuciṃ vyapanayanti meghāśca pravarṣayantaḥ pāṃśūñ śamayanti ||
children.translated_text: And when that alms-food in the bowl had been consumed by that Blessed One, the pratyekabuddha, at that very moment four masses of cloud arose on all four sides, and cool winds began to blow, removing impurity from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; and the clouds, raining, settled the dust.

children.text: atha tasminneva divase dvitīye 'rdhabhāge vividhasya khādanīyabhojanīyasya varṣaṃ pravarṣati ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the second half of that very day, a rain of various kinds of hard and soft food fell.

children.text: idamevamrūpaṃ bhojanamodanasaktavaḥ kulmāṣamatsyamāṃsam idamevamrūpaṃ khādanīyaṃ mūlakhādanīyaṃ skandhakhādanīyaṃ patrakhādanīyaṃ puṣpakhādanīyaṃ phalakhādanīyaṃ tilakhādanīyaṃ khaṇḍaśarkaraguḍakhādanīyaṃ piṣṭakhādanīyam ||
children.translated_text: There was food of this sort: boiled rice, parched-grain flour, beans, fish, and meat; and there were edibles of this sort: edible roots, edible stalks, edible leaves, edible flowers, edible fruits, sesame edibles, edibles of sugar candy and jaggery, and flour preparations.

children.text: atha rājā kanakavarṇo hṛṣṭatuṣṭah udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapārṣadyānāmantrayate paśyatha yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ adyaiva tasyaikapiṇḍapātadānasyāṅkuraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, delighted, satisfied, elated, pleased, gladdened, and filled with joy and happiness, addressed the accountants, chief officials, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers: "Look, gentlemen: today itself the sprout of that one alms-offering has appeared.

children.text: phalamanyadbhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The fruit will be something further."

children.text: atha dvitīye divase saptāhaṃ dhānyavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti tadyathā tilataṇḍulā mudgamāṣā yavā godhūmamasūrāḥ śālayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then on the second day a rain of grain fell for seven days, namely sesame seeds, rice grains, mung beans, black gram, barley, wheat, lentils, and <s>śāli</s> rice.

children.text: saptāhaṃ sarpivarṣaṃ pravarṣanti saptāhaṃ karpāsavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti saptāhaṃ nānāvidhadūṣyavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti saptāhaṃ saptaratnānāṃ varṣaṃ pravarṣanti suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamukteraśmagarbhasya musāragalvasya ||
children.translated_text: For seven days a rain of ghee fell; for seven days a rain of cotton fell; for seven days a rain of various kinds of cloth fell; and for seven days a rain of the seven jewels fell: gold, silver, beryl, crystal, red pearls, <s>aśmagarbha</s>, and <s>musāragalva</s>.

children.text: sarvasya rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyānubhāvena jāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ dāridryasamucchedo babhūva ||
children.translated_text: Through the whole power of King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, the poverty of the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was eradicated.

children.text: syāt khalu bhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vimatirvā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājā kanakavarṇo babhūva ||
children.translated_text: It may be, monks, that you have doubt or uncertainty: "Was someone else at that time, on that occasion, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>?"

children.text: na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: It should certainly not be seen in this way.

children.text: ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājā kanakavarṇo babhūva ||
children.translated_text: I was, at that time, on that occasion, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.

children.text: tadanena bhikṣavaḥ paryāyeṇa veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: By this method, monks, it should be understood.

children.text: sacedbhikṣavaḥ sattvā jānīyurdānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam apīdānīm yo 'sau apaścimakaḥ kavalaścarama ālopaḥ tato 'pyadattvā asaṃvibhajya na paribhuñjīran sacellabheran dakṣiṇīyaṃ pratigrāhakam ||
children.translated_text: If, monks, beings knew the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts, then even now they would not eat that last mouthful, that final morsel, without giving and without sharing from it, if they could find a worthy recipient, a receiver of offerings.

children.text: na caiṣāmutpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Nor would stinginess, once arisen, take possession of their mind and remain there.

children.text: yasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ sattvā na jānate dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam yathā ahaṃ jāne dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam tasmātte 'dattvā asaṃvibhajya paribhuñjate āgṛhītena cetasā utpannaṃ caiṣāṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādattaṃ tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: But because, monks, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts as I know the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts, therefore they eat without giving and without sharing, with a grasping mind; and stinginess, once arisen in them, takes possession of their mind and remains there.

children.text: na naśyate pūrvakṛtaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ na naśyate sevanaṃ piṇḍatānām
children.translated_text: The good and bad done in the past does not perish; service to those who live on alms does not perish.

children.text: na naśyate āryajaneṣu bhāṣitaṃ kṛtaṃ kṛtajñeṣu na jātu naśyati ||
children.translated_text: Speech uttered among noble people does not perish; what is done for the grateful never perishes at all.

children.text: sukṛtaṃ śobhanaṃ karma duṣkṛtaṃ vāpyaśobhanam
children.translated_text: A well-done, beautiful deed, or a badly done, unbeautiful one:

children.text: asti caitasya vipāko avaśya dāsyate phalam ||
children.translated_text: there is a ripening of this, and it will surely give its fruit.

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikādevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayaḥ sarvāvatī ca parṣadbhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Delighted, those monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and the entire assembly rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
